title: Department: Mechanical Engineering
text:
Department/Section: Mechanical Engineering (code: mechanical)
Website: https://iitrpr.ac.in/mechanical/

The Department offers a comprehensive B.Tech. program in Mechanical Engineering that provides students with the flexibility to pursue minors in a wide range of interdisciplinary fields, thereby equipping them with a broader perspective and diverse skill set to meet the evolving demands of industry and research. At the postgraduate level, the Department offers specialized M.Tech. programs in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanics & Design, Thermal & Fluids Engineering, and Computational Mechanics, each designed to provide in-depth knowledge, advanced technical expertise, and research-oriented learning opportunities. The faculty members are organized into three core groups – Design, Manufacturing, and Thermal. Within these groups, the Department actively engages in cutting-edge research and development in several prominent areas, including Additive Manufacturing technologies, Bio-Mechanical Engineering applications, Energy Efficiency and Sustainability solutions, Intelligent Mechanical Systems, and Micro/Nano Engineered Systems.

Welcome to
Department of Chemistry
The department of chemistry was established in 2009 to conduct cutting edge interdisciplinary research and impart high quality education in emerging areas of Chemical Science. The department was started with only four faculty members and three PhD students, and has grown significantly in last 14 years. It has 15 regular faculty and has more than eighty PhD students and 8 Post-doctoral fellows.

As a Department of Humanities and Social Sciences (HSS) in an Indian Institute of Technology that sets international parameters of academic excellence, this particular department strives to demonstrate its uniqueness and relevance to the vision of an IIT. The thrust of HSS is of course wedded to the visionary remark that Jawaharlal Nehru made while conceptualizing the IITs in the initial years of an independent India: “I know you can measure with your techniques and rules the hardness and strength of this metal or that, of stone and iron and whatnot. … How do you measure the strength of an individual? The human being as material is not only a difficult material but an exciting material because it is a live material, a growing material, a changing and dynamic thing

The Department of Biomedical Engineering (DBME) was established on February 2021 by superseding the Center for Biomedical Engineering (CBME) program, established earlier in May 2013.

The main goal of DBME is to meet the challenges of affordable healthcare facing the nation by encouraging research and entrepreneurship in interdisciplinary areas, encompassing engineering, medical sciences, and natural sciences. The center has following focus areas of research: Biomedical Imaging; Medical Devices; Cancer Diagnostics and Therapy; Biomaterials; and Tissue Engineering. The Health Center at IIT Ropar is dedicated to promoting the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of all members of the campus community, including students, faculty, and staff. Our mission is to provide accessible, high-quality, and compassionate healthcare services that support the overall health and success of the institute’s members.

We offer a comprehensive range of integrated services such as general medical care for common illnesses and minor injuries, preventive health check-ups and screenings to support long-term wellness, and mental health and counseling services to provide emotional and psychological support. We, along with our colleagues are committed towards making IIT Ropar the R&D powerhouse of the world. R&D section of the institute acts as the conduit for industrial interaction and faculty participation in sponsored research by providing administrative, financial and managerial support for the execution of all research and development projects in the Institute. The primary role is to sense the emerging landscape of various technology domains, prepare and enable the technology roadmap of the institute by interfacing with the industry, various ministries, peer academic institutions, and monitor the execution of the numerous sponsored R&D and consulting activities of the institute.
Research as a theme has always been the center of attention at IIT Ropar. Today, the R&D office has a staff of around 6 maintaining individual accounts of over 100 projects at any given time, processing papers related to purchase, travel, appointment, and salaries.

title: Event: NABL Gunvatta Yatra – Awareness Programme on NABL Accreditation & Its Benefits at IIT Ropar
text:
Title: NABL Gunvatta Yatra – Awareness Programme on NABL Accreditation & Its Benefits at IIT Ropar
Event description: Greetings from the Central Research Facility (CRF), IIT Ropar.

We are delighted to invite you to the NABL Gunvatta Yatra, a high-impact awareness programme on NABL Accreditation of Labs and its Benefits, organized jointly by CRF, IIT Ropar and the National Accreditation Board (NABL / QCI).

Accreditation plays a pivotal role in establishing credibility, reliability, ensuring measurement accuracy, and maintaining quality control in cutting-edge research and industrial applications. This workshop is specifically designed to provide valuable insights into quality standards, calibration protocols, and the strategic advantages of operating NABL-accredited facilities. For more details please find the attached NABL Flyer.

Why You Should Attend:

Gain Deep Insights: Understand the core framework of NABL accreditation and international testing & calibration standards.

Enhance Research & Quality Standards: Learn how accreditation elevates lab credibility, funding prospects, and commercial capability for institutional facilities.

Network & Collaborate: Interact directly with NABL subject matter experts, industry representatives, and peer researchers.

Earn a Certificate: All registered participants attending the full session will receive a Certificate of Participation.
Event location: Seminar Hall, Department of CSE, Ramanujan Block
Event type: seminar

title: Event: OPTICA IIT Ropar Orientation 2026
text:
Title: OPTICA IIT Ropar Orientation 2026
Event description: The OPTICA IIT Ropar Student Chapter is excited to welcome the incoming batch and invite you to our Orientation Session on 21 August 2026.

Our chapter has been actively building a community around optics, photonics, and light-based technologies through engaging activities, technical discussions, and opportunities to learn beyond the classroom.

But OPTICA, formerly known as The Optical Society of America (OSA), is much bigger than just our campus chapter. It is a worldwide community of students, researchers, educators, and industry leaders working together to advance the science and technology of light. Being part of it connects you to a global network that goes far beyond the walls of IIT Ropar

Whether you’re someone who has always been fascinated by lasers and light, a curious beginner wondering what photonics is all about, or simply looking for an enthusiastic community to learn and create with, there’s a place for you at OPTICA.

text:
Title: From Numerical Solvers to Data-Driven Machine Learning in Differential Equations (NS2ML-DE)
Event description: The goal of NS2ML-DE workshop is to equip participants with theoretical knowledge of numerical methods, and hands on practical training followed by data-driven machine learning algorithms such as Physics Informed Neural Networks etc.

Emphasis will be placed on applying these techniques to solve differential equations that govern real-world challenges in science and technology.

The workshop will feature hands-on sessions using MATLAB/PYTHON, where participants will implement numerical algorithms and machine learning algorithms starting from very basics to the advance level.

Upon completion of the workshop, participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of the entire process, from developing a mathematical model to constructing efficient numerical algorithms and implementing advanced computational strategies for simulations.

This workshop is designed for motivated and ambitious individuals, including Bachelor's and Master's students, research scholars, postdoctoral researchers, faculty members, and industry professionals.

title: Event: Expert talk by Prof. Sunando Dasgupta from the Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Kharagpur as part of the departmental seminar series in the Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Ropar
text:
Title: Expert talk by Prof. Sunando Dasgupta from the Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Kharagpur as part of the departmental seminar series in the Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Ropar
Event description: Expert talk as part of the departmental seminar series for 31st Aug 2026, at 3 PM. Prof. Sunando Dasgupta from the Department of Chemical Engineering at IIT Kharagpur will deliver a lecture titled "From Dendrites to Blood Drops: Interfacial Transport in Microfluidic Systems." The abstract of the talk is provided below for your reference. The venue will be communicated soon.

Abstract: Transport processes at the interface provide insights into a number of diverse processes at the micro-scale wherein surface tension, intermolecular interactions, electrohydrodynamic effects, and fluid transport play pivotal roles. These interfacial processes underpin diverse applications in droplet and digital microfluidics, biomicrofluidics, disease diagnostics, electrochemistry, and energy-storage systems. This presentation provides an overview of interfacial transport phenomena and explores the underlying physics of three distinct microfluidic processes. Starting with an overview, this presentation will delve into the physics of three different processes, namely, evolution of dendritic structures during charging, dried blood droplet morphology-based detection of Thalassaemia and coalescing droplets in plasma separation and haematocrit estimation in blood. Despite their distinct physical settings and applications, these systems share a common foundation in the interplay of forces acting at fluid–fluid, fluid–solid, and electrochemical interfaces. Understanding these interactions provides valuable insights into the formation, evolution, and dynamics of microscale structures and droplets. The presentation highlights how fundamental interfacial physics can be translated into practical microfluidic technologies for energy storage, biomedical diagnostics, and point-of-care applications.

Speaker Bio: Prof. Sunando Dasgupta is a Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering at IIT Kharagpur. He currently heads the Advanced Technology Development Center at IIT Kharagpur. He has been conferred the title of Fellow of the National Academy of Engineering, India. He obtained his B.Tech. (1985) and MTech. (1987) in Chemical Engineering from Jadavpur University and IIT Kanpur, respectively. Subsequently, he pursued a Ph.D. at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in the USA in 1992.

His research interests broadly span interfacial transport phenomena, microfluidics, wetting and thin-film dynamics, electrochemical systems, and bio-microfluidics, with applications in energy and low-cost diagnostic technologies. Prof. Dasgupta has authored more than 190 research papers and has supervised numerous doctoral students. He has also held several academic and administrative leadership positions at IIT Kharagpur, including Dean of Sponsored Research and Industrial Consultancy and Head of the Advanced Technology Development Center.

title: Event: Prof. Manojkumar Ramteke from Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Delhi will be delivering a talk on "Fault Detection, Control, and Model Maintenance of Process Systems using Machine Learning"
text:
Title: Prof. Manojkumar Ramteke from Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Delhi will be delivering a talk on "Fault Detection, Control, and Model Maintenance of Process Systems using Machine Learning"
Event description: Prof. Manojkumar Ramteke from Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Delhi will be delivering a talk on "Fault Detection, Control, and Model Maintenance of Process Systems using Machine Learning".

Machine learning models are increasingly transforming process systems engineering by enabling advanced monitoring, prediction, and control. However, conventional machine learning models often suffer from limited physical interpretability, a lack of incorporation of process knowledge, and computationally intensive training due to backpropagation. To address these limitations, several novel learning paradigms have been developed that integrate process physics, eliminate the need for backpropagation, and improve model accuracy and computational efficiency. A forward-learning neural network framework has been proposed for real-time updating of data-driven models using high-frequency process data, achieving accurate fault detection on benchmark datasets such as the Tennessee-Eastman process, nuclear power flux, and wastewater treatment plant datasets. Building upon this concept, a Kernel-based Forward Propagating Neural Network (K-FP-NN) has been developed that employs layer-wise forward updates rather than backpropagation, thereby providing enhanced adaptability for model predictive control of a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR).

To improve model reliability in dynamic industrial environments, the concept of machine unlearning has been introduced to selectively remove the influence of erroneous or obsolete data from trained models without requiring complete retraining, thereby significantly reducing computational overhead. The effectiveness of this approach has been demonstrated on the Tennessee-Eastman process and wastewater treatment plant datasets. Furthermore, a unified continual machine learning and machine unlearning framework has been developed to enable adaptive learning and corrective model maintenance in the presence of systemic drift. The framework has been validated on benchmark process systems, including a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR), batch polymerization of methyl methacrylate (PMMA), and a gas–liquid absorption system (GLAS), demonstrating its ability to maintain model accuracy under evolving process conditions.

title: IIT Ropar — UG ADMISSIONS
text:
UG ADMISSIONS
B.Tech
BSc - BEd
About the B.Sc - B.Ed Program

The Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) is a 4-year integrated programme under which the students will have a Dual Major undergraduate degree in a specific discipline along with B.Ed. Keeping in view the mandate of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and subsequent initiatives by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) (Ministry of Education, Government of India, New Delhi), the Department of Education at this institute offers B.Sc.-B.Ed (Secondary Stage) with Majors in three different disciplines, namely, Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics. Apart from preparing teachers for the reconfigured school education system in the country, the ITEP will help impart disciplinary knowledge in the abovementioned subjects so that the students will gain in-depth knowledge. It would also ensure their admission to higher studies in the disciplinary streams, including higher professional education.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY CELL
For Students
For Faculty/Staff

IIT Ropar has constituted a grievance cell to eradicate any kind of caste-based discrimination pertaining to the students belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Class.

The cell addresses academic and non-academic issues related to complaints received from the students in reserved categories. Understanding the concept of unity in diversity, the institute strives to maintain an environment where all communities can participate in academic/research/co-curricular activities without any caste/creed related discrimination.

title: IIT Ropar — Department of Chemistry
text:
Department of Chemistry
Welcome to Department of Chemistry The department of chemistry was established in 2009 to conduct cutting edge interdisciplinary research and impart high quality education in emerging areas of Chemical Science. The department was started with only four faculty members and three PhD students, and has grown significantly in last 14 years. It has 15 regular faculty and has more than eighty PhD students and 8 Post-doctoral fellows. The department has active research programs in emerging areas like Biomaterials, Biosensors, Catalysis, Drug Delivery, Materials, Organometallic Chemistry, Renewable Energy, Supramolecular Syntheses, Synthetic Organic Chemistry, Theoretical Chemistry, Ultracold Chemistry, etc. The research activities at the department are supported by state-of-the-art research facilities. The department has received funding through several sponsored national and international research projects.

title: IIT Ropar — Biomedical Engineering
text:
Biomedical Engineering
The Department of Biomedical Engineering (DBME) was established on February 2021 by superseding the Center for Biomedical Engineering (CBME) program, established earlier in May 2013. The main goal of DBME is to meet the challenges of affordable healthcare facing the nation by encouraging research and entrepreneurship in interdisciplinary areas, encompassing engineering, medical sciences, and natural sciences. The center has following focus areas of research: Biomedical Imaging; Medical Devices; Cancer Diagnostics and Therapy; Biomaterials; and Tissue Engineering. Because of the diverse research backgrounds of our faculty, there is a strong thrust on interdisciplinary research at the center. Going forward, the center seeks collaboration with national and international universities/institutes and partnership with industries to realize its goals.

title: IIT Ropar — Department of Physics
text:
Department of Physics
The Department of Physics at IIT Ropar was established in 2009 with an ambition to pursue high-level teaching methodologies and top-notch research in advanced areas of experimental & theoretical physics, and interdisciplinary areas of science and technology. Presently, the Department supports the undergraduate program of the institute and offers MSc. and Ph.D. programme in Physics. Our curiosity-driven research programs train young scientists to acquire knowledge and mould them as global leaders in science and technology as well as to communicate and engage with the broader society. The doctoral candidates and postdoctoral fellows are mentored in diverse areas of physical sciences, but are not limited to; flexible nano-structures for renewable energy, ion-beam surface modifications, physics of Graphene and nano-devices, low dimensional strongly correlated electron systems, nonlinear light scattering and interfacial structure of biologically relevant interfaces, nuclear structure and reaction dynamics, astrophysics, neutrino physics, mesoscopic physics and optomechanics, nano-scale optics and meta-materials, quantum optics, quantum information and computing, and quantum gravity and string theory

title: IIT Ropar — IIT ROPAR GUEST HOUSE
text:
IIT ROPAR GUEST HOUSE

In order to provide accommodation to the guests from other IIT's, Educational Institutions, Student Guardians etc visiting IIT Ropar for official work/ project work or for attending conference/seminar/workshop/JEE/GATE meeting etc. and at times for guests of IIT staff / parents of students, the institute runs a Guesthouse from the Visitor Guest House.

Download Application form for accomodation

Please fill it up and get it signed by appropriate authority before submitting the application.

GUIDELINES FOR GUESTHOUSE ACCOMMODATION
Check-in and Check-out time will be 01:00 pm and 11:00 am respectively.
One day minimum charge shall be levied for all bookings unless these are cancelled at least 24 hrs before the commencement of the booked date. Similarly, in case a guest fails to occupy the booked accommodation, the same will be cancelled after one day of the booking date.
Student requiring accommodation for their parents are required to get their requisition forwarded through their respective Wardens and Dean of Students.
Not more than two persons will be allowed in double occupancy bed room.
Booking is not permitted for guests undergoing medical treatment/ advice who are suffering from communicable disease or are bed ridden or are post-delivery case.
Pets/Dogs/Cats etc. are not allowed in the Guest House.
MHRD/Govt. of India clearance is required for the guest/visitors holding foreign passport for staying in the Guest House.
In case of emergency due to heavy booking, a single occupant of the room may be asked to share the accommodation with another guest. The accommodation in the Guest House shall be provided to the people in the order of precedence in which they are shown in table.
Request for availing dining facility to be communicated well in advance at the reception.
Accommodation will be provided on the basis of approval of competent authority and subject to the availability.
GST Charges will be extra as applicable.

* If the payment is to be made from the institute / project fund, no bill will be raised and only budget of the respective department/section will be deducted. But in case of Projects or other external funding events, budget will be deducted and deposited in the IRG. For that purpose bill may be raised on the request of the guests/organizers/PIs as the case may be.

title: IIT Ropar — VISION & MISSION
text:
VISION & MISSION

IIT Ropar community has undertaken an important exercise of developing the Mission, Vision and Strategic Plan for the coming years. The exercise was carried out in active consultation with Indian Institute of Management Calcutta who have got technical expertise in this area. A participative bottom up approach was followed in formulating the Mission, Vision and Strategic Plan. Inputs from the entire IIT Ropar fraternity, MHRD, Board of Governors, Alumni and Industries were considered in the process. Finally we have arrived at the following Motto, Mission and Vision statements for our institute.

Motto

धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् (Deploy our intellect on the right path)

Mission

To foster a transformative learning environment and a culture of excellence enabling creation of knowledge and development of socially responsible, enterprising leaders contributing significantly to national progress and humanity.

Vision

To be a trendsetter among the technology universities born in this millennium.

title: IIT Ropar — DIRECTOR
text:
DIRECTOR

Prof. Rajeev Ahuja is a globally distinguished computational materials scientist who serves as the Director of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar since April 2021. He concurrently holds the position of Professor of Computational Materials Science at Uppsala University, Sweden, where he has been associated for over three decades. He also held the additional charge of Director of IIT Guwahati from November 2023 to May 2024.

Prof. Ahuja is widely recognised as one of the most highly cited researchers in Sweden and India, and ranks among the top five materials scientists in both countries. His research has shaped foundational understanding in energy materials, high-pressure physics, and condensed matter theory over a career spanning more than 30 years.

Prof. Ahuja completed his doctoral degree from the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee in 1992. In the same year, he joined Uppsala University, Sweden, as a Post-Doctoral Fellow. He rose through the academic ranks at Uppsala University, becoming Assistant Professor in 1996, Associate Professor in 2002, and Full Professor in 2007.

His primary areas of research are computational materials science and condensed matter physics, with a strong focus on energy applications. These include batteries, hydrogen storage and production, and sensors, as well as high-pressure physics. His theoretical work, particularly in density functional theory, has made significant contributions to the design of energy storage materials and the study of electronic structure under extreme conditions.

Prof. Ahuja has published over 1,250 scientific papers in peer-reviewed journals, including high-profile publications in Science, Nature, Nature Materials, and PNAS. His Google Scholar citation count exceeds 59,000, with an h-index of 114 and an i-10 index of 880. He has supervised over 30 PhD students and more than 35 postdoctoral fellows.

Prof. Ahuja has received numerous national and international distinctions across his career. He is an elected Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry, United Kingdom (FRSC) and a Fellow of the American Physical Society (APS), USA, recognised for his seminal contributions to energy storage materials and computational studies of condensed matter under high pressure. He is also an elected member of the Royal Society of Sciences of Sweden (KVS).

He received the Wallmark Prize for 2011 from the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (KVA). He has also been honoured with the Eder Lilly and Sven Thureus Prize and the Benzelius Prize from the KVS. He was awarded the Beller Lectureship at the APS March Meeting 2017. In 2021, IIT Roorkee conferred upon him the Best Alumnus Award for excellence in research.

Prof. Ahuja serves as Associate Editor of Nano Energy. He is on the Advisory Board of Journal of Materials Chemistry A and Materials Advances, both published by the Royal Society of Chemistry, England.

Prof. Rajeev Ahuja
DIRECTOR, IIT ROPAR
director [at] iitrpr [dot] ac [dot] in
+91-1881-231006
Director's Message

Welcome to IIT Ropar!

This institute was founded on a simple but powerful idea: that world class science and engineering education must reach every corner of India, and that great research must address real problems. Since our first academic session in 2008, we have worked every day to live up to that idea.

Today, the institute comprises 12 academic departments spanning engineering, sciences, and humanities, Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Humanities and Social Sciences, Mathematics, Mechanical Engineering, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, and Physics. Together, they offer a full range of undergraduate B.Tech, M.Tech, M.Sc and PhD programs across disciplines. We have also recently launched a B.Tech in Digital Agriculture and a joint M.Sc in Data Science and Management with IIM Amritsar, both reflecting the direction in which we are deliberately growing.

We have chosen to be research intensive and impact-driven. Our faculty works at the frontiers of artificial intelligence, sustainable energy, defence technology, biomedical engineering, water science, and materials research. The results are visible. Our collaboration with the Army Technology Board on autonomous systems and directed energy has placed IIT Ropar at the forefront of strategic national research. Our Centre of Excellence in AI for Agriculture, ANNAM AI, is reshaping how technology can serve Indian farmers. Individual faculty members have received recognition from the Google Research Award, the Indian Immunological Society, the Indian Physical Society, and international chemistry bodies, a reflection of the quality and diversity of research being done here.

Our laboratories, incubators, and interdisciplinary programmes are designed to turn curiosity into capability and capability into contribution. Whether you are a JEE qualifier considering your choices, a researcher looking for a vibrant academic home, or an industry partner seeking meaningful collaboration, I invite you to look closely at what is being built here.

IIT Ropar is growing. Our community of students, faculty, alumni, and partners is shaping something that will matter well beyond this campus. I welcome you to be part of it.

title: IIT Ropar — ABOUT IIT ROPAR
text:
ABOUT IIT ROPAR

The Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar) is an Institute of National Importance, established in 2008 by the Ministry of Education under the Institutes of Technology (Amendment) Act of 2011. It is one of the eight Indian Institutes of Technology established to expand the reach and enhance the quality of technical education in the country.

The first academic session commenced at IIT Delhi, and the institute began functioning from its transit campus in Rupnagar on 1 August 2009. Today, IIT Ropar operates from a world-class permanent campus in Rupnagar, Punjab, a campus that reflects both the promise of modern science and the deep historical legacy of the land it stands on.

Vision and Motto

IIT Ropar's motto- Dhiyo yo nah prachodayat, drawn from the Gayatri Mantra, means: Deploy our intellect on the right path. It captures the institute's aspiration to nurture not just technical expertise, but wisdom, purpose, and responsibility. In just over 17 years, IIT Ropar has grown from a young institution to a nationally and globally recognized centre for education, research, and innovation, building, as its entrance pillars symbolize, the future on the foundations of a great civilization.

Our Campus

Located in the historic city of Rupnagar, Punjab, the institute's permanent campus spans 525 acres along the banks of the Sutlej River, a site deeply intertwined with the ancient Indus Valley Civilization. Nestled at the foothills of the Shivalik Range, the campus is approximately 50 km from Chandigarh, the state capital, and is well connected to the Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport in Mohali.

The geographical and historical context of the site is reflected in the institute's entrance architecture, which features four 41-foot high stone-carved pillars inspired by Harappan aesthetics, constructed in collaboration with the Archaeological Survey of India. Their molecular forms at the top, rising above Indus Valley motifs at the base, embody IIT Ropar's foundational philosophy: building modern science on the roots of a great civilization.

The campus is certified as a 5-star GRIHA-rated green campus and houses state-of-the-art academic blocks, eight hostels, a central library, sports complexes, and advanced research laboratories.

Academic Programmes

IIT Ropar comprises 12 academic departments, including Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Humanities and Social Sciences, Mathematics, Mechanical Engineering, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, and Physics.

The institute offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programmes across engineering, sciences, and interdisciplinary domains. The M.Tech programmes span Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, and Biomedical Engineering. The PhD programme is offered across 11 departments in four modes- Regular, Direct, External, and Part-time.

Among the institute's distinctive offerings is the B.Tech programme in Digital Agriculture, launched in 2025, which reflects the institute's commitment to using technology to address India's most pressing agricultural challenges.

IIT Ropar has also recently partnered with IIM Amritsar to launch a two-year residential degree programme in Data Science and Management, the Master of Science in Data Science and Management (MSDSM).

Research and Innovation

IIT Ropar has established a strong identity as a research-intensive institution. More than 500 startups have been incubated from IIT Ropar till date.

The institute has been designated as the Centre of Excellence in AI for Agriculture (Annam AI) under the Ministry of Education's national AI initiative, integrating artificial intelligence and data analytics to enhance agricultural productivity, optimize resource utilization, and improve climate resilience, empowering farmers and strengthening rural innovation ecosystems.

The IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation, iHub AWaDH (Agriculture and Water Technology Development Hub), is a national deep-tech hub established under the Department of Science and Technology's NM-ICPS Mission.

Recognized as the Most Promising Agritech Innovation Hub by eight or more national agencies, iHub AWaDH is shaping India's deep-tech ecosystem through research, entrepreneurship, and impactful collaborations.

IIT Ropar also runs the Technology Business Incubator Foundation (TBIF), which supports early-stage ventures in emerging technology domains.

TBIF has recently entered into collaboration with the Foundation for QC Innovation to advance quantum computing and deep-tech innovation in India.

Campus Life

IIT Ropar offers a vibrant and inclusive campus life. Students participate in annual festivals, the cultural fest Zeitgeist, the sports fest Aarohan, and the technical fest Advitiya, alongside a range of clubs, societies, and outreach initiatives.

The institute's Career Development and Placement Cell (CDPC) maintain strong industry connections. Top recruiters at IIT Ropar include Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Goldman Sachs, Oracle, and Texas Instruments.

The institute also houses a wellness centre, Snehita, and provides health services, transport facilities, and a Day Care Facility, ensuring a supportive and holistic environment for students and staff.

Expert talk by Prof. Sunando Dasgupta from the Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Kharagpur as part of the departmental seminar series in the Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Ropar
15:00:00
31 Aug 2026
event

Expert talk as part of the departmental seminar series for 31st Aug 2026, at 3 PM. Prof. Sunando Dasgupta from the Department of Chemical Engineering at IIT Kharagpur will deliver a lecture titled "From Dendrites to Blood Drops: Interfacial Transport in Microfluidic Systems." The abstract of the talk is provided below for your reference. The venue will be communicated soon. Abstract: Transport processes at the interface provide insights into a number of diverse processes at the micro-scale wherein surface tension, intermolecular interactions, electrohydrodynamic effects, and fluid transport play pivotal roles. These interfacial processes underpin diverse applications in droplet and digital microfluidics, biomicrofluidics, disease diagnostics, electrochemistry, and energy-storage systems. This presentation provides an overview of interfacial transport phenomena and explores the underlying physics of three distinct microfluidic processes. Starting with an overview, this presentation will delve into the physics of three different processes, namely, evolution of dendritic structures during charging, dried blood droplet morphology-based detection of Thalassaemia and coalescing droplets in plasma separation and haematocrit estimation in blood. Despite their distinct physical settings and applications, these systems share a common foundation in the interplay of forces acting at fluid–fluid, fluid–solid, and electrochemical interfaces. Understanding these interactions provides valuable insights into the formation, evolution, and dynamics of microscale structures and droplets. The presentation highlights how fundamental interfacial physics can be translated into practical microfluidic technologies for energy storage, biomedical diagnostics, and point-of-care applications. Speaker Bio: Prof. Sunando Dasgupta is a Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering at IIT Kharagpur. He currently heads the Advanced Technology Development Center at IIT Kharagpur. He has been conferred the title of Fellow of the National Academy of Engineering, India. He obtained his B.Tech. (1985) and MTech. (1987) in Chemical Engineering from Jadavpur University and IIT Kanpur, respectively. Subsequently, he pursued a Ph.D. at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in the USA in 1992. His research interests broadly span interfacial transport phenomena, microfluidics, wetting and thin-film dynamics, electrochemical systems, and bio-microfluidics, with applications in energy and low-cost diagnostic technologies. Prof. Dasgupta has authored more than 190 research papers and has supervised numerous doctoral students. He has also held several academic and administrative leadership positions at IIT Kharagpur, including Dean of Sponsored Research and Industrial Consultancy and Head of the Advanced Technology Development Center.

Prof. Manojkumar Ramteke from Dept. of Chemical Engineering, IIT Delhi will be delivering a talk on "Fault Detection, Control, and Model Maintenance of Process Systems using Machine Learning"
16:00:00
10 Aug 2026
event

Prof. Manojkumar Ramteke from Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Delhi will be delivering a talk on "Fault Detection, Control, and Model Maintenance of Process Systems using Machine Learning". Machine learning models are increasingly transforming process systems engineering by enabling advanced monitoring, prediction, and control. However, conventional machine learning models often suffer from limited physical interpretability, a lack of incorporation of process knowledge, and computationally intensive training due to backpropagation. To address these limitations, several novel learning paradigms have been developed that integrate process physics, eliminate the need for backpropagation, and improve model accuracy and computational efficiency. A forward-learning neural network framework has been proposed for real-time updating of data-driven models using high-frequency process data, achieving accurate fault detection on benchmark datasets such as the Tennessee-Eastman process, nuclear power flux, and wastewater treatment plant datasets. Building upon this concept, a Kernel-based Forward Propagating Neural Network (K-FP-NN) has been developed that employs layer-wise forward updates rather than backpropagation, thereby providing enhanced adaptability for model predictive control of a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR). To improve model reliability in dynamic industrial environments, the concept of machine unlearning has been introduced to selectively remove the influence of erroneous or obsolete data from trained models without requiring complete retraining, thereby significantly reducing computational overhead. The effectiveness of this approach has been demonstrated on the Tennessee-Eastman process and wastewater treatment plant datasets. Furthermore, a unified continual machine learning and machine unlearning framework has been developed to enable adaptive learning and corrective model maintenance in the presence of systemic drift. The framework has been validated on benchmark process systems, including a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR), batch polymerization of methyl methacrylate (PMMA), and a gas–liquid absorption system (GLAS), demonstrating its ability to maintain model accuracy under evolving process conditions.

Frequently Asked Questions

Ques.1: How to edit my submitted application for summer internship 2026?

Ans.1 You can edit your submitted application by login to the portal using your ID and Password.

Ques.2: What to upload for the Transcripts demanded in the document section?

Ans.2 Transcript is the consolidated sheet indicating your marks/CGPA earned in previous semesters. In case you do not have the same, you can attach your previous semesters' gradesheets.

Ques.3: Is it necessary to attach bonafide certificate with an application?

Ans.3 Yes.

Ques.4: What is the format for bonafide certificate?

Ans.4 The bonafide certificate can be in the format as issued by your institute/college/university. The candidate should include his/her present year of study and the degree pursuing.

Ques.5: Can any candidate who is presently not enrolled in any UG or PG program in any university/college/institute may apply for this internship?

Ans.5 For summer internship, the candidate needs to be a bonafide student of institute/college/university (mentioned in the published advertisement).

Ques.6: When the list of selected candidates will be released or when we will be notified?

Ans.6 After the last date of an application (mentioned in advt.), the process of scrutinization will commence, which will take few days time. You need to regularly visit the website for an update, however, an intimation email from the department will also be forwarded to the selected candidates.

Ques.7: How should I select Research Supervisor?

Ans.7 The candidates are advised to visit the website of IIT Ropar and select the appropriate department and research supervisor according to his/her interest. After selecting, the candidates fill the name of research supervisor in the online form.

Important Instructions
The candidates must select a Research Supervisor in their relevant field of study/course. They have an option in the form to select at most 3 Research Supervisors.
The candidates are required to do their internship in one department under one supervisor only.
Hostel accommodation on a sharing basis will be provided subject to availability on a chargeable basis. The application for accommodation (only after being selected for internship) should reach the office of Dean of Student Affairs through the faculty supervisor and the HoD for permission. The cost towards food, accommodation and access to other amenities have to be paid by the student. Accommodation is only available if a student pursues internship between 15th May, 2026 to 15th July, 2026.
No financial assistance will be provided to the candidates.
The internship at IIT Ropar will be conducted from 15/05/2026 to 15/07/2026 only.
The requests for change in the dates will not be permitted due to logistical constraints.
Minimum 8 weeks internship duration is required to issue the certificates.

title: IIT Ropar — SCHOLARSHIPS
text:
SCHOLARSHIPS

THE INSTITUTE OFFERS FOLLOWING SCHOLARSHIP/FREESHIP TO THE STUDENTS.

Institute Merit-cum-Means (MCM) Scholarships

The Institute offers Merit-cum-Means scholarships to under-graduate students in engineering and technology. These are permissible to about 25% of the students. The present value of Merit-cum-Means scholarship is Rs. 1000 per month for general category students and the recipient is exempted from paying tuition fee.

4-year B.Tech. students are eligible to receive Merit-cum-Means scholarship at the time of joining the Institute. The criterion of merit for the first year is All India Rank (AIR) in the JEE. The scholarships are renewed on a yearly basis until he/she clears all academic requirements of the programme, provided that he/she continues to satisfy the eligibility and continuation criteria.

For continuation of MCM, the performance of the students will be reviewed at the end of each semester. The first such review will be held at the end of the second semester.

Continuation of MCM Scholarship:

For the general category students, the requirements of merit for the continuation of Institute Merit-cum-Means Scholarship are:

CGPA must be 6.0 or more; and
Earned credits should not be less than 20 times the number of semesters registered for;
SGPA in the previous semester must be 6.0 or more
Institute Merit Prizes and Certificates

The Institute offers merit prizes and certificates to the top 7% of the students of each 4-year B.Tech. Programme for the 1st and 2nd semester. The value of merit prize is Rs. 2500. The rules are as follows:

For Merit Prizes and Certificates, the top 7% of the students admitted or sanctioned capacity whichever is less will be eligible in order of merit. In case the 7% limit is exceeded by virtue of more than one student having same merit, those students will also be eligible for these awards. The students having SGPA/CGPA less than 8.50 will not be considered for the award of merit prizes and certificates.
If 7% departmental strength is less than one, the students with highest CGPA subject to minimum 8.5 will be awarded the merit prizes of Rs.2500/-.
A prize of Rs.2500/- will be paid to all students entitled to merit prizes. This will be in addition to any scholarship that student may receive from any source whatsoever.
The award will be given to the top 7% of the students each semester based on their SGPA in the previous semester.
The award of 1st year students will be given in 2nd semester based on their performance in 1st semester.
There will be a common merit list of all students for the first year students. The merit list from 2nd to 5th year will be made discipline wise.
Any student except final semester, having less than 18 earned credits in the semester under consideration will not be eligible for merit prizes. All the credits of courses repeated by the student in the semester under consideration will not count towards the 18 earned credits mentioned above.
All graduating students subject to the 7% limit will be considered eligible for awards on SGPA basis obtained during 8th/10th semester. In case of a tie, merit prize will be awarded to the student with higher CGPA.
Institute Free Studentship

The Institute offers free studentship to 10% of the students on the basis of means alone. The recipient is exempted from paying tuition fee. Students who are not eligible for the award of MCM Scholarship on the basis of their parent's income will not be considered eligible for the award of Free Studentship Scholarship.

For continuation of Free studentship, the scholar must have to maintain the following criteria:
CGPA must be 6.0 or more; and
Earned credits should not be less than 20 times the number of semesters registered for;
SGPA in the previous semester must be 6.0 or more
Scholarship Provision for Students of SC/ST Category

Tuition fee exemption is admissible to all SC/ST students irrespective of their parents/guardians income.

The Institute offers a scholarship of Rs. 300/- per month and exemption from paying room rent of the hostel, only to those SC/ST students whose parent'/guardians' income does not exceed the limit prescribed by the Government of India from time to time for the award of Merit-cum-Means scholarship.

The students can opt for free mess facilities (basic menu) and Rs. 250/- per month as pocket allowance in lieu of the amount of the scholarship.

All the eligible SC/ST students while on training or doing courses during semester breaks or required to stay in the Institute during the semester breaks or exempted to take meals from the hostel due to medical reasons etc. may be given a payment of Rs. 70/- as pocket allowance (per month) and a per diem allowance in lieu of free mess facilities on the basis of prevalent average rate of mess charges as applicable from time to time.

Where an SC/ST candidate fails in the examination for the first time, the award may be renewed subject to a maximum limit of 5 years.

Post-Metric Scholarship

The SC/ST can opt for Post Metric Scholarship offered to them by the State Government. For further details, Students can visit respective State Government website.

Scholarship for ST Students

Notification for Scholarship for ST Students Click Here

The student can opt for this scholarship awarded by Government of India (Ministry of Tribal Affairs). Students are required to apply for this scholarship to:

https://scholarships.gov.in/

Top Class Education Scholarship for SC/ST Students

The student can opt for this scholarship awarded by Government of India. Students are required to apply for this scholarship to:

https://scholarships.gov.in/

Other Scholarship

In addition to above mentioned scholarships there are few other scholarships awarded by NGO's and some external agencies.

Scholarship for B.Tech. - M.Tech. Dual Degree

Students belong to B.Tech.-M.Tech. Dual degree programme who have good academic performance are given a scholarship in the final year, which is at par with that given to students of M.Tech. programmes.

NOTE

For all the scholarships only affidavit on a judicial stamp paper of Rs 20/- duly signed by Magistrate / S.D.O/B.D.O / Tehsildar / Revenue Officer of his Jurisdiction as per requisite proforma in support of income proof OR Income Tax Return will be acceptable.

ILLUMINANCE 26 - International Day of Light 2026
09:00:00
Lecture Hall Complex

It is our great pleasure to inform you that the Optica IIT Ropar Student Chapter is launching the first edition of Illuminance on 16 May 2026, a platform dedicated to celebrate light, innovation, and discovery on the occasion of the International Day of Light. Recognized by UNESCO, this global initiative highlights the importance of light and light-based technologies in science, education, and technological advancement. Aligned with this year’s theme, “Light for a Sustainable Development,” the event seeks to emphasize the role of optics and photonics in addressing global challenges and to inspire the next generation toward STEM education and research. This event aims to bring together researchers, faculty members, college students, and school students through a series of invited talks and interactive outreach activities. The program will include: Invited talks by experts in the field of optics and photonics. Live optics demonstrations and a quiz for school students.

Apr
Nirvana - The Wellness Fest 2026
10:00:00
Auditorium, IIT Ropar

Nirvana – The Wellness Fest Nirvana, the flagship annual fest of the Board of Wellness Affairs, is a vibrant and immersive celebration dedicated to fostering community, holistic health, and inner harmony. Spanning three enriching days, the fest transforms the campus into a lively hub of positivity, creativity, and connection. It brings together students, peer mentors, and invited experts to co-create an inclusive space where everyone feels welcomed and valued. The fest features a diverse range of activities, including engaging games, interactive food stalls, wellness workshops, and inspiring talks. Participants can explore sessions such as yoga, meditation, fitness activities, and expressive art events. Live music performances and club events add energy and excitement, while wellness pavilions offer spaces for relaxation and reflection. Each segment is thoughtfully curated to promote mental well-being, physical vitality, and emotional balance. Beyond entertainment, Nirvana focuses on meaningful experiences. It encourages self-reflection, stress relief, and stronger interpersonal connections. Whether it is unwinding in a calming meditation session, enjoying vibrant performances, or bonding with peers, every moment contributes to a sense of belonging. Nirvana is more than just a fest. It is a journey toward self-discovery and well-being, leaving participants with renewed energy, clarity, and a deeper connection to themselves and the community around them.

Dr. Durba Pal has been selected for the Rajib Goyal Young Scientist Prize 2026 in the field of Life Sciences

Kurukshetra University has announced the recipients of the prestigious Rajib Goyal Prize for Young Scientists for the academic session 2023-24, recognising four outstanding researchers from across the country for their significant contributions to science. The awardees, all below the age of 45, are: Dr Gopinath Packirisamy from Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (Applied Sciences), Dr Debabrata Maiti from Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (Chemical Sciences), Dr Durba Pal from Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (Life Sciences), and Dr Smarajit Karmakar from Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Hyderabad (Physical Sciences). Each Rajib Goyal Prize carries a medal, citation and a cash award of Rs 1 lakh.

06 Feb 2026 - 08 Feb 2026

Advitiya 2026, IIT Ropar's annual technical fest, is back to set the benchmark for technological innovation and intellectual grit. This year, the fest is themed "A Space Odyssey," transforming our campus into a launchpad for the next generation of engineers and creators. We bring together a massive lineup of high-stakes competitions, including app development battles, AI and algorithm challenges, fin-tech simulations and cyber-security hunts. Beyond the screen, expect to see the future in motion with robotics showcases, aerospace contests, and creative design modules. Whether it’s solving complex mathematical problems or dominating in gaming and finance, Advitiya is where the brightest minds come to push past the ordinary. If you’re obsessed with the "how" and the "why," you belong here. This is ADVITIYA 2026, where deep-tech meets raw creativity.

title: IIT Ropar — Mechanical Engineering
text:
Mechanical Engineering
The Department offers a comprehensive B.Tech. program in Mechanical Engineering that provides students with the flexibility to pursue minors in a wide range of interdisciplinary fields, thereby equipping them with a broader perspective and diverse skill set to meet the evolving demands of industry and research. At the postgraduate level, the Department offers specialized M.Tech. programs in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanics & Design, Thermal & Fluids Engineering, and Computational Mechanics, each designed to provide in-depth knowledge, advanced technical expertise, and research-oriented learning opportunities. The faculty members are organized into three core groups – Design, Manufacturing, and Thermal. Within these groups, the Department actively engages in cutting-edge research and development in several prominent areas, including Additive Manufacturing technologies, Bio-Mechanical Engineering applications, Energy Efficiency and Sustainability solutions, Intelligent Mechanical Systems, and Micro/Nano Engineered Systems.

Faculty Advisors Roles and Responsibilities

It is the responsibility of Faculty Advisor to be well-versed with academic rules and regulations and go through the Handbook of Information for respective batches.

Advice on courses:

At the time of registration, faculty advisor has to guide students to finalize the academic programme, keeping in view factors such as minimum/maximum number of total credits, past performance, backlog of courses, SGPA/CGPA, pre-requisite, workload, and student's interests, amongst others.

The following are the special provisions for academically weaker students:

If a student requests, faculty advisor can allow 1-1.5 credits over and above the prescribed limit, if he/she feels that the student will be able to take these credits for completion of his/her course requirement.
Faculty advisor can recommend to waive off the pre-requisite for any particular course, if a student has gone through it once in a regular semester, if it affects the future courses.

Probation/Restart:

If a student is placed on probation/restart, faculty advisor shall monitor the student's progress.

He/she has to advise the student on the courses and credits required to be taken.
Maintain proper records of course plan, separately, for each student.
Faculty advisor shall ask students to prepare a course chart/plan of courses for helping the students in completion of course requirements/degree within the stipulated time, if he/she is placed on probation.
Such plans to be forwarded to the respective Dean (Academics) through HoD.
Talk to parents/guardians of the students and have a meeting with them, if faculty advisor feels necessary.

Faculty Advisors shall closely monitor the performance and attendance of probation students in order to ensure corrective measures in respect of cases where the students are continuously absent from the classes. Further, the assistance of Student Counsellor may be taken wherever required for corrective action. For this, the faculty advisor can ask the concerned instructor for attendance, marks, and other feedback.

Special measures for academically weaker reserved category students: Faculty advisors are encouraged to have one to one meetings with each student at regular intervals. A faculty advisor can have special attention to advise them on academic and non-academic matters. A faculty advisor shall closely monitor the performance of such students. The performance report of such students needs to be forwarded to Dean (Academics) through HoD.

Faculty Advisors shall give his/her recommendations if a student wants to withdraw the semester on medical grounds.

Student-Faculty Advisor meetings, as per academic calendar, shall be conducted by Faculty Advisor.

The report of the same in the prescribed format (given at Annexure-I) should be forwarded to HoD and concerned Dean within a week after the meeting for information/further action.

1st Student-Faculty Advisor Meeting to be held to see if the course instructors have provided the course outline, grading policy, policy on missed quizzes, any misconduct during class/quiz/assignments, and any other initial issues in the course.
2nd Student-Faculty Advisor Meeting to see the progress of the course, monitor the mid-sem exam performance based on the data requested and received from course instructors, and give suggestions to the students for improvement.

Courses required by the students during summer semester, based on their performance, shall also be collected by the Faculty Advisor and forwarded to the respective Dean (Academics) through HoD.

Faculty Advisors shall take care of the timely disposal of online registration requests on AIMS during registration/Add-Drop period.

Faculty Advisors should closely monitor the progress of final year students to make sure that they complete the degree within stipulated time.

Faculty Advisors are encouraged to have one to one meetings with each student at regular intervals. They may approach the course instructor if students require any specific attention/support in a particular course.

Any other work not mentioned above, required for helping academically a student to improve his/her performance shall be taken up by the Faculty Advisor by consulting HoD/concerned Dean.

To foster a healthy and friendly atmosphere for discussions, the faculty advisor may arrange tea/coffee with snacks during Student-Faculty Advisor (SFA-1 and SFA-2) meetings.

NABL Gunvatta Yatra – Awareness Programme on NABL Accreditation & Its Benefits at IIT Ropar
10:00:00
Seminar Hall, Department of CSE, Ramanujan Block

Greetings from the Central Research Facility (CRF), IIT Ropar. We are delighted to invite you to the NABL Gunvatta Yatra, a high-impact awareness programme on NABL Accreditation of Labs and its Benefits, organized jointly by CRF, IIT Ropar and the National Accreditation Board (NABL / QCI). Accreditation plays a pivotal role in establishing credibility, reliability, ensuring measurement accuracy, and maintaining quality control in cutting-edge research and industrial applications. This workshop is specifically designed to provide valuable insights into quality standards, calibration protocols, and the strategic advantages of operating NABL-accredited facilities. For more details please find the attached NABL Flyer. Why You Should Attend: Gain Deep Insights: Understand the core framework of NABL accreditation and international testing & calibration standards. Enhance Research & Quality Standards: Learn how accreditation elevates lab credibility, funding prospects, and commercial capability for institutional facilities. Network & Collaborate: Interact directly with NABL subject matter experts, industry representatives, and peer researchers. Earn a Certificate: All registered participants attending the full session will receive a Certificate of Participation.

OPTICA IIT Ropar Orientation 2026
14:00:00
Room S101, Part A, Super Academic Block

The OPTICA IIT Ropar Student Chapter is excited to welcome the incoming batch and invite you to our Orientation Session on 21 August 2026. Our chapter has been actively building a community around optics, photonics, and light-based technologies through engaging activities, technical discussions, and opportunities to learn beyond the classroom. But OPTICA, formerly known as The Optical Society of America (OSA), is much bigger than just our campus chapter. It is a worldwide community of students, researchers, educators, and industry leaders working together to advance the science and technology of light. Being part of it connects you to a global network that goes far beyond the walls of IIT Ropar Whether you’re someone who has always been fascinated by lasers and light, a curious beginner wondering what photonics is all about, or simply looking for an enthusiastic community to learn and create with, there’s a place for you at OPTICA.

IIT Ropar Director Prof. Rajeev Ahuja Conferred with Chief of Army Staff Commendation

Prof. Rajeev Ahuja, Director, IIT Ropar, has been conferred with the Chief of Army Staff Commendation by Gen Upendra Dwivedi, PVSM, AVSM, Chief of the Army Staff. This recognition by the Indian Army Chief is a direct acknowledgement of IIT Ropar’s growing contributions to defence technology and research. Prof. Ahuja said, “I am thankful and greatly humbled by this honour bestowed on me by the Chief. I owe this to the hard work put in by Team IIT Ropar to create a defence research and innovation ecosystem to help strengthen the security of the Nation. This recognition will give us renewed impetus to fulfil our pledge towards ensuring Atmanirbharta in defence.” At IIT Ropar, defence research and innovation is not just a mandate. It is a mission. From Resilient Habitat to Autonomous Armoured Vehicles and Directed Energy Weapons, our teams are working on some of India’s most critical frontier technologies backed by the Army Technology Board and Army Formations.

IIT Ropar to develop 2 projects for Army valuing Rs 120 Crore

Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Ropar, has secured two projects from the Army Technology Board (ATB) with a combined outlay of Rs 120 crore. The projects are expected to use artificial intelligence for various things, thereby reducing risks to soldiers operating in hostile environments.

Theme: "Yoga for Healthy Ageing" The Indian Institute of Technology Ropar is pleased to invite you to participate in Yoga Sangam 2026, organized as part of the celebrations of the 12th International Day of Yoga (IDY) on 21 June 2026. Recognized across the world for its physical and mental benefits, Yoga helps improve flexibility, strength, concentration, and stress management. Reflecting this year’s theme, “Yoga for Healthy Ageing,” we encourage everyone to embrace yoga as a pathway to both personal well-being and collective harmony. In celebration of this occasion, we are organizing a guided yoga session. The session will offer participants an opportunity to experience different yoga practices and techniques while coming together as a community in the spirit of wellness and unity.

ILLUMINANCE 26 - International Day of Light 2026

Lecture Hall Complex

It is our great pleasure to inform you that the Optica IIT Ropar Student Chapter is launching the first edition of Illuminance on 16 May 2026, a platform dedicated to celebrate light, innovation, and discovery on the occasion of the International Day of Light. Recognized by UNESCO, this global initiative highlights the importance of light and light-based technologies in science, education, and technological advancement. Aligned with this year’s theme, “Light for a Sustainable Development,” the event seeks to emphasize the role of optics and photonics in addressing global challenges and to inspire the next generation toward STEM education and research. This event aims to bring together researchers, faculty members, college students, and school students through a series of invited talks and interactive outreach activities. The program will include: Invited talks by experts in the field of optics and photonics. Live optics demonstrations and a quiz for school students.

06
Jul
From Numerical Solvers to Data-Driven Machine Learning in Differential Equations (NS2ML-DE)
09:00:00
06 Jul 2026 - 10 Jul 2026

The goal of NS2ML-DE workshop is to equip participants with theoretical knowledge of numerical methods, and hands on practical training followed by data-driven machine learning algorithms such as Physics Informed Neural Networks etc. Emphasis will be placed on applying these techniques to solve differential equations that govern real-world challenges in science and technology. The workshop will feature hands-on sessions using MATLAB/PYTHON, where participants will implement numerical algorithms and machine learning algorithms starting from very basics to the advance level. Upon completion of the workshop, participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of the entire process, from developing a mathematical model to constructing efficient numerical algorithms and implementing advanced computational strategies for simulations. This workshop is designed for motivated and ambitious individuals, including Bachelor's and Master's students, research scholars, postdoctoral researchers, faculty members, and industry professionals.

03
Apr
Nirvana - The Wellness Fest 2026
10:00:00
Auditorium, IIT Ropar

Nirvana – The Wellness Fest Nirvana, the flagship annual fest of the Board of Wellness Affairs, is a vibrant and immersive celebration dedicated to fostering community, holistic health, and inner harmony. Spanning three enriching days, the fest transforms the campus into a lively hub of positivity, creativity, and connection. It brings together students, peer mentors, and invited experts to co-create an inclusive space where everyone feels welcomed and valued. The fest features a diverse range of activities, including engaging games, interactive food stalls, wellness workshops, and inspiring talks. Participants can explore sessions such as yoga, meditation, fitness activities, and expressive art events. Live music performances and club events add energy and excitement, while wellness pavilions offer spaces for relaxation and reflection. Each segment is thoughtfully curated to promote mental well-being, physical vitality, and emotional balance. Beyond entertainment, Nirvana focuses on meaningful experiences. It encourages self-reflection, stress relief, and stronger interpersonal connections. Whether it is unwinding in a calming meditation session, enjoying vibrant performances, or bonding with peers, every moment contributes to a sense of belonging. Nirvana is more than just a fest. It is a journey toward self-discovery and well-being, leaving participants with renewed energy, clarity, and a deeper connection to themselves and the community around them.

Dr. Durba Pal has been selected for the Rajib Goyal Young Scientist Prize 2026 in the field of Life Sciences

Kurukshetra University has announced the recipients of the prestigious Rajib Goyal Prize for Young Scientists for the academic session 2023-24, recognising four outstanding researchers from across the country for their significant contributions to science. The awardees, all below the age of 45, are: Dr Gopinath Packirisamy from Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (Applied Sciences), Dr Debabrata Maiti from Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (Chemical Sciences), Dr Durba Pal from Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (Life Sciences), and Dr Smarajit Karmakar from Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Hyderabad (Physical Sciences). Each Rajib Goyal Prize carries a medal, citation and a cash award of Rs 1 lakh.

24
Feb
18th Institute Foundation Day
16:00:00
Swami Vivekananda Auditorium, IIT Ropar

The Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar) cordially invites you to celebrate its Foundation Day on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, marking another significant milestone in the Institute’s journey of academic excellence, research leadership, and national service. This special occasion reflects IIT Ropar’s unwavering commitment to advancing research and development, innovation, and entrepreneurship, and its growing role in shaping the future of higher education and technology-driven growth in the country. Keynote Address The Foundation Day Celebration will be graced by the Keynote Address of Shri. Gulab Chand Kataria Hon’ble Governor of Punjab and Administrator of Chandigarh

Advitiya 2026 - Tech Fest from 6-8 Feb 2026
10:00:00
06 Feb 2026 - 08 Feb 2026

Advitiya 2026, IIT Ropar's annual technical fest, is back to set the benchmark for technological innovation and intellectual grit. This year, the fest is themed "A Space Odyssey," transforming our campus into a launchpad for the next generation of engineers and creators. We bring together a massive lineup of high-stakes competitions, including app development battles, AI and algorithm challenges, fin-tech simulations and cyber-security hunts. Beyond the screen, expect to see the future in motion with robotics showcases, aerospace contests, and creative design modules. Whether it’s solving complex mathematical problems or dominating in gaming and finance, Advitiya is where the brightest minds come to push past the ordinary. If you’re obsessed with the "how" and the "why," you belong here. This is ADVITIYA 2026, where deep-tech meets raw creativity.

Punjab govt to adopt artificial intelligence in agriculture

In a bid to boost agricultural productivity and sustainability through the use of cutting-edge technologies, the Punjab government on Thursday said it is preparing to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) in the agriculture sector with the support of a Centre of Excellence established at IIT Ropar.

1

INTERNAL AUDIT MANUAL
INDIAN INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY ROPAR

ROLE AND SCOPE OF INTERNAL AUDIT
Internal auditing is an independent, objective assurance and consulting activity designed to
add value and improvement in an organization's operations. It helps an organization to
accomplish its objectives by bringing a systematic and disciplined approach to eva luate and
improve the effectiveness of risk management, control, and governance processes. Internal
auditing is a catalyst for improving an organization's effecti veness and efficiency by
providing insight and recommendations based on analyses and assessments of data and
business processes. With commitment to integrity and accountability, internal auditing
provides value to governing bodies and senior management as an objective source of
independent advice. The Internal Audit serves a “THIRD EYE’ for the management to
control and watch the efficiency and working of various units under them. The term
‘INTERNAL’ means work carried out by using one’s internal institute employees.
The scope of internal auditing within an organization is broad and may involve topics such as
the efficiency of operations, the reliability of financial reporting, deterring and investigating
fraud, safeguarding assets, and compliance with laws and regulations.
Internal auditing frequently involves measuring compliance with the entity's policies and
procedures. They advise management and the Internal Audit enjoys reasonable freedom in the
discharge of its functions.
OBJECTIVES OF INTERNAL AUDIT
The appraisal of past transactions and happening , probing into deviatio n from established
policies and procedures, detection and prevention of error s and frauds, proper utilization of
assets or safeguarding them, and assessing the effective control in operations, to preserve the
entire organization against wasteful operations are included in the protective functions of the
internal audit.
2

The constructive appraisal of activities moves beyond the financial accounting aspects into
operational auditing. Appraisal of management methods and performances, whether
established polic ies and procedures are adequate for the attainment of objectives, critically
analyse and review soundness and adequacy of operating controls are included in the
constructive appraisal activities. They also include the review of discharging of
responsibilities and suggesting measures for streamlining the organizational working.
The duties and responsibilities of an internal auditor are wide. It is difficult for an internal
auditor to ascertain the extent to which his appraisal should go and where his respon sibility
ceases while appraising a partic ular operation. A conscientious internal auditor with good
imagination and practical experience can render valuable service to the management.
The services of internal auditor will be utilized by all levels of management in the
investigation of any special problem/function, in addition to normal audit function; he must
be constantly alert to changing situation.
The internal auditor should function independently. Independence denotes freedom from
conditions that threaten objectivity or the appearance of objectivity. Objectivity is an
unbiased mental attitude that allows internal auditors to perform engagements in such a
manner that they have an honest belief in their work product and that no significant quality
compromises are made. Objectivity requires internal auditors not to subordinate their
judgments on audit maters to that of others. Threats to objectivity should be managed at the
levels of the individual auditors, audit assignment, functional and organizati onal level. He
should not get himself involved in line function. He should act independently without fear
and favour or prejudice.
For the efficient discharge of his functions, the internal auditor should study and understand
the organizations plans, polic y, procedures and objectives. He should give a thoughtful
approach to his work. In discharging his functions, he must be courageous and critical, yet
fair in his views and interpretations.

3

DUTIES OF INTERNAL AUDIT
Major duties and responsibilities of int ernal audit functions are summarized as
below:
 Study of prescribed accounting procedures , including maintenance of records in the
institute with a view to ensuring that they are correct, adequate and free from any defects
or lacunae;
 Reports risk manageme nt issues and internal controls deficiencies identified directly to
the audit committee and provides recommendations for improving the organization’s
operations, in terms of both efficient and effective performance;
 Provides support to the institute's anti-fraud programs;
 Watch over the implementation of the prescribed procedures and the orders issued from
time to time;
 Scrutiny and check of payments and accounting work of the accounting units;
 Investigation of important arrears in accounting and other connected records;
 Periodic review of all accounts including cash book, bank reconciliation statement and
store records as well as physical verification of stores;
 Pursuance/settlement of objections taken in test audit notes issued by statutory audit
offices and other matters relating to statutory audit;
 To examine and report on points or irregularities brought to its notice by the statutory
audit;
 To examine the contracts and agreements executed by the Institute.

PERIODICITY OF INTERNAL AUDIT
The record of all the Departments/Centers/Units/Sections is required to be test checked by
the internal audit wing every year. The audit plan showing the period of audit of each unit is
to be got approved annually from the competent authority before 31 st March each year.
After audit of each unit the inspection report of each unit showing the observations of audit
along with action taken on previous year’s observations, if any, is to be issued to the unit
with the approval of the competent authority. Each unit /department/ wing will attend to the
preliminary observations o f internal audit wing promptly so that it may not be included in
the final inspection report. The each audit unit will give the reply to the inspection report

FOLLOW UP ACTION ON INSPECTION REPORTS
