Facility available at IIT Ropar
The institute is actively involved in collaborative programs with international organizations and
universities. The institute has the following facilities other than the basic academic facilities. Virtual
Classrooms (NKN) Two virtual classrooms have been set up at IIT Ropar. NKN interconnects the
institutions engaged in research, higher education and scientific development in the country.
Library:
The Nalanda Library, IIT Ropar is an invaluable storehouse of knowle dge and learning resources,
which plays a fundamental and advanced role in support of various academic and research activities
at the institute. The objective of the library is to provide users with the required information
resources and support by offering latest services which are integrated with teaching, learning
and research activities.
21
4

Apart from textbooks and recommended reading materials prescribed for each course offered at the
institute, the library houses a growing collection of research monographs, reports, multi -volume
reference works, dictionaries, encyclopedias, handbooks, and so on. The Library also possesses a
substantial collection of theses, dissertations, and annual reports, standards in the field of science,
engineering, technology, humanities and social sciences. The library facilitates access to electronic
journals through its participation in consortia, such as E -ShodhSindhu (eSS). The library also
subscribes to several e -journals directly from publishers as well as t hrough reputed subscription
agencies. At present, users can consult more than 25,000+ books (available on shelves) and
thousands of electronic books, e-journals. The library provides online access to a range of specialized
databases, including economic and political databases such as Prowess IQ and CMIE States of India,
as well as scientometric databases like Scopus, MathSciNet, and Web of Science. To support
researchers in enhancing scientific writing skills and ensuring the originality of their research work,
the library provides online access to tools such as Overleaf, Grammarly and Turnitin.

The library circulation operations have been automated using RFID -based LMS-KOHA software. The
Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC) which is in the public domain enables users to search
documents in possession of the library. The library is using the Radio Frequency Identification
Technology (RFID), a state -of-the-art auto -identification technique that helps in self -servicing and
enhanced security . A dedicated e -resources section is provided in the library to browse CDs and
DVDs of books, theses, and dissertations. Additionally, the library has established an Institutional
Digital Repository (IDR) using open source DSpace software to archive and pr ovide online access to
the intellectual output of the institute. IDR is available publicly which facilitates the dissemination of
scholarly work while promoting institutional visibility. To further enhance resource accessibility, the
library has developed a web -based Subject/Research Guide using the Subject plus tool. The guide
enables users to explore comprehensive library resources based on subject areas or research
interests, including e-journals, books/e-books, databases, and theses/dissertations.
Hostel Accommodation
The Institute campus has four boys hostels (Satluj, Beas, Chenab, Brahmaputra) and 3 girl hostels
(Raavi, Brahmaputra, T6) with a total capacity of 2984 available at the main campus. All hostels are
well furnished along with common rooms for recreational activities for each hostel. The campus also
has an expansive and airy common dining area. All hostels are provided with excellent drinking
water facilities. Each hostel has common facilities - indoor, recreation and games. The hostel complex
also includes a few shops that cater to the basic needs of the residents. IIT Ropar also provides
gymnasium facilities within its campus for its students. Lush green IIT campus add enormous fuel in
the daily life of the students. We have lively and enchan ting campus life wherein the students are
provided with all the amenities for the recreational activities. Here at IIT Ropar, students rejuvenate
their hidden talent and relive their hobbies. State of the art classrooms with Audio visual aids and
state of the art laboratories with latest research facilities enhance the teaching learning process
while high-tech library with tremendous books, journals, periodicals etc. help them to connect with
the entire world of information and knowledge. We have also intro duced drastic changes to the mess
menu with detailed options given to students w.r.t. the food items they would like to have in the Mess
by fixing the base menu and providing extra items in the menu which they student can opt for at an
extra cost. At IIT Ropar, students relish research and extracurricular activities to grow as an aspiring
engineer with moral and ethical integrity.
*Note: Hostel accommodation will be provided on a sharing basis only depending upo n the
availability.
21
5

Health Care
Medical Centre (24x7)
The Institute Medical Centre is located in the Utility Block in Main Campus. The Medical Centre
consists of dedicated full time Medical Officers, Visiting Specialists and Para -Medical staff
(Pharmacists and Nursing Staff) which have been appointed to provide the medical services to
Students, Faculty, Staff and their dependents. The Medical Centre provides Routine OPD, Day Care,
First-Aid & 24x7 Emergency Services. There are two Ambulanc es with basic life support available
24x7 for medical emergencies and for referral services to the higher centres. In addition, the
Institute empanelled various Multi and Super Speciality hospitals in the city of Ropar, Mohali and
Chandigarh for providing the Secondary and Tertiary medical care to the clientele of IIT Ropar.
Medical Centre aims to enhance the healthcare experience of the IIT Ropar campus community by
providing healthcare with respect, consideration and confidentiality
Student Activities
The Institute has a Society for Publication and Communication Skills Development. In addition, there
are Music, Dance, Dramatics, Arturo Photography, Fine Arts clubs, Girl up Club, Electoral Club,
Epicure-The Cooking Club, Literary, Music clubs and also Scien ce & Technology, Robotic Societies,
Monochrome, Computer Integrated Manufacturing, Astronomy, Quiz, Coding clubs, where the
students can participate and develop a well – rounded personality. Apart from above all, an Outdoor
Adventure and Social Activities Club and Fitness club are also there for the wellness of Students.
General Facilities
The Institute has a branch of SBI as well as a Post office to cater to the needs of the faculty members,
staff and students.
Student Life at Institute
At present, the tran sit and main campuses have excellent facilities for several sports, including a
cricket field, three lawn tennis courts, a football field, a hockey field, a gymnasium, a basketball court,
badminton courts, an athletics track, table tennis room and also fac ilities for several athletic events.
The institute encourages its students to participate in inter -IIT sport events and other competitions.
Space for recreational and creative activities is also available.
Industry and Alumni Relations:
Industry relations
The Industrial & Corporate Relation Cell office works in the direction to strengthen the relations with
industry and reputed international research institutes in order to develop strong research and
academic collaborations. The institute is well connected to Industry and is a member of
Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). Industry Institute Conclaves are conducted in the Institute to
develop Industrial Associates of the institute. The Conclaves are focused on bringing together
industry leaders and academ ia together on the same platform to discuss and brainstorm topics
related to industrial expectations from institutions, curriculum structure and discuss issues and
opportunities related to industrial projects & consultancy. Experts from the industries are invited
regularly to deliver lectures under Industrial Lecture Series. Centre for Innovation and Business
Incubation (CIBI) of the institute is already hosting six startups, which is a part of Technology
Business Incubator (TBI).
21
6

Alumni relations
Our Institute has been actively working to sustain the bonding and to ensure greater participation of
its Alumni in its academic and extra activities through various initiatives in association with the IIT
Ropar Alumni Association (founded in Feb. 2013). Some of the initiatives are as follows:
1. Alumni Student Mentorship Program (ASMP):It’s a platform for tapping in the multitude of
experience and knowledge of the Alumni for the benefit of the students and Alumni alike. As
distinguished IIT Ropar gr aduates, Alumni hold a wealth of information and knowledge that current
students can benefit from. Their expertise and advice are more valuable to students wanting to sail a
similar kind of boat ranging from MBA (India, Abroad), MS, various kinds of jobs, civil services,
entrepreneurship, etc.
2. Hangout with Alumni: Conducting regular Alumni -Student interaction sessions including
webinars, podcasts, and in -person meets, when feasible, to bridge the gap between them and allow
the experiences, learnings, exam p reparation strategies, and above all, their valuable college
memories, to reach the existing students. In this, we have Alumni speak about various topics based
on students’ responses and needs.
3. Alumni Student Relationship Cell: The ASRC has been linked with the placement and internship
team of IIT Ropar, for facilitating more and better opportunities to the students through alumni in
the form of internships, live projects, and placements. The vast alumni network spread over
hundreds of corporate giants brings home the opportunity to call them for hiring at our campus.
4. Recreational Activities: The Alumni office and ASRC plans to regularly engage with the Alumni via
recreational activities like inter -year online games and championships, organized in collabo ration
with various clubs of IIT Ropar. These initiatives are meant to foster healthy and vibrant
relationships with these much precious jewels of the institute.
5. Alumni Awards: To recognize, appreciate and encourage our emerging young alumni members for
their leadership potential and professional and/or societal impactful contributions and
accomplishments, to enhance the awareness of their achievements and contributions, and to
strengthen our bonding with emerging alumni members, Emerging Young Alumni Awards are
instituted.
The Alumni have shown a lot of enthusiasm in participating in these initiatives and to keep working
towards building a brand for our young institute IIT Ropar.
Recreational/Extra Curricular activities
In order to take care of various students activities, we have a Student Affairs Section with the
following functional units:
1. Board of Hostel Affairs (BOHA)
2. Board of Cultural Activities (BOCA)
3. Board of Science & Technology (BOST)
4. Board of Sports Activities (BOSA)
5. Board of Literary Activities (BOLA)
6. Board of Academic Affairs (BOAA)
7. Board of Wellness Affairs (BOWA)
8. Institute Student Mentorship Program (ISMP)
9. Outdoor Adventure and Social Activities Club (ODAC)
10. National Service Scheme (NSS)

21
7

Board of Hostel Affairs (BOHA)
The Board of Hostel Affairs (BOHA) oversees all hostels and mess facilities at the institute,
ensuring a comfortable and well-managed residential experience for students. It monitors food
quality, menu
21
8

planning, and overall mess operations through the Mess Committee. For hostel-related concerns, the
Hostel Committee addresses student issues and works towards improving hostel life. BOHA also
organizes cultural celebrations, special dinners, and various activities to enhance student
engagement. A major h ighlight is the General Championship (GC), a prestigious inter-hostel
competition that fosters camaraderie and competitive spirit. All these activities are managed under
the leadership of the General Secretary, BOHA.

Board of Cultural Activities (BOCA)
The Board of Cultural Activities (BOCA) at IIT Ropar is the heart of the institute’s cultural scene,
fostering artistic expression and vibrant student engagement. It oversees a diverse array of clubs,
including Alankar (Music Club), Arturo (Photography Clu b), D’Cypher (Dance Club), Epicure
(Culinary Club), Undekha (Dramatics Club), Vibgyor (Fine Arts Club), and Panache (Fashion Club).
Throughout the year, BOCA organizes exciting events like jamming nights, Bhangra sessions, ramp
walks, and street plays, ens uring a lively campus atmosphere. The flagship event, Zeitgeist, is IIT
Ropar’s annual cultural fest, featuring renowned celebrities, musicians, and comedians, drawing
immense participation. BOCA also proudly represents IIT Ropar at the Inter -IIT Cultural Meet, held
every December, where students compete against peers from all 23 IITs in a prestigious display of
talent and creativity. Through these initiatives, BOCA not only enriches the cultural landscape on
campus but also fosters leadership, teamwork, and artistic excellence.

Board of Science and Technology (BOST)
The Board of Science and Technology at IIT Ropar is a vibrant hub of innovation, comprising 11
dynamic clubs —Aeromodelling, Automotive, CIM, Coding, Fincom, Robotics, Softcom, Zenith,
Esportz, Monochrome, and Softcom. We explore diverse domains, including mechatronics, software
development, cyber security, game development, and competitive coding , fostering a culture of
technical excellence. Our board extends its reach into high-power model rock etry, astronomy,
esports, computational simulations, and design , pushing the boundaries of scientific exploration.
We also focus on case studies, quantitative finance, and advanced computational techniques ,
providing students with real -world problem-solving skills. Engaging in national and international
competitions, we showcase our expertise on global platforms. From cutting -edge robotics and
automation to financial modeling and digital art , our clubs cater to every tech enthusiast. With
hands-on projects, workshops, and mentorship, we empower students to innovate and lead in the
evolving technological landscape.

Board of Sports Activities (BOSA)
We have a Board of Sports Activities (BOSA) which encourages the students to participate in local /
Inter-
/ Intra-college / Hostel Sports Activities to boost their performance in inter IIT Sports meet under
the guidance of Sports Officer & professional coaches.
All sports facilities including gymnasium are being upgraded to enhance the quality of facilities at t he
Institute. There are international level modern sports fields / grounds with floodlights facilities.
Since 2016, BOSA, IIT Ropar is organizing an Annual Sports Festival “AAROHAN” in which students of
various Colleges, Institutes and Universities participate in more than 13 sports events.

Board of Literary Affairs (BOLA)
The Board of Literary Affairs at IIT Ropar is dedicated to nurturing and promoting literary excellence
and creativity within the campus. It oversees and organizes all literary activities, providing a vibrant
platform for students to explore and showcase their talents. Under its umbrella, the board hosts
various clubs, including poetry, quizzing, debating, oratory, filmmaking, Model United Nations
(MUN), and a movie club, caterin g to diverse literary and artistic interests. Additionally, it proudly
21
9

organizes MALHAR, the annual literary fest of IIT Ropar, which celebrates the spirit of literature,
culture, and expression through a series of exciting events, competitions, and interactive sessions,
fostering a dynamic and intellectually stimulating environment for the student community.
Board of Academic Affairs (BOAA)
The Board of Academic Affairs (BOAA) acts as a crucial link between students and the
administration, focusing o n addressing academic concerns effectively. With representatives from all
branches of each year, BOAA ensures clear communication between students and professors. It
advocates for student interests, influencing positive changes in academic policies. The bo ard plays a
vital role in improving the overall academic experience, aiming to create a supportive environment
where every student's voice matters. Its efforts promote collaboration and address challenges to
enhance learning throughout the college community.

Board of Wellness Affairs (BOWA)
The Boards caters the mental health and counseling needs of the students, faculties and staff. Our
system is especially working towards addressing the psychological difficulties of the students and
promoting wellness among the whole campus community. Our main focus is to create a proactive
and preventative environment for mental health care for all. The objective of this cell is to increase
the help seeking behavior among the community, and to remove the fear of stigma by close others
and to make the counseling services more user friendly.
There is another unit working in coordination with the Board of Wellness Affairs i.e. a Counseling
Cell named as “Snehita Wellbeing Cell”. This cell conducts various educational activ ities/sessions for
student’s well -being like – Dealing with Academic Anxiety, Self Discipline & Wellbeing, Time
Management, Power of Happiness, Relaxation Exercises & Mindfulness etc. Snehita Buddies have
been constituted to address the stress related concerns of students under Snehita Wellbeing Cell.

Institute Student Mentorship Program (ISMP)
The Institute Student Mentorship Program (ISMP) at IIT Ropar is a student-driven initiative designed
to help fresher’s adapt to college life. It provides guidance on academics, co -curricular activities, and
maintaining a balanced lifestyle. Each fresher is assigned a mentor, a carefully selected senior
student who offers support and advice throughout th e year. ISMP ensures a smooth transition into
IIT Ropar by organizing interactive sessions, activities, and events that introduce fresher’s to the
campus culture. The program fosters a strong support system, encouraging personal and academic
growth. Through mentorship, fresher’s gain insights, resources, and confidence to make the most of
their college journey.

Outdoor Adventure and Social Activities Club (ODAC)
The Club organizes events specifically designed to help students, faculty, and staff members improve
their fitness and overall well -being. Every year, on occasions such as National Unity Day, Yoga Day,
and others, the club organizes events like the IIT Ropar Unity Run, Yoga Day in coordination with the
Board of Sports Affairs, the celebration of Bicycling Day, and the Holy Run, among others.

NSS (National Service Scheme)
With the goal to work for the betterment of society and instill the spirit of social service among the
young students, IIT Ropar established NSS at institute level, headed by Facu lty in Charge, IIT Ropar.
Currently, NSS, IIT Ropar has over 100 active members from different disciplines, working
vigorously for community health care, literacy drives, and environmental protection. Blood donation
camps, informative lectures on human values are organized regularly. The aim of the organization is
to produce engineers, who are socially responsible, and work for the development of the nation.
30
Location and Accessibility
The Institute is located at Ropar, the headquarters of Rupnagar district, Punjab. This institute, with
its establishment, joins a string of premier educational institutions in Punjab. The town of Ropar, the
district headquarters, is 42 kms from Chandigarh, the capital of Punjab. Rupnagar is well connected
by both road (National highway NH21 / NH205) and railways (the Delhi -Ambala-Una railway line
passes through Rupnagar)
31
FORMAT – A: FORMAT OF SPONSORSHIP CERTIFICATE
(Part-time- ERP)
We understand that this sponsorship is covered by the following conditions:

i) The candidate will be continuing in the present place of work till he / she completes the research work.

ii) Necessary facilities will be provided for the proposed research work of the candidate.

iii) The Research Supervisor(s) from the Institute will be given access to the facilities necessary for the
research work of the candidate in our organization.
iv) The Joint Research Supervisor/Coordinator will be identified by the candidate at the time of
registration in the External Registration PhD programme.

v) The Joint Research Supervisor/Coordinator from the organization will ensure that half yearly reports
are submitted through the Research Supervisor at the Institute to the PG office. Failure to comply
with will result in cancellation of registration.

vi) The organization confirms that the Joint Research Supervisor has completed PhD in Govt. recognized
Institution/University. The organization can nominate Coordinator for the candidate in case Joint
Research Supervisor is not available in the organization.
vii) The organization will ensure that the candidate devotes sufficient time to his/her research work so
that the submission of the thesis will be done within the time frame stipulated by the Institute.
viii) In the event of any intellectual property ge nerated by the student during his/her proposed research,
the Organization agrees to the sharing of IP rights as determined by a Committee constituted by IIT
Ropar for this purpose.

ix) The thesis is a public document, and shall include all the work carried out by the student for the Ph.D.
degree. The organization shall agree that sensitive/confidential information will not be included in
the problem formulation or, subsequently, during the course of research.
x) All material in the thesis can be submitted for pub lication in peer -reviewed journals/ conferences;
the organization waives the right to deny permission for publication, for reasons of confidentiality or
for any other reason, for any material contained in the thesis.
xi) Publications: In the case of publications arising from the thesis, only those who have directly
contributed to the research work can be listed as authors. In case of any difference of opinion, the
decision of the internal committee of IIT Ropar shall be final.

title: PDF: Procedure-for-Issue-of-Duplicate-Degree-Certificate-and-Grade-Sheets-at-IIT-Ropar
text:
Procedure for Issue of Duplicate Degree Certificate / Grade Sheets from IIT Ropar

The duplicate Degree certificate / Grade Sheets are issued only if the original Degree certificate
/ Grade Sheets are lost or stolen.

A. PROCEDURE

The following procedure is to be adopted by the candidate for getting duplicate Degree
certificate / Grade Sheets issued from IIT Ropar:

1. Lodge an FIR (First Information Report) for the same to the nearest Police Station.
2. Publish in the newspaper about the loss of the Degree certificate / Grade Sheets.

3. Provide an affidavit prepared by a Notary on a non -judicial stamp paper. (The matter to
be printed on the affidavit is detailed below)

4. Write an application addressed to “The Dean (Academics), IIT Ropar” mentioning the
loss of your degree and reference of the above documents.

5. Attach a photocopy of the original Degree C e r t i f i c a t e/ G r a d e s h e e t s
conferred on you by IIT Ropar (if available).

B. CHARGES
a. For Duplicate Degree Certificate : Candidate has to pay online an amount of Rs.2500/-
(Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred Only) in India or US$ 250 (US Dollar Two
Hundred Fifty Only) in abroad.
b. For Grade Sheet (for one or all grade sheet): Candidate has to pay online an amount
of Rs 2500/- (Rupees Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred Only) in India or US$ 250
(US Dollar Two Hundred Fifty Only) in abroad
c. Postal Charges Extra.

d. The following is the steps to be used for payment:

a. Go to https://www.onlinesbi.sbi/
b. Select SB Collect
c. Select IIT Ropar (Institute name)
d. Select payment category: FEE FOR DUPLICATE DEGREE CERTIFICATE / GRADE SHEETS
e. Enter your entry number and click on Fetch payment details
f. Fill the details and complete the payment procedure.
g. Please fill the correct Mobile number and email ID to get payment status.

C. PROCESSING
Attach all the above documents in Original along with your application and send it at the
following address:

Dean (Academics),
Academic Section
East Wing, 2nd Floor,
M. Visvesvaraya Building
Indian Institute of Technology Ropar,
Rupnagar-140001 (Punjab) INDIA

Kindly note that it takes approximately 15 working days from the day of receiving the
above documents to process an application for the issuance of a duplicate Degree (this excludes
postal time).

CHIEF GUEST
Shri Satyanarayan Nuwal is the
Founder and Chairman of the Solar
Group of Industries, a globally
recognized Indian enterprise engaged
in the manufacture and export of
industrial explosives, high-energy
materials, and advanced defence
systems. A self-made entrepreneur
and visionary industrialist, he has made
outstanding contributions to India's
explosives industry and indigenous
defence manufacturing, significantly
advancing the national vision of Aatma-nirbhar Bharat. In
recognition of his exceptional contributions to the nation, he
was conferred the Padma Shri by the Hon'ble President of India
in 2026. He has also been awarded the honorary degree of
Doctor of Literature (D.Litt.) in 2023 for his distinguished
contributions to industry, innovation, and nation building.
Born in Bhilwara, Rajasthan, in 1952, Shri Nuwal's early life was
deeply influenced by his father, Shri Nandlalji Nuwal. After
completing his matriculation in 1967, he spent a formative year
at the Vedamata Gayatri Ashram, Mathura, under the guidance
of his spiritual Guru, Pandit Shri Ram Sharma Acharyaji. He
married at the age of nineteen and faced severe financial
hardships after the failure of his first business venture.
Seeking livelihood, he moved to Ballarshah in Maharashtra,
where he initially endured extremely difficult circumstances,
even spending nights on a railway platform. A chance
opportunity in the explosives trade, supported by the
generosity of Sattar Bhai of Chandrapur, who rented him an
explosives magazine for a nominal 1,000 per month, became
the turning point in his life. He entered the explosives business
in 1979, laying the foundation of what would later become the
An architect of India's indigenous explosives and defence manufacturing
Solar Group. In 1984, Imperial Chemical Industries (ICI), then the
world's largest explosives manufacturer, appointed him as its
consignment agent, and he soon became the country's largest
explosives dealer.
In 1995, Shri Nuwal established Solar's first explosives
manufacturing unit under the Small-Scale Industries (SSI)
framework. Over the next three decades, Solar Group evolved
into India's largest manufacturer and exporter of industrial
explosives. Today, the Group operates manufacturing facilities
across ten countries on four continents, employs more than
15,000 people, and exports its products to over 90 countries,
accounting for the largest share of India's explosives exports.
Recognising the nation's growing defence requirements, Shri
Nuwal led Solar Group's entry into defence manufacturing in
2010 through the establishment of Solar Defence & Aerospace
Limited (SDAL). Under his leadership, one of the world's largest
manufacturing facilities for HMX and its compositions was
established in Nagpur, ending India's dependence on imports
of this critical strategic material. Today, Solar exports HMX and
its compositions to several countries, including the United
States, Israel and Europe.
Shri Nuwal envisions Nagpur emerging as a global hub for the
design, development and manufacture of weaponised drones,
autonomous systems and artificial intelligence-enabled
defence technologies. In pursuit of this vision, Solar has
established state-of-the-art infrastructure for the development
and testing of next-generation unmanned systems. A
dedicated Loiter Munition Test Facility and a 1.25-km runway for
the development and testing of MALE (Medium Altitude Long
Endurance) and HALE (High Altitude Long Endurance) class
Unmanned Aerial Vehicles were inaugurated by the Hon'ble
Prime Minister of India in March 2025.
Solar Group's defence products, manufacturing facilities and
technological capabilities have been widely appreciated by the
senior political and military leadership of the country, reflecting
the Group's growing contribution to India's defence
preparedness and strategic self-reliance.

CHAIRPERSON
Mr. Adil Zainulbhai is the Chairman of the
Board of Governors, IIT Ropar. He also serves
as Chairman of the Capacity Building
Commission of India (CBC), set up by the
Government of India in April 2021 to help civil
servants at all levels acquire the training and
tools needed to deliver performance for
citizens, under Mission Karmayogi. As
Chairman, CBC, he leads the Commission's
efforts in upgrading Central Training
Institutions, helping ministries develop
Capability Building Plans, and driving citizen-centric training programmes
across sectors including the Railways, postal services, and police forces.
Since April 2025, he has also served as Chairman of the Board of
Governors at IIT Goa, extending his role in academic governance to a
second IIT.
He earlier served as Chairman of the Quality Council of India (QCI) from
2014 to 2022, where he was involved in initiatives to improve the quality of
goods and services and the efficiency of government processes,
including measuring the impact of Swachh Bharat and other flagship
schemes across infrastructure, healthcare, education, and coal.
Mr. Zainulbhai retired as Chairman of McKinsey India in 2013, after a 34-
year career with the firm. He has co-edited the book Reimagining India,
featuring 60 authors including prominent businessmen, academics,
economists, and journalists; the book was ranked #1 in non-fiction in India
on release and #2 on Amazon's International Business List in the US.

Larsen & Toubro Ltd., and Cipla, and is also active in community and social
causes as a Board member of Piramal Swasthya, Piramal Foundation,
Anant National University, and other foundations.

DIRECTOR
Prof. Rajeev Ahuja is a globally distinguished
computational materials scientist who serves
as the Director of the Indian Institute of
Technology (IIT) Ropar since April 2021. He
concurrently holds the position of Professor of
Computational Materials Science at Uppsala
University, Sweden, where he has been
associated for over three decades. He also
held the additional charge of Director of IIT
Guwahati from November 2023 to May 2024.
Prof. Ahuja is widely recognised as one of the
most highly cited researchers in Sweden and
India, and ranks among the top five materials scientists in both countries.
His research has shaped foundational understanding in energy
materials, high-pressure physics, and condensed matter theory over a
career spanning more than 30 years.
Prof. Ahuja completed his doctoral degree from the Indian Institute of
Technology Roorkee in 1992. In the same year, he joined Uppsala
University, Sweden, as a Post-Doctoral Fellow. He rose through the
academic ranks at Uppsala University, becoming Assistant Professor in
1996, Associate Professor in 2002, and Full Professor in 2007.
His primary areas of research are computational materials science and
condensed matter physics, with a strong focus on energy applications.
These include batteries, hydrogen storage and production, and sensors,
as well as high-pressure physics. His theoretical work, particularly in
density functional theory, has made significant contributions to the
design of energy storage materials and the study of electronic structure
under extreme conditions.
Prof. Ahuja has published over 1,250 scientific papers in peer-reviewed
journals, including high-profile publications in Science, Nature, Nature
Materials, and PNAS. His Google Scholar citation count exceeds 59,000,
with an h-index of 114 and an i-10 index of 880. He has supervised over 30
PhD students and more than 35 postdoctoral fellows.
Prof. Ahuja has received numerous national and international

DEPARTMENTS AND CENTERS
There are eleven academic units, namely the Departments of
Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Civil
Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical
Engineering, Humanities & Social Sciences, Mathematics,
Mechanical Engineering, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering,
and Physics. Each of these academic units offers individual courses,
while some courses are offered jointly by multiple academic units
and are classified as interdisciplinary courses.
There are seven centers, namely: a) Centre for Applied Research in
Data Sciences, b) Indo-Taiwan Joint Research Centre on Artificial
Intelligence and Machine Learning, c) Centre for Engineering
Education, d) Centre of Excellence for Studies and Applied Research
in Defence and Security (CoE-SARDS), e) Centre of Research for

and Autonomous System (DRAS), and g) Centre for Engineering
Solutions in Disaster Resilience (EESDR).

Engineering (sAIDE).

CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES
The Student Affairs Section works to build a supportive campus
environment where students grow academically, socially, and
personally. Through a wide range of resources and activities, the
section helps students become well-rounded, socially responsible
individuals. This is carried out through co-curricular activities
organized jointly by faculty and students, including cultural festivals,
14 /
sports tournaments, and technical competitions that give students a
platform to showcase their talents outside the classroom. These
activities are led by student boards and bodies, working under the
guidance of faculty advisors.
Along with the concerned Faculty Advisors, the Student Affairs
Section organizes annual festivals including ADVITIYA (Technical
Fest), ZEITGEIST (Cultural Fest), AAROHAN (Sports Fest), and
MALHAR (Literary Fest). The Board of Wellness Affairs also launched
a new wellness festival, NIRVANA, in April 2026. Besides these
festivals, students organize the Inter Year Sports Championship and
General Championship, which draw participation from institutions
across India. These events build healthy competition and encourage
cultural exchange among students from different backgrounds.

4. Board of Literary Activities (BOLA)
5. Board of Sports Activities (BOSA)
6. Board of Wellness Affairs (BOWA) & Snehita Well-Being Cell

The Snehita Wellbeing Cell (SWBC) at IIT Ropar is committed to the
overall psychological well-being of the Institute community, with a
focus on the mental health and counselling needs of students,
faculty, and staff. Through professional counselling services, crisis
intervention, and preventive mental health programmes, the cell
helps individuals manage psychological and stress-related
challenges. SWBC promotes a proactive and inclusive approach to
mental health, conducting educational sessions on academic
anxiety, self-discipline, time management, and mindfulness. To
strengthen peer-level support, the cell has set up "Snehita Buddies,"
a student volunteer network that helps address stress-related
concerns and works to reduce the stigma around seeking help.
The Board of Wellness Affairs (BOWA), a student-led body operating
under SWBC, works alongside the cell to lead advocacy and
awareness through peer-driven activities. Together, SWBC and
BOWA aim to build a campus environment where mental well-being
is a shared priority, ensuring that counselling and wellness services
remain approachable, accessible, and user-friendly for the entire
Institute community.

and LinkedIn Workshop (July 2025) led by career coach Ms. Palak
Gupta; "From Strong Engineer to Strong Hire" (August 2025); an
alumni talk by Janmeet S. Makkar; a Certified Consulting Readiness
session; and "Campus to Corporate: Bridging the Gap between
Academics & Industry" in collaboration with Career Launcher.

Meeting in September 2025, bringing together placement heads
from across the IIT system to align placement policies and strategy.

LYNK 2025, in September 2025, themed "Aligning Horizons: Talent,
Ideas and Industry for a Smarter Future," featuring speakers from
Flipkart, HPCL, Accenture, Infosys, Bajaj Auto, Myntra, Zoho, Bharat
Forge, Schneider Electric, and others.

Philips (December 2025), an invited talk by Dr. John Jose, Convenor
of the All IITs Placement Committee, on planning an engineering
career (February 2026), and a talk by Mr. Sachin Kumar of BHEL on
leadership development (February 2026).
Industry MoUs signed this year include partnerships with Cognavi
India Pvt. Ltd. (student placements and global talent development),
Vihaas Design Technologies (internships and placements),
Greenfinch Real Estate Engineers and Consultants (energy efficiency
and decarbonisation), Pattern Technologies India Pvt. Ltd. (research
and e-commerce collaboration), IvyCap Ventures Advisors (research,
innovation, and entrepreneurship support), DigiMantra (internships,
placements, and R&D), and Infosys Limited (the Infosys Springboard
digital learning platform).

The IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation (iHub-
AWaDH), established in August 2020 under the DST National
Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS),
continues to serve as a national platform for translating deep-tech
research in agriculture, water, and Cyber-Physical Systems into
technologies, enterprises, and skilled talent.
Over the past five years, the Hub has supported 193 startups,
developed 86 technologies, and commercialised or transferred 17 of
them. It has built a network of 31 Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) Labs
across the country, supported over 1,650 researchers, engaged
220+ ecosystem partners, created more than 2,400 jobs, and trained
over 8,800 participants through its skilling programmes. Its startup
portfolio spans more than 20 states, with Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh,
and Karnataka leading in the number of startups supported.
The Hub's work is guided by the 3I3P framework — Innovation,
Investment, and Implementation, supported by Policy, Processes,
and Programme — which was featured in the Department of Science
and Technology's DREAM 2047 publication.
Key initiatives this year included the 100Startups100Days
programme, which concluded at IIT Ropar in December 2025 with
over 100 awardee startups and �3.71 crore invested across 83
startups. IIT Ropar was the only IIT to host four events at the India AI
Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi, including the Agri AI Global
Summit. At Bharat Innovates 2026, held in Nice, France in June
2026, IIT Ropar led the Agri and Food Technologies theme and
represented 36 startups. The Hub also signed MoUs with Dassault
Systèmes and Fraunhofer IGB (Germany), and began new
international collaborations with the International Livestock
Research Institute (Kenya) and George Mason University (USA).
Notable technologies developed under the Hub include the AI-
enabled IoT-based Digital Entomologist for biodiversity monitoring,
now deployed across six countries and accepted as a New Work Item
The IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation (iHub-
ANNAM.AI is IIT Ropar’s Centre of Excellence for Artificial Intelligence in
Agriculture, established by the Ministry of Education, Government of
India, as part of a national initiative to set up AI Centres of Excellence
across key sectors, under the “Make AI in India, Make AI Work for India”
mission.
In February 2026, ANNAM.AI co-hosted the Agri AI Global Summit with
the Embassy of Israel in India and Reichman University, as part of the
India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi — a
significant national platform that showcased IIT Ropar’s agri-tech work.
At its Smart Agri Summit in March 2026, ANNAM.AI announced the
rollout of 100 hyperlocal weather stations, provided free of cost,
beginning with deployment across Punjab and with planned expansion
to states including Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, Odisha, Bihar,
Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Alongside
this, ANNAM.AI launched a fully funded AI-skilling programme targeting
10,000 students, rural youth, and agri-professionals.
In June 2026, ANNAM.AI represented IIT Ropar at Bharat Innovates
2026 in France, where it formalised a collaboration with global
agricultural major Syngenta. The partnership began with the launch of
HACK CORE 2026, a national-level AI hackathon addressing crop
health, pest management, soil intelligence, and climate-resilient
farming, with winning teams earning a visit to Syngenta’s research
centre in Atessa, Italy.
ANNAM.AI has built partnerships with several state agricultural
universities and government bodies, including ICRISAT and NABARD
BIRD, to scale technology adoption and strengthen engagement with
farmers. The M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation recently joined
the initiative to support the next phase of agricultural transformation —
from the Green Revolution to Green Intelligence. Over the past four
months, agriculture experts from 14 states have been onboarded, with
more joining from across the country, to help validate India’s first Digital
Public Infrastructure (DPI) being built for agriculture.ANNAM.AI
continues to pursue joint R&D with leading agricultural universities to
address region-specific farming challenges and promote sustainable
agricultural practices.

Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar, established in 2008, is one
of the premier institutes in India, known for its research, education,
and infrastructure. The green campus provides an ideal setting for
academic, research, and extracurricular activities, designed to
promote innovation, creativity, and collaboration among students,
faculty, and researchers.
IIT Ropar began functioning in the academic year 2008–09 from the
campus of its mentor institute, IIT Delhi. The foundation stone for its
permanent campus was laid on 24 February 2009. In just over 15
years, the Institute has grown into one of the fastest-growing among
the newer generation of IITs, with a built-up area of approximately 25
lakh sq. ft. The Hon'ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi,
dedicated Phase 1C — the Academic and Residential Complex — to
the nation on 20 February 2024.
This year, the Institute commenced operations of a new Lecture Hall
Complex (LHC) and a 500-seater air-conditioned girls' hostel, further
strengthening its academic and residential infrastructure.
The Institute is now planning the next phase of infrastructure
development to support its academic expansion. This phase
envisages an Academic Building (Lecture Hall Complex and
Workshop), a Research Park, hostels, residences, and indoor sports
facilities.

DIRECTOR’S REPORT
Prof. Rajeev Ahuja

/ 1
Esteemed Guests, Members of the
Board of Governors and the Senate,
Faculty Colleagues, Proud Parents,
and My Dear Graduating Students and
Scholars,
Good morning.
As the Director, it is my privilege to
w e l c o m e y o u a l l t o t h e 1 5 t h
Convocation of IIT Ropar. Today, I am
proud to witness the culmination of
your hard work. Congratulations!
This past year has been another landmark one for IIT Ropar. We
redesigned our undergraduate curriculum for greater flexibility,
deepened our role in India's national AI mission, expanded our
defence research partnerships, and strengthened our position
as a leading hub for AgriTech innovation. We also continued to
invest in research infrastructure, global collaborations, and the
wellbeing of our student community.
As we celebrate your achievements today, I want to highlight
your remarkable accomplishments. Our students have
excelled in academics, research, deep tech entrepreneurship,
sports, and community service, representing IIT Ropar at
national and international platforms and earning recognition for
their talents.
We take pride in our growing alumni network, which continues
to expand its presence across academia, industry, and public
service worldwide. As you join this "dreaming big" community,
we eagerly look forward to hearing your stories of impact in the
years to come.
Looking ahead, we reaffirm our commitment to providing a high
quality, research driven, and inclusive education, with
continued investment in state of the art infrastructure and R&D
facilities to create a world class learning experience at IIT
Ropar.

I want to remind you that real education is a balanced blend of
acquiring knowledge and developing character and values.
This balance will guide you throughout your lives. I encourage
you to continue learning, growing, and contributing to society.
Proud parents and dear guests, thank you for your support and
trust in this Institute. Once again, congratulations to the
graduating class of 2026. May your future be filled with
success, happiness, and purpose!
As customary, I will now present a brief report of IIT Ropar.
Academics
Today, at this convocation, 761 students are graduating,
comprising 377 B.Tech, 177 M.Tech, 65 M.Sc, 01 B.Sc, 01
Diploma and 140 PhDs.
Currently, we have over 3800 students on campus across
undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programmes.
This year, in a major academic reform, IIT Ropar revamped its
B.Tech curriculum for the 2026–27 academic session, moving
away from a rigid course structure to a flexible, student-driven
framework. The new structure lets students complete core
courses by the end of the third year, dedicating the final year
and a half to electives, internships, research, startups, and
cross-disciplinary learning. It supports 160 credits, including up
to 30 credits of open electives, and introduces an
Interdisciplinary Integrated Dual-Degree Programme allowing
eligible students to pursue a B.Tech and M.Tech together in
emerging fields. This reform aligns with the National Education
Policy 2020 and the National Credit Framework.
We also launched a new one year PG Diploma in UAV
Operations and Drone Technology, in partnership with Rajiv
Gandhi National Aviation University (RGNAU).
Female student enrolment at IIT Ropar has continued to grow
steadily, reflecting our sustained commitment to inclusivity.
Rankings
IIT Ropar was ranked 32nd in the Engineering category and
47th in the Research Institutions category in the NIRF 2025
rankings, with an overall rank of 56. The institute ranked 11th
among India's top Government engineering institutes and 8th
among all IITs, as per the Outlook-ICARE Rankings 2026. While
these numbers reflect a competitive national landscape, we
remain focused on the fundamentals viz. research output,
faculty quality, and graduate outcomes, that will drive
improvement in the years ahead.
Placements
Despite continued global uncertainty in the hiring market, IIT
Ropar has recorded a strong placement season in 2025-26.
Over 127 companies visited the campus across diverse sectors,
and our B.Tech. students achieved an overall placement rate of
about 83%, a clear sign of sustained recruiter confidence in our
graduates.
Core engineering disciplines stood out this year, with Chemical
Engineering posting the highest placement percentage at
around 95%. The overall average package came in at
approximately 22 LPA, while Mathematics and Computing
secured the highest package of the season. We also saw 69
Pre Placement Offers (PPOs) this year; a clear sign that
internship based hiring continues to grow as a pathway into full-
time roles.

government bodies, national scientific organisations, and
global funding agencies, spanning sustainable energy,

around 1,130 industrial consultancy projects worth
approximately 80 Crore, reflecting our growing role as a trusted
technology partner to industry, and has secured approximately
5.50 Crore in CSR funding to further strengthen our research and
outreach efforts. This research ecosystem is anchored by our
Section 8 companies to carry research from the lab into the real
world. ANNAM.AI, our Centre of Excellence for AI in Agriculture;
the Technology Business Incubator Foundation (TBIF), which
nurtures startups from idea to enterprise; the Defence and
Research Innovation Foundation (DRIF), which channels our
research strength into defence and strategic technologies; the
IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation (iHub-AWaDH),
our DST-supported hub driving deep-tech innovation in
agriculture, water, and cyber-physical systems; and SCHOOL
OF CONTINUOUS ACTIVE LEARNING, focusing on
educational support, capacity building, and bridging the gap
between academic research and industrial training. Together,
these arms of IIT Ropar ensure that IIT Ropar's research doesn't
stop at publication, but continues on into technology,
enterprise, and national impact.
Startups and Entrepreneurship
Ahead of the India AI Impact Summit 2026, IIT Ropar hosted
"100 Startups 100 Days," a national deep-tech acceleration
programme in December 2025, in partnership with iHub-
AWaDH, ANNAM.AI, and our Technology Business Incubator
Foundation (TBIF). The programme brought in partners
including HDFC Bank, Canara Bank, the Embassy of Israel in
India, and several national incubation networks. As on date, IIT
Ropar has incubated more than 510 deeptech startups.
Defence and National Security Collaborations
This has been a defining year for IIT Ropar's role in defence
research. In a recent development, the Institute has secured
two projects from the Army Technology Board (ATB) with a
combined outlay of Rs 120 Crore. In September 2025, we
signed an MoU with the Indian Air Force for indigenous
technology development in support of the Atmanirbhar Bharat
mission. Building on our existing partnership with the Western
Command of the Indian Army, we signed a fresh MoU with
DIPAS-DRDO in February 2026, focused on human
performance augmentation, high-altitude sustenance, smart
energy, and waste management. IIT Ropar and the Indian Army
have also partnered to launch a Master of Technology in
Defence Technology for officers.
Most recently, in June 2026, we signed a three-party MoU with
C2C Advanced Systems and Aaizel International Technologies
covering AI, cyber resilience, environmental intelligence,
geospatial analytics, and climate technologies.
We also signed an MoU with VUI Consultancy to advance AI-
driven cybersecurity research, in the presence of Shri Dinkar
Gupta, former Director General of the National Investigation
Agency and Professor of Practice at IIT Ropar.
Academic and Institutional Partnerships
This year, we formalized a student and faculty exchange MoU
with more than 30 academic institutions and industries
including Mayo Clinic, iDG10 Solutions Private Limited, SIET
Nilokheri, Rocket Learning, Vidyavardhaka College of
Engineering, Punjab Police, The International Centre for
Automotive Technology, Western Sydney Univeristy, Dr. K.N
Modi University, Pattern India, SVNIT Surat to name a few.
AgriTech and ANNAM.AI
ANNAM.AI, our Centre of Excellence for AI in Agriculture, had
an outstanding year. In February 2026, we co-hosted the AgriAI
Global Summit with the Embassy of Israel in India and Reichman
University, as part of the India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat
Mandapam, New Delhi, a significant national platform
showcase for IIT Ropar's agritech work.

nurtures startups from idea to enterprise; the Defence and
Research Innovation Foundation (DRIF), which channels our
research strength into defence and strategic technologies; the
IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation (iHub-AWaDH),
our DST-supported hub driving deep-tech innovation in
agriculture, water, and cyber-physical systems; and SCHOOL
OF CONTINUOUS ACTIVE LEARNING, focusing on
educational support, capacity building, and bridging the gap
between academic research and industrial training. Together,
these arms of IIT Ropar ensure that IIT Ropar's research doesn't
stop at publication, but continues on into technology,
enterprise, and national impact.
Startups and Entrepreneurship
Ahead of the India AI Impact Summit 2026, IIT Ropar hosted
"100 Startups 100 Days," a national deep-tech acceleration
programme in December 2025, in partnership with iHub-
AWaDH, ANNAM.AI, and our Technology Business Incubator
Foundation (TBIF). The programme brought in partners
including HDFC Bank, Canara Bank, the Embassy of Israel in
India, and several national incubation networks. As on date, IIT
Ropar has incubated more than 510 deeptech startups.
Defence and National Security Collaborations
This has been a defining year for IIT Ropar's role in defence
research. In a recent development, the Institute has secured
two projects from the Army Technology Board (ATB) with a
combined outlay of Rs 120 Crore. In September 2025, we
signed an MoU with the Indian Air Force for indigenous
technology development in support of the Atmanirbhar Bharat
mission. Building on our existing partnership with the Western
Command of the Indian Army, we signed a fresh MoU with
DIPAS-DRDO in February 2026, focused on human
performance augmentation, high-altitude sustenance, smart
energy, and waste management. IIT Ropar and the Indian Army
have also partnered to launch a Master of Technology in
Defence Technology for officers.
Most recently, in June 2026, we signed a three-party MoU with
C2C Advanced Systems and Aaizel International Technologies
covering AI, cyber resilience, environmental intelligence,
geospatial analytics, and climate technologies.
We also signed an MoU with VUI Consultancy to advance AI-
driven cybersecurity research, in the presence of Shri Dinkar
Gupta, former Director General of the National Investigation
Agency and Professor of Practice at IIT Ropar.
Academic and Institutional Partnerships
This year, we formalized a student and faculty exchange MoU
with more than 30 academic institutions and industries
including Mayo Clinic, iDG10 Solutions Private Limited, SIET
Nilokheri, Rocket Learning, Vidyavardhaka College of
Engineering, Punjab Police, The International Centre for
Automotive Technology, Western Sydney Univeristy, Dr. K.N
Modi University, Pattern India, SVNIT Surat to name a few.
AgriTech and ANNAM.AI
ANNAM.AI, our Centre of Excellence for AI in Agriculture, had
an outstanding year. In February 2026, we co-hosted the AgriAI
Global Summit with the Embassy of Israel in India and Reichman
University, as part of the India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat
Mandapam, New Delhi, a significant national platform
showcase for IIT Ropar's agritech work.
In March 2026, at our Smart Agri Summit, ANNAM.AI
6 / / 7
announced the rollout of 100 hyperlocal weather stations,
beginning with deployment across Punjab, alongside a fully
funded AI-skilling programme targeting 10,000 students, rural
youth, and agri-professionals.
In June 2026, IIT Ropar was represented by ANNAM.AI in
Bharat Innovates 2026, France where it formalised
collaboration with global leaders in agricultural production-
Syngenta. This partnership began with the launch of HACK
CORE 2026, a national level AI hackathon addressing crop
health, pest management, soil intelligence, and climate-
resilient farming, with winners earning a visit to Syngenta's
research centre in Atessa, Italy.
Annam.AI has collaborated with several state agricultural
universities, government entities and signed public private
partnerships to scale up the adoption of technology and to
connect effectively with farmers for continuous engagement.
Some of these include very eminent bodies like ICRISAT,
NABARD BIRD to mention a few. Recently, MS Swaminathan
Research Foundation also came on board to join us in the
implementation of the next big agricultural transformation,
Green revolution to Green Intelligence. Agriculture experts
were onboarded from 14 states in 4 months and continue to be
onboarded from across the country, to validate the nation's first
DPI being built for agriculture.
Annam.AI continues to explore joint R&D with leading Agri
universities in the country to solve region-specific agriculture
problems, while bringing about sustainability in agricultural
practices. On a daily basis, ANNAM.AI teams lead outreach
efforts around Ropar, and orient them to build trust in the new
technologies, thus co creating the technology with the farmers
for the farmers.
Student Wellbeing and Campus Life
Student life at IIT Ropar continues to be shaped by a strong
culture of care, community, and holistic growth. Our Snehita
Wellbeing Cell continues to offer confidential counseling and
psychological support, addressing academic stress,
adjustment challenges, and emotional wellbeing through
proactive outreach and orientation programmes, supported by
a peer network of Snehita Buddies. This year, the student led
Board of Wellness Affairs went a step further, launching
NIRVANA, the Institute's first dedicated wellness festival,
featuring keynote sessions on resilience, wellness exhibitions,
health camps, and collaborations with organizations such as
Sangath and TCS Research. Campus life remained vibrant
through our flagship festivals, ADVITIYA for technology,
ZEITGEIST for culture, AAROHAN for sports, and MALHAR for
literature, alongside the many technical, cultural, sports, and
literary clubs, the Outdoor, Adventures and Social Activities
Club, and the National Service Scheme, all of which continue to
give our students avenues to grow beyond the classroom.

new 500 seat, fully air conditioned girls' hostel, a step that
reflects our growing focus on student comfort and on
supporting the steady rise in female enrolment at IIT Ropar.

ease classroom capacity and give our growing student body
more comfortable, well equipped spaces to learn in. Several
more projects aimed at improving everyday campus life for our
students are currently in the pipeline, and we look forward to
sharing progress on these in the years ahead.

Graduating Class of 2026, proud
parents, respected faculty, esteemed
members of the Senate and Board of
Governors, and Director IIT Ropar,
Professor Rajeev Ahuja.

when I was asked to stand before
India's finest young engineers and scientists as your Chief

India, I started a small unit to manufacture industrial explosives
in Nagpur. I did not have a business degree. I did not have a
mentor from IIT or IIM. What I had was patience, and the
willingness to fail many times before I got something right. I had
Convocation
th
Thursday, 6 August, 2026
TH
2 / / 3
already failed at an ink manufacturing business. I had failed at a
leasing business. I had failed at running a transport company.
Failure was not new to me. It was, in a strange way, familiar
ground.
What was new was the discipline of staying with one idea long
enough to see it through. Solar Industries did not become
India's largest manufacturer of industrial explosives overnight.
It took years of trials, approvals, and small wins nobody was
watching.
In 2010, we took the biggest risk of our journey. We moved from
industrial explosives into military grade ammunition and
defence manufacturing, a field then dominated entirely by
government ordnance factories. People told me a private
company from Nagpur had no business competing there. We
did it anyway.
Today, our defence arm, Solar Defence and Aerospace
Limited, builds solid propellant boosters for the BrahMos
missile, components for the Pinaka rocket system, and India's
first indigenous loitering munition, Nagastra. Bhargavastra, our
counter drone system, can bring down an entire drone swarm
with a single salvo, something no other system in the world
does quite the same way. When these systems were used
during Operation Sindoor last year, it was not just a company
milestone. It was proof that Indian private industry, built by
Indian hands, can stand at the frontier of national defence.
Earlier this year, I stood before the President of India to receive
the Padma Shri. I mention this not for pride, but because of what
it represents, a boy who dropped out of school in Class 10 was
recognised by the highest office in this country for work in one
of its most sensitive and technical sectors. If that is possible,
understand what is possible for you, with your degrees, your
training, and everything this institute has given you that I never
had.
What Thirty Years Taught Me
Graduates, let me share a few things I now know for certain.
First, your background does not decide your ceiling. Your
persistence does. I did not have the vocabulary, the network, or
the capital that many of you already carry into your careers.
What I had was the refusal to stop trying. Whatever gap you feel
today, in confidence, in exposure, in connections, close it with
consistency, not despair.
Second, trust takes years to build and a moment to lose. In the
explosives and defence business, there is no room for
shortcuts. One error is not a delay. It can be a tragedy. I built my
company's name on a simple principle; deliver what you
promise, every single time, even when no one is checking. That
principle will serve you whether you build rockets, write code,
or run a village school.
Third, patriotism is not a slogan. It is a decision you make in
your work. When I chose to move Solar Industries into defence
manufacturing, I was not chasing the largest contract. I was
choosing to reduce my country's dependence on foreign
suppliers for something as critical as its own security. Every one
of you, in whatever field you enter, will have a version of that
same choice, whether to build only for yourself, or to build for
something larger than yourself.
Fourth, don't wait for the system to make room for you. Make
your own room. No one invited a school dropout from
Rajasthan into India's defence manufacturing sector. I built the
credentials nobody could deny, through results, not through
requests.
A Nation That Needs Builders
You are graduating at a remarkable moment for India. This
country is no longer content to simply consume technology
built elsewhere. From agriculture to artificial intelligence, from
drones to defence systems, India is choosing to build its own
future with its own hands. I have seen this shift up close. When I

built elsewhere. From agriculture to artificial intelligence, from

future with its own hands. I have seen this shift up close. When I
4 / / 5
started, nearly every advanced explosive technology in this
country came from abroad. Today, our engineers design and
build systems that our own armed forces depend on, and other
nations now buy from us.
I understand IIT Ropar has itself become part of this story this
year; working with the Indian Air Force, the Army's Western
Command, and DRDO on indigenous technology
development. That is exactly the spirit I am speaking of. This is
not work confined to a company like mine. It belongs to every
young engineer, scientist, and innovator this country produces
including every one of you sitting here today.
Whatever you choose to build in agriculture, in AI, in energy, in
defence, in public service, build it here, for this country, with the
same stubbornness I once brought to a small explosives unit in
Nagpur. India does not need more people chasing comfortable
jobs. It needs builders. It needs people willing to enter difficult,
unglamorous, heavily regulated fields and stay there long
enough to master them.
A Word on Struggle
I know many of you have already faced setbacks, a project that
failed, a rank that didn't meet your expectations, a placement
that didn't go the way you hoped. I want you to hear this from
someone who slept on a railway platform not knowing where
the next month's meal would come from; struggle is not a sign
that you are on the wrong path. It is often simply the price of the
path worth taking.
Do not measure your worth by your worst year. I have had
many. What matters is whether you get up the next morning and
go back to work. That is the only formula I know, and it is the
only one I trust.

never had; a degree from one of India's finest institutions. Do

Build with patience. Build with integrity. And build for your
country, not only for yourself.

text:
Convocation
th
Thursday, 6 August, 2026
TH
INDIAN INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY ROPAR
भारतीय �ौ�ोिगकी सं�थान रोपड़
CHAIRMAN’S SPEECH
Shri Adil Zainulbhai

/ 1
761! That's how many of you are
graduating today — BTech,
MTech, M.Sc and PhD, all in one
room. Some of you have been here
four years, some two, some longer
than that if you count the pandemic
year none of us want to count.
Whatever your path, today it ends
the same way: you walk out of here
an IIT Ropar graduate.
I want to start with a claim, and I want to defend it: there
has never been a better time to graduate in India than
right now.
I know that sounds like the thing every dignitary says at
every convocation. So let me tell you why I actually
believe it.
You are walking into a working life of roughly sixty years.
Most of you will still be working in your eighties. Think
about what that means. The technology you'll retire on
doesn't exist yet. Half the job titles you'll hold haven't
been invented. That used to be a frightening thought. I
don't think it is anymore — not for this batch, not
graduating from an institution built the way this one was.
Here's why. India today is doing something it has never
done before: building its capacity and its confidence at
the same time. We're the fastest-growing major
economy in the world. We're the country every global

th

761! That's how many of you are
graduating today — BTech,

room. Some of you have been here
four years, some two, some longer
than that if you count the pandemic
year none of us want to count.
Whatever your path, today it ends
the same way: you walk out of here
an IIT Ropar graduate.

has never been a better time to graduate in India than
right now.
I know that sounds like the thing every dignitary says at
every convocation. So let me tell you why I actually
believe it.
You are walking into a working life of roughly sixty years.
Most of you will still be working in your eighties. Think
about what that means. The technology you'll retire on
doesn't exist yet. Half the job titles you'll hold haven't
been invented. That used to be a frightening thought. I
don't think it is anymore — not for this batch, not
graduating from an institution built the way this one was.

done before: building its capacity and its confidence at
the same time. We're the fastest-growing major
economy in the world. We're the country every global
company wants a supply chain foothold in. And we're

has never been smaller. When I started my career, the
best jobs, the best labs, the best opportunities were
somewhere else, and the ambition was to go find them.
That's not the story anymore. Increasingly, the frontier is
here. AI research is here. Chip design is here. The
deepest problems in health, energy, and infrastructure
that the world needs solved — India has more of them,
and more reason to solve them, than almost anywhere
else.
That's the opportunity in front of you. I want to be honest
about what it demands in return.
It demands that you stay a learner. The degree you're
holding today certifies what you knew as of this year. It
does not certify what you'll need to know in 2035. The
engineers and researchers who do well over a sixty-year
career aren't the ones who learned the most in college —
they're the ones who never stopped treating themselves
as students. That habit, more than anything on your
transcript, is what IIT Ropar actually gave you.
It demands that you go toward hard problems, not away
from them. India doesn't need more people optimizing
ad clicks. It needs people willing to work on water, on
public health at scale, on manufacturing, on the boring,
unglamorous infrastructure that a billion-person
economy runs on. Some of the most interesting
engineering problems in the world right now are not in
Silicon Valley. They're in figuring out how to give 1.4
billion people clean water, reliable power, and a
functioning healthcare system, using tools that didn't
exist ten years ago. That is not a lesser ambition than
joining a famous company. For many of you, it's a bigger
one.
And it demands humility about what you don't know yet,
even with an IIT degree behind your name. I've sat on
boards and hiring committees for forty years. The person
who assumes they've arrived because they got the
degree is, without exception, the person who stalls first.
The ones who keep growing are the ones who stay a
little uncomfortable, a little unsure, for their entire career.
Let me say something about this institution, because I
don't think you fully know the story you're part of.
IIT Ropar is not old. It was founded in 2008. Some of you
are nearly as old as the campus you're graduating from.
Every IIT before you had decades of infrastructure,
decades of alumni, decades of reputation to lean on.
You didn't have that. What you had instead were faculty
and a founding leadership who had to build something
from very little, fast, and get it right. That's a different kind
of education than the one you'd get at a hundred-year-
old institution. You've learned, whether you noticed it or
not, what it takes to build something rather than just
inherit it. That instinct — build, don't just occupy — is
going to matter more in your career than almost anything
else you picked up here.
Prof. Rajeev Ahuja and the faculty have spent years
turning a green field into what you're sitting in today.
That work isn't finished, and it isn't supposed to be.
Neither is yours.
So here is what I'd ask of you, specifically, as you leave.

Don't wait for permission to do ambitious work. Nobody
is going to tap you on the shoulder and tell you you're
ready. You'll never feel fully ready. Start anyway.
Go where the hard problems are, even if the path is less
obvious than the one everyone else is taking. Ten years
from now, the people who took the interesting, harder
route will be doing far more interesting work than the
ones who took the safe one.
And come back to this place. Not literally, necessarily —
but stay connected to it. IIT Ropar is going to need this
batch, and every batch after you, to build its name the
way you build a company: through the people who carry
it out into the world and do something worth noticing.
Every one of you is now part of how this institution gets
known. Wear that seriously.
Congratulations to all 761 of you. Your families are
watching today with a kind of pride that doesn't come
around often — take a moment to actually look at them
before you leave this hall. You've earned this. Now go
build something worth the sixty years ahead of you.
Thank you.
