PREAMBLE

IIT Ropar is striving to develop itself into an Institution -of-Excellence in Research, Development
and Consultancy through original research of highest standards and leadership in technology
innovation.

In addition to formal UG and PG programs, IIT Ropar encourages faculty, academic staff, staff and
students to unde rtake sponsored research projects and industrial consultancy to strengthen the
research impact of the Institute.

In order to fill the above and to create an ambiance in which new ideas, research and development
and consultancy flourish, IIT Ropar has established a Research and Development (R&D) Division.

R&D facilitates faculty, academic staff, staff and students in conducting research and consultancy
in compliance with the policies and guidelines of the sponsoring agencies and the Institute. The
goal of R&D is to assure compliance while facilitating research through SINE and IRIS Grant to
the faculty members and various consultancy projects.

This manual presents R&D policy framework about rules and regulations to execute sponsored
research projects and industrial consultancy.

Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 4 of 36

DEFINITIONS
Institute
Institute refers to Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IITRPR).

Director
Director refers to the Director, Indian Institute of Technology Ropar.

Dean, R&D
Dean, R&D refers to the Dean of Res earch and Development, Indian Institute of Technology
Ropar.

BR&D
Board of Research and Development (BR&D) shall consist of members of each Department to be
nominated by the respective HODs.

Department
Department refers to all the academic schools, acade mic centres, centres of excellence and
academic service centres at Indian Institute of Technology Ropar.

Sponsor
Sponsor refers to the organization that offers a sponsored project/industrial consultancy to the
Institute and provides necessary financial support for successful completion of the project in time.

Principal Investigator
Principal Investigator (PI) is a member of the faculty (including Emeritus) of the Institute with
necessary expertise and competence to conduct a sponsored research/industrial consultancy.
Normally, the faculty who submits the project proposal and negotiates with the sponsor and is
instrumental in getting the project funding is the Principal Investigator (PI) under these rules. In a
special case, PI may be appointed by the Director on the recommendation of the Dean, R&D and in
consultation with the concerned Head of Department for administrative reasons if the original PI
leaves his/her service or is not available for the project for any other reason.

Co-Investigator or Co-Principal Investigator
Co-Investigator or Co -Principal Investigator (Co -PI) is the working/retired faculty member co -
opted by the Principal Investigator to work jointly with him/her and approved by the funding
agency and/or Dean, R&D.

Individual Research and Development Grant
Individual Research and Development Grant (IRDG) is the research and development grant -in-aid
offered to an individual faculty member or a research fellow by the sponsor towards the cost of
equipment, contingency and overhead expenses, fellowship etc.

Project Research Staff
Project Research Staff is a person appointed/engaged on contract in conformity with the provisions
of these guidelines in a sponsored research project as a fellow or associate or with a similar
designation and receiving fellowship.

Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 5 of 36

Project Staff
Project Staff is a person appointed/engaged on contract (excluding project research staff) following
the provisions of these guidelines to work on a sponsored research project. The project staff
includes research, technical and office personnel.

Consultant
Consultant is a person appointed as consultant for a specific period to carry out a specific job.

Institute Development Fund (IDF)
A part of the institutional overhead charges received for any sponsored research and indus trial
consultancy project is credited to a separate R&D fund, to be operated by Dean, R&D. This fund is
designated as IDF. A part of the R&D fund shall be transferred every year to the Institute
Development Fund which shall form the corpus of the Institute.

Departmental Development Fund (DDF)
A part of the Institute overhead charges from sponsored research projects shall be transferred to the
DDF of the concerned academic Department(s). The objective of this fund is to provide additional
grants to the Department for its development activities.

Professional Development Fund (PDF)
There shall be a Professional Development Fund for individual academic staff, the objective of
which shall be to help individuals in his/her professional development. A part of the Institute
overhead charges from sponsored research projects shall be transferred to the PDF of the concerned
academic staff and utilized by him/her as per R&D norms.

Research & Development Fund (RDF)
There shall be a Research & Development Fund to meet v arious expenditures of the R & D Office
such as any Fellowship / Project advance, Seminar Series, R&D Conclave and any other
miscellaneous expenses etc.

Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 6 of 36

GUIDELINES

1. SPONSORED RESEARCH PROJECTS
Sponsored research project refers to one in which the PI d oes not charge honorarium/consultation
fee. Funds shall be used by the PIs as approved in the respective budget head by the funding
agency. For projects from industry and other agencies, any balance funds at the end of the project
may remain with the Inst itute. In such cases, the balance funds will be distributed to faculty and
staff involved in the project in accordance with R&D guidelines.

1.1. Projects involving IIT Ropar Faculty only
The Institute encourages investigation of basic and applied areas of scie nce and technology,
and high-end technology development in the form of sponsored projects. Research grants for
such projects are given by government agencies and industries (both national and
international). These projects are usually of 2-5 years duration with periodic appraisals, while
research objectives and goals may be refined along the way.

1.2. Collaborative Projects
Faculty may also participate in collaborative projects with other domestic or foreign partners.
In such projects, even though there may be an overall project, there must be a separate budget
and scope of work statement to be done by the faculty and staff of the Institute. The summary
statement provided to the Institute should be based primarily on the portion to be done by the
Institute. The Institute will treat this like any other sponsored project.

1.3. Institute Projects
In case the Institute is awarded a sponsored project directly, or a proposal is submitted at the
Institute level, the Principal Investigator would be identified by the Director.

1.4. Preparation of the Proposal and Guiding Notes
The project proposal should be formulated according to the format prescribed by the
concerned sponsoring agency. While making an estimate of the funds required for a project,
the following budget heads to be taken into account:

a) Salary of Project Staff (with designations)
b) Equipment
c) Consumables
d) Travel (specify if there is need for international travel)
e) Contingency
f) Institute Overheads Charges (IOC)

All project proposals are to be sent to Dean, R&D for endorse ment. The „Project proposal
form‟ duly completed must be submitted along with the proposal. The R & D Office will
assign a unique internal number to the project proposal.

IPR issue: All IPR related issues will be governed as per the agreement between the Institute
and the funding agency.

MoU/Agreement preparation: The Institute has guidelines for drafting MoU/ Agreement.

The project normally will be started after the receipt of funds. The project expenditure for
equipment and consumables will be mainta ined in a separate stock register by PI. The
statement of expenditure and utilization certificate will be prepared at the end of every
Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 7 of 36

financial year by the designated Institute officer and sent to the sponsoring agency through
admin head of R&D i.e. AR/DR /JR of R&D . The procurement, and recruitment procedure
may be started after receiving the sanction letter and payments may also be made as loan
from the R&D/institute funds, for successful completion of projects within specified period.

Collaborative projects between two or more Institutions/organizations can be submitted only
after the approval of respective competent authorities. The funds will be received by the host
Institute /organization of the PI and the host Institute /organization will have the
responsibility to transfer the funds to the collaborative Institute s/organizations as specified in
the project proposals. If the sponsor agrees, funds can be released by the sponsor, separately,
to the participating Institutes.

1.5. Submission of Progress Reports and other Deliverables
It is the responsibility of the PI to send timely reports and other deliverables to the sponsoring
agency through the admin head of the R & D section, e.g., AR/DR/JR. Statement of account
to be submitted will be made available to the PI on request to the designated Institute officer.
After completion of the project, the final report should be submitted to the funding agency
through the admin head of the R & D section, e.g., AR/DR/JR with a soft copy for the record
of the Dean, R&D and for public information/RTI purposes. A completion certificate should
be obtained by the PI from the funding agency for successful completion of the project based
on which project account will be closed with intimation to the R&D Office. The project fi le
will be closed with the submission of the final technical and financial project report and
transfer of the non-consumables to the Central stock register.

2. CONSULTANCY PROJECTS
The Institute has expertise in various research areas to provide knowledge an d intellectual inputs
which are of interest to the industry. It encourages its faculty to undertake consultancy work which
is an important tool in industrial growth of the Country.

2.1 Guiding Notes
A consultancy project/task/work is one where faculty and res earch staff provide knowledge
and intellectual inputs to industry (within India and abroad), primarily for the purposes of the
concerned industry. This is effectively a contract work in which all outputs belong to the
client.

All payments for consultancy work must come in the name of the Dean, R&D (IIT Ropar R
and D Account) of the Institute. The Institute will then do the needful for complying with
statutory laws and then give the honorarium to the faculty/staffs the case may be.

The requirement originat es from the industry concerned. The faculty is expected to estimate
the time and cost required to accomplish the task.

Proposal is prepared by the PI and it should specifically mention breakup of funds, normally
consultancy fee as the primary component. It may also have a budget for supporting
manpower, equipment, travel, contingency, Institute overheads and expenses for IPR (if need
be).

In case equipment is to be returned to the funding agency/organization after completion of the
project, this should b e clearly spelt out in the/proposal itself. All consultancy proposals must
be sent to Dean,R&D for endorsement and approval along with the consultancy project
agreement form.
Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 8 of 36

The Office of R&D will assign a unique internal number to the project proposal.

The Institute normally requires the cost of the consultancy project to be deposited by the
client, in full, before the commencement of work. However, based on the needs of the client
and circumstances, the Institute may, in exceptional cases, permit comm encement of work
with payment to be made as per agreed upon milestones. The expenditure and disbursements
will be made through normal Institute procedures. The project expenditure for equipment and
consumables will be maintained in a separate stock register by PI.

In international consultancy projects:

a) Funds are received in foreign currency
b) The research collaboration of IIT Ropar with the other party/funding agency
should be in conformity with the laws of all the countries involved and/or
International laws.

IPR issue: All IPR related issues are agreed between the Institute and the funding agency.
Preferably, IPR will be jointly shared by IIT Ropar and the funding agency.

MoU/ agreement preparation: Institute has guidelines for drafting MoU/Agreement. W hen
MoU is clear from all angles and acceptable to both the parties, it is sent to the Director,
IIT/Dean, R&D for approval along with the Note File (Summary of MoU). A copy of the
duly signed MoU will be sent to the other party and a copy retained in the office of Dean,
R&D. After approval, PI/HoD/Dean, R&D/Director as the case may be will sign the MoU.

Project responsibility: These projects are headed by a Principal Investigator (PI), and may
have Co-Principal Investigators (Co-PIs) and the deliverables are the responsibility of the PIs.
The Institute provides the PIs necessary support.

The statement of expenditure and utilization certificate will be prepared at every financial
year end by the competent designated authority. After completion of the proj ect, the final
report should be submitted to the funding agency. The project file will be closed with the
submission of the final technical and financial project report and transfer of the non -
consumables and consumables to the Department/R&D stock register.

3. TESTING

The word refers to testing a component or a product against a standard. Examples could be testing
the strength of concrete in construction, compaction strength of soil, calibration of pressure gauges,
and chemical identification of unknown spe cies. The Institute will undertake testing jobs provided
facilities are available and such testing does not interfere with any teaching or research work. The
testing jobs can be initiated by faculty once a request is received for the testing job.

3.1. Guiding Notes
The procedure for overall operation of the project is similar to that of consultancy projects.

Certification: The Institute (through its faculty) is not authorized to undertake certification in any
form. At best, one can say that, on a given day, wi th a given sample, a well-defined test yielded the
following results.

Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 9 of 36

4. SPECIAL GRANTS
Sometimes, there are special grants given to the institute for purposes, such as, grants for
infrastructure improvement, laboratory improvement, conferences (from DST/CSI R etc..),
donations (e.g. alumni), performing specific experiments / methods in teaching/learning, etc..,
where no direct deliverables are envisaged.

4.1. Guiding Note
Such grants may be treated as a project for operational reasons. For such projects, the Inst itute
overheads may be or waived. The decision will be taken on a case -by-case basis by the Dean,
R&D/Director.

5. MANPOWER RECRUITMENT, ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA AND PAYMENT

5.1 Open selections will be held for all project staff positions. The broad guidelines for hiring of
manpower under various R&D projects are laid down in Appendix-A. The same may be
revised or changed by the Board of R&D as and when deemed necessary.

5.2 Project research staff shall be paid a consolidated fellowship per month and other project
staff shall be paid consolidated amount of compensation per month as per funding agency
norms or decided by the PI in consultation with the selection committee of the project staff
during the recruitment process.

5.3 The designations available for the project re search staff and project staff, eligibility criteria
viz, qualification, experience, age and consolidated emoluments will be as specified by the
sponsoring agency/Institute. Any changes/ additions/deletions to the same can be made by
approval from the Sponsoring agency.

5.4 All appointments for project posts shall be on contract only.

5.5 The project research staff shall work for fulfilling the objectives of the project.

5.6 Transfer of project staff from one project to another, either on completion or midway, may be
permitted by Dean, R&D.

5.7 The tenure of appointment of a project staff will be at the most for the remaining duration of
the project. The severance notice may be issued to the project staff by the PI one month prior
to the termination of appointment.

5.8 The project staff appointed in the project shall seek permission of the PI before applying for
higher studies and employment outside IIT Ropar.

5.9 On the completion of one year and on the recommendation of an Assessment Committee,
appointed by Dean, R&D for th e purpose, the enhancement of fellowship of a project
research staff may be considered by the Dean, R&D. The composition of the Assessment
Committee shall be as specified under clause - 12.

5.10 A contractual project staff appointed under budgeted provision sh all execute a Contract
Agreement with PI and HOD at the time of joining with the explicit provision that the
contract may be terminated by either side, the staff or PI and HOD, by giving one month‟s
Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 10 of 36

notice or one month‟s consolidated emoluments in lieu of the notice. The contracts will be
complete when countersigned by Dean, R&D who will retain the original contract agreement.

5.11 Selection of project research staff shall normally be made as per the Institute norms.
However, guidelines prescribed by the sponso ring agency shall be adhered to as far as
possible.

5.12 All appointment letters shall be issued under the signatures of AR/DR/JR on the
recommendation of the selection committee approved by the Dean (R&D).

5.13 The appointment letter to be issued to project staff should spell out all terms and conditions of
the contract including the time limit.

5.14 In special circumstances, as desired by the PI, ad -hoc appointment on a research post of a
person having the prescribed qualification can be considered by the Dean, R&D o n the
recommendation of the PI for a period as mentioned by PI.

5.15 Short term assignment on work hire on per hour basis or per unit -of-work basis may be
permitted by the Dean, R&D on the request of the PI. However, PI can appoint interns on a
project as when required. No permission from Dean (R&D) is required for such
appointments.

5.16 The project research staff shall be entitled to HRA as per the Institute rules which shall be
charged to the salary head of the respective project and must be mentioned during wr iting for
the project proposal.

5.17 Leave: Leave entitlement for the research/project staff shall be entitled as per policy as
specified by the sponsoring agency. Any changes/ additions/deletions to the same can be
made by R&D.

5.18 The project staff shall
i. Follow general code of conduct as approved for Institute employees, and
ii. Maintain record and secrecy of the research findings/technical information and shall
not get involved in unauthorized communication of any official document or
information.

5.19 The Dean, R&D ma y, at his/her own discretion or on the recommendation of the PI/HOD,
constitute committee(s) to conduct disciplinary proceedings against project staff, if necessary.
On the basis of the report of the committee, suitable disciplinary action may be initiated , and
punishment be imposed by the Dean (R&D).

5.20 Project staff of one sponsored project can be hired for another similar project (if he /she
fulfills the eligibility criteria) with the same or another PI for smooth running of the project.

6. FINANCE AND ACCOUNTS

6.1 At the time of submission of a project proposal, the PI shall make a provision of Institutional
Overhead Charges (IOC) at the rate of 20% of the total project cost or at the rate specified by
the sponsoring organization.

Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 11 of 36

6.2 The financial delegation power of Dean, R&D for all projects fund is upto Rs. 15.00 Lakhs.

6.3 All purchase proposals will be routed by PI to the R & D Office, which shall be processed as
per rules and availability of funds. The purchases upto Rs 1.00 Lakh from the project funds
shall be approved by the concerned Project‟s PI/CI and the payment may be processed
through signature of Admin head of R&D i.e. AR/DR/JR of the R & D Division.

6.4 Salary / Fellowship of the project staff shall be released on monthly basis upon the
recommendation of PI / CI which should reach the office of Dean, R&D latest by 20th of
every month so that the salary can be released within the next 9 working days. If the
recommendation of PI is not received by the 20 th of every month, the salary of the project
staff will be released assuming that the performance of the staff is satisfactory.

6.5 The PI of the project may initiate the process of hiring of manpower and procurement of
items based on the sanction order received. The loan shall be provided by the R&D Section
from its RDF/interest/income earned for the same so the PI can start the project on time basis.
The funds will be recouped once it is received from the funding agency.

6.6 In case of unavailability of funds but otherwise sanctioned from the sponsoring agency, th e
salary of the project staff, payment to vendors for committed expenditure will be released and
procurement may also be initiated from R&D funds after recommendation from PI as loan
against the project, on the basis of project sanction/approval letter, wh ich will be reconciled
as when project funds are available.

6.7 Unutilized funds in the sponsored research / consultancy project budget heads, such as; travel,
contingency, or similar, may be transferred to the PDF account of the PI/Co -PI of the project
for better financial utilization.

6.8 PIs/HODs shall arrange to maintain stock/asset registers. These shall be submitted to the
Audit/Institute as and when called for.

6.9 PI/ HoD will be authorized to extend delivery period, for valid and justifiable reasons in
writing and waive off Late delivery charges for procurement through their respective
sponsored projects .

6.10 The R&D Office will provide an account of expenditure to the PI either periodically or as and
when needed by the PI.

6.11 Accounts for sponsored projects shall be maintained under the budget heads specified in the
sanction letter from the sponsor. Minor adjustments in approved budget heads may be
permitted by the Dean, R&D.

6.12 All expenditure shall normally be made within the proposed date of completion (PDC ) of the
project. Exceptions may be permitted by the Dean, R&D with the consent of the sponsor.

6.13 In the event of non -availability of fund in a project, to meet the excess expenditure (if any)
due to unforeseen reasons, the sponsoring agency will be approac hed by the PI through HOD
and Dean, R&D to sanction additional fund to permit the expenditure from another project of
the same sponsor.

Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 12 of 36

6.14 TA/DA Rules

The most expeditious and convenient mode of travel should be used to minimize periods of
absence from the Institute. Admissible DA or actual boarding and lodging expenses will be
paid on production of receipt wherever required as per entitlement. PI of project is authorized
to approve travel amount upto Rs. 1.00 Lakh for PI/project staff/ Interns and if the a mount
exceeds Rs. 1.00 Lakh, it will need an approval of Dean (R&D) for undertaking a
domestic/international journey. All air travels to be undertaken as per GoI rules.

Expenses on local travel by taxi will be reimbursed against receipt as per actual or entitlement
whichever is less. Wherever taxi bill is not available taxi bill to be reimbursed as per actual
based on certification and proper justification by the PI.

Advance for travel upto Rs. 1.00 Lakh shall be approved by the PI for PI/project staff / Interns
and if the amount exceeds Rs. 1.00 Lakh, it will need the approval of Dean (R&D).
Reimbursement of charges to travel agents for ticket purchase assistance, visa assistance,
insurance, porter charges or any other charges ancillary to the project/c onsultancy related
incurred in the process of travel, etc., shall be admissible from project funds. However, if the
sponsor has specified any specific condition(s), viz, mode of travel, class of travel, etc.., for
travel under the project that shall be fol lowed normally. Approval of Dean, R&D will be
required for any deviations from above.

6.15 Out of Pocket Expenses for Field Work
Out of pocket expenses, expenses not provided in the TA/DA, will be payable for the actual
period of field work at the workplace at the rates given in the Annexure– 1.

6.16 The PI may engage institute students (who may or may not be getting fellowship/
assistantship) as student assistants for the project work.

6.17 A request for payment of an advance as per the purchase rules to PI or Co -PI, duly forwarded
by the concerned PI, may be considered for approval by Dean, R&D. Further, an imprest for
each financial year during the project tenure may be sanctioned to PI by Dean, R&D.

6.18 Adjustment account for an advance drawn shall be submitted within 30 days of return from
the journey or date of issuing the cheque/transfer of money, whichever is later. In other
cases, TA claims should preferably be settled within 60 days from joining the Institute after
completion of the journey.

6.19 An individual shall normally be allowed to draw another advance only after adjusting the
previous one taken by him/her.

6.20 All payments to project staff, persons engaged on work hire and students engaged for project
work will be made by the R & D Office by only online transfer.

7. MEDICAL FACILITIES

Medical facilities shall be provided to the project staff as per the provisions laid down for the
students of IIT on payment of annual insurance charges (for medi -claim and personal accident
insurance). Cashless facility to the pr oject staff for OPD in empaneled hospitals within/outside
Rupnagar is not permissible. However, the project staff can utilize the services of in -house medical
facilities.
Approved in 45th BoG meeting

Page 13 of 36

8. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI)

8.1 Only the faculty and other academic staff in the service of the Institute can be PIs of a
sponsored research project.

8.2 The PI will, at his/her discretion, co-opt the names of other faculty members as Co-PIs or Co-
Investigators with their consent. A retired faculty member can be co -opted if the funding
agency permits the same explicitly, but only as a Co-Investigator.

8.3 The PI will prepare research project proposal in conformity with:
● Permitted designation and emolument/fellowship rates for project staff, with
qualification and experience as specified by the sponsoring agency.
● Provision for institution overhead charges shall as per the rules of the Institute or as per
the guidelines of the sponsor.
● Other guidelines for sponsored projects, and rules, regulations and statute of the
Institute

8.4 All research proposals shall be submitted to the sponsors through the concerned HOD and
Dean, R&D.

8.5 It shall be the responsibility of the PI to get project work completed satisfactorily within the
sanctioned grant and duration.

8.6 The PI shall ensure that the head-wise expenditure does not exceed the budgetary allocation.

8.7 The PI and R&D office shall maintain the details of equipment purchased out of project funds
separately for each project and send a copy of the record to Dean, R&D for placing the same
before the audit authorities, for verification or as and when required for any other purpose.

8.8 The PI shall be responsible for maintenance of Laboratory Record Book (LRB) as required
for Intellectual Property Right (IPR) submission, periodical and /or final technical report(s) of

title: PDF: Procedure Timeline
text:
Research and Development (R&D) Section Purchase Procedure:
A comprehensive set of purchase forms, workflows and Important Information added here to facilitate
transparent, efficient, and standardized procurement processes for Sponsored and Consultancy Projects
which are available under Download Forms and Important Information Tabs on the Institute Website
under R&D Section Webpage. The Procurement Process is completely digitized , with provisions for e-office
processing and online submissions to streamline approvals and documentation.
The forms are designed to assist PIs/faculty members/researchers and Project staff in understanding the
standardized procedures related to project execution, procurement, finance, and compliance. It acts as a
repository of key documents and instructions necessary for smooth functioning of R&D activities.
1. Classification of Purchases
The purchase procedure is categorized based on the cost of procurement , ensuring appropriate levels of
scrutiny and approval:
● Minor (Direct) Purchase (up to ₹2 lakhs/for non-scientific item up to ₹50,000/-)
○ Processed using SP-01 Indent
● Medium (Committee) Purchase (₹2 lakhs to ₹25 lakhs/for non-scientific item up to ₹5 Lakhs)
○ Includes SP-02 Indent and SP-02A NIQ (quotation-based procurement)
● Major (Bidding) Purchase (above ₹25 lakhs/Bidding of non-scientific items >₹5 lakhs)
○ Requires SP-03 Indent and formal committee-based approvals
This classification ensures control mechanisms and compliance with Govt procurement norms.
2. Committee-Based Evaluation System
For higher-value purchases, a structured evaluation mechanism is followed:
● SP-03A SPC for SP-02/03 ( < Rs. 25 Lakhs) – Committee for medium and major purchase
● SP-03B PFC for SP-03 (>Rs. 25 Lakhs) – Finalization Committee for major purchases
Additionally, technical and financial evaluations are handled through designated forms:
● SP-04 Technical Evaluation
● SP-05 Financial Evaluation
This layered approach promotes fairness, transparency, and technical validation before finalizing
procurement decisions.
3. Bid Processing and Special Requests
The purchase system includes provisions for handling exceptional situations:
● SP-07 GeM Custom Bid
● SP-08 GTE Proposal (Global Tender Enquiry)
These forms ensure continuity of procurement even under limited vendor participation while maintaining
compliance standards.
4. Post-Procurement and Inspection
After procurement, proper verification and documentation are mandatory. The e-Invoice can be forwarded
digitally along with MIIR through department office for stock entry:
● SP-06 MIIR: Material Inspection Report
● Ensures that delivered goods meet specifications before payment processing
This step is crucial for quality assurance and Inventory management in research purchases.
5. Documentation and Tendering Support
Additional forms support documentation and tender processes:
● SP-11 CPPP Tender Document
● SP-12 Clarification Request
● SP-13 Corrigendum Request
● SP-14 EMD Bank Guarantee
● SP-15 Negotiation Request
● SP-15A Negotiation Invitation
● SP-15B Negotiated Offer
These ensure proper record-keeping and adherence to procurement policies.
6. Integration with Digital Workflow
The entire purchase process is integrated with:
● E-office systems
● Email-based submission options
● Defined workflows & timelines
This reduces paperwork, improves efficiency, and enhances traceability of approvals and transactions.
❖ In addition to the eFile/eReceipt tracking in eOffice, access to the Real-time updated Register of
Indents/Purchase Orders & Debarred Vendors Register along with processing time of all indents are
available under the R&D Download Forms/Important Information sections.
7. Inventory Management
Personal Inventory is managed on Samarth Portal . Before processing the MIIR for payment after
Department Stock entry, every non-consumable item is entered on the samarth portal and issued/notified to
the Indenter. Prior to that all the bills are entered in the Daily Receipt Register (DRR) of the Stores, R&D.
8. Purchase Orders and Sanctions
Final procurement approval and execution involve:
● Sanction Sheet, Indian Purchase Order, Import Purchase Order, Amendments to orders,
Customs/Transport clearance, etc. A set of forms are available for R&D Office Use .
These forms formalize the transaction and define contractual obligations, including delivery terms and
compliance requirements.
The purchase forms provided by IIT Ropar’s R&D section establish a well-structured, transparent, and
scalable procurement framework . By categorizing purchases, incorporating committee-based evaluations,
and digitizing workflows, the institute ensures financial discipline, accountability, and efficiency in
handling research-related procurements. This system supports both routine and complex purchases while
maintaining compliance with institutional and governmental guidelines.
❖ Indent/PO Register for office records/suo moto disclosure under GFR 174(i)/Govt Procurement

(3) The Principal will disqualify from the tender process all bidders who do not sign this Pact or violate this provisions.
If the Principal obtains knowledge of conduct of a Bidder, Contractor or Subcontractor, or of an employee or a representative or an associate of a Bidder,
Contractor or Subcontractor which constitutes corruption, or if the
Principal has substantive suspicion in this regard, the Principal will inform the same to the Chief Vigilance Officer.
(1) The Principal appoints competent and credible Independent External Monitor for this Pact after approval by Central Vigilance Commission. The task of
the Monitor is to review independently and objectively, whether and to what extent the parties comply with the
obligations under this agreement.
(2) The Monitor is not subje to instructions by the representatives of the parties and performs his/her functions neutrally and independently. The Monitor
would have access to all Contract documents, whenever required. It will be obligatory for him/her to treat the information and documents of the
Bidders/Contractors as confidential. He/she reports to Secretary, MoE.
(3) The Bidder(s)/Contractor(s) accepts that the Monitor has the right to access without restriction to all Project documentation of the Principal including
that provided by the Contractor. The Contractor will also grant the Monitor, upon his/her request and demonstration of a valid interest, unrestricted and
unconditional access to their project documentation. The same is applicable to Sub-contractors.
(4) The Monitor is under contractual obligation to treat the information and documents of the Bidder(s) Contractor(s) Sub-contractor(s) with confidentiality.
The Monitor has also signed declarations on 'Non-Disclosure of Confidential Information' and of 'Absence of Conflict of
Interest'. In case of any conflict of interest arising at a later date, the IEM shall inform Secretary, D/o Higher Education.
(5) The Principal will provide to the Monitor sufficient information about all meeting among the parties related to the Project provided such meetings could
have an impact on the contractual relations between the Principal and the Contractor. The parties offer to the
Monitor the option to participate in such meetings.
(6) As soon as the Monitor notices, or believes to notice, a violation of this agreement, he/she will so inform the Management of the Principal and request
the Management to discontinue or take corrective action, or to take other relevant action. The monitor can in this regard
submit non-binding recommendations. Beyond this, the Monitor has no right to demand from the parties that they act in a specific manner, refrain from
action or tolerate action.
(7) The Monitor will submit a written report to the Secretary, D/o Higher Education within 8 to 10 weeks from the date of reference or intimation to him by
the Principal and, should the occasion arise, submit proposals for correcting problematic situations.
(8) If the Monitor has reported to the Secretary, D/o Higher Education, a substantiated suspicion of an offence under relevant IPC / F Act and the
Secretary, MoE has not, within the reasonable time taken visible action to proceed against such offence or reported it to the
Chief Vigilance Officer, the Monitor may also transmit this information directly to the Central Vigilance Commissioner.
(9) The word ‘Monitor’ would include both singular and plural.
This Pact begins when both parties have legally signed it. It expires for the Contractor 12 months after the last payment under the contract, and for all
other Bidders 6 months after the contract has been awarded. Any violation of the same would entail disqualification of the bidders and exclusion from
future business dealing. If any claim is made / lodged during this time, the same shall be binding and continue to be valid despite the lapse of this pact as
specified above, unless it is discharged / determined by Secretary, D/o Higher Education.
(1) This agreement is subject to Indian Law. Place of performance and jurisdiction is the Office of the Principal, i.e. New Delhi.
(2) Changes and supplements as well as termination notices need to be made in writing. Side agreements have not been made.
(3) If the Contractor is a partnership or a consortium, this agreement must be signed by all partners or consortium members.
(4) Should one or several provisions of this Pact turn out to be invalid, the remainder of this Pact remains valid. In this case, the parties will strive to come
to an agreement to their original intentions.
(5) Issues like Warranty / Guarantee etc. shall be outside the purview of IEMS.
(6) In the event of any contradiction between the Integrity Pact and its Annexure, the Clause in the Integrity Pact will prevail.
(7) The actions stipulated in this Integrity Pact are without prejudice to any other legal action(s) that may follow in accordance with the provisions of the
extant law in force relating to any civil or criminal proceedings.

ABOUT US
Where Dreams Meet Reality
Advitiya 2026, IIT Ropar's annual technical fest, is back to set the benchmark for technological innovation and intellectual grit. This year, the fest is themed "A Space Odyssey," transforming our campus into a launchpad for the next generation of engineers and creators. We bring together a massive lineup of high-stakes competitions, including app development battles, AI and algorithm challenges, fin-tech simulations and cyber-security hunts. Beyond the screen, expect to see the future in motion with robotics showcases, aerospace contests, and creative design modules. Whether it’s solving complex mathematical problems or dominating in gaming and finance, Advitiya is where the brightest minds come to push past the ordinary. If you’re obsessed with the "how" and the "why," you belong here.

This is ADVITIYA 2026, where deep-tech meets raw creativity.
50+ Events
100+ Colleges
5000+ Participants
Our Videos
TEASER
THEME
A Space Odyssey
The horizon was never the limit; it was just the beginning. This year, Advitiya embarks on the theme “ A Space Odyssey” , a mission to navigate the vast landscape of human potential.

This isn't just a journey; it’s a test of technical endurance. It is the distance between a raw concept and a world-shaping execution. In this odyssey, every line of code is fuel, and every mechanical design is a vessel built to withstand the pressure of the impossible.

We are moving beyond the expected to explore the deep layers of technology:

§ The Digital Void: Where logic and algorithms form the backbone of new worlds.

§ The Engines of Discovery: Where hardware and robotics push the limits of physical reality.

§ The Strategic Orbit: Where the laws of finance and the mechanics of gaming redefine human interaction.

The rules of gravity no longer apply;only the laws of innovation remain.

Prepare for liftoff. The galaxy is waiting.

Mission

Institute Student Mentorship Program
(ISMP) is a student initiative of IIT Ropar, which aims to provide a comprehensive and in-depth knowledge to freshmen on critical issues like academics, co and extra-curricular activities and how to bring about an optimum balance between them which proves decisive in shaping an individual's contentment levels in the institute.

To ensure this, every fresher is allotted a mentor who obviously is a senior student with substantial experience in plethora of matters to guide the freshmen through the transition process. The mentors are selected through a rigorous process to make sure they can guide mentees to take informed decisions in all spheres.

amongst universities across the globe.

TESTIMONIALS

Aneeket

Computer Science and Engineering, 3rd Year

Ropar was a new place, as it was for other freshers. Away from freinds and family, I felt lonely initially, had signs of homesickness. At first, it felt impossible to spend 4 years of my life here, but thanks to the ISMP programme here. The activities of ISMP gives the opportunity to meet other people on campus, make new freinds and gather experiences. I got to know about the various clubs at the college. Also, each student gets a mentor from second year who gives you breif idea of the functioning of the college and provide tips for balancing studies and co curricular. After 10 days of this programme, this place felt home, with a new family of new freinds. In short, it's fun, amusing and an experience for life.

Diksha

Mathematics and Computing, 3rd Year

Being a person who have never stayed away from family, coming to such a new place and living all alone appeared no more than a nightmare. But ISMP helped me a lot getting over all this. Introducing me to a lot of amazing people and whole of the place the program helped me a lot in being comfortable in the college. The activities conducted by the clubs introduced me to them and helped me find people with similar interests. The days were a nice combination of both the informative and fun sessions. On the whole, the activities kept me engaged throughout the day and made me ready for the things to come.

Nitish

Computer Science and Engineering, 3rd Year

Being from Punjab, I was quite surprised at finding rather few students from the home state and numerous from others. At times, I even felt out of place listening to people converse in their native language when I did not have anyone to talk to. I never knew anyone beforehand unlike almost everyone else, who had friends from coaching. But I soon made a lot of friends, thanks to the institute’s ISMP programme. The mentor interactions played a significant role in breaking the ice and helped get over the feeling of loneliness that had begun to dawn on me. The major takeaway was getting to know the campus well and the various opportunities it offered while getting acquainted with its people and culture. The various activities organised by the different clubs helped me meet people with shared interests and were instrumental in developing a bond with my seniors.

Priyasha

Electrical Engineering, 3rd Year

When you enter the premises of a college, it's an entirely new world. It was a no different situation for me. Just like a regular teen I too was skeptical about mine. Beginning our day with the dynamic bhangra sessions was enough to break the dormancy and fill us with energy. The club activities and the sports sessions with a few senior interactions aided me to know about my interests, explore the campus, and bridge the gaps between the seniors and freshers. It also gave me the chance to interact with students, not only of my department but others as well. These things helped me make new friends and cope up with all my general concerns. At last, I can say that ISMP helped me in a stable transition into college life.

Sudhanshu

Computer Science and Engineering, 3rd Year

The moment I made it here to the college, I knew this was a new phase in a whole different atmosphere from the past and a new atmosphere always demands the individual to accept and inhabit it with the people already in it. To get to know the structure and working of the system, to get along with the people who came with you, and who came before you, eventually learn about your interests and types of activities you want to be a part of, ISMP provided the necessary push to every single one of us.

If I were to call it a necessity over an option, I wouldn’t be exaggerating. It holds all the introductory interactions among freshers and freshers and among freshers and seniors, and also helps you explore through the various clubs present in the college. I found my people in the group we were a part of during our ISMP days, I found a supportive and friendly senior in the mentor who was assigned to us, and so many seniors I can turn to when I feel troubled. After attending the sessions of the clubs I am currently part of, I just knew, I had to join them and stick to them.

ISMP helps you make many acquaintances, you find your friends, your advice panel in seniors you come in touch with, and helps you explore the inner you by having a go at all the club activities. You can trust us on that, you’ll sure be enjoying a ride that goes up and up.

Kalarchita K

Mechanical Engineering, 3rd Year

I’m kalarchita sophomore of IITRPR. Here I’m going to brief my view about my ISMP. everything about the institute is new for me. And to know about me , I’m an introvert and never used to open up or express anything.It was a tough task for me to socialise among my fellow mates. This is the place where ISMP helped me the most. So far I can say the best period of my first year is ISMP. ISMP conducted mentor interaction different types of tasks to make me come out of my comfort zone and open up. Apart from all the mentor interaction sessions we had club sessions and sports hours. Where it was planned and divided among the students for 6 days. This provides us with a chance to experience everything and decide in which we likely want to excel.They took us to two different field trips. These are the two best experiences.last but not the least they’ve conducted treasure hunt and performed cultural night. These two events worth remembering cause the fun and joy it created in me were immeasurable.

College life is all about culture and how to socialise ourselves in it. ISMP helped me a lot to overcome my fear and other parameters , successfully made me a person who will deal with things is a better way.

Mohamed Mazhar Laljee

Chemical Engineering, 3rd Year

My happiness knew no bounds when I got selected for admission in one of the prestigious 23 IITs. I was looking forward to the new experience but thoughts about how good or bad it would be and the realisation that I’d have to befriend people from different parts of the country belonging to different cultural backgrounds worried me a little. Fortunately, IIT Ropar’s induction programme (called ISMP) took care of my concerns. The assigned student mentors did a great job in facilitating the breaking of ice among the freshers and between the freshers and seniors as well. Team building activities, sports and interactive sessions during the programme helped us in knowing our batchmates, and having a lot of fun at the same time. The mentors also gave us an excellent overview of life at the institute, opportunities that might come our way, various club activities and helped in striking a balance between academic and non-academic stuff. Memories made during this period will stay with us for years to come. ISMP thus plays an integral role in facilitating a fresher’s smooth transition from school life to college life.

Ishan Sawant

Mechanical Engineering, 3rd Year

One of the best things about ISMP is the vast number of activities you do throughout the day. This is important as we are kept engaged throughout the day and this led to the feeling of already belonging there. When I came here, I did worry about homesickness as Punjab is quite far from my hometown. However, the interactions with the freshmen and seniors through the activities made me forget about it. Understanding the IIT culture through ISMP made me realise the numerous areas for self development and self growth which will help me in becoming a valuable human being. ISMP ensures smooth transition from common school level mindset to a professional mindset. It is one of the many life changing experiences you will ever encounter.

Ritik Garg

Computer Science and Engineering, 3rd Year

Being the youngest in my family, my parents were quite anxious before the college admissions, about how would I assimilate into the new atmosphere at a completely oblivious place. I also had uncertainties and ambiguities about the new phase of my life, which were further compounded by the constant disquietness of my family members. However, the very first interaction with the ISMP mentors significantly alleviated the anxieties of my parents, after they observed the courteous and affable behavior of the mentors towards their juniors, which definitely was not a pretense, as can be assured from personal experience.

ISMP has been an unparalleled and memorable experience of my college life. It not only made me familiar with the college and its customs but also paved a way for an exceptional interaction with the seniors. It is hard to imagine a college life without the assistance of seniors, who are accessible to mentor you, support you, and accelerate your journey towards success. ISMP enabled me to interact with people, assimilate into the new atmosphere, enjoy the transition, and unconstrain my spirit to embrace the new teachings in my life.

ABOUT US

About IIT Ropar

ISMP

Director's Message

Vision and Mission

The Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar), established in 2008, is a premier engineering and research institution located in Rupnagar, Punjab. Nestled near the Sutlej River and surrounded by the scenic Shivalik Hills, the campus spans over 500 acres and blends sustainability with aesthetics, including architecture inspired by the Indus Valley civilization. It is one of the eight newer IITs established by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), Government of India, in 2008. With its foundations laid on 24th February, 2009, IIT Ropar now offers undergraduate (B.Tech), postgraduate (M.Tech, M.Sc), and doctoral (Ph.D) programs across various engineering, science, and humanities disciplines. IIT Ropar has been consistently ranked among the top engineering institutions in India by various national and international ranking agencies.

IIT Ropar currently offers a 4-year B. Tech. programme in Civil Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Computer Science & Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mathematics and Computing, Engineering Physics, Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, Digital Agriculture and Electrical Engineering (Integrated Circuit Design and Technology). Known for its strong emphasis on innovation and interdisciplinary research, the institute houses cutting-edge centres like the DST Technology Innovation Hub on Agriculture and Water (AWaDH) and a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence. IIT Ropar boasts state-of-the-art infrastructure, designed to support both academic and extracurricular activities. The campus features modern lecture halls, well-equipped laboratories, and extensive research facilities. Students benefit from a well-stocked library, advanced computer centres, and numerous specialised workshops.

Student life at IIT Ropar is dynamic and enriching, offering a healthy mix of academics, creativity, and community. Alongside a rigorous academic schedule, students engage in diverse clubs and societies ranging from robotics and astronomy to drama and photography. Annual fests like Zeitgeist and Advitiya bring energy and collaboration to campus life. The institute also promotes wellness through sports, fitness programs, and mental health initiatives. Hostel life is central to the experience, fostering friendships, late-night conversations, and a strong sense of belonging. The overall environment encourages both personal growth and innovation.

The Institute Student Mentorship Program (ISMP) at IIT Ropar is a student-led mentorship initiative aimed at easing the transition for first-year students into campus life. As soon as freshers arrive, each one is paired with a carefully selected senior mentor trained through a rigorous process to make sure they can guide mentees to take informed decisions in all spheres.. Mentors guide small groups of freshmen through everything from academic planning and course registration to social integration, co-curricular participation, and even navigating hostel routines . Communication is informal and frequent, happening via in-person catch-ups and virtual meets before the session begins.

The ISMP fosters a close-knit, empathetic environment. Mentorship isn't just knowledge transfer; it's about developing confidence, a sense of belonging, and a supportive peer network throughout the first year.

Professor Rajeev Ahuja

Director

Dear Students,

It is a great pleasure and honor for me to serve as the Director of Indian Institute of Technology Ropar.

The Indian Institute of Technology Ropar was established in 2008 to provide a significant niche in the education and research of science and technology. Over a period of more than a decade, IIT Ropar has emerged as a leading institution in engineering, pure sciences and social sciences.

Today, IIT Ropar is positioned to make key contributions to the advancement of technology solutions and sustainability research and to help lead the way toward sustainable growth of technological resources. The institute is preparing the next generation of leaders who will carry this path forward in the years ahead.

The Institute is committed to create an ambience for nurturing innovation, creativity and excellence within its students. We, at IIT Ropar, strongly support interdisciplinary research and development for the benefit of Industry and Society.

We emphasise on developing all round leadership skills. We are proud to say that the Institute is ideally placed to exploit the synergy within the engineering and science departments at the Institute. In doing so, we believe the Institute will continue to create unique and novel programmes to make significant contributions to Science and Technology as a domain. We are confident that all our efforts will grow into significant epitomes of achievements in the larger academic parlance. Hopefully, our labors in all the major areas of science and technology will produce fruitful results in academic innovation, top-tier journal publications, citations and technology developments.

On a final note, I request all to take care of themselves and their families during this difficult time of COVID crisis. This too shall pass, and we will again embark on our journey to make IIT Ropar as one of the best academic destinations of our nation.

Rajeev Ahuja

The institute, apart from establishing a robust teaching environment, is keen to facilitate and support cutting-edge research in a variety of areas. This aspect, we believe, will enable the students to acquaint themselves with latest developments in their respective areas of study and pursue their own research interests. This would also result in a constant revision of courses that are being taught. The institute encourages its faculty members to initiate research work and provides an initiation grant and also the basic facilities for its sustenance. It also encourages faculty members to establish collaborative research ventures with other research labs and industry. In this regard, the institute is keen to establish the Central Research Facility. The institute has already started its PhD Programme, so that the research environment is further augmented, expanded, and made even more vibrant.

THE NALANDA LIBRARY

The Central Library at IIT Ropar is the ultimate study hub for students and faculty. Packed with over 22,000 books and a plethora of electronic resources including e-journals and online databases like Scopus and Web of Science, it's the perfect place for all your academic endeavors.

Here's why you'll love our library:

Open Around the Clock: Our reference section is open 24/7, ensuring you have access whenever inspiration strikes. Plus, you can check out books during regular institute hours.

Versatile Study Spaces: Whether you prefer quiet corners for solo study sessions or collaborative zones for group discussions, we've got diverse areas tailored to your needs.

Streamlined Operations: Say goodbye to manual cataloging! Our library runs on the Koha Integrated Library Management System, making book searches and circulation processes a breeze.

Extensive Collection: Explore a wide array of topics with our collection of over 13,000 books spanning various disciplines, complemented by extensive electronic resources.

Easy Access with OPAC: Navigate our library effortlessly with the Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC). Search, reserve, and access documents conveniently to enhance your research experience.

Comprehensive Support: From citation analysis to plagiarism support, our research services have you covered, ensuring quality research every step of the way.

Conducive Environment: We maintain a conducive study environment by enforcing guidelines on noise levels, food, and phone usage, ensuring a peaceful atmosphere for everyone.

Borrowing Privileges: Enjoy borrowing privileges with transparent policies on borrowing durations and fines for overdue items, accessible to students, faculty, and staff alike.

The Student Council of IIT Ropar: Your Voice, Your Community

The Student Council is the heart of student life at IIT Ropar. It is a group of dedicated student leaders who work every day to make campus life better for everyone. When students step onto our campus, the council is there to make sure they feel welcome, supported, and heard. We proudly act as the main bridge between the student body and the college administration.

How the Council is Formed

Our council is built on fairness and teamwork. Every year, students choose their leaders through an open and democratic voting process. This ensures that the council truly reflects the diversity and choices of the student body.

Led by the Council President, the team includes representatives from different areas of campus life. Together, they take on the responsibility of guiding the student community with honesty, care, and a strong sense of duty.

Listening and Solving Problems

We believe that every single student’s opinion matters. The Student Council is always open and ready to listen to your ideas, concerns, and suggestions.

Finding Solutions:
Whether you are facing a challenge with academics, hostel life, or campus facilities, the council works hard to find the best possible answers.

Working with the College:
We regularly meet with teachers, staff, and the administration. By sharing your feedback with them, we turn your ideas into real improvements.

Protecting Rights:
We always stand up for student rights, ensuring that the campus rules are fair and that everyone is treated with respect.

Learning Beyond the Classroom

College is not just about passing exams; it is also about personal growth and discovering who you are. The council plays a massive role in making sure students develop well-rounded personalities. We do this by organizing a wide variety of activities throughout the year:

Workshops and Seminars:
We host special learning sessions with experts to help students build new skills and prepare for their future careers.

Campus Festivals:
The council helps manage exciting cultural and technical events. These give students a platform to show their talents, learn how to work in teams, and have fun.

Health and Wellness:
We also care about your well-being, supporting sports events and mental health initiatives to keep the campus healthy and active.

A Community Built for You

The guiding rule of our Student Council is simple: it is entirely "by the students, for the students, and of the students."

Ultimately, the Student Council is one of the most important parts of the IIT Ropar experience. We are here to amplify your voice and support your goals. By creating a safe, encouraging, and lively environment, we make sure that every student has the opportunity to thrive, succeed, and make lifelong memories.

AAROHAN
, the annual sports fest of IIT Ropar, is a three-day extravaganza that unites athletes and enthusiasts from the institute and neighbouring universities.
Beyond fierce competition, Aarohan fosters camaraderie and sportsmanship across a diverse range of sporting events, from football to cricket, basketball to volleyball, athletics to weightlifting and gym.
Participants showcase their skills while forging lasting bonds, making it more than just a competition but a celebration of passion and friendship.

IIT Ropar organises marathons from time to time, bringing the campus together in a celebration of fitness, endurance, and community spirit. Beyond these events, sports form an integral part of campus life. From early-morning practice sessions to evening matches echoing with cheers, students enthusiastically take to the fields, courts, and tracks. Supported by quality facilities and experienced coaching, they pursue excellence and recreation alike, creating a campus culture that is active, energetic, and deeply committed to well-being.

Then comes the Inter IIT Sports Meet (IISM), the crown jewel of the IIT sporting calendar. Every year, athletes from all 23 IITs converge across two or three host campuses, turning them into battlegrounds of grit, skill, and unyielding institute pride. Stadiums erupt with chants, last-minute winners spark wild celebrations, and every point is fiercely contested. For the students who don their institute colours, IISM is more than a tournament—it is a test of character, a showcase of excellence, and a stage where sporting memories are etched into IIT folklore.

The culture at IIT Ropar extends far beyond academics, creating an environment where students are encouraged to explore their passions, develop new skills, and build lifelong connections. The institute boasts a vibrant student community driven by a diverse range of clubs and societies that cater to interests in music, dance, drama, photography, fine arts, fashion, literature, debating, filmmaking, coding, robotics, entrepreneurship, and much more. Through these clubs, students regularly organize workshops, performances, competitions, exhibitions, and social initiatives, ensuring that campus life remains dynamic throughout the year.

The Board of Cultural Affairs (BOCA) serves as the heart of the institute's creative ecosystem, nurturing talent through clubs such as Alankar (Music), D'Cypher (Dance), Undekha (Dramatics), Arturo (Photography), Vibgyor (Fine Arts), Panache (Fashion), and Epicure (Culinary Arts). Alongside cultural activities, technical, literary, entrepreneurial, and social organizations provide countless opportunities for students to learn, lead, and innovate. Together, these clubs foster a spirit of creativity, collaboration, and excellence that defines the unique culture of IIT Ropar and culminates in flagship events such as ZEITGEIST, the institute's annual cultural festival.

ZEITGEIST
is the annual cultural fest of IIT Ropar, held every year around the end of October. Over the years, it has grown into one of the most anticipated college festivals in North India, bringing together students from across the country for three unforgettable days of celebration, creativity, and fun.

For every student at IIT Ropar, ZEITGEIST is much more than just a fest—it is an experience. The campus comes alive with excitement, music, laughter, and an energy that is hard to put into words. Students eagerly wait for these three days, which create memories that last a lifetime.

The festival attracts participants from numerous colleges and universities who come to compete, perform, and showcase their talents in a wide range of events. From the glamour of Lashkara, the fashion show, to the electrifying performances in War of Bands, the intensity and the excitement of Xuberence, ZEITGEIST offers something for everyone. Alongside these flagship events, the fest hosts numerous competitions, workshops, and activities that keep the campus buzzing throughout the celebration.

Over the years, ZEITGEIST has hosted an impressive lineup of artists and entertainers including
Diljit Dosanjh, Vishal–Shekhar, Mohit Chauhan, KR$NA, Anuv Jain, Sunanda Sharma, Hardy Sandhu, The Local Train, Zakir Khan, Samay Raina, Biswa Kalyan Rath, Anubhav Singh Bassi
, and many more, making it one of North India's most vibrant college festivals.

At its heart, ZEITGEIST is a celebration of youth, talent, and togetherness. It is a place where friendships are formed, talents are discovered, and thousands of students come together to create moments they will cherish long after the fest is over. Every year, ZEITGEIST continues to raise the bar, making it one of the most vibrant and memorable cultural festivals in the country.

MALHAR

MALHAR, our college’s beloved literary fest, is a vibrant three – day celebration that brings our community together through the joy of literature and creativity. The literature clubs of our college conducts various exciting events like challenging quizzes, poster making competitions, spirited debates, JAM, etc. where participants can showcase their knowledge, artistry and engage in lively discussions.

The key highlight of the fest is the
Book Fair
, which lasts for all three days of the fest and has books from such a wide range of genres, that there is something for everyone. Each day of Malhar ends on a high note with enchanting evening sessions – whether it’s a classical music performance, Sufi Night, heartfelt poetry recitals (Kaavya Sammelan), or an open mic night, these events provide a perfect mix of relaxation and inspiration, leaving everyone with cherished memories and a deeper appreciation for the arts.

STEPPING BEYOND CAMPUS

The Literary Board continues to foster a culture of expression, creativity and intellectual engagement. Several clubs under the board proudly represented our institute at prestigious competitions beyond campus walls. We participated heartily in Rendezvous (IIT DELHI) in JAM, APD (Asian Parliamentary Debate), MUN, etc, securing podium finishes, mentions and glorious achievements. Then came INTER IIT CULT MEET 8.0, in which all clubs participated with great zeal in their respective domains. Commendable participation was shown in similar events of IIT Roorkee and Hindu College, Delhi. All these helped students, especially freshers, get exposure to new ideas and talent. It contributed in their confidence and skill development, along with strengthening the college’s literary culture.

As we welcome new students to the institute, we hope they experience new friendships, lessons and stories for the upcoming years. We wish them to have more such opportunities, explore their potential, and contribute to the legacy of the Literary Board together.

REVANCHE
, is a two day adventure where you can expect to have the time of life!

With hundreds of teams and skilled players battling it out, on the fields of BGMI and COD, in the intense duels of Clash Royale and an offline FIFA competition hosted on state-of-the-art PC setups, you just might escape reality!
