, our annual technical fest is a 3 day journey of excitement and allure where you can explore your passion and potential in
technology
. It doesn’t matter if you’re a novice who’s only looking for a glimpse into something new or an expert who’s looking for an opportunity to leave their mark, Advitiya has a place for everyone!

Here’s a peek into what you’re in for:

Be it robotics, aeromodelling, automatives or coding, with your days filled with events such as
robo wars, derby racing, drone racing, exciting astro quizzes, workshops and talks,
which are strategically aligned with the present day needs, and nights filled with DJ along with a distinguished Star Night, Advitiya promises to be a getaway worth your time.

Read the blog
here.

At IIT Ropar, we believe in the culture of complete and holistic wellbeing for the student community. Driven by the vision of holistic health and emotional balance, the institute has a vibrant campus ecosystem committed to personal growth. With that in mind, the idea of an annual techno-wellness fest was conceived in 2024, appropriately named
‘Nirvana’
.

Nirvana (nirvāṇa)
is an indic word for freedom, liberation, and enlightenment. In its literal and philosophical sense, Nirvana represents liberation, the cessation of struggle, and the ultimate blowing out of the fires of stress and anxiety. By bringing thousands of students together to participate in expressive art therapy, mind gyms, mental health dialogues, and community bonding, the fest creates a shared environment of warmth and positivity.

In 2026, Nirvana attracted more than 5,000 students towards an event dedicated to the importance of wellbeing, featuring:

Overnight Hackathon:
Bridging the gap between technology and wellness, the fest gave space to individuals with interest in AI to express their knowledge for the betterment of society.

Mental Health Advocates:
Speakers like
Geeta Mehrotra, Avik Ghose, Mayuri Duggirala, Aarti Samani, and Ishan Shivanand
built an everlasting impact on the campus fraternity.

Gatekeeper Session:
Led by esteemed psychiatry experts from AIIMS Bathinda,
Dr. Jawahar Singh and Dr. Bharat Udey
, the session taught us about the identification of early signals of stress and depression and to offer genuine support to ourselves and our peers.

Wellness Pavilion:
Hosted an impressive array of our collaborators like
Axxnet, Arclabs, Yourdost
, as well as the
Indian Red Cross Society and Manashakti
.

Inspirational Stories:
Indian Army Kargil War veteran
Major D.P. Singh
and 3-time Commonwealth Games weightlifting medalist
Vikas Thakur
shared their impactful and ever motivating life stories, building a sense of mental resilience among individuals of all ages.

The main theme of the fest was
Carnival
, a picturesque event that included fun games ranging from sumo fight, to zorbing, to maze, and all other kinds of carnival activities.

It is evident that Nirvana will continue to include more in the upcoming years and have a longer impact on those who join us. It provides a rare space where everyday stress dissolves, self-awareness deepens, and thousands of individuals unite to build a kinder, healthier community.

E-SUMMIT
is the flagship annual entrepreneurship festival organized by the Entrepreneurship Cell (E-Cell) and TBIF, IIT Ropar. It is a two-day powerhouse of innovation, strategy, and startup culture that brings together founders, investors, industry leaders, and students under one roof.

At its core, the summit is built around a rich lineup of keynote sessions, panel discussions, an Investors Arena, and hands-on workshops, all designed to bridge the gap between ideas and execution. The
Startup Expo
takes center stage as a strategic platform where early-stage teams get to showcase their ventures at one of India's premier technical institutions, putting their vision in front of the people who matter most.

Past editions have welcomed remarkable speakers including
Ashneer Grover (former MD, BharatPe), Anubhav Dubey (Co-founder, Chai Sutta Bar), Dr. Munish Jindal (Founder, HoverRobotix), Akshay Singh (Founder & CEO, Evigway Technologies), and Lt. Gen. S S Mahal
— a testament to the summit's standing in India's entrepreneurial ecosystem.

Beyond the mainstage, E-Summit offers an electrifying slate of competitions catering to every kind of problem-solver and strategist:

Startup Sprint:
Pitching original business ideas.

Pitch 120:
Fast-paced solutions under pressure.

GTM Strategy War:
Go-to-market strategy challenges.

Consulting Case Competition:
Solving real-world business consulting problems.

Lok Sabha MUN:
Boardroom-style parliamentary debate.

Corporations Crisis Board:
High-stakes corporate crisis resolution simulation.

IPL Auction House:
Adrenaline-fueled bidding and squad management.

Beyond Transformers Hackathon:
AI-driven developmental hackathon.

And because innovation deserves a celebration, the summit wraps up with standout cultural events including standup comedy, dance performances, and pronites, making E-Summit as much a cultural experience as it is an entrepreneurial one. If you're building something, strategizing something, or simply hungry to be in the room where it happens — this is your summit.

IIT Ropar provides top-notch facilities in its hostels. The campus comprises several hostels allocated to students based on their academic year.
Brahmaputra, Chenab,
and
Sutlej
hostels are designated for undergraduate boys, while
Ravi
hostel is reserved for undergraduate girls. Each hostel is equipped with state-of-the-art amenities, including:

A fully furnished
Gym
with proper machinery.

Table Tennis
and a
Badminton
court to encourage physical activity.

Laundry
and iron services to meet the basic needs of the students.

Four
Elevators
for easy access to different floors.

Television in the
Common Rooms
of all hostels for entertainment.

Round-the-clock
Security
with stationed guards and safety equipment.

24/7 water and power supply, with backup generators for emergencies.

To cater to the needs of students,
BOHA (Board of Hostel Affairs)
, comprised of students, is formed. This council assigns hostel representatives to tackle any concerns students encounter during their residency.
Furthermore, BOHA arranges diverse cultural events and contests during festivities such as Garba, Ganesh Chaturthi, and Baisakhi, alongside fostering informal gatherings and recreational activities among students on weekends.
Moreover, the board oversees hostel decorations during significant celebrations like Diwali.

The campus also features
three fully air-conditioned common messes
for both boys and girls. To ensure food quality, the Board of Hostel Affairs appoints mess representatives to handle student complaints and make menu changes if necessary.

The
Utility Block
in the Residential Area has the following facilities:

A General Store:
Welcome to your ultimate one-stop shop for everything you didn't know you needed! Whether you are hunting down last-minute party essentials, looking for essential garments and gadgets, or just craving a midnight snack to fuel an all-nighter, we’ve got you covered. Open from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM, we are always ready to fulfill your daily needs with a smile.

Stationery Shop:
Welcome to the Stationery Sanctuary! Need a high-end calculator for quantum physics or a precise ruler for intricate circuit diagrams? From basic pencils to advanced protractors, we are open from dawn till dusk (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM) to fuel your academic adventures. Just remember: we can’t provide the solutions to your toughest engineering problems—only the paper to write them down!

A Salon:
Step into the ultimate zone where bad hair days meet their doom. Featuring stylists with skills sharper than a freshly shaved pencil, this joint gives your locks the VIP treatment they deserve. Whether you are hitting the books or partying harder, we will make sure your hair is as flawless as your algorithms. Open from 8:00 AM until the last early birds stop chirping!

SBI IIT Ropar Branch & ATM:
Banking made effortless. The State Bank of India campus branch and ATM provide seamless, reliable, and highly efficient financial services tailored for students, faculty, and staff. Featuring extended operational hours, it ensures that your on-campus transactions are always smooth, secure, and customer-friendly.

Post Office:
Your campus connection to the outside world. The IIT Post Office handles all your essential mailing needs with absolute ease, from dispatching urgent letters to receiving heavy parcels. It offers students and staff convenient, hassle-free access to vital postal logistics without ever needing to step off campus.

Cafes:

Dubey Cafe:
Need a late-night snack, fresh fruit fix, or a dairy delight? We’ve got you covered, even when the clock strikes 3 AM. Whether you're cramming for exams or just hungry after a midnight adventure, swing by for a quick bite and a cozy chat.

Maggie Hotspot:
Craving midnight munchies? Head to Maggie Hotspot, the campus night café! Open till 2 am, it serves Maggie, iced tea, burgers, and sandwiches—your go-to for late-night bites.

Coffee Day:
Craving a sweet escape? This bakery and coffee haven in campus serves up pastries, ice cream, snacks, and coffee to fuel your study marathons. Perfect spot for a quick, tasty break!

Students Activity Centre:
Step into our vibrant Student Activity Centre at IIT! Explore diverse club rooms buzzing with creativity, from tech enthusiasts to art aficionados, where passions meet possibilities.

This includes:

Alankar Club Room

BOST Room

Arturo Room

Vibgyor Room

Welcome to the ultimate destination where hunger meets happiness! Life at IIT Ropar is not just about lectures, assignments, and deadlines—it is also about discovering your favorite food spot and creating memories with friends over snacks and late-night cravings. The campus food outlets provide students with a wide variety of options, ranging from refreshing beverages and healthy juices to fast food and comforting meals. Whether you are looking for a quick bite between classes, a caffeine boost before an exam, or simply a place to relax and socialize, these outlets become an important part of everyday campus life.

Maggie Hotspot:
Late-night cravings? Maggie Hotspot is here to save the day! A favorite among students, this spot becomes especially lively during study sessions, assignment deadlines, and evening hangouts. From comforting Maggi variations to quick snacks and refreshments, it serves as a go-to destination whenever students need a fast and satisfying bite.

Farmer's Cafeteria:
Looking for a proper meal instead of just snacks? Farmer's Cafeteria provides students with a variety of meal options and serves as a convenient place for enjoying filling and wholesome food on campus. Whether it is a quick lunch, dinner with friends, or simply a break from routine meals, this cafeteria offers students a comfortable dining experience and a place to relax.

Bake-O-Mocha:
Looking for a café experience right inside the campus? Bake-O-Mocha is more than just a refreshment spot—it provides students with a proper café-like environment where they can relax, enjoy good food, and spend quality time with friends. With a wide variety of food and beverage options available, it caters to different tastes and preferences of students. Whether you are taking a break between classes, catching up with friends, or looking for a comfortable place to sit and unwind after a busy day, Bake-O-Mocha offers a welcoming atmosphere that makes it one of the enjoyable hangout spots on campus.

Amul Outlet:
The Amul outlet is a useful and popular addition to campus life, providing students with a mix of refreshments and quick food options. It becomes especially helpful for students looking for something light and convenient during the day. Whether someone wants a short snack break or a quick meal option, the outlet provides a practical and easily accessible choice.

Verka Outlet:
Verka serves as another refreshing corner within the campus, offering students a simple and convenient option during busy days. It is often visited by students who are looking for refreshing products and quick alternatives while moving between classes, hostels, and other campus activities.

Kerala Canteen:
Kerala Canteen brings diversity to the campus food culture by providing students with a different culinary experience. Known for its satisfying meals and distinctive flavors, it gives students an alternative to their daily routine and adds variety to food choices available on campus.

Burger House:
Burger House is a lively food destination that attracts students looking for enjoyable meals and a change from their regular routine. The place is often filled with students spending time together, making it not just a food outlet but also a social space where conversations and campus memories are created.

Desi Urban Chai:
Desi Urban Chai has become a familiar part of campus life and serves as a place where students often gather outside academic settings. It creates an environment suitable for casual conversations, short breaks, and interactions among friends, making it more than just a refreshment point.

Sohail Juice Corner:
Sohail Juice serves as a refreshing stop for students throughout the day. It offers students a place to recharge and enjoy refreshing beverages while taking a break from lectures, assignments, and other activities. It remains a popular option, especially during warm weather and busy schedules.

title: BOST | ISMP'26 IIT Ropar
text:
BOARD OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY (BOST)

Technical

Sports

Cultural

Literary


iota Cluster

club.iotacluster@iitrpr.ac.in

iota Cluster is the official Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning club at IIT Ropar, comprising a community of developers and researchers committed to exploring the true depth of AI beyond the hype. Our mission is to foster a practical, project-driven learning environment where students tackle complex problems, from core data science to advanced deep learning architectures. Through hands on workshops, rigorous hackathons, and peer-to-peer mentorship, we ensure that every member can develop strong technical fundamentals regardless of their starting point. We prioritize originality and practical execution, equipping students with the skills and collaborative network necessary to build technically meaningful projects that leave a lasting impact.

Aeromodelling club

aeromodelling@iitrpr.ac.in

The Aeromodelling Club is a dynamic hub for aviation enthusiasts and tech hobbyists passionate about the art and science of flight. It offers a hands-on platform where members design, build, and fly various airborne vehicles, ranging from traditional balsa wood gliders and remote-controlled (RC) planes to advanced drones and quadcopters. Combining principles of aerodynamics, structural engineering, and electronics, the club bridges the gap between theoretical physics and real-world mechanical creation. Beyond technical skill-building, it fosters a collaborative environment for teamwork, precision engineering, and competitive spirit, making it the perfect launchpad for anyone looking to command the skies.

Automotive club

automotiveclub@iitrpr.ac.in

The Automotive Club IIT Ropar brings together students through a wide range of technical and non-technical activities, including workshops, competitions, industry interactions, guest lectures, and automotive events, One of the Biggest event of Advitiya - Full Throttle . By promoting hands-on learning, teamwork, and innovation, the club serves as a platform for students to explore and contribute to the evolving world of automobiles and mobility.

CIM

cimclub@iitrpr.ac.in

The Computer Integrated Manufacturing (CIM) Club serves as a platform for students to explore the intersection of CAD (Computer Aided Design), Simulations, CAM (Computer Aided Manufacturing), and combining Automation and AI with CIM. We aim to provide technical training with hands-on projects, helping them get ready for Industry 4.0.

Coding club

codingclub@iitrpr.ac.in

The Coding Club at IIT Ropar serves as the epicenter of competitive programming on campus, driving a rigorous culture of algorithmic problem-solving and mathematical thinking. The club fosters a collaborative environment where seniors actively mentor junior members, cultivating top-tier talent through intense problem-solving sessions, regular campus contests, and deep dives into advanced Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA). This relentless focus not only helps members rapidly scale the ranks on platforms like Codeforces, but it also builds the elite, optimized problem-solving foundation necessary to excel in prestigious global tournaments like the ICPC and tackle the high-stakes technical interviews required by top-tier software and quantitative finance firms.

FinCOM

fincom@iitrpr.ac.in

FINCOM - The Finance and Economics Club is the official Finance and Consulting community of IIT ROPAR focused on fostering interest in finance, product management, Consulting, Data-Science and Quantitative Analysis through sessions, competitions, hackathons,workshops and Guest Talks. Let's learn,build and grow together.

Monochrome

monochromeclub@iitrpr.ac.in

Monochrome is the official designing club under the Board of Science and Technology (BOST) at IIT Ropar. The club serves as a platform for students to explore graphic design, branding, photo manipulation, and digital content creation. Through workshops, design labs, competitions, and real-world projects, Monochrome helps beginners and enthusiasts develop skills in tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, and Canva. The club actively contributes to the visual identity of major institute events and fosters a community where creativity, innovation, and design thinking thrive.

Robotics club

robotics@iitrpr.ac.in

The Robotics Club, IIT Ropar, brings together passionate students interested in engineering, technology, and innovation. Through hands-on projects, competitions, workshops, and collaborative research, we provide a platform to explore cutting-edge robotics and intelligent systems.

SoftCOM

softcom@iitrpr.ac.in

SoftCom is the official software community of IIT Ropar, serving as a dynamic hub where passionate developers unite to innovate, collaborate, and master modern technology. By bridging the gap between theoretical concepts and real-world implementation, the club fosters hands-on development across diverse domains, including web and application development, game design, cybersecurity, and blockchain tech. Whether through building scalable applications, securing digital systems, exploring decentralized networks, or hosting hackathons, SoftCom provides an ecosystem for students to transform their ideas into impactful code.

Zenith (Astrophysics and Space Tech Club)

zenithclub@iitrpr.ac.in

Zenith – The Astrophysics and Space Tech Club is a community of students united by a passion for exploring the cosmos and pushing the boundaries of space exploration and innovation. Whether you're intrigued by black holes, fascinated by rockets, eager to analyze astronomical data, or excited to capture the night sky through telescopes, Zenith offers something for everyone. Our activities span four major domains—Astrophysics, Model Rocketry, Machine Learning & Data Analysis, and Telescope & Astrophotography—providing opportunities to learn, build, observe, and innovate. Through hands-on projects, stargazing sessions, competitions, and interactions with experts, we foster curiosity, creativity, and a spirit of exploration. No prior experience is required—just a willingness to learn and a desire to reach for the stars.

ESportZ Club

sa.esportz@iitrpr.ac.in

ESportZ Club, IIT Ropar is the official gaming and esports community of IIT Ropar, bringing together passionate gamers through tournaments, events, live streams, and interactive sessions. From casual gaming to competitive esports, we foster teamwork, skill development, and a thriving gaming culture on campus.

title: FAQs | ISMP'26 IIT Ropar
text:
How can we help you?

You can also browse the topics below to find what you are looking for.

FAQS

Hostel Life

Infrastructure and Extra-Curricular


Medical & Health

Hostel Life

How are hostels allotted to freshmen? Does my hostel change every year? How many students live in a room?

Allotment of hostels is done while keeping in mind the required interaction among the freshers. Room allotment is completely random. The first and second year ug students are accommodated in rooms of two and also Third year and possibly Fourth year ug students will also have rooms of two. There are four hostels for boys Chenab, Satluj, Beas and Brahmaputra Boys and two for girls Raavi and Brahmaputra Girls. There is a separate Air-Conditioned mess, where all students can dine simultaneously.

I have never lived in a hostel before. What should I expect from IIT hostels?

Hostel life is going to be very different from your home. In the beginning you may feel the need of a larger room where a smaller number of students live, but at the end of your stay, you would be crying to stay back. You are going to cherish your hostel memories for the rest of your life. Apart from academics and co-curricular activities, hostel life plays a major role in shaping one's life. Away from parents and siblings, hostel life has a lot to offer. It inculcates in you, a bit of sincerity, a shred of responsibility, and a great sense of adjustment. Living in a hostel shapes your personality and teaches you time management. You could expect a nice hostel life here as the hostels are newly constructed and are filled with a number of facilities required that you will never forget.

What facilities are available in the hostel?

The facilities available in the hostels of the institute are as follows:

1. Laundry service (paid - nominal rates)

2. 24-hour electricity backup

3. Common room (TV room which is no less than a theatre during cricket and football finals)

4. RO filtered water

5. Open terrace

6. Gallery for better ventilation

7. Bathroom equipped with geysers

8. Individual almirahs

9. Room cleaning service

10. Wi-Fi zone and high speed LAN port (unlimited data download) is available in each room which also enables intra-hostel data sharing.

In case of any problem, the caretaker is always approachable (Office timings). There will be a student hostel representative for each hostel to listen to your problems and present them to the hostel committee.

Visit
this
blog for more details.

What about the mess food? Is the food tasty and healthy? Do we have a say in the menu?

There are 2 common air-conditioned messes for the students. Mess fees are included in the hostel fee and are to be paid every semester. Quite honestly, it would be an overstatement to say that mess food is tasty when you would be coming here after eating home-cooked food for almost 18 years of your life. However, it is hygienic, nutritious, satisfying, and already paid for.

A weekly menu is decided at periodic intervals and is usually fine. Every resident has a say in deciding the weekly mess menu through the complaints and suggestion forms provided from time to time by the mess committee, which itself is a body made up of students. Also, there is a complaint register available in the mess in case you find the quality of food degraded or have any other complaint regarding the food. Feedback is always welcomed. For immediate actions, you can also contact the mess representatives.

Is there any ragging at IIT Ropar? What if some senior approaches us?

IIT Ropar has a zero-tolerance policy. We do not accept ragging in any form. In case of any uncomfortable situation arising, please inform us. It is to be noted, however, that seniors might approach you and interact with you asking you simple questions regarding your branch, hometown, personal interests, hobbies, etc. If at any point of the interaction, you feel uncomfortable, you must let him/her know and be rest assured that he/she will leave you alone. In case he/she doesn't, you can always contact the authorities.

What about cleanliness in hostels?

Your rooms, washrooms, and bathrooms are cleaned daily by the sweepers. However, to maintain cleanliness is your responsibility. In case of improper functionality, you can contact the caretaker or the Hostel Representative of your hostel.

What about the weather in Ropar?

You could enjoy and feel every weather to a great amount in Ropar (especially, if you are coming from places like Gujarat, Hyderabad, etc. you will feel as if the weather is at its extreme here). Weather at Ropar is hot and humid in summers extending till the end of July. You are suggested to keep a handkerchief/napkin with you. Monsoon is pretty pleasant, starting from August to mid-September. Winter starts from October and extends till the first week of February, with temperature as low as 5-6 degrees. You are advised to get warm winter clothing during December and January.

What about security and medical facilities?

Security guards guard your hostel as well as campus all the time. Though, remember to lock your almirahs and room for proper security of your personal belongings.

A Medical centre is present in the Utility Block. A doctor and a nurse are always present to treat any medical emergency at any point in time. College ambulance is also available 24*7 at the service. In case of serious problems, free tests are also done in some of the Ropar hospitals and laboratories on proper recommendation by the doctor on the campus.

Where should I dry my washed clothes?

Hostels are equipped with common washing machines, along with a laundry person, which takes a nominal price. All hostels have space to dry clothes in direct sunlight. For ground floors, there are clotheslines to dry the clothes, whereas for upper floors, a gallery is sufficient.

What to do after reaching college?

After you reach the college, you need to register yourself first, for college as well as for hostels.

Hostels are well equipped with LAN and WiFi. LAN and WiFi usage don't require registration.

Register yourself with the library as soon as possible, as it will be the sole source for your initial study. This registration will issue you the institute ID Card.

Get your bonafide certificates on the first or very next day as it will help you to get a new mobile connection and a bank account at the IIT Ropar branch of SBI.

Get yourself an account at SBI branch IIT Ropar asap, as it will be the only account you can handle and easy access from the campus for your stay on campus.

After that, ISMP waits for you. Different clubs organize different activities to make you familiar with their clubs and to know your interests.

What are the documents required at the time of registration?

The following ORIGINAL documents are preferred with at least 2 attested photocopies:

1. Class X certificate and marksheet

2. Class XII certificate and marksheet

3. If your DOB is not mentioned in Class X certificate, then bring a proof of DOB

4. Caste Certificate (if applicable)

5. JEE Branch and institute allotment letter, admit card

6. 10 passport-sized coloured photos (though you must carry more, that you'll need around the year)

7. 5 stamp-sized coloured photos.

8. Receipt of payment with JEE and Hostel Fee Challan.

9. Medical Certificate (attested by a registered medical officer)

10. If applicable, bring an affidavit for the gap of study

11. If applying for a scholarship, bring an affidavit/certificate of income of parents duly attested by first class magistrate/Tehsildar/Revenue Officer. If parents are govt. employees submit copies of IT Returns from their employers also.

Note: Please read the instructions carefully on www.iitrpr.ac.in for latest updates regarding documents.

How to reach IIT Ropar? What is the location of IIT Ropar?

One can reach IIT Ropar by different means.

By Road:
One can travel by road on his own vehicle. The roads are quite well maintained.

By Air:
The nearest airport is in Chandigarh, about 48 kilometres from Rupnagar. Any interested visitor wishing to come to Rupnagar/Ropar could take a flight from his/her respective place to Chandigarh (if a direct flight to Chandigarh is not available then a flight from Delhi to Chandigarh). There are regular running flights from the capital to Chandigarh. Further, one can take a taxi or a bus from Chandigarh Airport, which would take about 2 hours on the higher side to reach the Main Campus of Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar).

By Train:
Train is one of the cheapest and comfortable means to travel. Regular trains are plying between Delhi and Rupnagar. The Delhi-Ambala-Una railway line passes through Rupnagar. The duration of the journey is around 6 hours from Delhi. Anyone wishing to visit the campus may also take a train from his/her place to Ambala or Chandigarh, and then a taxi ride or one can board a bus to the IIT Ropar Transit Campus, It just takes around 1-1.5 hours. From the Transit Campus, regular buses are available for IIT Ropar Main Campus.

Daily trains between Delhi and Roopnagar(ROPAR):

1. Delhi To Ropar: Jan Shatabdi (12057); Himachal Express (14553)

2. Ropar to Delhi: Jan Shatabdi (12058); Himachal Express (14554)

From all over India, there are multiple trains to Chandigarh (56 km from IIT Ropar) and Ambala (80 km from IIT Ropar). Ropar railway station is around 8 km from IIT Ropar campus. There will be a campus bus available on railways station to IIT Ropar from time to time.

By Bus:

From Delhi: All buses going towards Mandi, Manali, Nangal, Una, Anandpur Sahib go via Ropar.

From Chandigarh: In addition to Mandi, Manali, Una buses, all buses going towards Amritsar, Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur go via Ropar.

Ropar bus stand is around 7 km from IIT Ropar. It is better to get off at the old bus stand of Ropar as it is slightly nearer. From there, one can go for a cycle-rickshaw or auto are easily available.

Hoping to see you soon :) !!!!

Maps and addresses are also available in the '
' section.

What are the necessary things that I should buy?

Some of the things that you should buy either from utility block or your hometown are:

Scientific Calculator
- fx 991 ES (preferably) or Fx 991-MS. You will need this more than your books for the next four years (right from your first semester). So, it is better to buy it from home.

A well-conditioned medium-size college bag.
A bag to carry books, notebooks, and a laptop.

Lab Coats:
A blue lab coat is required for Mechanical Workshop and a white one is required for Chemistry Lab. They are available in Utility Block, or you can borrow from your seniors.

Drafter:
A drafter is also needed for Engineering Drawing Subject.

But no special need of buying daily stuff like a bucket, mug, and mattresses from home as they will be available to buy inside the campus on the day of registration.

Some locks and keys as you will have to lock your luggage on the first day as it will be very busy. After that, it will be ok.

Are there any guidelines for mentors? Am I safe with them?

Following is the Mentoring Code of Conduct. So you are most safe with them.

Aim:

The code of conduct is designed to establish a set of guidelines to create a benchmark for ethics and good practice and ensure that mentors conduct their practice in a professional yet friendly and ethical manner. The code is also meant to inform mentees and to promote public confidence in the Institute Student Mentorship Program (ISMP) as a process for personal and professional development.

Code of Conduct:

1. Commit to the relationship and the ISMP for one full academic year.

2. Attend and actively participate in all mentoring training and special events, and in the long run, suggest and execute any idea relevant to the ISMP.

3. Trust and confidentiality are the backbones of successfully mentoring and must be maintained at all times. Be careful about sensitive issues. A mentee's personal life may be difficult to discuss early in the relationship.

4. Should abide by all rules set up by the Proctorial Committee during the initial interaction and period. All meetings with freshers should happen in open and visible regions and not in any closed rooms.

5. No illegal drugs/alcohol/tobacco should be promoted or consumed within the mentorship activities/meetings.

6. Never use physical discipline/abusive language/ultimatums as a tool for putting your point across. Any instance of ragging during mentorship activities is strictly forbidden and will be reported to concerned authorities.

7. Failure to comply or an outright violation of any of the above may lead to termination from the ISMP for all purposes.

At the time of registration, are my parents allowed to stay with me in the hostel?

Parents are allowed only till the common room and not further. You need to book hotels for their stay.

What are the places near IIT Ropar to travel?

Visit
this
blog.

Can I choose my roommate?

A roommate is initially alloted on the basis of “chit-system” but can be changed next year on mutual agreement.

What furniture is provided in the room?

Freshers are provided with two single beds, two study table and chair pairs and two almirahs.

What items are prohibited inside the hostel?

Use of electronics like electric kettle, inductions, iron, heaters etc isn’t allowed.

Should I bring my own mattress, pillow, and bedsheets?

Yes, the college doesn’t provide mattresses,pillows or bedsheets but they are easily available in the utility block and can be purchased from there.

What facilities are available in the Hostel?

1. Laundry Service
2. Washing machines if the students wish to wash their clothes themselves.
3. 24-hour electricity backup
4. Common Room that has theatres,couches and bean bags
5. RO Filtered Water
6. Open Terrace
7. Geysers in washrooms
8. Room Cleaning Service
9. Games like Table Tennis, foosball, Badminton Courts in some hostels
10. Wi-Fi zone and high speed LAN Port in each room.
11. Gym
12. Vending Machines

Is there a curfew for freshers?

Only for the first month of college, freshers aren’t permitted to go out after 11 pm. Otherwise, no curfew.

Is there a hostel warden available at all times?

Hostel warden is usually a professor from some branch. He/she isn’t physically present in the hostel at all times and visits the hostels periodically. However, students are provided with their contact numbers.

What should I do if electrical or plumbing problems occur?

A QR code is pasted in the hostel. You can scan it and submit your complaints, which will be looked after shortly.

What are the unwritten rules of hostel life?

No unwritten rules, just treat the hostel as your home- interact nicely with fellow hostellers, maintain cleanliness and help others!

Are there hostel competitions and cultural events?

Yes, general championship is organised every year where different hostels compete in fields like tech, culture etc

Infrastructure and Extra-Curricular

What about college library?

There is a 24*7 college library available to the students. The institute library has wide range of texts of the latest publications. It also has renowned journals and magazines. Apart from books of academic interest, there are several titles of general interest genre such as biographies, popular science, fiction etc. The library provides LAN and Wi-Fi for access to online information. It also has an online catalogue named OPAC. Through this you can search for, and reserve books from your room, without even coming to the library. Moreover to ensure that the students study peacefully and comfortably the library houses spacious air-conditioned cabins with charging connections and internet services available along with many more study tables for students.

I like playing sports. What are the sporting facilities available at IIT Ropar?

Sports is a major part of a student's life. Sports are a really important mode of recreation for all students. It is encouraged to play at least one sport. Sporting facilities that are made available are:

1. Lawn Tennis courts

2. Cricket ground

3. Volleyball courts

4. Football ground

5. Ground for athletic events

6. Badminton courts(Badminton courts are outdoor cement courts)

7. Hockey ground

8. Table Tennis tables

9. Basketball courts

10. Chess boards (in each hostel)

Moreover, college provides a certain number of sporting instruments too. However, it is advised to the students to get their own sports instruments. In case you need anything you can always contact the Sports Secretary or the respective sport representative.

Coaches are also available to train you for learning the sport as well as for performing better in Inter-IIT Sports Meet.

Is there any auditorium in the college?

There is a large hall in RadhaKrishnan Complex. It is large enough to hold all the students and is used for organizing all the extra- curricular events in the college including the research conclave, fresher's night, guest talks and other socio-cultural events.

DJ Nights and Star Nights of fests are organized in open grounds, which adds on a natural flavor to events.

The main auditorium is under construction and expected to be ready soon.

What about the classrooms and laboratories in the college?

The campus consists of air-conditioned classrooms in Lecture Hall Complex, with a seating capacity of more than 150. The classrooms are spacious with comfortable seats for the students to study comfortably. In addition, there are different lecture rooms dedicated to each department.

Practical approach is the key to learning which is encouraged. It is ensured that students get accustomed to the laboratory atmosphere before starting the experiment and know well in advance about all the safety measures which have to be taken care of in the laboratory. Laboratories like Physics, Chemistry, Computer and Design & Manufacturing etc. are made available with well- equipped and advanced machinery. It is made sure that students are well instructed before starting any working session.

I like dancing/music/working out. Are these facilities available?

There are individual clubs for them. There is a music room which is well equipped with acoustic guitars, bass guitars, tablas, drums set, congas, mics, amplifiers, etc. is located in Utility Block. Jamming sessions are also organized on weekends and they provide a soothing experience.

Under Dance Club, bhangra and western dance are the main sub categories. Several workshops are held from time to time for practice and exploration.

For all those who like working out, there is a well-equipped gymnasium in Sutlej Hostel which remains open from 6am to 8:30 am in morning and 5:30 pm to 9pm in evening. You can contact the respective club representatives anytime if you need any help regarding the above mentioned activities.

Like old IITs, is any cultural fest organized in IIT Ropar?

Yes, IIT Ropar organises its 3 day long Cultural fest, the ZEITGEIST annually. Various cultural events, star nights, competitions are held during Zeitgeist. Numerous celebrities like Mohit Chauhan, Vishal-Shekhar, Hawas Group, Gajendra Verma, Sharry Mann, Ranjit Bawa, Diljeet Singh Dosanjh, DJ Olly, Zakir Khan, SITAR Metal Band and Zephyrtone have graced the stage of ZEITGEIST. It's a never before experience. It is one of the biggest stages that IIT Ropar provides you to showcase your talent. It's a treat to see such magic unfold against your eyes. It becomes an experience of lifetime for you.

To know more about Zeitgeist, read the blog
here
.

Do IIT Ropar organise sports or technical fests of their own?

IIT Ropar organizes both the sports fest, Aarohan and the technical fest, Advitya which are just amazing and adds a lot to the college memories of yours.

BOSA organizes AAROHAN, the annual sports fest of IIT Ropar where students from various prestigious colleges come to IIT Ropar and participate in various sports to compete for the gold.

IIT Ropar held the eighth edition of its annual technical Fest Advitiya, in 2024. Advitiya 2024 had the scientific spirits soaring and the technological temper ablaze. The events, workshops and talks organized at Advitiya are strategically aligned with the present day needs and offers a takeaway of fun and knowledge.

Various events, DJ nights and comedy shows are organized. All clubs take part actively in organizing their events, as well as in participating in their own events.

Read the blog for Advitiya
here.

Read the blog for Aarohan
here.

Are there any inter college events in IIT?

Every year, Inter IIT Meets are organized, in which teams from various IITs participate and showcase their talent.

Technical, Sports and Cultural Meets are organized so that you can participate in the field you like. Moreover, due to less strength of students in IIT Ropar, there is a greater probability that you can get a chance to participate in it in the first year itself :).

Which are the various clubs/societies working in the college?

Following is the list of boards and the clubs under them :

BOARD OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY(BOST)

1. Aeromodelling Club

2. Automotive Club

3. CIM

4. Coding Club

5. Esportz Club

6. FinCOM

7. Iota Cluster

8. Monochrome

9. Robotics

10. Softcom

11. Zenith

BOARD OF LITERARY AFFAIRS(BOLA)

1. Alfaaz

2. Alpha

3. Debsoc

4. Enarators

5. Enigma

6. Filmski

7. MUN Club

BOARD OF CULTURAL ACTIVITIES(BOCA)

1. Epicure

2. Vibgyor

3. Alankar

4. Undekha

5. Arturo

6. Dcypher

7. Panache

BOARD OF SPORTS ACTIVITIES(BOSA)

1. Aquatics

2. Athletics

3. Badminton

4. Basketball

5. Chess

6. Cricket

7. Football

8. Hockey

9. Lawn Tennis

10. Table Tennis

11. Volleyball

12. Weightlifting

Apart from these clubs we have other organisations that are very much active in their working like SME (Society of Mechanical Engineers), Enactus, Pehchaan-Ek Safar, and BloodConnect. In the first week of the academic year, the representatives will conduct an orientation programme telling the freshers about the different clubs/organisations and their activities. The doors of these clubs are always open for all. You all have worked hard for the past two years, this is your opportunity, seize it.

Links to pages of these clubs are provided in the footer of the website (Quick Links).

What if I become a victim of depression and feel homesick?

Well, when you stay away from your home it's natural for you to feel homesick. It will take some time for you to adapt to a â€˜IIT lifestyleâ€™. Whenever you face depression, you can consult the Counselling Centre located at Utility Block of the college. Confidentiality is strictly maintained. Also, spending some time with your friends would help you cope up with depression. Feel free to approach seniors, as they have already gone through such a phase and can give you good advice.

I have an interest in participating in events that take place in different colleges. How do I go about it?

IIT Ropar actively participates in the events that take place in other colleges be it cultural, technical or sports. The college encourages its students to participate. The college even provides funds to the students participating if the student has prior permissions from the required representative.

I am a shy guy. How do I improve my social skills?

The college hosts a variety of events/fests throughout the session and these are fully organised and volunteered by students of IIT Ropar and participation in these events can help improve social skills. Some of them are :-

Aarohan
is our annual Sports fest through which students display their talent in sports field.

Zeitgeist
is our annual Cultural fest which helps in nurturing the talent in all the students..

Advitiya
is our annual intra-college technical fest that aims at improving the technical skills of the students and encourages innovative and lateral thinking.

Inter Year Sports Championship(IYSC)
is also held every year in which students from different year compete against each other and showcase their skills.

Above all,
GC (General Championship)
is being organised starting from this year itself just like all the old IITs and comprises events from all the domains mentioned above.

Is there any counselling cell in IIT Ropar?

This institute has a lot to offer for its students, in terms of academics, co-curricular and extracurricular opportunities. With the increased opportunities, often come related problems like stress, anxiety or depression. On face value, these problems might seem trivial, but they end up affecting us in a negative manner. Hence, one should reach out for help.

IIT Ropar houses a great counselling cell consisting of excellent counsellors. The details about IIT Ropar's Counselling cell can be found
here.
.

If I want to make robots, cars and quadcopters, where should I go?

The clubs like Aeromodelling Club, Robotics Club and Automotive Club provide you these types of opportunities. Various events (inside and outside the college) are organised in which these activities are carried out in the form of teams. Appropriate financial support is also provided if proper proposals are presented in advance.

There is a mechanical workshop, in which various tools and machines (including 3D Printer, Lathes, CNC etc.) are available. With prior permission, these are made available for making projects.

I like coding, but don't have laptop? Will it affect my coding?

Certainly not. Well equipped computer labs are present in the CSE Block with Ubuntu Operating System. Coding club is also there to teach you and help you progress. Competitions are also held in Advitiya (Technical Fest) for competitive programming.

I like to watch movies. Is there any theatre in the college?

Movie Screening Club is an active club, which streams 1-2 movies per month. They are shown in lecture hall-cum auditorium (M6) present in LHC. For new releases, you can always go to malls like Elante Mall, Chandigarh or VR Punjab which are at a distance of almost 1-2.5 hours travel.

I like photography. What are the facilities?

Arturo Club (Photography Club of IIT Ropar) captures all events that are organised in college. For photography enthusiasts, it is the appropriate club. Various sessions are also conducted in which students are taught how to operate DSLR, photography techniques and the use of editing softwares.

What are fests?

Fest is a time when you can relax yourself from the academics. You can participate in events and competitions that are held in it, which helps you to learn teamwork. Along with that, you can organise events. Managing an event will definitely bolster your confidence. Star Nights, DJ Nights and Comedy Shows are times when you can let go all your worries and create some amazing memories.

How are the computing and internet/wifi facilities at the institute?

The institute is equipped with a 24 hour general computer lab facility with all the standard softwares. The campus provides super fast internet facilities in hostels and academic area. LAN and wifi are available in each room of hostels.

What is ISMP?

Visit
this
blog.

Are bicycles allowed or recommended?

Yes ,students are permitted to use bicycles. Dedicated stands have also been installed in front of the hostels.

What clubs and societies can hostel residents join?

Students are allowed to join any club they want to. Regular club sessions are organised by the clubs.


How is evaluation and grading done?

Evaluation in each semester comprises a mid semester and an end semester exam, along with quizzes, practicals etc. depending on the course and the course coordinator.

Grading Scheme-

Each subject has some credits, and the grade is assigned on the basis of the performance either relative or absolute as decided by the course coordinator. The various grades that can be assigned are:

Eg.
If a student has three courses in a semester say sub1(4 credit course),sub2(3 credit course) and sub3(4 credit course) with grade B, B-, A- respectively, then the semester grade point will be (4*8 + 3*7 + 4*9)/(4+3+4) = 8.09

What all courses will I be taught in the first year?

In the first year, it is aimed that students should be given an introduction to most of the core branches. So we have

1. Introduction to computing

2. Principles of electrical engineering

3. Physics

4. Chemistry

5. Mathematics (Calculus and Linear Algebra)

6. Various labs including Mechanical Workshop and Engineering Drawing

7. English

8. Other courses that may help in upcoming semesters

This scheme is designed to aid you in having an overview of other branches. This is done as all branches of engineering are somehow interdependent and in todayâ€™s era one needs to link them to scale heights in their field. Also this will help you freshers to choose wisely at the end of first year whether to change your branch based upon your CGPA or not.

What is the procedure of grading?

Grading is primarily done in two ways:

1.
Relative Grading:
Your grade is governed by the overall class performance, that is the highest marks, class average, standard deviation, etc. The range of marks for a grade varies accordingly.

2.
Absolute Grading:
As the name suggests, your grade won't depend on the overall class performance. The range of marks for a particular grade is fixed.

What is the difference between CGPA and SGPA?

SGPA stands for Semester Grade Point Average whereas CGPA is the Cumulative Grade Point Average. The credit weighted average of all the courses in a particular semester gives the SGPA whereas CGPA = total credit average of SGPA of all semesters.

Are there any scholarships or fee concession programs we can apply for?

The institute offers Merit-cum-Means scholarship to about 25% of the students. The recipients of the scholarship are exempted from paying the tuition fee and get a scholarship of Rs.1000/- per month. The criteria for the same are based on the ALL INDIA RANK (AIR) in the JEE and financial background (only those students are eligible, whose parental income is below Rs.4.5 lac per annum). Further as per IIT rules, there is a limit that the total scholarship received from all sources for a student should not exceed Rs.50,000/- per annum. IIT Ropar also provides Institute Free Studentship to 10% of the students on the basis of financial background only. The recipients of the free studentship are exempted from paying the tuition fee. The criterion of 10% free studentship is similar to that of MCM Scholarship. Also all SC and ST category students are given full tuition fee waiver irrespective of their parent's / guardian's income. Besides these, the institute also offers merit prizes and certificates to the top 7% of the students of each 4-year B.Tech program for 1st and 2nd Semester. The value of the merit prize is Rs.2500/-. Many other organizations in India and abroad also offer some assistance to the students of IIT Ropar.

What is the mode of payment of fees?

As of now, you can pay the fees in either of the following two modes:

1.
Online mode:
SBI Collect

2.
Offline mode:

a) Cash deposit at IIT Ropar, SBI branch

b) Demand draft in favor of "DIRECTOR, INDIAN INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY ROPAR,HOSTEL A/C" (Account No. 30836912866) payable at Roopnagar (Punjab).

What are the placement statistics for IIT Ropar?

Placement Statistics for 2024-25: 71.82% of students are placed, which comprises 87.95% students from CSE, 73.07% from EE, 59.32% from ME, 88.57% from M&C, 65.21% from CHE, 50% from CE and 42.1% from MME.

Detailed placement statistics can be found
here.

Breaking the stereotype of IT companies hiring most IIT students, IIT-Ropar students got most of the job offers from auto giants Mahindra & Mahindra, Tata Motors, SML Isuzu, and construction company Larsen and Tourbo.

"I am happy that the institute has broken all previous placement records, but what pleases me more is the fact that most of the placements have been made in core engineering companies. We have seen a 20% rise in such companies hiring our students," said IIT-Ropar director Professor Sarit Kumar Das.

IIT Ropar registrar Sanjay Bhatnagar said 42 companies came to the campus for recruitments, including public sector undertakings (PSUs) like Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) and Bharat Dynamics. "One of the students has even secured an international placement," he said.

IIT-Ropar head of training and placement Ravi Mohan Parsad said the placement season also saw an increase in the number of students opting for the option. "Companies like Infosys, Amazon, Arista Networks, Saavn, Timetooth Technologies, and Vehant Technologies recruited our students. Along with them, a large number of first time recruiters like Deloitte, Takshashila Consulting, DEShaw, Directl, BookMyShow, Tesco, Smartpix, Chegg India also took part in this year's placements, said Dr Ravi Mohan Parsad. International companies like Works Applications and Tonichi Insatsu also took part in the annual placement," he said.

Which companies approach IIT Ropar for placements?

Some of the past recruiters are Amazon, Microsoft, EBay, Flipkart, Hyundai and Zomato.

Detailed list of past recruiters can be found
here.

What are the available branches for a Btech student at IIT Ropar?

There are currently 9 branches available for the B.Tech programme:

1. Civil Engineering

2. Chemical Engineering

3. Computer Science

4. Electrical Engineering

5. Mathematics and Computing

6. Mechanical Departments

7. Metallurgical and Materials Engineering

8. Digital Agriculture

9. Electrical Engineering (Integrated Circuit Design and Technology).

What are the features of New Curriculum at IIT Ropar?

The New Curriculum of B.Tech Programme is based on education theories/curriculum theory which focuses on hands-on-learning technique, giving students an opportunity to link with the society and to address their problems by engineering principles, and also giving emphasis to creativity and innovation.

How many options are available for BTech course?

There are four options available for the students: 1. BTech, 2. BTech with Minor, 3. BTech with Concentration, and 4. BTech with Honors.

Medical & Health

Is there a health center on campus?

Yes, a medical centre is there on the campus- along with a pharmacy

Is ambulance service available?

Yes, ambulances are present.

Apart from medical centre, is there availability of proper hospitals in Ropar?

Yes, hospitals are present nearby where all sorts of body check-ups are available.

Interesting Places to visit near Ropar

Diksha Mittal
(2019 Batch Mathematics and Computing)

Jun 27 '20 · 2 min read |
&nbsp840

I don’t know if people would consider it a place worth visiting or not but for me its surely a bliss and I would surely recommend everyone to visit the beautiful place once. No matter, if it’s the happy time after the exams or the times of sadness when I wished for solace, canal is always an extremely close option for me each and every time. The tranquility and peace it have to offer is immense and those deep moments of self introspection are great. Enjoying the sunset at the canal with friends and music and some nice food packagings are sufficient to complete my day on a happy note. On the whole, just a bus to tc and 5-10 minutes walk is enough for any mood for me.

Aneeket Mangal
(2019 Batch Computer Science and Engineering)

Jun 26 '20 · 2 min read |
&nbsp840

The indian artefact of minimalism and abstraction, Chandigarh is an hour drive from Ropar. It is one of the most globalized Indian cities equipped with meticulous infrastructure. Clean roads and green ambience adds to the charm of ‘the city beautiful’. Feel the divinity of alluring Sukhna lake here, and let your soul sink into its pious water. It's vintage yet modern. There are exquisite gardens which breathe serenity and high rise buildings and malls, oozing with the city vibes. Chandigarh is classic. Visit here, I guarantee, your heart will go on singing on the roads, Ilahi mera dil aaye aaye.........

Sudhanshu Kumar
(2019 Batch Computer Science and Engineering)

Jun 27 '20 · 2 min read |
&nbsp840

Virasat-e-Khalsa is a magnificent museum that narrates the history of Sikhism and Punjab by using technology and hand-made artefacts.

Spread across 6500 acres of land, it is envisioned as the world's largest historical museum dedicated to a single community. The presentation is splendid and simple, the architectural perspective leaves you awe-struck and the best part is that it is free to visit. The visitors are also provided with audio phones on submission of a personal ID proof. They are synced with the narrator's informative on the various artefacts present inside.

The premises are explicitly clean and the beauty around is a bliss to feel. There is a library attached with old books and newspaper clippings from the past, which is very rare and precious.
So, take your time and enjoy the masterpiece of architecture and impeccable service that gives you a ride through the history of Sikhs and Punjab. This is a must visit place, that will remain in your heart for long.

Nitish Goyal
(2019 Batch Computer Science and Engineering)

Jun 26 '20 · 2 min read |
&nbsp840

Punjab boasts of its wealth and elegance through its diverse culture while also reminding us of the land’s humility through its memoirs and pious shrines. An excellent combination of the two is the district of Fatehgarh Sahib. Every year during the month of December, the Shaheedi Jor Mela is organised at the Gurudwara Fatehgarh Sahib to pay homage to the young Sahibzadas who lay down their lives while fighting injustice. It is considered to be one of the biggest festivities of the State and people from all across the country come to be part of it. Fatehgarh Sahib is about an hour’s drive away from Ropar and buses are easily available. This might just become one of the many reasons to stay back at the campus during your vacations!

Priyasha Pratap
(2019 Batch Electrical Engineering)

Jun 26 '20 · 2 min read |
&nbsp840

Remember the Manali trek from Yeh Jawani Hai Deewani? Well, the Triund trek isn't exactly like it but, of course, not a bad option too, to experience the beautiful snow-covered peaks and profound valleys. Triund is one of the easiest Himalayan treks with less expense and enduring participation. With a campfire in the night and surrounded by mountains, you will never want to leave the place that's filled with serenity and breathtaking views. And the best part! a dog will always be following you, making your journey a little more special!

Mohit Sharma
(2016 Batch Mechanical Engineering)

Older · 3 min read |
&nbsp840

Places nearby -Chandigarh

You all might have heard college life is incomplete without some unforgettable and adventurous trips and Ropar is surrounded by beautiful places to visit. Talking of the surroundings of Ropar we don't even need to think where to start from, yes of course we are talking of "Chandigarh- rightly known as the city beautiful".

Chandigarh is the best-planned city in India, with architecture which is world-renowned, and a quality of life, which is unparalleled. The face of modern India, Chandigarh, is the manifestation of a dream that Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru envisaged and Le Corbusier executed.

But you need to know what places of interest is the city endowed with. As a first time visitor one is fascinated by the tourist attractions like the Rock Garden, Rose Garden, Sukhna Lake, Chhatbir Zoo, Elante Mall, etc.

Hereby i will provide you a glimpse of the city that awaits your presence: See the intricate work done at the Rock Garden which adds to its resplendence:

The Sukhna Lake will surely be a retreat for eyes and the peace garden would replenish your soul.

The ones from Chandigarh would know the grandeur associated with Secor 17 plaza before the existence of malls in the city.

The Elante Mall came up as one of the biggest malls in the city and has brands to serve all your interests. It has lately become the meet up place for residents just adding to the city's splendor.

Last but not the least Chandigarh is known as the Clean and Green city so why not mention about Rose Garden which exhibits beautiful flora and holds a great annual event the Rose Festival.

So just a long weekend is awaited and you may have a tour of the marvellous city just a few kilometers away from our college.

Welcome to Ropar

"Wow I got admitted to IIT Ropar it was one of my top choices in Josaa. "

"Oh I got IIT Ropar but it was among my bottom preferences."

"OK so I have got admission in IIT Ropar maybe this was in my destiny."

I know that all you freshers can surely relate to one of the above categories. Whether you were here by choice or not but we assure you that your future is secure once you have joined this institution. So no need to worry about anything and just explore "Life At Ropar".

Hereby I would take you through a tour through the city of Punjab i.e. Roopnagar or Ropar.

Firstly let us have a glimpse of the Ropar Canal which will be a place for your evening walks or a place you will often keep visiting to break the monotony of life and start afresh.

Believe me friends the sunrises and sunsets at this place are a great retreat for eyes and the sound of flowing water is soothing to the ears. I am sure it will be one of your favorite time pass to visit the canal.

What to expect in college?

Yashasvi Chaudhary
(2023 Batch Computer Science and Engineering)

May 23 '24 · 4 min read |
&nbsp756

You made it. The continuous hard work of two years (or maybe more?) to crack that one dreaded exam: the JEE Advanced. Remember the sleepless nights to solve that one problem? Remember waking up early in the morning, setting a routine for the day? Or maybe rushing to the coaching centres, huddled up in a chilly classroom, attending classes after classes. You had that one bull’s eye you had to hit. And you’ve made it. Relax a bit now!

Your journey to this point has been a testament to your unwavering determination, perseverance, and intellectual prowess. It's a remarkable feat that reflects not only your academic excellence but also your resilience and commitment to success.

As you embark on this exciting new chapter of your life, entering into the esteemed halls of an IIT, take a moment to acknowledge the magnitude of your accomplishment. You have earned the privilege to be part of a community known for its excellence in education, research, and innovation. However, remember that your journey has just begun. The challenges you'll encounter at IIT will be significant, but they are also opportunities for growth and discovery. Embrace them with enthusiasm and an open mind.

Leaving home and stepping into a new world at IIT Ropar can feel overwhelming. But as you enter those big gates, remember: you're finding a new family. It's a place full of supportive folks who'll help you grow. After the orientation ends, your family will leave, and you'll be with your new hostel mates. At first, you might feel shy and find it hard to talk to people. But trust me, it gets easier. Take your time settling in. Stay open to making new friends and spending time with them. Soon enough, IIT Ropar will feel like a second home—a place you'll love being in.

As you step onto the campus grounds, you'll find yourself immersed in a whirlwind of activities. From mingling with seniors and fellow batchmates to engaging in friendly competitions and club events, the possibilities are endless. These interactions will offer you insights into different clubs and activities, helping you discover where your interests lie. Additionally, cultural nights, movie nights and events organized by ISMP will provide a vibrant glimpse into the rich tapestry of our college culture. So, get ready to dive into a world brimming with excitement and exploration right from the moment you arrive!

There are many fests and events hosted by the institute throughout the year! These gatherings are not just a welcome break from your routine but also offer a chance to dive into some thrilling experiences. Whether you're itching to showcase your talents or simply eager to soak in the vibrant atmosphere, there's something for everyone! Picture this: our annual fest, Zeitgeist, where creativity knows no bounds; Aarohan, our sports fest igniting fierce competition and team spirit; Malhar, the literary fest brimming with wordsmiths and storytellers; Revlanche, the ultimate e-sports showdown for gamers; and last but not least, Advitiya, our technical fest pushing the boundaries of innovation. But wait, there's more! These events aren't just for us - we throw open our doors to participants from other colleges, adding an extra dash of excitement and diversity to the mix. And let's not forget the atmosphere during these fests—it's nothing short of dazzling, with glitz, glamour, and unforgettable moments waiting to be made!

Get ready for a rollercoaster ride of memories right in the heart of our hostels! When exam season rolls around, it's all hands on deck as we gather with our buddies for intense study sessions, cracking doubts, and lending each other a helping hand. But it's not all about hitting the books - get ready for movie nights and spontaneous fun activities that'll have you in stitches and counting down the days till the next one!

And let's talk about festivals - we don't just celebrate them, we dive headfirst into the festivities with infectious enthusiasm! Imagine the thrill of "hostel wali holi" - it's legendary, and celebrating it with your crew amplifies the joy tenfold! From the dazzling lights of Diwali to the adrenaline rush of dahi handi competitions, the kite flying during makar Sankranti and much more! Our hostel life is a non-stop carnival of excitement and camaraderie.

The culture at IIT fosters independence and self-directed learning. While professors offer guidance and expertise, students are expected to take ownership of their education, actively seeking out resources and opportunities for growth. The emphasis shifts from rote memorization to critical thinking, problem-solving, and innovation. Overall, the transition from school to IIT represents a leap into a more specialized, challenging, and intellectually stimulating academic environment, where students are empowered to explore their passions, push the boundaries of knowledge, and emerge as leaders in their respective fields. Adapting to this change is the most important perspective for a fresher who is leaving the comfort of his/her home for the first time. Some adapt to it slowly and some are able to grasp it at an early stage. Take your time. Your friends, seniors and mentors will always be ready to help you in this journey of transition.

Loosen yourself a bit, make friends not only from your own dialect or ethnicity, but make friends from all over India. It’s one of the best exposures you will get. Interacting with your peers can broaden your horizons in so many ways. Everyone comes from different backgrounds, cultures, and walks of life, and getting to know people from diverse backgrounds can open your eyes to new perspectives and ideas you may have never considered before. Beyond that, building relationships with your classmates can actually enhance your academic experience. Study groups, for example, are a great way to collaborate, share knowledge, and tackle tough assignments or projects together. You'll find that discussing concepts with others can deepen your understanding and help you grasp difficult concepts more easily. But it's not just about academics. Interactions in college can also enrich your personal growth and development. You'll learn how to communicate effectively, resolve conflicts, and work as part of a team, all essential skills that will serve you well both in college and beyond.

Amidst the college chatter, you'll undoubtedly encounter discussions about the rigors of academia and the prevailing sense of competition. Whether grappling with coding, electrical engineering, or mathematics, challenges will abound. Yet, with strategic planning and unwavering dedication, conquering these obstacles and excelling in examinations is entirely within reach.

Soon enough you will be introduced with the curriculum and your first semester will begin! (exciting, isn’t it?). Now, the most important question among the newcomers is from where to study, what to study, how to prepare for quizzes and upcoming exams. Calm down! Take a breath, we know you are excited but among all this you may forget that there is a huge world within IIT which is not just about studying and grades! The aim here, at IITs, is to develop your overall personality which includes your speaking skills, management skills or any such domain you are interested to explore further. Being great at academics and doing splendid in extracurriculars are not two mutually exclusive sets. Hope you understand this. What matters is the balance.

Initially, the college experience may appear overwhelming, yet as time progresses, it evolves into a repository of cherished memories, narratives to be recounted for a lifetime. Here's to embracing the adventure that awaits at IIT Ropar! You stand on the precipice of embarking upon a transformative journey. Seize the opportunity to extract the utmost value from these four years ahead! Cheers and welcome again to IIT Ropar!

Facilities

Rajmohini Soni
(2019 Batch Civil Engineering)

Jul 6 '20 · 4 min read |
&nbsp978

IIT ROPAR aims at providing best possible resources to every student living on campus. To ensure ease of living, the students can avail the following facilities.

A) HOSTELS

IIT ROPAR has 4 hostels namely,

Chenab

Beas

Sutlej

Raavi

The male students pursuing B-tech, M-tech or PhD degree, reside in the first three hostels mentioned above. The female students live in separate Raavi hostel.

For all Hostels, each room has a maximum sharing of two students.

The hostels provides the following facilities,

RO filter water : Common to a floor

Sweepers for everyday cleaning of rooms and washrooms.

Geysers are installed in bathrooms.

Laundry and Ironing services can be availed. Automatic washing machines are also installed.

Well equipped gym for fitness purposes.

Separate LAN ports for each student.

Godrej Almirahs, study table, a chair and a single bed for each student.

A common room with installed television for recreational purposes.

Daily Newspapers

Guest rooms need to be pre-booked by the students for relatives on campus visit.

B) The Utility Block:

All basic requirements are fulfilled at a single place.

The following shops are present:-

Barber Shop

• A separate cubicle for females is also present within the shop.

Stationery Shop

General Store

Fruit Shop

Juice Corner

In addition to these; a South Indian canteen and main cafeteria is there within the utility block.

C) MESS:

The Annapurna Mess is divided into two wings to avoid overcrowding.

A weekly menu is prepared which changes every 2-3 months.

Proper cleanliness and quality of food is ensured through regular checks.

A student feedback register is also maintained.

Recently, an app was developed for tracking attendance, providing menus and showing daily food wastage so that it can be reduced.

D) WEATHER:

High temperature and little humidity can be felt during day times in summers. Evening and nights are fairly moderate and pleasant. Reasonable amount of rain is encountered from July to September.

Winter could be harsh with minimum temperature dropping to 4°-5°C. People from coastal areas, specifically South India, may face problems.

E) LIBRARY:

A 24 X 7 open library, with the majority of books required by students available.

An institute ID card is made for each student for issuing of books.

F) SECURITY:

Enough security guards are present at each hostel and other buildings too.

On leaving the campus, students has to make an entry at the Main gate.

No student is allowed to leave or enter the campus between 11PM - 5AM. Strict fines are imposed on students who don't follow these guidelines.

G) RAGGING:

IIT ROPAR is strictly a no ragging campus.

In any case of misconduct, strict action is definitely taken against the defaulters.

Every student is provided with a mentor under the ISMP initiative and they are dedicated to help the students.

H) CLUBS:

There are many cultural, literary and scientific clubs active in IIT ROPAR. These clubs help in holistic personality development of students in addition to academics.

I) ACADEMICS:

For academics please see the "ACADEMICS" post in the FAQ section of ISMP website.

J) SPORTS:

The following sports facilities are available:-

3 Basketball courts

4 Tennis courts

5 Volleyball courts

2 badminton courts

1 Athletics ground

1 Hockey ground

2 Table Tennis courts

Coaches for all sports activities are always available to guide the students in their specific interests.

Inter year interactions

Akansh Caimi
(2021 Batch Chemical Engineering)

September 10 '22 · 7 min read |
&nbsp155

INTER-YEAR INTERACTIONS!

Hey there! I am a 2nd-year undergrad student from the chemical department, IIT Ropar. Furthermore, being on campus for six months or so, I've socialized with loads and loads of seniors from all year and every branch you can think of, owing to the beautiful culture of interaction the institute offers.
Being completely blunt, interactions with peeps will make you survive here and enjoy your journey to the fullest.

Let us start with your batchmates, the 1st year. It is obvious you're definitely going to interact with them the most. You will all have the same classes, labs, clubs, and whatnot! My advice will be to talk to (or at least try to) as many peeps as you can at the start, remember, this is not just about making friends; it is also about making connections that will help you in the future. You do not have to go the extra mile to talk to them, they all are as new as you are. Go on, start with a smile and a hi!

Skipping on to the seniors! The part which makes your spine tickle. I've seen students being hesitant (dare I say, scared) to approach seniors, which I find absurd because seniors are the most important part of your institute. Stepping onto the campus, with a confused and overwhelmed look, you first meet your mentor (a 2nd-year student from your branch), who helps you in and around the campus. Transitioning from a JEE life into college life isn't easy to handle, but your mentor makes it smoother.

Anyways, the second-yearites are the ones who're managing the clubs. They are the ones who'll guide you about the little intricacies of college life since they're the ones who were in your shoes just a couple of months earlier. Many of them have started to find their footing in various specializations, from academics to arts, and you will always find someone willing to guide you in anything that interests you. This is the year you will be the closest with, try to get out of your comfort circle and talk to them. Not going to lie, I have a better friendship with a couple of seniors than I have with my batchmates!

Coming to the third year, this is the year which you'll probably get to see the least of, but also the one you should probably get the most inspired by. With internship season right on their heads coupled with a ginormous academic load, they have chosen their fields of specialization and are working to be masters in them. Also, being in the college for two years, they are well versed in the administrative and academic structure of the college, and therefore the student council, as well as the mentors for all the clubs, are usually from this year. Don't keep the 3rd year peeps aloof, you're sure to learn a lot from them.

Next, the fourth yearites! Determined and busy, since placement season is on, they're the ones who'll make you realize the value of college life since they're at the end of it. They have the most peculiar anecdotes and the best perspective of life since they know what sticks even after college and what is just momentary. The fourth year watches your batch with fondness because they see their past in you.
MTech and Ph.D. interactions are also one of the most crucial ones since they're your TAs as well friends if you seem to share any common interests. Since many of them are from different colleges, they share experiences of different places with you.

Summing up, inter-year interactions are one of the most memorable things about your college life. You'll learn from them, have fun with them, sometimes get reprimanded, and sometimes get appreciated by them. It's a cycle that goes on since your seniors will enrich you with their experiences, and you'll do the same to your juniors. Ultimately, you will find yourself in a special bond with them. All I would like to say is don't leave a blank spot in your canvas painted with memories :)

Managing Social Life and Academics

(2023 Batch Mathematics and Computing)

May 23 '24 · 4 min read |
&nbsp99

Managing academics and social life
Life at IIT is not as glamorous as it may seem from the outside. The relentless stream of weekly assignments, quizzes, midterms, and finals keeps students perpetually on their toes. Alongside these academic demands, carving out time for coding or pursuing personal passions becomes a formidable challenge. This reality is often overlooked by those who haven't experienced it. However, let's be honest: within IIT, there are two main types of students, “the disciplined ones” and “the all-nighters.” The disciplined ones complete their daily tasks, revise lectures, and get a good night's sleep before exams. Conversely, the all-nighters cram the night before exams yet still manage to score comparably, if not higher, than their more disciplined peers. Your first task upon entering IIT is to identify which category you belong to. Once you do, navigating your path forward will be much easier.

At IIT, it is essential to transition out of the intense “JEE phase,” interact with people, and make friends who can support you in this new environment, far from home. Fun and relaxation are crucial components of a balanced life. Some students try to schedule every minute for studying, but this often leads to inefficient use of time. Overworking can result in diminishing returns, where longer study hours yield progressively less productivity. Freshmen often struggle to balance academics and social life, so here are some tips to help you achieve that balance.

Firstly, assign specific time slots to your daily tasks. After dinner is an excellent time for socializing since everyone is generally free from classes and out on “night strolls” at that hour. However, remember your ultimate goal: do not stay out all night socializing and then sleep through your lectures or study sessions. Joining a club that aligns with your interests is another great way to maintain balance.

At IIT Ropar, we have numerous clubs managed by dedicated seniors. Participating in club activities allows you to pursue your passions and increase your skill while meeting people with similar interests. Additionally, being active during festivals and other event preparations can help you build a network of valuable contacts which increases your social skill.

In conclusion, college life is the first significant step towards adulthood. For many of us, this is the first time we live away from the protective shell of our families. To avoid feeling lonely or depressed, it is crucial to establish a supportive social circle. Set your priorities and work diligently towards them. Do not fear making mistakes; these experiences will help you learn and grow. This is what IIT life is about: continually evolving into a better version of yourself.
