Dr. HVR Mittal an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics at IIT Ropar, India. He obtained his PhD degree from Indian Institute of Technology Mandi at Himachal Pradesh, India (2016) and his MSc (honours) in Mathematics from Panjab University (Chandigarh – India) in 2010. From 2016 till 2021 he held assistant Professor position at IIT Palakkad, Kerala and several postdoctoral positions at University of York (UK), United Arab Emirates University (UAE), University of Southern Brittany (France) followed by King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia). His research is an interdisciplinary blend of computational fluid mechanics and numerical analysis which encompasses development and applications of new finite difference numerical schemes to complex real life problems. For instance, analysing the wake structures for flow past oscillating/non-oscillating cylinders, the rheology of deformable fluid particles like drops/bubbles in various fluid environments and detecting, tracking and forecasting of hazardous oil spills in oceans. The research outcomes are published in prestigious journals like Scientific reports (Nature), SIAM journal on Scientific Computing (JSTOR), Physics of Fluids (AIP), International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer (Elsevier), Ocean Engineering (Elsevier) etc.

About the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering (MME)
The Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering at IIT Ropar was established in November 2017 by upgrading the Center for Materials and Energy Engineering. Currently, the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering offers B.Tech. and PhD programs. The Department has faculty members in all the major areas of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering. The focus areas of the Department are Physical Metallurgy, Extractive Metallurgy, Mechanical Metallurgy, Energy Materials, Functional Materials and related areas.
The Department provides a platform for interdisciplinary studies with academia and industry. The curriculum is designed to encourage innovative thinking to enable students to be Industry ready. IIT Ropar has devised a very flexible curriculum to provide the best possible multi-disciplinary and in-depth learning.
The Department welcomes original thinkers and dedicated individuals to be a part of this symbiotic environment and positively influence the world of Metallurgy and Materials.The Department encourages student-faculty interaction. Each batch of B.Tech. students is assigned to a Faculty Advisor and a student is encouraged to discuss all academic/professional matters with his/her Advisor.

The details of admission modes are provided in the Handbook for PhD students. Interested candidates can refer to the
Handbook for complete details of the various PhD programs
. Typically, interviews for admission to the PhD program are advertised in March/April and October/November timeframe and the interviews are held in April/May and November/December timeframe.
Project based candidates can be admitted any time of the year, based on the suitability of the candidate and availability of funding.
Modes of Entry
Regular Institute Fellowships
for candidates who have a MTech/ME degree or have completed their BTech/BE/MSc within the last two years).
Direct PhD Program
for candidates who are in the final year of their BTech/BE programs.
Project Fellowships
for candidates who are funded by a faculty member's research grant (interested students should contact the relevant faculty - usually openings are advertised here and here, in addition to individual faculty web-pages).
External Registration Program (ERP)
for professionals who are employed in an academic/research origanization and wish to carry out the majority of their research in their home organizations. No fellowship is provided in the ERP program.
Part-time PhD program
for candidates who wish to follow the PhD program in a part-time mode at IIT Ropar. No fellowship is available for part-time PhD program.
Institute Staff
who wish to pursue a PhD program may do so after successfully taking teh admission interviews. No fellowship is provided in this case either.
The PhD Timeline and Degree Requirements
Within 2 weeks of joining, the studentsshould have formed their Doctoral Scrutiny Committee (DC). The students should meet with the DC members at least once every semester and provide updates on their progress.
Candidates with an MTech degree are required to do a minimum of 12 credits of course work.
Following the completion of coursework, the candidates should take a comprehensive examination (which has both written and oral components) within 18 months of admission.
The candidates are then required to present a thesis proposal within 24 months of admission.
The candidates must present an open seminar (also called the synopsis seminar) at least 6 months prior to the final thesis defense.
The final thesis defense is held after the thesis has been submitted and feedback received from the referees. There are at least two external referees, one from within India and another from outside the country.

title: Chemical Engineering | IIT ROPAR
text:
Dr. Aaditya Pandey is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering
at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar. He received his Ph.D. for his research on
forward osmosis membrane processes for fruit juice concentration and shelf-life
enhancement. He brings interdisciplinary expertise spanning mechanical engineering,
packaging technology, and chemical engineering, with a focus on developing sustainable
solutions for chemical and allied industries. During his postgraduate studies, he was
a visiting graduate scholar at the University of New Brunswick, Canada, where he worked
on an industry-oriented research project in collaboration with Oval International, USA.

His industrial experience as a Production Process Analyst provides practical insights
into manufacturing operations, process efficiency, quality improvement, and production
optimization. He integrates this industry-oriented perspective with his research to
develop scalable, resource-efficient, and commercially viable technologies for chemical
and allied industries.


Ph.D. – Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee

M.Tech – Packaging Technology, Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee

B.Tech – Mechanical Engineering, Kumaun Engineering College Dwarahat

Visiting Research Fellow – University of New Brunswick, Canada


Membrane Processes and Separation Engineering:
Advanced membrane
materials and processes for efficient separations, fouling mitigation, flux
enhancement, resource recovery, and novel industrial applications, with emphasis
on process intensification, operational stability, and scale-up.

Sustainable Packaging Materials and Polymer Upcycling:

High-performance sustainable packaging, bio-based and functional composites,
barrier materials, active packaging, recycled polymer valorization, and circular
solutions for packaging waste and shelf-life enhancement.

Sustainable Water Treatment and Process Optimization:

Membrane-integrated and hybrid treatment technologies for industrial wastewater,
water reuse, and resource recovery, supported by process modelling.

Technology Scale-up and Sustainability Assessment:
Pilot-scale
validation, techno-economic analysis (TEA), and industrial translation of lab research.

title: Arghya Banerjee | Chemical Engineering
text:
Dr. Arghya Banerjee completed his Ph.D in Chemical Engineering from the
National University of Singapore in 2016. His Ph.D focussed on understanding the structure
of the cobalt catalyst under reaction conditions
during the Fischer-Tropsch reaction using first principle quantum chemical tools like
Density Functional Theory (DFT). After his Ph.D, he joined the Department of Chemical and
Bio-medical Engineering at Nanyang Technological
University, Singapore as a post-doctoral fellow where his work focussed on the design of
suitable catalysts for the upgradation of bio-oil obtained from biomass pyrolysis. He
returned to India in November, 2017 and joined the
Gasification and Liquefaction Research Division at CSIR-CIMFR, Dhanbad as Scientist. He was
associated with BITS, Pilani as an Assistant Professor from April 2019 to July 2020. He
joined IIT Ropar in July 2020. His research
expertise is in the field of molecular modelling based catalyst design. His current research
interests include catalyst design for catalytic conversion of CO2/syngas and biomass
derivatives to chemicals and fuels.

I am an Associate Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar. I graduated from the University of Auckland, New Zealand in 2002 with a Bachelor of Engineering degree in Computer Systems. After a brief stint as a Software Engineer in the healthcare industry, I joined the graduate program at Yale University and earned my PhD in Biomedical Engineering in May 2009. My doctoral dissertation involved statistical modeling of brain activation patterns for robust analysis of Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) data. Prior to joining IIT Ropar, I worked as a Research Associate at Oregon Health & Science University.
My research interests focus on applying computational and statistical methods to address challenges in medical imaging. Particularly, development of image/signal processing, pattern recognition and machine learning techniques to assist in biomedical image analysis and diagnostic decision making.

title: Chemical Engineering | IIT ROPAR
text:
Dr. Jayaram Valluru is Assistant Prof. in Dept. of Chemical Engg., IIT Ropar, India.
Process Systems Engineering is his area of research, where focus is on developing
novel algorithms for Bayesian State and Parameter estimation, Soft-Sensing, Data
reconciliation, Fault Detection and Diagnosis using first principles knowledge as
well as machine learning approaches. Dr. Valluru also has research experience in
developing integrated Model Predictive Control and Real-Time Optimization
frameworks for large scale chemical processes under uncertainty, development, and
implementation of industrial data-driven soft sensors for quality prediction and
process monitoring for mining, extraction and upgrading units of oil sands processes.

His future interests are in developing novel Hybrid estimation algorithms, i.e.,
integration of process knowledge (flow sheet information/process model equations)
using BIG data techniques, for developing soft-sensing and data reconciliation
frameworks for process unit/entire plant. Further, developing intelligent control
frameworks using advanced Machine learning techniques for continuous and batch
processes is of another area of research interest to be explored. Application areas
include large scale continuous and batch chemical processes.

title: Chemical Engineering | IIT ROPAR
text:
The knowledge of the structural and topological properties of porous materials is vital
to understanding fluid transport and confinement effects within them. My research
involves the application of different structural characterisation techniques, namely,
gas adsorption, liquid intrusion, NMR and thermogravimetric methods, to a variety of
porous materials and using the information obtained to better understand or optimize
process and/or reaction conditions. A primary focus area of research is the development
of appropriate experimental methodologies to determine the spatial location and
distribution of carbon deposits with catalysts. I also have keen interest in the
synthesis and characterization of novel structured materials and nanoparticles for
applications related to different separation process applications and drug delivery.
Additionally, I also have a keen interest in chemical process safety and the design of
chemical process equipments.

text:
Dr. Neelkanth Nirmalkar
is an Associate Professor of
Chemical Engineering at the Indian Institute of
Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar), India, where he leads
research on sustainable technologies for energy and
environmental applications. He earned his Ph.D. in
Chemical Engineering from the
Indian Institute of
Technology, Kanpur (IIT Kanpur)
and was a
Research Fellow at the
University of Birmingham,
UK
.

His work combines chemical engineering fundamentals
with scalable nanobubble processes for water, energy,
and environmental applications. It spans three
streams:
(1) energy and climate change, (2)
bioengineering, and (3) membrane technologies.

A major focus of Dr. Nirmalkar’s research is
nanobubble technology
, including
generation, characterization, interfacial and mass-transfer behavior, existence,
stability,
colloidal interactions, nucleation, and dynamics. His group develops applications in

water and wastewater treatment, advanced oxidation, disinfection, pollutant
degradation, particle flotation, crystallization, CO₂ utilization, fuel combustion,
and industrial processes.
Recent studies explore ozone and electrochemically
reactive nanobubbles, nanobubble-assisted crystallization, enhanced CO₂ conversion
and absorption, and effects on fuel combustion.

Dr. Nirmalkar has published extensively in leading international journals and built a
strong program linking
fundamental nanobubble phenomena with technology
development and industrial applications
. His broader interests include
hydrogen
production and water electrolysis, electrochemical CO₂ reduction, fuel additives
and combustion, critical mineral extraction, environmental biotechnology, water
and wastewater treatment, and advanced membrane technologies
. He has also
invented several technologies, including a patented
nanobubble-generation device

transferred to
Nanokriti Pvt. Limited
, reflecting his commitment to commercialization.

Recent Research

Electrochemical sulfinylation of phenols with sulfides: a metal- and oxidant-free cross-coupling for the synthesis of aromatic sulfoxides

Rakesh Kumar, Irshad Maajid Taily and Prabal Banerjee

The site-selective C–H functionalization of arenes is of indisputable importance in organic chemistry. Herein, we have demonstrated an electrochemical regioselective oxidative cross-coupling towards the direct C(sp
2
)–H sulfinylation of phenols with sulfides under mild reaction conditions. The designed methodology furnished aryl sulfoxides in good to moderate yields under exogenous metal and oxidant-free conditions. Moreover, the exploitation of traceless electrons to carry out the tandem site-selective oxidative aryl chalcogenation is the striking feature of this methodology.

Switchable Reactivity of Cyclopropane Diesters toward (3 + 3) and (3 + 2) Cycloadditions with Benzoquinone Esters

Navpreet Kaur, Pankaj Kumar, Arijit Hazra, and Prabal Banerjee

Herein, we describe an unprecedented (3 + 3) cycloaddition reaction of the donor–acceptor cyclopropanes with quinone esters toward the construction of chroman scaffolds in moderate to good yields. Interestingly, the strategy is also adjustable toward a (3 + 2) cycloaddition by just switching the Lewis acid to furnish benzofuran scaffolds. Based on the choice of Lewis acid used, the same set of precursors has been used to deliver the benzopyran and benzofuran derivatives

Accessing Complex Tetrahydrofurobenzo-Pyran/Furan Scaffolds via Lewis-Acid Catalyzed Bicyclization of Cyclopropane Carbaldehydes with Quinone Methides/Esters

Navpreet Kaur, Pankaj Kumar, Shiv Dutt, and Prabal Banerjee

Herein, we report a straightforward one-pot synthesis of tetrahydrofurobenzopyran and tetrahydrofurobenzofuran systems via an in situ ring-expansion of the cyclopropane carbaldehydes followed by a [2 + n] cycloaddition with the quinone derivatives. The transformation not only unveils a new reaction mode of cyclopropane carbaldehydes with quinone methides/esters, but also promotes a step-efficient diastereoselective route to the sophisticatedly fused oxygen tricycles that can be further dehydrogenated to access the valued dihydro-2H-furo[2,3-b]chromene frameworks.

?,ß
-Unsaturated Carbonyls for One-Pot Transition-Metal-Free Access to
3,6-Dihydro-2H-pyrans

Pankaj Kumar, Navpreet Kaur, Rakesh Kumar, and Prabal Banerjee

An efficient protocol has been developed for accessing mono, di, and trisubstituted 3,6-dihydro-2
H
-pyran derivatives by simply subjecting
?,?
-unsaturated carbonyls to the carefully optimized Corey-Chaykovsky reaction conditions. The strategy provides selectively substituted dihydropyran derivatives in good to excellent yields with a broad substrate scope under very mild reaction conditions. Easy transformation of the final 3,6-dihydro-2
H
-pyran to the valued 5,6-dihydro-2
H
-pyran-2-one and tetrahydro-2
H
-pyran derivatives expanded the scope of this methodology to diverse oxacycles. Further, the developed strategy also found application in a two-step route to racemic goniothalamin, which is widely studied for its cytotoxic behaviour.

Electricity mediated [3+2]-cycloaddition of N-sulfonylcyclopropanes with olefins via N-centered radical intermediates: access to cyclopentane analogs

Debarshi Saha, Irshad Maajid Taily, Nakshatra Banerjee and Prabal Banerjee

An external oxidant free electrochemical strategy is designed towards the b-scission of strained C–C bonds in cyclopropylamine. Moreover, the mechanistic studies ascertained that the methodology encompasses the
N
-center radical (NCRs) route and provides access to di- or tri-substituted cyclopentane analogs.

Direct Synthesis of Paracetamol via Site-Selective Electrochemical Ritter-type C-H Amination of Phenol

Irshad Maajid Taily, Debarshi Saha and Prabal Banerjee

The synthesis of paracetamol still relies on multistep protocols involving the utilization of a stoichiometric amount of oxidizing/reducing or other corrosive agents. Herein we report a regioselective electrochemical Ritter-type reaction at the C(sp2)?H of unprotected phenol toward the environmentally benign and direct synthesis of paracetamol. The reaction proceeds under exogenous oxidant- and catalyst-free conditions. The protocol is scalable, can be deployed to a variety of phenols, and offers a sustainable alternative for the synthesis of paracetamol.

Previously, he was an Assistant Professor in Chemical Engineering at BITS Pilani – Goa

title: Chemical Engineering | IIT ROPAR
text:
Dr. Saikat Roy did his postdoc from Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel. He completed
his Mtech+PhD dual degree in chemical engineering from IIT Bombay in the year 2016. As a
part of his PhD work, he studied the consolidation of colloidal gel via simulation
and theory and proposed a model which does fairly well in predicting the salient
features of the compressional rheology of gels. During his postdoctoral research, he
studied the behaviour of frictional granular matter via
simulation and theory. His research interests mainly lie in Granular Mechanics, Soft
Condensed Matter and related Solid Mechanics, Jamming and Glass transition,Complex fluid
Rheology.

Dr. Snigdha Mishra is a chemical engineer specializing in sustainable waste recycling,
hydrometallurgy, and circular economy solutions. She previously worked as a Research
Associate at University of Leicester in collaboration with cleantech startup DESCycle,
from 2024 to 2026. Her work primarily focused on the intensification of the metal
recovery process from e-waste. She earned her Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering from IIT
Delhi, where her doctoral work focused on developing green hydrometallurgical processes
for extracting valuable metals from electronic waste for which she was awarded GYTI
Appreciation Award in 2020. During her Ph.D. she also had the opportunity to visit
University of Leeds as Commonwealth Split-site scholar. Prior to this, she completed her
M.Tech in Chemical Engineering at IIT (BHU) Varanasi, where she worked on potable water
production using capacitive deionization. She did her B.Tech from Banasthali University.
Her academic vision is to combine scientific innovation with sustainability,
contributing to both industrial practice and environmental responsibility.

title: Dhilip's Group@IIT Ropar
text:
Dr. T. J. Dhilip Kumar


Dr. T. J. Dhilip Kumar obtained his Master and Doctoral degrees from Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT-M). After completing Ph.D. in 2006, he worked as a postdoctoral research fellow at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas in the field of fundamental studies on Hydrogen storage materials and then, from 2008 to 2010 worked at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor on the modeling of atmospheric nitrate reactions. His doctoral work was adjudged the best thesis in Physical Chemistry for the year 2006 by IIT Madras. He joined IIT Ropar as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Chemistry in September 2010. He worked as Associate Professor from December 2015 to August 2024. Currently he is working as Professor. From 2014-17, worked as Associate Dean (Post-Graduate) and from 2017-18 worked as Associate Dean (Research). Dr. Dhilip was the Head of the Department from June 2018 – June 2021. His research interests include quantum dynamics of molecular collisions and designing materials for energy storage.

Dr. Dhilip received CRSI Bronze Medal for the year 2024.

Our research team is actively engaged in the development of nanostructured and carbonaceous materials, specifically designed for use in energy conversion and storage devices.

Our focus includes the creation of electrochemical biosensors for chemical and electrochemical applications. The motivation behind our interest in enhancing the viability of alternative renewable technologies such as fuel cells and batteries, stems from the environmental risks associated with current non-renewable energy sources, coupled with their limited availability.
​

​

To address this challenge, we are conducting in-depth fundamental analyses of newly designed electrocatalysts for fuel cells and batteries, utilizing a variety of electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopic techniques. In addition to our work on renewable energy alternatives, we are also dedicated to developing electrochemical biosensors. These sensors play a crucial role in detecting trace levels of pollutants in the environment and specific biological components in bodily fluids. Our goal is to efficiently and rapidly determine the health condition of individuals with accuracy. We are committed to achieving cost-effective and highly sensitive electrochemical detection methods.

Dr. J. Kalaiselvi completed her Ph.D. at IIT Madras and has been a faculty member at IIT Ropar since 2016. She leads the AMPE4RE Lab (Applied Motor drives & Power Electronics 4 Research & Education), which focuses on advancing research in motor drives and power electronics. Her research interests include EMI/EMC issues in power converters and motor drives, as well as fault diagnosis and fault tolerance in converter and motor drive systems. The lab strives to bridge the gap between fundamental research and real-world applications in energy-efficient systems.

title: Chemical Engineering | IIT ROPAR
text:
Dr. G. Sridhar has over three decades of experience spanning research and development,
technology development and commercialization, industry, government, and institutional
leadership in the energy and bioenergy sectors. He is an alumnus of the Indian Institute of
Science (IISc), Bengaluru, and has worked in both industrial R&D and the public-sector
research ecosystem, including Siemens Corporate Technology and SSS-NIBE.

As Director General of SSS-NIBE, he led initiatives in bioenergy research, technology
development, capacity building, technology translation and national programmes in
renewable energy. His work has covered biomass conversion, decentralized energy systems,
biofuels, clean cooking, waste-to-energy and emerging pathways for sustainable energy
transition.

Areas of Expertise

Biomass Gasification and Thermochemical Conversion

Producer Gas and Hydrogen-fuelled Engines

Clean Cooking and Biomass Combustion

Green Hydrogen and Sustainable Energy Systems

Integrated biorefineries – fuel, chemicals, materials, biochar, carbon products

Biomass resource and supply chain management

Technology Development, Translation, Transfer and Commercialization

Energy Policy, Innovation and Institutional Development

Research and Development Focus

Dr. Sridhar is particularly interested in developing integrated approaches for
biomass and
waste valorization
, including thermochemical and biological conversion routes, biochar and
other value-added products, decentralized energy systems, and pathways for reducing
emissions from agricultural and organic residues.

He is also interested in mentoring students and researchers, developing industry-oriented
research programmes, supporting technology translation, commercialization, and establishing
collaborative platforms between academia, industry and government.


Dr. Sridhar has contributed to nearly
50 research publications and patents
in the areas of
biomass conversion, gasification, combustion, producer gas engines and sustainable energy
technologies.

Central Policies on Sand Mining in India
The central government regulates sand mining primarily through environment and mining legislation, aiming to curb illegal extraction, ensure sustainable practices and protect ecosystems.
Overview
Sand is classified as a minor mineral in India, with the central government setting overarching regulations while states like Punjab adapt these with local rules to address environmental, economic, and enforcement concerns.
Key Central Regulations
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act (MMDR Act)
1957 (amended, latest 2025)
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2025
Sustainable Sand Mining Management Guidelines
2016
Enforcement & Monitoring Guidelines for Sand Mining
Punjab State Sand Mining Policy
Punjab, with rivers like the Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi, has tailored its sand mining policies to address local environmental concerns, illegal mining, and construction demands.
Punjab Minor Mining Policy, 2023
Comprehensive framework for minor minerals including sand and gravel, covering lease auctions, royalty rates, environmental restoration, and district-level task forces.
View Official Document
Amendment to Punjab Minor Mining Policy, 2023
Updates including revised timelines for e-auctions, enhanced penalties for violations, and integration of GIS-based monitoring for sand mining sites.
Key Features of Punjab's Approach
🖥️
E-Auction System
Sand mining leases allocated via online bidding to ensure transparency and reduce mafia control.
🔄
Replenishment Focus
District survey reports assess sand replenishment rates in rivers with GIS-based monitoring integration.
🚫
Crackdown on Illegal Mining
Intensified efforts with raids and seizures, enhanced penalties up to three times royalty rates.
📡
Technology Integration
Centralized IT solutions for monitoring, GPS tracking, and real-time reporting systems.
🏗️
Promotion of Alternatives
Encourages manufactured sand (M-Sand) for construction to reduce pressure on riverbeds.
⚡
Streamlined Permissions
Delegation of powers to district mining officers for simplified operations with oversight.
Important Note
Last Updated: October 2025
- Punjab's policies are dynamic, with updates driven by NGT rulings and central directives. For the latest details, check the

Punjab Department of Mines and Geology
or the

Ministry of Mines portal
.

title: SEnSRS - IIT Ropar
text:
Drone Mapping & Surveying
Advanced aerial surveying methods using RTK-enabled UAVs for centimeter-level geospatial accuracy.
Survey Equipment Ecosystem
RTK Drone
Real Time Kinematic (RTK) Drone Survey is an advanced aerial surveying method that uses an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with an RTK-enabled GNSS receiver to capture highly accurate geospatial data. RTK technology improves the positional accuracy of drone data, allowing centimeter-level accuracy without the need for extensive ground control points.
Primary Role
The drone equipped with a high-resolution camera and RTK GNSS receiver was used to capture aerial images in automatic flight mode.
Remote Controller
The remote controller features a built-in high-brightness touchscreen display that allows the operator to monitor live video feed, flight status, satellite connection, RTK signal strength, and mission parameters in real time. The dual external antennas improve signal stability and ensure reliable data transmission, which is essential for RTK-based aerial surveying.
Primary Role
Multiple control buttons, joysticks, and customizable keys are provided on the controller for accurate drone navigation and camera control. The built-in battery indicator and status lights help monitor the power level during field operations, ensuring uninterrupted survey work.
Base Station
The Base station continuously receives satellite signals from multiple GNSS constellations and transmits correction data to the drone controller. These corrections reduce positioning errors caused by atmospheric disturbances and satellite inaccuracies, allowing the drone to achieve centimeter-level accuracy.
Primary Role
The use of an RTK base station improves the overall precision of aerial survey data and reduces the need for multiple ground control points. This ensures reliable results for topographic mapping, volume calculation, construction survey, and GIS applications.
RTK Drone Survey Excellence
The survey of the project area was carried out using an RTK-enabled drone system consisting of a drone, remote controller, and GNSS RTK base station to achieve high-precision results. Our drone, equipped with a high-resolution camera and RTK GNSS receiver, captures georeferenced aerial images in automatic flight mode, ensuring reliable data collection for complex engineering and GIS mapping projects.
The drone was operated using a professional remote controller with a built-in display, which allowed real-time monitoring of flight status, satellite connection, and RTK signal during the survey. An RTK base station was installed on a stable location to provide real-time correction data to the drone, which improved positional accuracy to centimeter level. With the help of RTK correction, the drone captured accurate georeferenced images, which were processed using photogrammetry software to generate Orthomosaic, DEM, DSM, and contour data in the required coordinate system and datum.
Technical Capabilities
Provides centimeter-level positioning accuracy using RTK GNSS correction.
Supports real-time communication between drone, controller, and base station.
Equipped with high-resolution camera for detailed aerial image capture.
Capable of automatic grid flight mission planning for full area coverage.
Supports multi-GNSS satellites (GPS / GLONASS / Galileo / BeiDou) for better accuracy.
Enables real-time flight monitoring through smart remote controller display.
Reduces the requirement of Ground Control Points (GCPs) using RTK correction.
Generates accurate outputs such as Orthomosaic, DEM, DSM, and Contour maps.
Provides stable long-range signal transmission with dual-antenna controller.
Suitable for topographic survey, construction, mining, land mapping, and GIS work.
Ensures fast data collection with high reliability compared to conventional survey methods.
Compatible with photogrammetry and GIS software like Pix4D, DJI Terra, Agisoft, and ArcGIS.
Field Operations Workflow
Network Connection
Internet connection was established in the remote controller to receive RTK correction signals from the CORS network for high-accuracy positioning.
Mission Planning
The survey area was checked and the flight mission was planned in automatic grid mode using mission planning software.
Pre-flight Verification
Before takeoff, RTK status, satellite count, network connection, speed, overlap % and battery levels were verified to ensure proper accuracy.
Data Acquisition
The drone was flown over the project area to capture high-resolution images with required overlap, while continuously receiving correction data from the network base station.
Workshop & Practical Training
Classroom Session
An interactive classroom session demonstrating Drone surveying principles, equipment operation, and real-time data processing techniques for high-precision geospatial applications.
Hands-on Demo
Hands-on demonstration of RTK drone survey equipment was conducted to show the setup, operation, and real-time data acquisition using drone, controller, and Network CORS correction system.
Field Training
Field training on RTK drone surveying was conducted to provide practical knowledge on drone setup, mission planning, Network CORS connection, and accurate aerial data collection.
Data Processing
Drone data processing and surface modeling were performed to generate accurate orthomosaic, DEM, DSM, and contour data using photogrammetry software from captured aerial images.

title: SEnSRS - IIT Ropar
text:
DGPS Surveying
Centimeter-accuracy with real-time RTK — for topographic mapping, dam surveys, infrastructure, and environmental monitoring.
High-Precision Survey Ecosystem
GNSS Base Station
A high-precision receiver mounted on a survey tripod is used for accurate geospatial data acquisition in field surveying operations. The receiver collects signals from multiple satellite constellations such as GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, and BeiDou to determine precise three-dimensional coordinates.
Primary Role
When configured as a DGPS base station, it calculates positional corrections and transmits them to rover receivers in real time, enabling centimeter-level positioning accuracy.
Trimble TSC3 Controller
The Trimble TSC3 Survey Controller is a rugged handheld data collector designed for professional GNSS and total station surveying operations. It operates with field software such as Trimble Access, enabling real-time data collection and management.
Primary Role
Built for demanding environments, the TSC3 features a sunlight-readable display, full keypad interface, and durable field-ready design, making it ideal for topographic mapping.
Trimble R10 Receiver
Trimble R10 is a high-precision GNSS receiver used in surveying to collect accurate geospatial positioning data. It receives signals from multiple constellations enabling precise determination of 3D coordinates in real time.
Primary Role
Equipped with advanced multi-frequency signal tracking and a rugged field-ready design, it delivers centimeter-level positioning accuracy for topographic and reservoir surveys.
DGPS Operational Strategy
Our DGPS surveying methodology centers on achieving absolute spatial precision using a network of high-frequency GNSS receivers. By establishing a fixed base station on a known geodetic control point, we compute and broadcast real-time differential corrections (RTK) to mobile rover units, eliminating satellite-derived errors and atmospheric interference.
This dual-receiver architecture ensures that every captured coordinate—whether for topographic mapping, dam structural monitoring, or highway corridor alignment—maintains centimeter-level accuracy. The seamless integration between field data collectors and advanced post-processing software allows us to deliver high-resolution DEMs, contour maps, and GIS layers that form the foundation of critical engineering and environmental assessments.
Technical Capabilities
Multi-Constellation GNSS Tracking: GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou
Multi-Frequency L1/L2/L5 carrier phase measurements
RTCM differential correction messages for real-time precision
UHF radio modem & NTRIP internet streaming for corrections
Centimeter-level positioning accuracy in RTK mode
Continuous data logging for post-processed (PPK) surveys
Rugged IP67 rated equipment for harsh field conditions
Seamless integration with Trimble Access & post-processing software
High-precision contour mapping & reservoir capacity analysis
Accurate structural axis control for dam alignment projects
Field Operations Workflow
Base Setup
Establishment of GNSS base station on a known control point for real-time corrections.
Network Lock
Initializing satellite constellations and establishing UHF/NTRIP communication links.
Data Collection
Capturing high-precision topographic coordinates and elevation data in the field.
Quality Control
Validating coordinates through redundant observations and known control points.

Bathymetry Survey
Precision underwater mapping using autonomous catamaran platforms and survey-grade echo sounders.
Advanced Hydrographic Ecosystem
Bathycat USV
The BathyCat is a compact catamaran‑type autonomous survey boat designed for bathymetric surveys. The catamaran configuration provides high stability on water and allows integration of sensors such as GNSS receivers and echo sounders.
Primary Role
The USV can be remotely operated or programmed to follow predefined survey lines, ensuring systematic coverage and observer safety.
Futaba T6K Transmitter
The BathuCat USV is operated using a Futaba long-range RC transmitter. The controller operates on 2.4 GHz frequency with 8-channel control and frequency-hopping technology to ensure stable communication during survey operations.
Primary Role
Provides smooth throttle control and reliable long-range communication, allowing precise navigation and maneuvering of the USV during bathymetric surveys.
Bathylogger BL200 Ecosounder
The BathyLogger BL200 is a survey‑grade single beam echo sounder designed for hydrographic surveys. It measures water depth by transmitting acoustic pulses toward the waterbed and calculating the return time of the echo.
Primary Role
The system records depth together with GNSS coordinates for accurate georeferenced bathymetric mapping, suitable for reservoir and river analysis.
Operational Excellence
The bathymetric survey is conducted using a BathyCat Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) equipped with the BathyLogger BL200 survey‑grade single beam echo sounder. The system enables safe hydrographic data collection in reservoirs, lakes, ponds, and rivers while the operator remains onshore. During the survey, the BathyCat USV navigates along predefined survey lines across the water body.
The BL200 echo sounder continuously records depth measurements while the GNSS receiver logs the geographic location of each observation. The collected data forms the basis for bathymetric surface modelling. This integrated approach ensures high-resolution depth logging suitable for bathymetric mapping and sediment analysis, fully compatible with GIS and hydrographic software for bathymetric surface generation.
Technical Capabilities
Autonomous or remote‑controlled BathyCat USV platform for hydrographic data collection.
Survey‑grade single beam echo sounder (BathyLogger BL200) for accurate depth measurements.
Real‑time GNSS positioning for georeferenced depth recording.

Compatible with GIS and hydrographic software for bathymetric surface generation.
Stable catamaran design for operation in reservoirs, lakes, ponds, and rivers.
Long-range RC communication with frequency-hopping technology.
Full integration with GNSS receivers for centimeter-level precision.
Compact and portable system for rapid deployment in remote locations.
Safe hydrographic data collection with operator remaining onshore.

Terrestrial Imaging Hyperspectral Sensor
Advanced SPECIM IQ portable imaging system for high-resolution spectral analysis in field and laboratory.
System Architecture & Output
SPECIM IQ Hyperspectral Camera
A compact, portable imaging system developed by SPECIM (Finland) for field and laboratory use. It operates in the VNIR range (≈400–1000 nm) with 204 spectral bands, capturing a full spectrum for every pixel.
Primary Role
Using a push-broom imaging principle, it provides high spectral accuracy with a ~7 nm spectral resolution. Includes onboard processing, touchscreen control, and built-in calibration.
Trimble T110 Interface
Integrated touchscreen-based control and analysis system designed for efficient hyperspectral imaging. Enables precise control of exposure time, frame rate, and radiometric calibration.
Primary Role
Supports real-time visualization of spectral signatures, band selection, false-color rendering, and pixel-wise classification without an external computer.
Basic Processing Output
Standard output from SPECIM IQ includes radiometrically corrected reflectance spectra using dark and white reference calibration, ensuring accurate reflectance values for quantitative analysis.
Primary Role
Pixel-wise spectral signatures identify chemical composition, moisture content, vegetation health, and material differences across various research fields.
Data Acquisition Principle
The data acquisition in the SPECIM IQ hyperspectral camera is based on a push-broom scanning mechanism, where spectral data are captured line by line as the camera or target moves.
Each hyperspectral data cube is geo-referenced with location coordinates when mounted with an external GPS module. This capability is particularly useful for precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and field surveys, requiring high spectral accuracy and portable operation.
Technical Capabilities
Spectral range: VNIR, ~400–1000 nm
Spectral bands: 204 contiguous bands
Spectral resolution: ~7 nm
Imaging principle: Push-broom (line-scan) hyperspectral imaging
Spatial resolution: ~512 pixels per line
Calibration: Built-in dark and white reference for reflectance data
Interface: Integrated touchscreen with real-time visualization
Processing: Onboard data acquisition, preprocessing, and basic analysis
Data output: Calibrated hyperspectral data cubes in standard formats
Operation: Portable, battery-powered; handheld or tripod-mounted
Integration: Supports external GPS for geo-referenced measurements

About the Centre
The Centre of Excellence in Socio-Environmental Sustainability for River Sand Mining (SEnSRS) at IIT Ropar is a pioneering initiative focused on interdisciplinary research, capacity building, and evidence-based policymaking for sustainable river resource management. Recognizing the challenges posed by unsustainable sand mining — including ecological degradation, hydrological changes, socio-economic impacts, and governance issues — the Centre aims to develop scientific solutions and policy interventions for long-term sustainability.
In alignment with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, SEnSRS proposes to launch a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Programme from January 2026. The programme will integrate engineering, environmental sciences, social sciences, law, and emerging technologies such as AI, GeoAI, and digital governance tools to address key aspects of river sand mining and riverine sustainability.
1. Research Areas
Research under the programme will focus on a wide range of thematic areas, including but not limited to:
River Geomorphology and Sediment Dynamics
Environmental Impacts and Ecological Sustainability of Sand Mining
Hydrological Modelling and River Basin Management
GIS, Remote Sensing, and Drone-based Monitoring Applications
Socio-Economic, Legal, and Policy Dimensions of River Resource Governance
Sustainability Indicators and Decision Support Systems
Artificial Intelligence (AI), GeoAI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning for Predictive Modelling
Hyperautomation and Workflow Intelligence for Environmental Data Processing
Web-based GIS Dashboards and Spatial Decision Support Portals
Mobile and Web Application Development for Real-Time River Monitoring

text:
Academic-Industry Consortium
Revitalizing Rivers with Nanobubble Technology
The Initiative
Bridging the Gap in Water Quality
The Academic–Industry Consortium is a collaborative initiative established to advance research, field validation, and large-scale deployment of nanobubble-based solutions. Formed under a formal Memorandum of Understanding, the consortium brings together leading academic institutions and industry expertise to address persistent water quality challenges.
"The consortium was created to bridge the gap between infrastructure compliance and actual improvement in river and drain health."
Despite significant investments in sewage treatment systems, many water bodies continue to experience dissolved oxygen depletion and ecological stress. Our focus is on
in-situ and post-treatment solutions
that directly enhance water quality within the receiving water bodies themselves.
Project Lifecycle
1
Research Design
2
Pilot Implementation
3
Field Deployment
4
Monitoring & Validation
5
Documentation & Scale-up
Outcome Focused
We offer governments and stakeholders a credible pathway for piloting innovative technologies and advancing long-term rejuvenation programs.
Purpose & Scope
Establishing an academic–industry consortium to collaborate on research, pilot implementation, field deployment, validation, and scale-up of nanobubble-based solutions.
Drinking Water Treatment Plants (WTPs)
Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)
Open drains, canals, and wastewater conveyances
Rivers, streams, wetlands, lakes, and ponds
Irrigation water systems
Groundwater remediation
Industrial and mixed wastewater streams
Climate-linked interventions (GHG reduction)
The Consortium also undertakes carbon credit assessment, validation, and monetization support.
Strategic Objectives
Quality Compliance
Achieving statutory and performance-based treated water quality compliance.
Pollutant Reduction
Reduction of BOD, COD, TSS, nutrients, pathogens, and odor.
Climate Alignment
Methane and nitrous oxide reduction aligned with climate commitments.
Scalable Solutions
Deployment of affordable, scalable, low-energy, and modular solutions.
Data Generation
Generation of regulatory-grade monitoring data and peer-reviewed documentation.
Advanced Solutions
Two-Stage In-Situ Treatment
Nanobubble Oxygenation
Injects billions of gas nanobubbles into the water column with high surface area and low rise velocity.
Rapid Dissolved Oxygen (DO) uplift
Supports aerobic biodegradation
Low energy consumption
FBG Biofilm Modules
Facultative Bacteria Generator (FBG) modules provide a surface for attached-growth biofilms.
High surface-area for biofilm attachment
Provides anoxic conditions to denitrify
Resilience to hydraulic shock loads

title: About Us - IIT Ropar TIF (AWaDH)
text:
The Indian Institute of Technology Ropar
(IIT Ropar), established in 2008 by the
Ministry of Education
,
Government of India
, is one of the country’s premier institutions of national importance. Renowned for its academic excellence, research-driven approach, and innovation ecosystem, IIT Ropar has rapidly advanced in national and international rankings.
It is ranked
12th
among all engineering institutes in India (2025), according to the Indian Institutional Ranking Framework, and placed
22nd
in NIRF Engineering Rankings (2024). Globally, it has been featured in the
801–1000 band
in the
Times Higher Education (THE)
World University Rankings and listed in the
QS Asia 351–400
bracket.The institute offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs across engineering, sciences, and interdisciplinary domains, with a strong emphasis on cutting-edge research and global collaboration.
is recognized for its focus on sustainability, deep-tech innovation, and rural transformation. It is home to several Centres of Excellence, and significant agritech initatives including the
ANNAM.AI
CoE by
Ministry of Education
and iHub – AWaDH under the
DST’s NM-ICPS program
, driving research and startup ecosystems in agriculture, water, and allied technologies. With a dynamic faculty, world-class infrastructure, and a growing international footprint,
is shaping the future of innovation and nation-building.
About iHub – AWaDH
The IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation (iHub – AWaDH) is a national deep-tech hub established under
DST’s NM-ICPS
Mission with an initial support of ₹110 Cr ($13.2M USD). Driving innovation at the intersection of Agritech, Water, and CPS, iHub – AWaDH has mobilized over ₹200 Cr (~$24M USD) through partnerships with
Startup India
,
MeitY
,
HDFC Bank
,
Dassault Systèmes
, and others.
It has incubated 150+ startups, facilitated ₹120 Cr+ (~$14.5M USD) in overall funding, and enabled 10,000+ startups through training and CPS labs. Recognized as the
Most Promising Agritech Innovation Hub
(2022 onwards by 08+ National agencies), iHub – AWaDH is shaping
India’s deep-tech ecosystem
through research, entrepreneurship, and impactful collaborations.

title: Privacy Policy - IIT Ropar TIF (AWaDH)
text:
Privacy Policy for IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation (iHub – AWaDH)
Who we are
Suggested text:
Our website address is: https://ihub-awadh.in.
Comments
Suggested text:
When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.
An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.
Media
Suggested text:
If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.
Cookies
Suggested text:
If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.
If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.
When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select “Remember Me”, your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.
If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.
Embedded content from other websites
Suggested text:
Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.
These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.
Who we share your data with
Suggested text:
If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.
How long we retain your data
Suggested text:
If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.
For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.
What rights you have over your data
Suggested text:
If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.
Where your data is sent
Suggested text:
Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.
About AWaDH
IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation (“we”, “our”, “us”) respects your privacy and is committed to protecting it. This Privacy Policy explains our policies and practices regarding the information we collect from and about you. By using our website (https://ihub-awadh.in/), you agree to the terms of this Privacy Policy.
Information About Website and Org:
This Privacy Policy applies to our website, related mobile websites, and applications (collectively, “Site”), which are owned and operated by IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation. The purpose of our Site is to provide visitors with information about our initiatives, allow for the ability to receive and process donations, facilitate networking, update contact information and communication preferences, share stories and feedback, and continuously improve upon our programs and services.
Information We Collect from and About You
Information You Provide to Us
“Personally identifiable information” is information that identifies you as an individual, such as your name, street address, telephone number, email address, and billing information. We will not collect any personally identifiable information unless you voluntarily provide it to us. If you choose not to provide this information, you can still access most of the Site, but some functionalities may not be available.
We may collect personally identifiable information when you join or update your information, make a donation, or participate in Site activities.
Information We May Collect Automatically
“Non-personally identifiable information” is information that does not identify you on an individual basis. This may include Site activity information such as pages visited, time spent on the Site, clicks per page, mouse movements, scrolls, page views, and events. We may also collect anonymous information such as zip codes, IP addresses, and aggregate data from surveys.
Tools We Use to Collect Non-Personally Identifiable Information
We use various tools to collect non-personally identifiable information, including:
Cookies: Small text files stored on your device to enhance your browsing experience. We use session cookies (temporary) and persistent cookies (remain until they expire or are deleted).
Conversion Pixels and Tags: Help us track page views and interactions
Web Beacons and Pixel Tags: Used in emails to track open rates and other metrics.
Session Logs: Track visitor navigation and usage patterns.
Social Media Integrations: May track aggregate sharing activity.
If you access our Site via a mobile device or through QR Codes, we may collect additional non-personally identifiable information such as service provider, operating system, unique device identifier, geolocation data, and transactional information.
How We Use Your Information
We may use the information collected from and about you to:
Fulfill user requests (e.g., account creation, marketing materials, newsletter preferences).
Create an online directory.
Respond to comments or information requests.
Contact you about promotions, programs, or communications from IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation.
Track and analyze Site usage and engagement.
Develop new products or services.
Contact you regarding donations.
Generate analytics to improve Site layout, content, offerings, and services.
Make inferences about your interests.
Comply with legal requirements.
Compile aggregate and statistical data for website design and popular features.
Sharing Your Personally Identifiable Information
We do not share, sell, or rent personally identifiable information with unaffiliated entities without your permission. Service providers, contractors, or subcontractors with access to your information are required to keep it confidential and use it only for the services they provide to us.
Access To and Control Over Your Personally Identifiable Information
To correct, update, or delete your personally identifiable information, contact us using the information in the “Contact Us” section below. We will process your request as soon as reasonably possible. This access is limited to information stored in our database for this Site.
Security of Your Information
We use reasonable administrative, technical, personnel, and physical measures to safeguard your information from loss, unauthorized use, and alteration.
Consent to Processing
By visiting our Site and providing your information, you consent to the collection, use, processing, transfer, and disclosure of your information globally, including in countries with different privacy protections than your own.
Links to Other Sites
Our Site contains links to other websites. We are not responsible for the privacy practices or content of other sites. We encourage you to review the privacy policies of any linked sites.

IIT Ropar played a key leadership role at Bharat Innovates 2026, leading the Agri & Food Technologies theme and showcasing India’s growing capabilities in research-driven deep-tech innovation, technology commercialisation, entrepreneurship, and global collaboration.
Conceptualised by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, Bharat Innovates 2026 marked an important milestone in India’s deep-tech journey, bringing together Higher Education Institutions, startups, investors, industry leaders, research organisations, and global innovation partners. The global showcase in Nice, France, provided an international platform for Indian technologies and startups to connect with investors, corporates, and research ecosystems worldwide.
The event was jointly inaugurated by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and French President H.E. Mr. Emmanuel Macron, highlighting the growing India–France partnership built on trust, technology, and a shared vision for the future.
The impact of Bharat Innovates 2026 reflected growing global confidence in India’s innovation ecosystem, with USD 254.5 million in funding commitments, 30+ strategic partnerships and agreements, participation from 2,000+ stakeholders across 29 countries, engagement with 500+ French investors, 1,350+ business meetings, showcasing of 80+ deep-tech startups, 40+ investor follow-up commitments, and collaboration with 50+ French and European universities, incubators, and research institutions.
As the lead institution for the Agri & Food Technologies theme, IIT Ropar, through iHub-AWaDH, a Technology Innovation Hub under NM-ICPS, DST, Government of India, and ANNAM.AI Foundation, the Centre of Excellence for AI in Agriculture supported by the Ministry of Education, showcased advanced deep-tech solutions focused on AI-enabled agriculture, precision farming, biodiversity monitoring, climate intelligence, cyber-physical systems, and sustainable resource management.
The IIT Ropar ecosystem showcased pioneering technologies, including the Biodiversity Sensor and the Cyber Physical System Plug-and-Play Laboratory. The CPS ecosystem enables experiential learning and innovation in embedded systems, IoT, automation, sensing, and cyber-physical technologies, supporting the establishment of 28 laboratories across 12 States and Union Territories and strengthening technology learning capabilities across HEIs.
Beyond agriculture and water technologies, IIT Ropar has built a multidisciplinary deep-tech innovation ecosystem through its incubators. iHub-AWaDH focuses on agriculture, water, AI, climate, and sustainability-driven innovations, while the Technology Business Incubator Foundation, IIT Ropar, supports startups across advanced manufacturing, mobility, healthcare, clean technologies, and emerging technologies.
Startups from the IIT Ropar ecosystem also represented India’s innovation potential on the global stage. Inphlox Water Systems Pvt. Ltd., supported by iHub-AWaDH under the HDFC CSR programme, showcased its ElectroX technology for sustainable water solutions. GudLyf Mobility, supported by IIT Ropar TBIF, presented indigenous Type IV high-pressure composite cylinders for hydrogen and CNG storage applications, highlighting advancements in clean mobility technologies.
A landmark outcome of Bharat Innovates 2026 was the launch of the Industry Innovation Bridge by Hon’ble Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India. Recognising IIT Ropar’s contribution towards innovation and technology translation, IIT Ropar has been entrusted with chairing the Industry Innovation Bridge, which will connect corporates, investors, startups, and HEIs to accelerate technology validation, commercialisation, and global scaling of Indian innovations.
Through its participation in Bharat Innovates 2026, IIT Ropar reaffirmed the role of Higher Education Institutions as engines of innovation, bridging the gap between research and industry. By integrating research, incubation, intellectual property support, industry partnerships, and market linkages, IIT Ropar continues to nurture young innovators and build globally relevant deep-tech solutions.
Bharat Innovates 2026 reflects India’s transition from technology adoption to technology creation, with IIT Ropar contributing significantly towards building a sustainable, scalable, and globally competitive deep-tech ecosystem.

title: PM VIKAS Scheme - IIT Ropar TIF (AWaDH)
text:
IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation Signs MoU with Ministry of Minority Affairs under the PM VIKAS Scheme
We are excited to announce the formalization of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between IIT Ropar Technology and Innovation Foundation and the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India under the PM VIKAS Scheme. This collaboration marks a significant milestone in providing advanced, fully sponsored skill development opportunities for 1,200 minority youth across Punjab — empowering them with the skills required to thrive in emerging technological sectors.
Program Overview
This partnership focuses on industry-aligned skill training, designed to enhance the employability of youth through technology-driven education. By offering Fully funded hands-on training in high-growth sectors, the program aims to prepare participants for future-ready roles that meet the current demands of the job market. The training focuses on practical skill acquisition that directly connects participants with job opportunities — improving both individual livelihoods and the broader economic landscape — without placing any financial burden on the participants or their families.
Program Objectives
Enhancing Employability:
Participants will receive training in technologically advanced sectors, ensuring they are equipped with the practical skills required by industries such as precision farming, drone technology, automotive manufacturing, and IT technical support.
Promoting Entrepreneurship:
In addition to technical training, the program also emphasizes entrepreneurial development, enabling youth to start their own ventures and contribute to the local economy by offering self-employment opportunities.
Facilitating Livelihood Generation:
By integrating participants into market and credit linkages, the program provides essential resources to help participants transition from training to sustainable employment or business ownership, ensuring economic stability and financial inclusion.
Specialized Training Domains
The programme includes specialized, fully sponsored training in the following domains:
Precision Farming Technician
Participants will gain expertise in smart agriculture technologies, including IoT, data-driven crop management, and automation systems, making them proficient in modern agricultural practices.
Junior Engineer –

Drone (R&D)
This module offers aerial systems design training, focusing on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and remote sensing applications in industries such as agriculture, surveying, and infrastructure monitoring.
Automotive Welding Machine Operator
The program will focus on advanced welding technologies critical for the automotive manufacturing industry, providing participants with the skills to operate and maintain automated welding systems and other precision tools.
IT Technical Support Executive
This domain prepares participants for roles in network management, system integration, and IT troubleshooting, catering to the growing need for skilled professionals in the digital infrastructure space.
Training Delivery
Industry-Relevant Curriculum
The training curriculum has been developed in collaboration with industry experts to ensure it meets the current and future needs of the job market. The focus is on delivering hands-on, real-world training, providing participants with a comprehensive understanding of their chosen domain.
Training Centres Across Punjab
Training will be delivered at strategically located centres across Punjab, providing easy access to youth from diverse backgrounds. These centres are equipped with state-of-the-art facilities to ensure immersive learning experiences and industry-standard education.
Impact and Vision for Viksit Bharat @2047
The PM VIKAS Scheme is far more than a training programme. It is a transformational, government-supported initiative to build a skilled, self-reliant workforce that contributes to India’s economic growth. By focusing on technology-driven skill development, this initiative supports the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision—building an empowered, innovation-driven economy.
Through capacity-building and competency-based skill development, we are helping to create a workforce that is ready to meet the technological challenges of the future. This initiative will also contribute to achieving the national goal of a self-reliant India by creating highly skilled professionals across diverse sectors.

Decoupled Crop Surveillance
Receiving information is the key to a cyber-physical system, and particularly important for crop surveillance and monitoring systems. The sensors capture environmental, crop, and activities taking place on the farm. The goal of this project is to decouple the sensing infrastructure from farms and provide surveillance as a service using modern sensors such as UAV, Satellite, Robots, etc.
Big Data Analytics with AI/ML
Due to the enormous spatial size of the farmland and regular interval of data-sensing makes the big data analytics challenging and costly. The overall cost includes the cost of storage, transmission, and computing resources. The goal of this project is to build affordable AI/ML solutions to help farmers in agriculture automation, decision support, precision agriculture, and market analysis.
Web platform and HCI
Farmers are not technology savvy. Most of the farmers find it difficult to use technological devices. In developing countries, farmers may even not be familiar with the English language. The aim of this project it to build human-computer-interface (HCI) that are farmer-friendly. Particularly we intend to consider the local culture in choosing the interface modality and structure.
Sustainable Hardware
Due to the vast fields, replacing batteries in sensors, wireless devices, and micro-controllers is a challenging task. Therefore, it is beneficial that battery requirements are minimized in computational and sensor devices deployed on the field. However, the state of the art of AI/ML algorithms have a huge computational requirement. Therefore, we aim to build custom electronic hardware solutions that are cheap efficient, specifically for precision agriculture and monitoring tasks.

title: Past Activities | Women's Forum
text:
Inspiring the Next Generation of Women in Science

The Women’s Forum at Indian Institute of Technology Ropar proudly organized a vibrant celebration of the International Day of Women and Girls in Science on 11 February 2026, bringing together enthusiastic school students, faculty members, industry leaders, and distinguished guests for an engaging and meaningful experience.The event aimed to foster curiosity, confidence, and aspiration among young girls by exposing them to diverse scientific fields and real-world applications. The program featured a range of interactive and intellectually stimulating activities, including:

A dynamic science project exhibition presented by school students, showcasing creativity and innovation
Expert talks on emerging and impactful domains, such as Artificial Intelligence by Dr. Abhilasha Nanda in modern transportation, and Game Theory in decision-making strategies by Dr. Shweta Jain
Hands-on interactive sessions in Optics, Robotics, and Aeromodelling, encouraging experiential learning by the Optica Society and the Robotics Club, respectively.
A thought-provoking short play by ‘Undekha’ The Drama Club of the Institute, highlighting the resilience, challenges, and achievements of women in science.

The event was graced by esteemed dignitaries, including Dinesh Siddaiah (Officiating Registrar), Radhika Trikha (CEO, Ihub-AWaDH), and Geeta Yadav (Chairperson, Women Forum). Their insightful addresses emphasized the critical role of institutional support, mentorship, and industry collaboration in empowering young women to pursue careers in STEM.

The Women’s Forum extends its sincere appreciation to the Optica Club, Robotics Club, Aeromodelling Club and Undekha Club for their enthusiastic participation and for inspiring students through live demonstrations and interactive engagement.

As we approach National Women’s Day, commemorating Sarojini Naidu, the event served as a powerful reminder of the longstanding contributions of Indian women in leadership, research, and innovation.

The overwhelming enthusiasm and participation of young students reaffirm a shared vision: the future of science is inclusive, diverse, and bright.

International Women’s Day Celebration 2026

08–12 March 2026 | Theme: “Give to Gain”

The Women’s Forum, IIT Ropar, successfully organized a five-day International Women’s Day Celebration from 08 to 12 March 2026, centered around the theme “Give to Gain.” The event was thoughtfully designed to promote empowerment through participation, awareness, wellness, innovation, and collective engagement across the institute community. The celebration witnessed enthusiastic participation from faculty members, students (both female and male), staff, and women’s safety and security personnel, making it a truly inclusive and vibrant initiative.

The celebration commenced on 08 March 2026 with an energetic Sports Day at the Sports Complex, aimed at promoting women’s fitness and encouraging active participation. The day featured a range of activities, including athletics such as the 100-meter race, fun races like the lemon-spoon race, hope race, and reverse race, along with tug of war and women’s cricket. The event fostered a spirit of teamwork, enthusiasm, and healthy competition among participants.

On 09 March 2026, the focus shifted towards holistic well-being through the session titled “Move to Empower – Chakra Healing & Aerobics for Wellness” held at the Spiral Ground. The chakra healing session was conducted by Ms. Amrit Varsha, a Nadi Shodhan practitioner, who guided participants towards achieving balance and inner harmony. This was followed by an aerobics session led by Ms. Yogita Saini, a certified fitness trainer, which energized participants and emphasized the importance of physical fitness. Together, these sessions highlighted the significance of mental and physical well-being.

The third day, held on 10 March 2026, was dedicated to innovation, awareness, and creative expression, and took place at the Auditorium Foyer and Senate Hall. The event featured a Rangoli and Mandala Art Competition based on the theme “Give to Gain.” This competition saw enthusiastic participation not only from IIT Ropar but also from Government College, Ropar, fostering inter-institutional collaboration, with participants from both institutions winning prizes. The event was graced by the presence of Dr. Kailash Chandra Jeena, Hon’ble Dean FAA, IIT Ropar. A keynote address was delivered by Ms. Jeya Shanthi, Director of the DRDO–Industry–Academia Centre of Excellence at IIT Delhi, on the topic “Women at the Frontiers of Defence Technology.” The day also included a cyber awareness talk titled “Stay Safe, Stay Strong,” delivered by Dr. Geeta, Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Ropar. Furthermore, a panel discussion on “Women Who Lead & Heal” brought together experts from academia, healthcare, and counselling, offering valuable insights into leadership, resilience, and well-being. The day was successfully integrated with knowledge sharing, creativity, and awareness.

On 11 March 2026, the fourth day of the celebration focused on mental well-being and personal safety. A meditation session by Heartfulness, conducted by Ms. Rajwinder Kaur from the Heartfulness Centre, Kharar, helped participants experience mindfulness and inner calm. This was followed by a self-defence workshop conducted by Ms. Jayanti Chatterjee, a certified martial arts trainer and black belt in Taekwondo and Karate. The workshop equipped participants with practical self-protection techniques, enhancing their confidence and sense of security.

The celebration concluded on 12 March 2026 with the grand finale titled “Shine to Rise” – a Talent Show and Valedictory Ceremony held in the Auditorium. The event featured a vibrant fashion showcase, solo and group dance performances, and singing performances that highlighted the diverse talents of participants. Special interactive activities involving children and their fathers added a unique and heartwarming dimension to the program. The audience also enjoyed fun games during the event, including a lively gol gappa competition. The event concluded with a prize distribution ceremony recognizing excellence, creativity, and enthusiastic participation, leaving the audience with a sense of joy and accomplishment.

A key highlight of the celebration was its broad, inclusive participation. Notably, the women’s safety and security staff also participated enthusiastically and secured prizes in various events, including sports, rangoli, mandala art, and talent competitions, reflecting the true spirit of inclusivity, empowerment, and recognition.Overall, the five-day celebration successfully embodied the essence of “Give to Gain,” fostering a culture of inclusivity, empowerment, and collective growth within the institute. It provided a meaningful platform for participants to engage, learn, express themselves, and celebrate the contributions of women across diverse domains, ranging from science and technology to wellness and creative arts. The Women’s Forum extends its sincere gratitude to the Hon’ble Director, IIT Ropar, the Institute Administration, faculty members, participants, organizers, and volunteers for their continuous support and encouragement in making this event a grand success.
International Day for Women and Girls in Science, IIT Ropar and INYAS event, 9th-Feb-2024

With more than 700 school students from Punjab area IIT Ropar in collaboration with Inyas organised the international day for women and girls in science on 9th February with special talks from role models Like Dr. Bhavneet Bharti, Dr. Anindita Bhadra, Ms. Vaishakha Poundarik, Dr. Shweta Jain and Dr. Neha Sardana, they presented various career paths to choose from in medical, science, sports and engineering. It was attended by more than 700 students from the Punjab region.

International Women’s Day 2024, IIT Ropar and INYAS event, 3rd to 5th March 2024
Celebration of an unforgettable 3-day International Women’s Day festivity at IITRopar!
Day 1 kicked off with high energy as we grooved to exciting aerobics fit dance led by the enthusiastic Ms. Yogita. We also learned essential self-defense techniques from the skilled Mr. Chand, and improved our tennis game under the guidance of Ms. Vishakha. The day continued with thrilling matches of tug of war, kho kho, and 7 stones, bringing together students, faculty, staff, and their families for a fun-filled Sunday.
On Day 2, we collaborated with INYAS to engage students in thought-provoking poster, slogan, and rangoli competitions.
Inspirational talks from the esteemed Padma Shri Janak ji on Sustainability and by former DST Scientist S K Varshney about gender equality, left us all inspired. The day culminated in captivating performances by the talented IIT Ropar community, followed by heartwarming prize distributions.
Finally, Day 3 started with welcome note by Director IIT Ropar, talk on zero waste life by Padma Shri Janak Paltana McGilligan followed by talk on Creating Gender Sensitive Environment at Higher Education Institutions by advocate Rajesh Gill and Stress management techniques by Doc D. Basera. The 3 day extravaganza of celebrating women and inspiring inclusion ended with vote of thanks by chair women’s forum Dr. Neha Sardana.

International Day for Women and Girls in Science, IIT Ropar and INYAS event, 10th-Feb-2023

With more than 150 school students from Ropar area, Invited Talk by Dr. Sunita Mishra, Sr. Principal Scientist, Materials Science and Sensor Applications, CSIR-CSIO and by Prof. Keya Dharamvir, Dept. of Physics, PU and SPSTI

International Women’s Day 2023, IIT Ropar and INYAS event, 2nd March 2023

Women’s forum Indian Institute of Technology, Ropar in collaboration with INYAS celebrated #InternationalWomenDay2023 with plethora of activities and lectures by eminent speakers. The guest of honor, Dr. SARMISHTHA BHATTACHARYA talked about the Cyclotron to probe nuclei and it’s applications. Doctor Lipika Gautam, discussed the Antibiotic Resistance: The road to post-antibiotic era. Doctor Subina Narang shared about Retinopathy of prematurity followed by Poster making, slogan writing and Rangoli making competitions for all students. Ms. Anita Budhiraja, of NIELIT discussed on the topic, Women Empowerment by skill development followed by a talk of Ms. Arvinder Kaur, on Women Nutrition and Health. The day was concluded by giving prizes to the winners from events carried on 10th Feb and 2nd March 2023.

Post covid the events started again in 2022 with Dr. Manju Khan as the Women’s Forum Chairperson and Dr. Neha Sardana as the event coordinator. International Women’s Day 2022 was celebrated in the esteemed presence of Dr. Rajeev Ahuja, Director IIT Ropar on 8th March 2022.
