For Recruiters

A collection of resources for companies to recruit at IIT Ropar.

RECRUITMENT TIMELINE
PROCEDURE
PLACEMENT POLICY
INTERNSHIP POLICY
FACILITIES
INDUSTRY LYNK
RESOURCES
Recruitment Timeline
Procedure
Engage with Placement Coordinators

Initiate the recruitment process by connecting with our Placement Coordinators for comprehensive guidance, scheduling, and support.
Contact via Email | Phone | Placement Portal

Submit Registration Forms and Job Descriptions

Complete the Internship Notification Form (INF) and/or Job Announcement Form (JAF), detailing your company profile, job responsibilities, compensation, location, and eligibility criteria. Please attach comprehensive job descriptions for each role.

Access Curated Student Profiles

Following approval, receive a curated database of eligible and interested candidates aligned with your specified requirements, including resumes, academic records, and relevant skills.

Conduct Pre-Placement Presentations and Assessments

Organize Pre-Placement Talks (PPTs) to acquaint candidates with your organization, culture, and opportunities. These sessions may be held virtually or on-campus. Subsequent assessment rounds may be conducted as per your selection process

Candidate Shortlisting

Shortlisting will be based on assessment outcomes and/or resume evaluations. The placement office will be notified of the selected candidates.

Interviews and Final Selection

Conduct interviews encompassing technical, HR, and managerial evaluations. Final selection outcomes will be communicated following completion of the interview process.

Placement Policy

The placement drive will be conducted as per the slot system, the SOPs are as follows:

a) Slot System

The placement process will follow a slot-based schedule (e.g., Day 0.0, 0.1, etc.), spanning 2–5 days based on the number of participating companies.

b) Pre-Interview Rounds

Coding tests and assessments will be conducted before the interview day.

c) Preference Order
Students must submit a daily preference order for scheduled companies.
An offer from a higher-preference company excludes the student from all lower-preference interviews.
An offer from a lower-preference company allows participation in higher-preference interviews.
If no preference is submitted, the first offer received is considered final.
d) Scheduling Conflicts

CDPC will assist in resolving interview clashes, but students must choose if rescheduling isn't possible.

e) Application Rules

Students may choose which companies to apply to. However, certain companies may be made mandatory by CDPC leadership.

f) Interview Eligibility

Students may appear for multiple interviews until they receive and accept a full-time offer as per the placement rules. Once an offer is accepted, the student will exit the placement process.

Internship Policy
Slot System: The internship drive will follow a slot-based schedule over 2–3 days, with sub-slots (e.g., Day 0.0, 0.1, 0.2) based on the number of participating companies.
Assessments: Coding rounds and tests will be conducted before the scheduled interview slots.
Preference Order:
Students must submit a daily preference list for companies.
Selection by a higher-preference company removes eligibility for lower-preference interviews.
Selection by a lower-preference company still allows participation in higher-preference interviews.
If no preferences are submitted, the first offer received will be considered final.
Interview Conflicts: CDPC will attempt to resolve scheduling clashes. If not possible, students must choose one company to proceed with.
Eligibility: Students may appear for interviews until they receive and accept an internship offer, after which they exit the process.
Application Flexibility: Students may apply to companies of their choice unless participation is made mandatory for specific companies or student groups by CDPC leadership.
Note:
In cases where interviews for multiple companies are scheduled concurrently, the CDPC SPOCs will make every effort to coordinate and resolve scheduling conflicts. However, if a company is unable to accommodate a rescheduling request, the student will be required to make a definitive choice regarding which company's interview process to participate in.
Facilities
Transport Assistance: Pickup services available from Chandigarh and Amritsar Airports and Railway Stations, as well as Ropar Railway Station, upon prior intimation.
Accommodation: On-campus lodging for the recruitment panel is available at the Visitors' Guest House (subject to availability).
Interview Infrastructure: Well-equipped seminar and conference rooms are available for group discussions and personal interviews.
Presentation Venues: A centrally air-conditioned auditorium and multimedia-enabled lecture halls with high-speed Wi-Fi are available for Pre-Placement Talks (PPTs), workshops, assessments, and other recruitment activities.
Virtual Engagement: Facilities for teleconferencing and video conferencing are readily available to support remote interactions.
Digital Access: Recruiters are provided access to a robust and efficient placement management system for streamlined viewing of student profiles and coordination of hiring processes.
Student Assistance: Dedicated student volunteer teams offer 24/7 support throughout the recruitment process.
Local Hospitality: Local sightseeing and hospitality arrangements can be organized upon request.
Professional Coordination: The placement process is managed by a committed team of experienced professionals, ensuring seamless coordination and support.
Industry LYNK

Industry LYNK is a flagship initiative at IIT Ropar, held annually to foster synergy between academic excellence and industry innovation. The event serves as a dynamic platform for strategic dialogue, collaboration, and student engagement with industry leaders across core and non-core sectors.

About Industry LYNK 2026

Industry LYNK 2026 is the flagship industry-academia interface event hosted by IIT Ropar. This one-day immersive experience fosters meaningful engagement between students, faculty, and industry leaders.

Industry Lynk is designed to
Collaborate with Pioneers

Network with top industry leaders, researchers, and innovators.

Drive Impactful Change

Our Strategic Focus Areas

IIT Ropar is positioning itself as a future-ready, industry-aligned institution. Industry LYNK 2025 will explore opportunities and innovation at the intersection of these four verticals:

Artificial Intelligence

Exploring how AI and data are transforming operations, decision-making, and value creation.

Sustainability

Focusing on sustainable industrial innovation that aligns with global and national imperatives.

Future of Workforce

Addressing how automation, upskilling, and workplace innovation are redefining workforce strategies.

Industry 4.0

Investigating how digitalization, IoT, and smart systems are reshaping the industrial value chain.

In this capacity, she conceptualizes and steers initiatives to synergize the science, technology, and innovation (STI) ecosystem across northern states. With a Ph.D. in Microbiology and academic experience at Punjab Agricultural University, she brings over two decades of leadership in advancing science, technology, and sustainable development.

Previously, Dr. Arora served as the Executive Director of the Punjab State Council for Science and Technology, the apex body for promoting S&T in the state, as well as Member Secretary of the Punjab Biodiversity Board and CEO of the Punjab Research & Innovation Council. She has spearheaded landmark initiatives including the State Action Plan on Climate Change 2.0 for Punjab, Mission Innovate Punjab to strengthen the STI ecosystem, and multifaceted programs for women’s empowerment, rural development, and environmental sustainability. She also led the Punjab State Climate Change Knowledge Centre and actively supported innovators on IPR protection and cleaner technologies.

Dr. Arora’s contributions have been recognized nationally and internationally. She is a recipient of the National Award for Women’s Development through Application of Science & Technology conferred by the President of India, the Punjab Sarkar Parmaan Patra for exemplary service in S&T, the Gr8 Women Award in Science & Technology from the Indian Television Academy, and the SDG Action Award 2020 for Environmental Sustainability from UNDP and the Government of Punjab. A retired officer of the Indian Police Service (1987 batch, Punjab cadre), Mr. Gupta served in senior leadership roles including Director General of the National Investigation Agency and Director General of Police, Punjab. Over his 37-year career, he was at the forefront of national security and counter-terrorism, from leading operations during Punjab’s insurgency in the late 1980s to overseeing VVIP security at the Intelligence Bureau, and later directing intelligence and law enforcement in Punjab. About the Medical Center – IIT Ropar

The Health Center at IIT Ropar is dedicated to promoting the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of all members of the campus community, including students, faculty, and staff. Our mission is to provide accessible, high-quality, and compassionate healthcare services that support the overall health and success of the institute’s members.

We offer a comprehensive range of integrated services such as general medical care for common illnesses and minor injuries, preventive health check-ups and screenings to support long-term wellness, and mental health and counseling services to provide emotional and psychological support. In addition, we conduct health promotion and awareness programs to encourage healthy lifestyle choices and are equipped to provide timely emergency care and first-aid support when needed.

The Health Center operates with the goal of reducing the impact of illness and injury on academic and professional performance by providing timely and effective care. We strive to ensure that your health needs are met efficiently, so you can focus on what matters most—your studies, research, work, and personal growth.

We are here not only to treat illness but to promote a culture of wellness across campus. Whether you need routine care, health advice, or emotional support, the Health Center is your partner in health at IIT Ropar.

title: CRF IIT Ropar
text:
Department Introduction

The Central Research Facility (CRF) is equipped with a vast array of high-end characterization tools, encompassing advanced analytical, spectroscopic, and microscopic techniques. These state-of-the-art facilities enable comprehensive material and sample analysis across diverse scientific disciplines. Open to both internal and external academic researchers, as well as industries and business houses, the CRF provides access to cutting-edge equipment on a payment basis, fostering innovation and collaborative research. To continually enhance our capabilities, we are excited to announce the addition of new advanced instruments, further expanding the scope and depth of research supported at the CRF.

Failed to load image
Lab Objectives
To provide access to sophisticated analytical instruments for academicians, scientists, and other users from academic institutes, R&D laboratories and industries, enabling them to carry out measurements for R&D work.
To organize short-term courses and workshops on the use and application of various instruments and analytical techniques.
To develop new techniques and methods of analysis to maximize the utilization of instruments, thereby exploring new dimensions in various areas of science and technology.
To support sponsored research and consultancy projects.
Vision

To become a premier hub of innovation and excellence in scientific research by providing state-of-the-art analytical and characterization facilities. Our vision is to foster collaborative, multidisciplinary research that drives technological advancement, supports academic pursuits, and empowers industries. We aim to continually upgrade our infrastructure, expand our expertise, and promote a vibrant research ecosystem that contributes significantly to scientific discovery and societal progress.

Mission

* Promote cutting-edge research support * Foster collaboration with academic industries * Develop innovative solutions * Nurture talent * Ensure knowledge dissemination

Seminar on SAXS by Anton Paar

Central Research Facility (CRF), IIT Ropar and Anton-Paar India Pvt. Ltd, organized an expert lecture on “Smal Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS) and its Advancements”. The lecture provided an overview of the principles, applications, instrumentation and recent development in SAXS – a powerful analytical technique for studying materials at nanoscale. Talk highlighted its significance in Materials science (Polymer, Metal Nanoparticles, Composites), Biochemistry, Nanotechnology, and Pharmaceutical research. By measuring the intensity of X-rays scattered at small angles, SAXS provides information about the size, shape, and distribution of particles, pores, and other structural features. SAXS has found widespread applications in various fields, including: * Materials Science: Characterization of polymers, nanoparticles, porous materials, and composites. * Biochemistry: Investigation of protein structure, assembly, and interactions. * Colloid Science: Study of colloidal dispersions, emulsions, and foams. * Nanotechnology: Development and characterization of nanomaterials. * Pharmaceutical Science: Analysis of drug delivery systems and protein-drug interactions. In conclusion, SAXS has become an indispensable tool for researchers studying a wide range of materials and processes at the nanoscale. Continued advancements in SAXS techniques and instrumentation are expected to further expand its applications and contribute to our understanding of the fundamental properties of matter.

The Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) is a powerful instrument for nanometer scale science and technology.

Principle:- The AFM principle is based on the cantilever/tip assembly that interacts with the sample; this assembly is also commonly referred to as the probe. The AFM probe interacts with the substrate through a raster scanning motion. The up/down and side to side motion of the AFM tip as it scans along the surface is monitored through a laser beam reflected off the cantilever. This reflected laser beam is tracked by a position sensitive photo-detector (PSPD) that picks up the vertical and lateral motion of the probe. The deflection sensitivity of these detectors has to be calibrated in terms of how many nanometres of motion correspond to a unit of voltage measured on the detector.

Applications:
1. Materials Science: Obtain 3-D images of surfaces with atomic resolution revealing features like defects, grain boundaries etc.

3. Semiconductors: Providing high-resolution potential profiles of semiconductor devices

Model – XEVO-G2-XS-QTOFEL (Waters) High-resolution MS (HRMS) is rapidly advancing into many fields of modern analytical sciences. Instruments such as Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance (FTICR) and modern orbitrap and TOF systems are now frequently used in laboratories, where only a few years ago traditional quadrupole and ion trap mass spectrometers dominated. In particular, the selective data-acquisition modes of triple quadrupole mass spectrometers (e.g., precursor ion scan or multiple reaction monitoring) are increasingly being replaced by full-scan or MS/MS experiments on HRMS instruments even in quantitative applications, because the information gained from high-resolution, accurate mass data often outweighs the benefits of highly selective measurements on low-resolution mass spectrometers.

Principle:- A mass spectrometer generates multiple ions from the sample under investigation, it then separates them according to their specific mass-to-charge ratio (m/z), and then records the relative abundance of each ion type.
The first step in the mass spectrometric analysis of compounds is the production of gas phase ions of the compound, basically by electron ionization. This molecular ion undergoes fragmentation. Each primary product ion derived from the molecular ion, in turn, undergoes fragmentation, and so on. The ions are separated in the mass spectrometer according to their mass-to-charge ratio, and are detected in proportion to their abundance. A mass spectrum of the molecule is thus produced. It displays the result in the form of a plot of ion abundance versus mass-to-charge ratio. Ions provide information concerning the nature and the structure of their precursor molecule. In the spectrum of a pure compound, the molecular ion, if present, appears at the highest value of m/z (followed by ions containing heavier isotopes) and gives the molecular mass of the compound.

Chemistry and Biochemistry
Pharmaceutical and Drug Development
Forensic Science
Environmental Analysis

A Nanoindenter is the main component for indentation hardness tests used in nanoindentation. Nanoindentation, also called depth sensing indentation or instrumented indentation, gained popularity with the development of machines that could record small load and displacement with high accuracy and precision. The load displacement data can be used to determine modulus of elasticity, hardness, yield strength, fracture toughness, scratch hardness and wear properties.

There are many types of nanoindenters in current use differing mainly on their tip geometry. Among the numerous available geometries are three and four sided pyramids, wedges, cones, cylinders, filaments, and spheres. The material for most nanoindenters is diamond and sapphire, although other hard materials can be used such as quartz, silicon, tungsten, steel, tungsten carbide and almost any other hard metal or ceramic material. Diamond is the most commonly used material for nanoindentation due to its properties of hardness, thermal conductivity, and chemical inertness. In some cases electrically conductive diamond may be needed for special applications and is also available. For precise measurements a laser goniometer is used to measure diamond nanoindenter angles. Nanoindenter faces are highly polished and reflective which is the basis for the laser goniometer measurements. The laser goniometer can measure within a thousandth of a degree to specified or requested angles. Testing Modes:- Quasistatic Nanoindentation Measure Young’s modulus, hardness, fracture toughness and other mechanical properties via nanoindentation. Scratch Testing Quantify scratch resistance, critical delamination forces, and friction coefficients with simultaneous normal and lateral force and displacement monitoring. Nanowear Quantify wear behavior over the nanometer to micrometer length scales as a function of number of sliding cycles, sliding velocity, wear area, and applied force. SPM Imaging In-situ imaging using the indenter tip provides nanometer precision test positioning and surface topography information.

4. SPM Imaging
In-situ imaging using the indenter tip provides nanometer precision test positioning and surface topography information.

PPMS is a powerful instrument for exploring a material’s magnetic, thermal and transport properties under controlled temperature and magnetic field environment.
Principle:- The PPMS works on the principle of creating a precisely controlled environment where a sample can be cooled, heated, and exposed to magnetic fields. It uses a closed-cycle cryocooler to vary temperature and a superconducting magnet to generate stable magnetic fields. As these conditions change, built-in modules measure the sample’s electrical, magnetic, and thermal properties—such as resistivity, magnetization, and heat capacity. Sensitive sensors track how these properties evolve with temperature and field, while the control electronics maintain smooth and accurate sweeps. This allows systematic and reliable study of a material’s behaviour under well-controlled physical conditions.
Applications:
Materials Science: Study magnetic, electrical, and thermal properties to understand phase transitions and structural effects.
Condensed Matter Physics: Explore phenomena like superconductivity, magnetism, and quantum phase behaviour under controlled temperature and field.
Superconductors: Measure critical temperature, critical fields, heat capacity, and magnetic shielding/flux-penetration properties.
Electronic Materials: Perform resistivity, magnetoresistance, and Hall measurements to evaluate charge-carrier behaviour.
Functional Materials: Characterize temperature- and field-dependent responses in thermoelectric, magnetic, and correlated-electron systems.

title: Central Workshop IIT Ropar
text:
Central Workshop

The Central Workshop was established in 2008 in conjunction with the inception of IIT Ropar. IIT Ropar is a constituent institute of the prestigious Indian Institutes of Technology (IIT) system, which has consistently served as a cornerstone of higher technical education in India.

Until 2018, the Central Workshop functioned under the administrative purview of the Department of Mechanical Engineering and operated from the institute’s transit campus. In 2020, it was relocated to the main campus of IIT Ropar, situated on the banks of the Sutlej River.

The Central Workshop is equipped with a comprehensive range of modern machinery and provides state-of-the-art facilities to support teaching, training, research, and development activities. It is staffed by a highly skilled technical team that facilitates project fabrication and the establishment of research infrastructure.

Our Mission

To provide state-of-the-art infrastructure and a conducive environment for students, faculty, and staff to transform conceptual designs into tangible prototypes.

Our Vision

To be a leading center for advanced manufacturing and fabrication, fostering a culture of innovation, practical skills, and interdisciplinary collaboration within IIT Ropar.

💬
Message from the Director
Prof. Rajeev Ahuja

Director, IIT Ropar

"

The Central Workshop stands as a vital pillar of experiential learning, skill development, and technological innovation at IIT Ropar. It provides a sustainable platform where students, researchers, and faculty transform ideas into prototypes and conceptual designs into tangible products. It focuses on supplementing theoretical knowledge with hands-on experience, fostering confidence, innovation, and engineering skills. Equipped with state-of-the-art facilities and guided by experienced technical staff and faculty, the Workshop fosters an ecosystem that encourages design thinking, product development, and translational research.

In an era increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence and advanced technologies, experiential learning has become indispensable. The Central Workshop serves as the cornerstone of such learning, particularly for young engineering students embarking on their academic journey with their first exposure to modern manufacturing systems and precision hand tools. Through structured hands-on training in diverse manufacturing processes, students develop not only technical competencies but also critical life skills—analytical thinking, teamwork, resilience, and innovation—essential for addressing real-world engineering challenges.

The manufacturing sector remains a key driver of national growth, significantly contributing to GDP and generating large-scale employment. As premier technical institutions, IITs carry a profound responsibility to cultivate skilled, competent, and visionary engineers who will lead the transformation of India’s manufacturing landscape. At IIT Ropar, we are committed to nurturing manufacturing leaders who will contribute meaningfully to inclusive growth, technological advancement, and the realization of a self-reliant India. The Central Workshop plays a crucial role in this endeavor, empowering our students with the skills, confidence, and innovative mindset required to meet future challenges and serve the nation with distinction.

"
💬
Message from the Head
Dr. Samir Chandra Roy

Head, Central Workshop

"

The Central Workshop at IIT Ropar is dedicated to serving all stakeholders of the Institute by providing equitable access to all manufacturing facilities through a transparent and hassle-free booking system. Our objective is to create an enabling ecosystem where ideas are transformed into tangible innovations. Our enthusiastic, young, and highly skilled technical team is committed to delivering the highest level of support to students and faculty members. From the initial stages of conceptual design to prototype development and final product realization, we actively assist users in converting their ideas into practical and functional outcomes.

The Central Workshop plays a pivotal role in supporting undergraduate teaching as well as postgraduate and doctoral research across various departments. Multiple laboratory and practical courses are conducted in the workshop, offering students invaluable hands-on experience with state-of-the-art machines and tools. We provide comprehensive infrastructural, facility, and technical support for project work, experimentation, and advanced research activities.

Beyond the Institute, the Central Workshop also extends its facilities and technical expertise to external academic institutions and industries, enabling them to utilize our infrastructure for their prototyping, fabrication, and research needs. This collaboration strengthens industry–academia interaction and promotes innovation beyond campus boundaries. In addition, the Workshop organizes various skill development and vocational training programs for students and working professionals. These programs aim to enhance employability, upgrade technical competencies, and bridge the gap between academic learning and industrial practice.

We are committed to maintaining a safe, inclusive, and healthy working environment. Our practical modules and training activities are thoughtfully designed to cultivate teamwork, foster innovation, and encourage research-oriented thinking. By promoting critical thinking, practical skills, and hands-on learning, the Central Workshop prepares individuals to meet real-world engineering challenges with confidence and competence. The Central Workshop remains steadfast in its pursuit of excellence, innovation, and service to the academic and industrial community.

"

✓
Rings, necklaces(anything that can caught in rotating machinery parts) must be removed before using any machine.
✓
Always wear eye protection and lab coats when using power operated hand or machine tools or while performing physical tasks.
✓
Don't touch any live wire inside the workshop.
✓
In case of fire, the electric supply should be disconnected you must know how to do this.
✓
Make sure that this work does not effect anybody else in the workshop.
✓
Don't bring eatables into the workshop.
✓
Never indulge in reckless behavior in the workshop.
✓
Don't keep any tooling or parts close to the edge of the workbench or table, from where it may fall and injure someone.
✓
Don't lean or rest against any machine.
✓
Don't talk to others while they are operating a machine. Similarly concentrate on your work and don't talk unnecessary while operating machine.
✓
Don't leave tools or work parts on the table of the machine bed even if machine is not in the operation. You must clean the area used by you to prevent injury to others through slipping/falling.
✓
Get first aid immediately for any injury you must always be aware of the location of the first aid box, fire extinguishers etc. Similarly, immediately inform the workshop instructor if anyone else get injured.
Remember
✦

All equipment in the workshop is designed to cut through metal so any such equipment can cut through human body parts very easily if people are careless and violate safety regulations. Hence, students MUST follow all safety rules strictly in order to be allowed to use the workshop. If you observe any violation of safety rules that is happening or about to happen, you MUST take immediate action to prevent it and inform the workshop supervisor.

✦

Non compliance with the above mentioned instructions will be taken very seriously and will lead to imposing a fine along with automatic failure in the course being taken by the student by debarring the student from using workshop for the rest of the semester. The minimum fine for first offense is Rs 100 and will be determined by the workshop supervisor and committee. Under all conditions the decision of the workshop supervisor and committee will be final and binding

✦

In case any tools are found missing a fine consisting of the tool's replacement price plus 10% extra charge on the price of the tool will be imposed on the concerned students.

Note

All workshop rules also apply to the spaces outside the workshop room, where students often work on projects when the workshop is too crowded.

text:
Sheet Metal Shop
ℹ️
About Sheet Metal Shop

The sheet metal implies metal and alloys in sheets rolled to thickness ranging from 10 S.W.G. and thinner. Sheet metal work has its own importance in manufacturing industry and it plays an essential role in various aspects of our day to day needs. The indispensable engineering articles made of sheet metal find their application in agriculture, building construction, house hold, offices, laboratories and shop equipment, heating and air conditioning, transportation, decorative work, toys and many other such areas. Using specialized sheet metal tools the various concepts from development of surface to actual fabrication are practiced. The various operations performed during sheet metal jobs are cutting, rolling, bending, and shaping. Different jobs are seam joint, lap joint, cylinder fabrication, tray fabrication, riveting and soldering applications

title: CoE-SARDS
text:
Our Story & Formation

Building a Legacy of Excellence in Defence and Security
The Centre of Excellence for Studies and Applied Research in Defence and Security (CoE-SARDS) at IIT Ropar was founded with a clear and compelling purpose: to bridge the gap between the Indian Armed Forces, academia, and the defence industry. Recognizing the need for innovation, collaboration, and specialized knowledge, IIT Ropar established CoE-SARDS as a hub for cutting-edge research and development, technical consultancy, and advanced training in defence and security.
Our journey began with the support of the Army Training Command (ARTRAC), which recognized IIT Ropar's potential to address the critical needs of the Armed Forces. Today, we are actively engaged with all three services. Having successfully executed vital defence projects we have established ourselves as a trusted partner in India's Defence Ecosystem to contribute significantly to national defence. Our story is one of growth, commitment and a relentless pursuit of excellence. Guided by distinguished General-ranked officers and supported by a dedicated team of specialized personnel, CoE-SARDS continues to build on its legacy, driving innovation and excellence in every Project we undertake.

Our Vision

Our vision is to lead the charge in making India self-reliant in defence technologies, paving the way for Atma-Nirbharta in defence and security.
At CoE-SARDS, we envision a future where India's defence and security apparatus is strengthened by homegrown research & innovation leveraging technical expertise and industrial collaboration. By nurturing startups and engaging with MSMEs, we are building a robust ecosystem that supports the defence and security needs of India.

Our Aim

A Secure Future Through Innovation
At CoE-SARDS, we aim to be the epicentre of strategic thought, operational excellence and technological innovation, serving as a crucial link between the Armed Forces, Defence Industry and Academia. Our aim is to commercialize defence solutions and R&D to ensure that our Armed Forces get access to cutting-edge technology developed within the country to evolve into a modern, agile, adaptive, technology- enabled, and self-reliant force to meet emerging challenges.

Our Mission
Empowering Armed Forces Through Knowledge and Technology

Our mission at CoE-SARDS is multifaceted.

Engage with defence and security stakeholders, including frontline formations, to understand their challenges and deliver practical and impactful solutions.
Promote and conduct ground-breaking research in defence and security to address critical needs of the Armed Forces.
Provide top-tier consulting and advisory services to Military and Central Paramilitary Organisations, drawing on our extensive technical expertise and strategic insights.
Deliver world-class training to defence and security personnel, leveraging our DGCA-certified drone RPTO centre and other specialized programs.
Foster innovation by collaborating with industry partners and mentoring deep-tech start-ups through the Technology Business Incubator Foundation (TBIF) at IIT Ropar.

OUR STORY
Where Research Meets Real-World Impact

The IIT Ropar Technology Business Incubator Foundation (TBIF) is a Section 8 non-profit established under the NIDHI TBI Scheme.

Our mission is to Enable and Empower. We provide an ecosystem with over 180+ Mentors, including industry stalwarts and senior army veterans.

"Innovation is the key to realizing the dream of 'New India'. We invest in technology to create a self-reliant future."

Our Vision

In order to make India globally competitive and to fulfill the vision of building a self-reliant India, start-ups and innovators play a vital role. The Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan is a chance for Indian start-ups to take charge of the innovations for which we are usually dependent on global suppliers.

Our startups are contributing to the mission by innovating and bringing to market products and services that are world-class yet affordable. They are quick to spot opportunities in adversity and innovate within their limited time and budget to make competitive products.

Our Mission

To catalyze the growth of a vibrant startup ecosystem by empowering entrepreneurs, startups, and researchers with access to advanced technologies, expert mentorship, and strategic funding.

IIT Ropar TBIF is dedicated to nurturing deep tech innovations in key areas such as manufacturing, defense, IoT, AI, and healthcare, with the goal of driving economic growth, technological advancement, and societal impact at both regional and national levels.

IIT Ropar - Technology Business Incubator Foundation, a Section 8 company established under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar), aims to strengthen the startup ecosystem locally and nationally. We are seeking applications for the position of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) responsible for leading the TBIF's operations and positioning the IIT Ropar as a prominent leader in nurturing technology-oriented and engineering startups.

Manage the incubator's daily operations spanning start-ups, MSMEs, academic collaborations, CSR and other activities with support of the incubator's team

title: DRIF | Defence Research and Innovation Foundation
text:
RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT
A Secure Future Through Innovation

Fostering technological innovation with access to cutting-edge technology will enable our Armed Forces to evolve into a modern, agile, adaptive, technology- enabled and self-reliant force to meet emerging challenges.

VIEW PROJECTS
ABOUT DRIF
04 / 04
INSTITUTIONAL MANDATE
Catalyzing Atma-Nirbharta

The Defence Research and Innovation Foundation (DRIF) at IIT Ropar is a premier national-level Section 8 platform. We serve as the critical strategic bridge uniting the Indian Armed Forces, deep-tech academia, and the defence industry.

Operating in close coordination with Indian Defence and Security Forces, we are mandated to converge strategic vision, operational excellence, and technological expertise. We accelerate indigenous capabilities—from rapid prototyping and high-altitude field trials to specialized military training and veteran resettlement.

VISION & MISSION

To achieve excellence in next-generation defence innovation and manufacturing, empowering the convergence of operational supremacy and technological excellence for a secure, self-reliant India.

Strategic Tech Development

Delivering rapid "Lab-to-Land" solutions. Core domains include Autonomous Systems (Drones, AI/ML), Cybersecurity, Battlefield Management, Directed Energy, New Gen Civil Engineering Projects, and Advanced Armour Materials, validated through rigorous high-altitude field trials.

Education & Resettlement

Specialized PhD, MTech in AI and Structural Engineering for Officers. Intensive Management Programs (MDP) and certification courses dedicated to upskilling Armed Forces Personnel for critical in service/post-service technical roles.

Startups & Indigenous Manufacturing

Incubating companies specializing in Command, Control, Communication, Computers Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance (C4ISR), and tactical electronic warfare. Forging MoUs between defence forces and industry to build a robust manufacturing ecosystem.

User-Specific Projects

Addressing distinct mission-critical problem statements directly from the Security Forces. Delivering practical, validated solutions that bridge the gap between operational requirements and deep-tech brilliance.

Armed Forces Engagement

Understanding operational needs and co-developing mission-ready solutions.

Tech Commercialization

Accelerating lab-to-field transition with IP protection and scale-up support.

title: DRIF | Defence Research and Innovation Foundation
text:
Our Team

Meet the visionaries, academics, and veterans driving India's indigenous defence innovation ecosystem.

Board of Directors & Leadership
Prof. Rajeev Ahuja

CHAIRMAN, DRIF & DIRECTOR, IIT ROPAR

At DRIF, our endeavour is to bridge the technology gap for the Defence Forces through IIT Ropar's academic excellence. By aligning IIT's research excellence with the strategic needs of our armed forces, we empower startups and innovators to undertake cutting-edge defence innovation and build dual-use technologies that strengthen national security. Seamlessly aligning with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, our mission is to transform deep-tech ideas into impactful deployable solutions, thereby ensuring Atmanirbharta for India’s defence ecosystem.

Lt Gen SS Mahal

PVSM, AVSM, VSM (RETD) | EX GOC-IN-C ARTRAC | PROFESSOR OF PRACTICE & MANAGING DIRECTOR

Our Vision is to rapidly accelerate technology commercialization and scale defence-tech startups to fulfill the Prime Minister’s vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat. Guided by the ethos of 'Nation First, Always,' our Mission is to provide innovators with critical resources—from specialized labs to strategic defence partnerships. Through this robust ecosystem, our Approach ensures breakthrough innovations transition seamlessly from laboratory concepts to field-ready solutions, driving India’s self-reliance in defence technology.

Mr Virbhadra Singh Rawat

DIRECTOR-DRIF

An experienced individual well versed with the policy formulation, planning and execution especially for Aerospace, Defence and Startups. A public procurements specialist with deep knowledge of finances. Member of various prestigious institutions like Indian Institute of Public Administration(IIPA), United Services Institute (USI) and Manohar Parikar Institute of Defence Studies & Analysis, Delhi. An alumni of National Institute of Financial Management (NIFM), Faridabad and Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, Delhi. Senior Advisor IIT Ropar and Proffesor of Practice IIT Ropar. Senior Advisor Defence & Security with ARTPARK @IISC,Bangalore and Advisor to Board with i-Hub DivyaSampark @IIT, Roorkee. Member Aerospace, Defence & Homeland Security committee at FICCI.

text:
ABOUT DRIF
Advancing
Indigenous Innovation

DRIF, IIT Ropar is a Section 8 Company committed to strengthening India's defence innovation ecosystem. We connect academia, industry, startups, researchers and the Armed Forces.

Backed

Section 8
Company

Multi-Stakeholder
Ecosystem

Focused on
National Security

WHO WE ARE

Translating innovative ideas into deployable defence solutions.

DRIF acts as a catalyst for enhancing India's defence preparedness and technological self-reliance.

We enable the entire innovation lifecycle—ideation, research, development, validation, commercialization and scaling—through collaboration, mentorship, funding support and access to testbeds.

Mission

To strengthen India's defence innovation ecosystem by fostering collaboration among the Armed Forces, academia, industry, startups, and researchers; enabling the development, translation, and commercialization of indigenous technologies; and advancing mission-oriented solutions that enhance national security and strategic self-reliance.

Vision

To be India's premier defence innovation ecosystem, driving self-reliance through cutting-edge, future-ready technologies.

title: Department of Electrical Engineering
text:
Welcome to
Department of Electrical Engineering

Department imparts the knowledge in three programs, a Bachelors programme with a total intake of 60 students per academic year, a Master of Technology and a Doctoral (Ph.D.) programme to upskill technical and research excellence in specialized avenues of Electrical Engineering. thisbaf

Objectives
To upskill the undergraduate and postgraduate students in Electrical Engineering.

The undergraduate program delivers the wide knowledge of Electrical Engineering in four broad areas like communication technology, control technology, electronics, and power & energy. To enhance the students with wide knowledge, the department provides different elective courses which are designed for the interested students. In addition to the undergraduate program, the department plays a vital role to bring forth the world-class postgraduates and researchers. The Masters program provides the students with a strong knowledge of three different areas of Electrical Engineering that are Signal Processing and Communication, Power Engineering and VLSI. There are around 120 research scholars working to solve the challenging problems in different areas of Electrical Engineering. The department always upgrades the experimental and computational facilities for taking up research & development and consultancy activities in various fields so as to produce state-of-the-art research output.

C. C. Reddy
reddy@iitrpr.ac.in
[mobile redacted]





Prof. Reddy did his Bachelor of Engineering in Electrical Engineering from the University College of Engineering, Hyderabad, India in 1995. After his BE, he worked as a faculty in Electrical Engineering at JNTU affiliated institutions, Hyderabad. After his ME & Ph.D. from the Indian Institute of Science (respectively in July 2005 and Jan 2008), Prof. Reddy joined, J-Power Systems Corporation, Hitachi, Japan, a joint venture company of Hitachi Cables Ltd. and Sumitomo Electric Company, and served as a Senior R&D Engineer in its Ultra High Voltage (UHV) research lab till 2011. He contributed to the design of the world's first nanocomposite HVDC power cable during this time (250 kV, between Hokkaido and Honshu). Currently, he is working as a Professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar since 2011) and Head of the Department, Electrical Engineering. He worked as the Dean of International Relations and Alumni Affairs earlier. He is an Associate Editor of IEEE Transactions on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation. He is a member of IEC, member of the Bureau of Indian Standards committee on Dielectrics, member of the Board of Studies of several universities in India. Prof. Reddy participated in academic-industry collaborative research in Japan with several universities of Japan (Toyohashi University; Waseda University; Tokyo City University; Numazu Institute of Technology, etc.). He also participated in the deliberations of the technical standards committee on Space Charge Measurements in dielectric materials. Prof. Reddy has published papers in reputed journals and conferences (IEEE/IET/IEEJ), in the fields of Nano-dielectrics, Power Cables (HVDC/AC), Power Transformers, Bushings; Mechanism of Breakdown, Space Charges, and Conduction in dielectric materials. He has guided fourteen Ph.D. students to their defense and currently guiding twelve Ph.D. students apart from several master's and bachelor students. He had authored a book on “Reliability and Life Estimation of Power Equipment”, with New Age International Publishers. He is working/worked on several projects with private industries like Reliance, Adani, KEI Industries, APAR Industries, Raychem Polymers etc. apart from public industries such as CPWD, CPRI, etc. He has been the Organizing Chair of (IEEE) CATCON 2017, General Chair of IEEE ICIIS 2018 and 2020, General Co-Chair of IEEE ICIIS 2017, 2019 and TPC Chair of CATCON 2020, and International Advisory Member of ISEIM since 2011, being held in Japan. Prof. Reddy has also contributed to the making of the institute by leading on several fronts including technical and non-technical fronts. Starting with faculty-in-charge of the guesthouse, faculty-in-charge of industrial relations, placement cell coordinator, the toughest administrative position "Dean of Student Affairs", with independent charge, and Dean of International Relations and Alumni Affairs. His student affairs deanship tenure saw growth of students from 600 to 2600, shifting campus, a phenomenal increase in student activities, largest student festivals in north India, apart from natural calamities like a flood in the campus and the Covid pandemic ( - all requiring huge time and energy, resulting in a double rate of aging personally).

Dr. Ranjana Sodhi earned her B.Tech degree in Electrical Engineering from NIT Hamirpur, in 2005. She has been active in the field of electrical engineering since 2005. Dr. Sodhi is currently an Associate Professor in the Department of EE at IIT Ropar. Dr. Sodhi's doctoral research work is around the Synchrophasor technology and its applications towards power system state estimation and voltage stability assessment, Power Quality Assessment and Control, Smart Home Automation and Cyber Security of Smart Grids.

I am currently a faculty member in the Department of Electrical Engineering at IIT Ropar and am seeking highly motivated candidates for PhD positions in the broad areas of VLSI DSP systems, FPGA-based system design, and System-on-Chip (SoC) design, along with Hardware Security. The research focus is on efficient algorithm-to-architecture mapping for DSP and emerging workloads, with emphasis on high-performance, energy-efficient, and scalable hardware implementations. This includes the design and optimization of computation architectures for signal processing and AI accelerators, as well as system-level integration in VLSI/SoC platforms and reconfigurable systems. In the domain of hardware security, the work involves the design, analysis, and detection of hardware vulnerabilities, including hardware trojans, with a focus on secure and trustworthy VLSI/SoC architectures. Candidates with additional interest or background in Flexible and Printed Electronics, including thin-film devices and emerging electronic technologies, are also encouraged to apply. Interested applicants are requested to send their CV, and a brief statement of research interests to akumar@iitrpr.ac.in

Prof. Rohit Sharma joined the Electrical Engineering department in 2012, where he is currently a Professor. Before joining IIT Ropar, Prof. Sharma was a post-doctoral fellow at the Interconnect Focus Center, Georgia Tech., Atlanta. He was working under the supervision of Prof. Paul A. Kohl. Prior to this, he worked as a post-doctoral fellow at the Design Automation Lab, Seoul National University, Seoul. He worked under supervision of Prof. Kiyoung Choi. He received the Ph. D. degree from Jaypee University of Information Technology in 2009 in Electronics and Communication Engineering. His Ph. D. supervisor was Prof. A. B. Bhattacharyya - from whom he learned the rudiments of high-speed interconnect design. His current research interests include design of high-speed chip-chip and on-chip interconnects, Graphene based nanoelectronic devices and interconnects, Signal and Thermal integrity in high-speed interconnects and application of Machine Learning in advance packaging and systems. He has been a Visiting Professor at the Small Scale Systems Integration and Packaging Center, Binghamton University (May - Jul 2027), and the Packaging Research Center, Georgia Institute of Technology (Sep 2023 - Feb 2023). He was a Research Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering at The Pennsylvania State University, USA (Mar 2023 - Apr 2024). He is a Distinguished Lecturer of the IEEE Electronics Packaging Society and an Associate Editor to the IEEE Transactions on Components, Packaging and Manufacturing Technology and a referee for several leading IEEE journals. He is a Program Committee member in all major IEEE EPS conferences including ECTC, EDAPS, EPEPS and SPI. He has been the chair of the IEEE CPMT Technical Committee on Electrical Design, Modeling and Simulation. He is a Fellow of the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET), UK and the Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (IETE), India and a Senior Member of the IEEE. Visit our research group website for more details.

He has been working as an Assistant Professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar, Rupnagar, India, since July 2018. title: Department of Chemistry, IIT Ropar
text:
Welcome to
Department of Chemistry

The department of chemistry was established in 2009 to conduct cutting edge interdisciplinary research and impart high quality education in emerging areas of Chemical Science. The department was started with only four faculty members and three PhD students, and has grown significantly in last 14 years. It has 15 regular faculty and has more than eighty PhD students and 8 Post-doctoral fellows.

The department has active research programs in emerging areas like Biomaterials, Biosensors, Catalysis, Drug Delivery, Materials, Organometallic Chemistry, Renewable Energy, Supramolecular Syntheses, Synthetic Organic Chemistry, Theoretical Chemistry, Ultracold Chemistry, etc. The research activities at the department are supported by state-of-the-art research facilities. The department has received funding through several sponsored national and international research projects. The department has published more than 1000 research articles in peer-reviewed journals. The department is visited by experts from India and abroad on a fairly regular basis. The department has active collaboration with universities and institutes in India and abroad.

The department supports the B.Tech. program at the institute. Since its inception, it has offered a Ph.D. degree in Chemistry and since 2015 offered two year MSc Chemistry programme. Every year 25 students join our M.Sc. programme through JAM. The department attracts a large number of summer trainees and masters students from other institutes for short-term research projects.

title: Department of Chemistry, IIT Ropar
text:
Undergraduate Courses

The chemistry department does not offer an undergraduate degree in Chemistry. However, it actively supports the undergraduate programs (B. Tech.) in Computer Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering at the institute. All undergraduate students of this institute are required to do two core courses and a course in Environmental Science and Engineering. Based on their preferences, students may choose one or more electives under the open electives category.

Core Courses
Code Name L-T-P-S-C
CY101 Chemistry for Engineers 3-1-2-6-4

Prerequisite: Nil
Quantum Mechanical principles of structure and bonding in molecules. Reaction rates. Free energy and entropy changes in chemical processes. EMF of galvanic cells, Liquid junction potential. Structure and stereoisomerism. Conformational analysis. Reactivity-acids and bases. Kinetic and thermodynamic criteria of reactions. Electrophilic and nucleophilic substitution reactions. Elimination reactions. Determination of mechanism. Transition metal complexes-crystal field theory, electronic spectra and magnetism. Organometallics-EAN rule, metal carbonyls, metallocenes. Inorganic solid-structure and applications.

Laboratory: Integrated course with an emphasis on experiment design. Focus on measurement techniques and the interpretation of results.

CY230 Introduction to Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry (Chemical Engineering Students only) 3-1-0-5-3

Structure-activity relationships in simple organic molecules; Oxidation: Cr and Mn compounds, peracids, and other peroxides; Reduction: metal hydride, dissolving metal, and hydrazine-based reductions. Cram-Felkin-Anh model; Strategies for C-C bond formation: acyloin, aldol, Cannizzaro, Claisen, Knoevenagel, and benzoin condensations; Carbohydrates: introduction and typical reactions of monosaccharide; Amino acids and peptides: physical properties of amino acids and synthesis of α-amino acids; Role of water and buffers in biological systems; Structure and function of biomolecules- carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, and proteins; Enzyme kinetics (including single molecule enzyme kinetics); Membrane transport and cell signaling; DNA as a hereditary material and genetic engineering; Viruses (including HIV1 infection); and Common metabolic pathways.

GE111 Introduction to Environmental Science and Engineering 3-1-0-6-3

Atmosphere, Composition & Behavior: Gaseous & particulate constituents of the atmosphere, temperature and pressure profile of atmosphere, Atmospheric Photochemistry: Electromagnetic radiations, kinetics of thermal and photochemical processes, Reactions in the upper atmosphere, photo processes in the troposphere, photochemical smog, photosynthesis, Ozone chemistry. Green Chemistry: Principle and applications, green chemical industrial process, sustainable fuel for automobiles and power generation. Air pollution: Standards, effect of air pollutants, origin and fate of air pollutants, atmospheric dispersion, and air pollution control at stationary and mobile sources.

Elective Courses
Code Name L-T-P-S-C
CY Materials Chemistry

Prerequisite: CYL101
Synthesis of molecular, non molecular and composite materials. Characterization techniques. Structure property relationships. Applications-Clean energy, environmental remediation.

CY Measuring Molecules

Prerequisite: CYL101
Spectrosocopy-Radiation matter interactions: UV-Vis: The electromagnetic spectrum, Brief introduction of Emission and Absorption spectra, Ultraviolet and visible radiation, Electronic transitions and the UV spectrum, The Beer-Lambert Law (and deviations from it), Chromophores, conjugation, and auxochromes, Selection rules, Empirical rules for calculating absorption maxima, Shifts in absorption maxima (intensity and wavelength), Steric effects in UV spectra, Light sources, Solution preparation and choice of solvent, Unknown compounds identification. IR: Theory, Bond properties & absorption trends, Mode of Stretching & Bending, Fourier Transformation Spectroscopy, Characteristic group absorptions of organic compounds, Data analysis, Sample preparation. NMR: Nuclear spin state, Magnetic Momentum, Absorption of energy & Mechanism of Absorption (resonance), Population density in nuclear spin state, chemical shift and shielding, Brief introduction of Continuous-Wave (CW) and Pulsed Fourier Transformation, Integration, Local diamagnetic shielding (Electronegativity, Hybridization effects & exchangeable protons), Magnetic Anisotropy, Spin-Spin splitting, Pascal’s Triangle, Coupling constant, brief introduction of 13C NMR, Data analysis with the help of 1H & 13C NMR spectra.

CYL240 Chemistry of Life-An Introduction

Prerequisite: CYL101
Cell: prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell structure, major cell organelles and their function, cell membrane and its function including cell signalling, cell cycle, and programmed cell death. Biomolecules: structure and function of carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, and proteins. Enzymes: classification based on their structure, role as biocatalysts, and enzyme inhibition. Vitamins: types and functions, and their role as coenzymes. Nucleic acids: understanding DNA as a hereditary material, structures of DNA and RNA, concept of gene and genome, basic outline of the central dogma, concepts of replication, transcription, and translation, mutations, viruses, an overview of genetic engineering/biotechnology (recombinant DNA/hybridoma), polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and DNA sequencing. Metabolism: ATP and energy generation, outline of glycolysis, β-oxication, the TCA cyle, de-animation, and the urea cycle.

CY457 Theoretical Chemistry

Prerequisite: CYL101
Born-Oppenheimer approximation, Semi-empirical and Ab initio methods, Molecular dynamics, Variational methods, Hartree-Fock approximations, Self-consistent field method, Restricted and unrestricted Hartree-Fock, Gaussian- and Slater basis functions, Hartree-Fock-Roothaan method, Correlations: Many-body perturbation theory, Configuration interaction and Coupled-Cluster methods, Density-functional theory: Local density approximation (LDA), Hybrid methods, The Mulliken charges, Orbital population, Vibration analysis,Potential energy surfaces and Quantum dynamics, Plane wave formalism.

CY458 Biomaterials

Prerequisite: CYL101; Basic understanding of cells, tissues, and proteins (optional)
Biomaterials, bulk and surface properties of biomaterials and their influence on tissue interface dynamics, classes of biomaterials used in medicine (metals, ceramics, composites, polymers, hydrogels / gels, and biologics), biodegradable biomaterials. Protein adsorption to surfaces, cell and tissue interaction with biomaterials, host responses to biomaterials (inflammation, immunity, systemic toxicity, hypersensitivity, blood coagulation, and tumoriegenesis), concept of biocompatibility. Testing biomaterials in vitro and in vivo. Application of biomaterials in medicine (soft and hard tissue replacement, and drug delivery)

CY459 Biomedical Nanotechnology

Prerequisite: Basic understanding of organic reaction mechanism, stereochemistry of carbon compounds, biomolecules, cells and tissues.
Biomedical Nanotechnology: An introduction to nanotechnology; fabrication and characterization of nanomaterials; quantum dot, carbon-based, magnetic, polymer-based , and bio nanomaterials; advantages of using nanoscale materials; biomedical nanotechnology Biomedical Nanotechnology in Diagnostics: High through put screening (HTPS) and diagnostics; point-of-care (POC) diagnostics; arrays; nanoparticle, quantum-dot, silicon nanowire-based detection systems; DNA biochips; label-free detection. Biomedical Nanotechnology in Therapeutics: Drug delivery; use of quantum dots, carbon nanotubes, and nanoparticles in therapy; polymeric nanoparticles and spheres; polymeric nanoparticles in photodynamic therapy; polymer therapeutics; liposomes; growth of neurons on nanomaterials; nanomaterials for brain protection and repair; nanorobotics for surgery. Biomedical Nanotechnology in Cancer Treatment: Rationale for using nanotechnology in cancer therapy; examples of abraxane and doxil; passive tumor targeting by enhanced permeability and retention effect; active targeting strategies in cancer therapy; multifunctional nanoparticles in cancer therapy; theranostics. Biomedical Nanotechnology in Implants and Prostheses: Implants and prostheses; reconstructive Intervention; biomaterials and biocompatibility; an overview on methods currently used for nanofabrication of implants

Potential risks: Toxicities of nanoparticles and carbon nanotubes; FDA approval, clinical trials, and regulatory pathways for nanoparticle therapeutics.

All Ph. D. students of chemistry department are required to successfully complete course work, as a requirement for their Ph. D. degree. All students, depending on their previous degree, are required to successfully complete a maximum of five courses (equivalent to 15 credits) or minimum of four courses (equivalent to 12 credits) to meet the course requirement of their Ph. D. degree. At the end of course work, students must clear a comprehensive examination (written and oral), which includes component from course work done and his/her research area.

Scholars need to take prior approval from concerned doctoral committee to register the courses.

Welcome to Humanities and Social Sciences Department

The Department offers core and elective courses in Economics, English, Linguistics, Management, and Philosophy across various undergraduate streams. It is a constant endeavor of the department to offer courses that acquaints technical students with the basics of the study of human behavior and society. The Department promotes doctoral programme and research work. The department possesses well-equipped Language Laboratory and a Language & Cognition Lab. The department has state-of-the-art infrastructure with a modern database such as Prowess, States of India, et al. that enables UG and PG students to access the latest macro and micro level data for research. Further, the department provides research publications database such as EBSCO, Science Direct, T&F, Springer, etc. so that the students can stay abreast with latest research happenings around the globe and contribute to the contemporary body of literature in their respective fields. Dedicated faculty members of the department make the environment conducive to a rich academic output. It is the sincere aim of the department to equip the students with skills, knowledge, and values that will help them turn into successful and upright personalities. It works in sync with the technical education provided to the students. However, another transformational change is taking place in terms of implementing a new curriculum for the B.Tech student from 2017 onwards. In this new curriculum, high emphasis is put on Humanities and Social Sciences department wherein many courses have been shifted from an earlier status of elective courses to core courses. Thus, at IIT Ropar, we have recognized the importance of equipping students with not only a hardcore technical knowledge of engineering but also giving a considerable amount of exposure to humanities and social sciences courses that deal with broader socio-economic challenges and humane concerns that reflect and inspire social change.

title: Department of Humanities and Social Sciences
text:
Welcome to
Humanities and Social Sciences Department
Nature and History of the Department

As a Department of Humanities and Social Sciences (HSS) in an Indian Institute of Technology that sets international parameters of academic excellence, this particular department strives to demonstrate its uniqueness and relevance to the vision of an IIT. The thrust of HSS is of course wedded to the visionary remark that Jawaharlal Nehru made while conceptualizing the IITs in the initial years of an independent India: “I know you can measure with your techniques and rules the hardness and strength of this metal or that, of stone and iron and whatnot. … How do you measure the strength of an individual? The human being as material is not only a difficult material but an exciting material because it is a live material, a growing material, a changing and dynamic thing. No two persons are alike and we have to build with that material… [and] function in the environment of India with the material of India… It is important that … engineers advance to become better men and women.” Nehru's remarks need not be taken literally but in their spirit. What matters is his idea of a human being as a living, growing, changing and dynamic material that defies the technoscientific methodology of quantitative measurement. The general disposition of HSS to encounter the challenge of the immeasurable qualities of the human condition constitutes the unique identity of the department. This department had humble beginnings with just a few members in the faculty (5-6) which did not increase beyond 8-9 till three years ago. In an almost sudden spurt of enthusiasm under the leadership of the current Director, it became the most rapidly expanding department with sixteen members of the faculty till date, in seven different disciplines: English Literature, Linguistics, Economics, Psychology, Sociology, Philosophy and Management. This is a phenomenal expansion both in the number of faculty and in the variety of disciplines, both factors essential to the creation of a complete academic department with a composite character.

Vision and Mission

IIT Ropar community has undertaken an important exercise of developing the Mission, Vision and Strategic Plan for the coming years. The exercise was carried out in active consultation with Indian Institute of Management Calcutta who have got technical expertise in this area. A participative bottom up approach was followed in formulating the Mission, Vision and Strategic Plan. Inputs from the entire IIT Ropar fraternity, MHRD, Board of Governors, Alumni and Industries were considered in the process. Finally we have arrived at the following Motto, Mission and Vision statements for our institute. Motto: धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् (Deploy our intellect on the right path) Mission: To foster a transformative learning environment and a culture of excellence enabling creation of knowledge and development of socially responsible, enterprising leaders contributing significantly to national progress and humanity. Vision: To be a trendsetter among the technology universities born in this millennium.

Message From Head of the Department

Welcome to the website of the department of Humanities and Social Science at IIT Ropar!

Department of Humanities and Social Sciences hosts the disciplines of Economics, English literature, Linguistics, and Philosophy. More recently, the department introduced Management as another discipline and various Management courses are now being offered in order to impart leadership skills to our undergraduate B. Tech students. The department is also in the process of introducing courses in other subjects, including Psychology and Sociology.

The department has grown substantially since its inception in the year 2009. The department has gradually come to occupy a unique position in IIT Ropar, an institution of higher learning that focuses on technological research and education. The department provides the students of engineering with skills to understand key Economic concepts, proper training to improve English communication skills, the power to express via Linguistics and English, the ability to appreciate Management and finally to deliberate Philosophically.

Our department continues to draw faculty members with diverse work experiences from the finest institutions in India and abroad. Across disciplines, they offer a wide variety of core and elective courses for undergraduate students in addition to PhD courses for our own graduate students. There has also been an increasing trend in the number of PhD students over the last few years. Our PhD programme is developing towards one of the best among the new IITs. The department has two dedicated labs for teaching and research, and we are planning to introduce more labs in the coming years. The department is also planning to introduce new programs in collaboration with other institutions in India as well as abroad. The department also organizes regular seminars in addition to workshops in various subjects for PhD and postgraduate students.

We aim to considerably expand our teaching as well as research activities in new directions in the coming years and I am sure that we will be immensely successful in addressing the issues that are of local, national, and global character via cutting edge research in the areas of humanities and social sciences. I am confident that in the coming decade the Department of HSS will emerge as one of the most sought after departments of IIT Ropar in terms of academic excellence.

﻿Jai Hind

Further, the department provides research publications database such as EBSCO, Science Direct, T&F, Springer, etc. so that the students can stay abreast with latest research happenings around the globe and contribute to the contemporary body of literature in their respective fields. Dedicated faculty members of the department make the environment conducive to a rich academic output. It is the sincere aim of the department to equip the students with skills, knowledge, and values that will help them turn into successful and upright personalities. It works in sync with the technical education provided to the students. However, another transformational change is taking place in terms of implementing a new curriculum for the B.Tech student from 2017 onwards. In this new curriculum, high emphasis is put on Humanities and Social Sciences department wherein many courses have been shifted from an earlier status of elective courses to core courses. Thus, at IIT Ropar, we have recognized the importance of equipping students with not only a hardcore technical knowledge of engineering but also giving a considerable amount of exposure to humanities and social sciences courses that deal with broader socio-economic challenges and humane concerns that reflect and inspire social change.

Sreekumar Jayadevan
Assistant Professor (Philosophy)
Room CM07, SAB C Tower (top floor), IIT Ropar, Rupnagar, Punjab 140001
sreekumar@iitrpr.ac.in
01881232269
Areas of Interest: Philosophy of technology, Philosophical issues related to technology and existence





I am a philosopher of technology by choice and an environmental humanities researcher somewhat by accident. Trained broadly in analytic philosophy, particularly the metaphysics of science, I spent a good part of my academic life worrying about scientific realism, while reality remained largely unconcerned! Teaching philosophy in engineering institutes gradually turned my attention from what science says about the world to what technology does to it, and to us. My work now centres on philosophy of technology, especially questions of existence, responsibility, and technological rationality. Funded projects and collaborations have meanwhile taken me from metaphysics to forests, elephants, tribal communities, and, more recently, AI data centres. Across these rather unlikely companions, I remain interested in one broad question: **what happens to our ways of living when science and technology reorganize our relationships with the world, with other humans, and with everything that is not human?**

ABOUT

The Research Scholars’ Day at the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences (HSS), IIT Ropar, serves as a vital intellectual crossroads, showcasing the diverse and rigorous inquiry characteristic of the department’s multi-disciplinary landscape. This annual event provides a formal platform for doctoral candidates to present their ongoing research, fostering an environment where specialised studies- ranging from the phonetic intricacies of Linguistics and the critical frameworks of Literature to the empirical modelling of Economics and Management- can engage in a productive cross-pollination of ideas. By bringing together scholars from Psychology, Philosophy, and Cognitive Sciences, the event highlights the department's commitment to both deep disciplinary expertise and the broader socio-cognitive implications of humanistic study. It functions not only as a celebratory milestone for the research community but also as a critical peer-review forum where scholars refine their arguments, methodologies, and presentation skills before an audience of experienced faculty and fellow researchers.

About the Department of Physics

The Department of Physics at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar is engaged in cutting-edge research and high-quality education in various frontier areas of physics including Condensed Matter Physics & Material Science, Gravity & String Theory, Light-Matter Interaction & Quantum Information, Nuclear & Particle Physics.

The department strives to provide excellent training to students through rigorous academic programs, modern laboratories, and collaborative research with national and international institutions. Our mission is to nurture curiosity, develop analytical thinking, and contribute to scientific innovation and technological advancement.

Message from the Head of Department

The Department of Physics at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar is dedicated to excellence in teaching and research, with a focus on advancing fundamental science and fostering technological innovation. Established in 2009, the department has developed into a dynamic academic unit supporting both experimental and theoretical research, along with interdisciplinary studies. The department offers undergraduate, M.Sc., and Ph.D. programs designed to cultivate analytical thinking, scientific curiosity, and research skills. Faculty members are actively engaged in diverse areas such as Condensed Matter Physics & Material Science, Gravity & String Theory, Light-Matter Interaction & Quantum Information, Nuclear & Particle Physics supported by modern research facilities and collaborations. With a strong emphasis on impactful research and innovation, the department continues to expand its contributions to frontier areas of science. We are committed to nurturing young researchers and advancing emerging fields, aligning with IIT Ropar's vision of excellence in science and technology.

Prof. Gagan Kumar

title: Gravity and Strings | Department of Physics
text:
❮ ❯
Gravity and Strings

The primary research areas of Gravity and String Theory group are quantum field theory and quantum theory of gravity. In this direction, the group explores the quantum properties of black holes, early stages of the universe and cosmic inflation, string theory in various limits, strong coupling dynamics of a quantum field theory, AdS/CFT correspondence and conformal field theory . These require the understanding of quantum field theory of matter fields and gravity on various curved backgrounds including black holes, various dark energy and inflationary models and developing new tools to explore perturbative and non-perturbative aspects of a quantum field theory in flat as well as non-trivial backgrounds.

title: B.Sc. - B.Ed. Programme | Department of Physics
text:
B.Sc. - B.Ed. Programme

The department has introduced an integrated 4-year undergraduate B.Sc.–B.Ed. programme from the July 2024 semester. This programme emphasizes a dual-major approach and seamlessly integrates teacher education within the broader higher education framework, enabling students to pursue both a Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) and a Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) degree simultaneously. A key advantage of this programme is that students can complete both degrees within four years, compared to the conventional five-year duration. Additionally, the programme offers flexibility, allowing students to exit after three years with a B.Sc. degree if they choose not to continue.

The curriculum is designed to provide academic flexibility, enabling students to choose majors and minors aligned with their interests and career goals while integrating teacher education components. The department will primarily offer 64 credits of coursework, spread across the first six semesters, for students majoring in Physics. Courses related to teacher education will be delivered by the Humanities Department.

Credit Structure

Total Minimum Credits – 160 (96 credits for HSS / B.Ed. + 64 credits for Sciences). Students must decide whether to pursue the Disciplinary or Interdisciplinary stream before the beginning of the 5th semester.

Disciplinary (Min 64 credits): 52 Core Physics + 7 (Introductory Chemistry + Calculus) + 12 Physics Elective = 64 (Physics) + 7 (others) = 71 credits. These students must take one additional course beyond Calculus from the Mathematics department to qualify the JAM eligibility criteria for M.Sc. programmes in IITs.
Interdisciplinary in Chemistry (Min 64 credits): 52 Core Physics + 4 (Calculus) + 3 (Introductory Chemistry) + 15 Chemistry Elective = 52 (Physics) + 18 (Chemistry) + 4 (other) = 74 credits.
Interdisciplinary in Mathematics (Min 64 credits): 52 Core Physics + 4 (Calculus) + 3 (Introductory Chemistry) + 12 Math Elective = 52 (Physics) + 16 (Math) + 3 (other) = 71 credits.

title: M.Sc Physics Curriculum | Department of Physics
text:
M.Sc. Programme

The Department has been offering a two-year M.Sc. Physics programme since 2015, with admissions through the Joint Admission Test for M.Sc. (JAM). The programme has grown steadily, with a regular intake of 25 students. It is designed as a research-intensive programme, comprising core courses, advanced electives, open electives from other departments based on student requirements, and a one-year research project. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on training using advanced research facilities, encouraging independent work and the development of strong analytical and technical skills. The programme provides a vibrant research environment that prepares students for diverse career paths. Several M.Sc. dissertations have resulted in high-quality research publications in international journals. Graduates pursue Ph.D. studies in reputed institutions in India and abroad or join organizations such as DAE, ISRO, DRDO, IUAC, and industries involving semiconductors, lasers, and vacuum technology. Students also have the option to continue into the Department's Ph.D. programme, subject to eligibility, making it a strong foundation for both research and professional careers.
