title: PhD Programme | Department of Physics
text:
Ph.D. Programme

The Department of Physics offers a rigorous and research-intensive Ph.D. programme across four major research areas: Condensed Matter Physics and Materials Science, Light–Matter Interaction and Quantum Information, Nuclear and Particle Physics, and Gravity and String Theory. The programme emphasizes early engagement in research, with foundational courses in Scientific Writing, Technical Communication, Research Methodology, and Ethics during the first year. This structure allows students to quickly integrate into research projects and develop essential skills for their doctoral journey.

The Department offers a Ph.D. programme in Physics with four major research areas: Condensed Matter Physics and Materials Science, Light–Matter Interaction and Quantum Information, Nuclear and Particle Physics, and Gravity and String Theory. The programme is strongly research-oriented, with no traditional coursework requirement; instead, from 2025 onwards, students undertake foundational research-related courses in the first year, including Scientific Writing and Technical Communication, and Research Methodology and Ethics. This structure helps students develop essential research skills and begin their doctoral work efficiently soon after joining the programme.

The Department has a strong track record of academic excellence, with Ph.D. scholars progressing to postdoctoral positions in reputed international institutions and securing faculty positions worldwide. Ph.D. admissions are taken twice a year, in July and January, while externally funded candidates such as CSIR-JRF/UGC-JRF/INSPIRE may apply through rolling advertisements throughout the year. Interviews for externally funded candidates are conducted regularly, and admissions are offered with flexibility, allowing students to join at different points during the academic cycle for smooth integration into ongoing research.

Admissions

Admissions Cycle: The institute conducts Ph.D. admissions twice a year, typically in June and December.

Additional Opportunities: Candidates holding a valid External Fellowship may apply throughout the year. Such candidates can contact faculty members directly via email or appear for a walk-in interview, subject to availability of positions.

₹2.0 lakhs support for international conference participation
Dynamic and collaborative academic ecosystem

Dr. Gagan Kumar
Professor & HOD
gk@iitrpr.ac.in +91-1881-232485 A-309, Har Gobind Khorana Block
Prof. Gagan Kumar is a Professor in the Department of Physics at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar), India. His research focuses on terahertz optics, plasmonics, metamaterials, guided wave devices, and ultrafast spectroscopy. He received his Ph.D. in Physics from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) in 2008, after completing his M.Sc. in Physics from Kurukshetra University in 2003 and B.Sc. (Non-Medical) from D.N. College, Hisar in 2001. Prof. Kumar has extensive international research experience, having worked as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the University of Utah, USA, and as a Research Associate at the University of Maryland, College Park, USA. He began his academic career in India at IIT Guwahati in 2013 as an Assistant Professor and later served as Associate Professor and Professor before joining IIT Ropar in 2025. His research group works on advanced photonic and electromagnetic structures with applications in terahertz technology, metamaterials, and optical devices.

Welcome to my homepage. Our research focuses on light manipulation, modulation, and its dynamics using innovative systems based on emerging materials like high-index topological insulators and phase-change materials. We harness unique structures such as curved-space metallic systems and metasurfaces to advance light control at nano- and microscales. Our work explores key applications including nanoscale waveguiding, deflection (prisms), focusing, and beam steering, with prospective projects developing compact solutions for advanced imaging and sensing.

title: Faculty Profile | Physics Department IIT Ropar
text:
AB
Dr. Debangsu Roy
debangsu@iitrpr.ac.in +91-1881-242159 A-M22, Har Gobind Khorana Block
Dr. Debangsu Roy is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Physics at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar. He received his Ph.D. in Physics from the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru. His research lies at the intersection of experimental condensed matter physics, quantum materials, and spintronics, with the overarching goal of developing materials and device platforms for emerging quantum technologies. His work spans spin and orbital transport phenomena, spin–orbit and orbital torques, harmonic Hall measurements, spin-pumping ferromagnetic resonance (FMR), magnetotransport, and quantum sensing. At IIT Ropar, he leads the Spintronic Materials and Devices Laboratory, where his group combines thin-film growth, microdevice fabrication, advanced magnetotransport characterization, and theoretical modeling to investigate quantum phenomena in low-dimensional and magnetic heterostructures. His recent research has focused on orbital torque effects in magnetic multilayers, nonlinear Hall phenomena, quantum materials with unconventional transport properties, and the suppression of thermoelectric artifacts in precision spintronic measurements. His research aims to bridge fundamental quantum physics with scalable device technologies, enabling energy-efficient spintronic memory and logic, quantum sensing, and future quantum information platforms.

Dr. Jena joined the Department of Physics as an Assistant Professor on 31st of December, 2013. His research expertise is in the field of nonlinear sum-frequency generation (SFG) vibrational spectroscopy and its application to probe the molecular structure various biomolecules and their interactions with interfacial water molecules at air/water and solid/water interfaces. He received his Ph.D. degree in 2008 from the Indian Institute of Technology, Madras, under the mentorship of Prof. Prem B. Bisht and Prof. S. Kasiviswanathan. During his Ph.D. program, he studied the nonlinear optical properties and relaxation processes of organic molecules by using the laser-induced transient grating technique. He joined Prof. Dennis Hore's group in 2007 as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Victoria, Canada studied interfacial water structure at solid / water interfaces using SFG vibrational spectroscopy. In 2011, he joined Prof. Sylvie Roke's group at Max-Planck Institute for Intelligent System, Germany and subsequently moved to EPFL, Switzerland worked on SFG scattering spectroscopy to probe formation and characterization of model membrane systems at the water / nanoscopic oil droplet interfaces.

Prof. Kumar is a selected member of Indian National Young Academy of Science (INYAS), National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI) and Fellow of Institute of Physics (IOP). Recently, the team led by Prof. Kumar, won the first prize in India in the Dare2Dream 4.0 competition held by DRDO, Ministry of Defence, Government of India. This award was given to develop Target Seeking and Proximity Sensing technologies for missile tracking. His research interest includes functional and renewable energy materials for optoelectronics and photovoltaics applications.

Dr. Pushpendra P. Singh
pps@iitrpr.ac.in +91-1881-242226 103 - TC
Pushpendra P. Singh is an experimental nuclear physicist with a passion for instrumentation. He earned a PhD in Physics from the Aligarh Muslim University for experimental investigations of low-energy incomplete fusion carried out at the Inter-University Accelerator Centre, New Delhi. His research focuses on low-energy nuclear reactions, rare-decay studies, and deployment of cyber-physical systems in the domains of environment, agriculture, and water. He received the "Prof. C. V. K. Baba Best Thesis Award - 2008" from the Indian Physics Association. He was awarded an INFN-International-Fellowship at the Laboratori Nazionali di Legnaro, Italy, in 2009 after a postdoctoral stay at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai. During his stay at LNL, he worked on sub-barrier fusion and (multi)-nucleon transfer reactions using an electrostatic separator and PRISMA spectrometer in the research group of Prof. Dr. Alberto M. Stefanini. After a term at Legnaro in 2011, he joined the Technical University Darmstadt / GSI - Helmholtz Centre for Heavy-Ion Research GmbH, Darmstadt, Germany, as a visiting scientist in the nuclear spectroscopy group of Prof. Dr. Norbert Pietralla / Prof. Dr. Juergen Gerl. At GSI, he has been associated with the Lund-York-Cologne-Calorimeter (LYCCA) and the Advanced GAmma Tracking Array (AGATA). He joined the Department of Physics at the Indian Institute of Technology Ropar in December 2013. He is a member of the NuStAR collaboration for the Facility for Anti-proton and Ion Research (FAIR) at Darmstadt in Germany, and collaborates with the scientists from JINR Dubna (Russia), TU Darmstadt (Germany), ANL (USA), LASTI (University of Hyogo, Japan), Aksaray University (Turkey), IUAC (New Delhi), TIFR (Mumbai), and AMU (Aligarh). He has been/is the principal investigator of a number of scientific projects approved by the national/international funding agencies, and is the author of >120 high-impact research articles.

AB
Dr. Rajeev Ahuja
Professor & Director of IIT Ropar
rajeev.ahuja@iitrpr.ac.in +91-1881-242482 A-318, Har Gobind Khorana Block
Rajeev Ahuja is Professor of computational Materials science at Uppsala University, Sweden. Currently, he is the Director of Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar, India. He was also holding the additional charge of Director of IIT Guwahati, India from Nov. 2023 to May 2024. He is one of the most highly cited researchers as well as top 5 materials Scientist in Sweden & India. He has done his Ph.D. from I.I.T. Roorkee in India in 1992. Same year he has joined Uppsala University, Sweden as post-doctoral fellow. He became Professor in 2007 at Uppsala University, Sweden. His main area of interest is material science with focus on energy such Batteries, Hydrogen Storage & production, sensors as well high-pressure physics. He has published more than 1200 scientific papers in peer-reviewed journals H-Index of 106, i-10 index 817 & no. of citations more than 52147. Dr. Ahuja has supervised 30 PhD students and more than 35 postdocs. He has been elected FRSC UK, APS-Fellow by American Physical Society (APS), USA and appointed in the Advisory Board of Journal of Materials Chemistry A & Materials Advances from Royal Society of Chemistry (England). He is Associate Editor of Nano Energy. He was also awarded Beller Lectureship for the APS March Meeting 2017. He been awarded the Wallmark prize for 2011 from KVA (Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences), and has previously received the Eder Lilly & Sven Thureus prize and the Benzelius prize from KVS. Dr. Ahuja is an elected member of the Swedish Royal Society of Sciences (KVS). He has been awarded Best Alumnus award from IIT Roorkee, India for excellence in research for 2021.

Dr. Rajesh V. Nair

Dr. Nair has earned his PhD degree from Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai in 2008. He carried out his post-doctoral research during the period 2008-2010 in Complex Photonic Systems, University of Twente, The Netherlands. He worked as Dr. K S Krishnan Fellow in Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Mumbai for the period 2010-2012 and later as Scientist D till 2013. Starting November 2013, Dr. Nair has joined as Assistant Professor in the Department of Physics at IIT Ropar. He has made notable contributions in the field of nano-optics such as the observation of sub-Bragg diffraction of waves in crystals, the first ever signature of three-dimensional photonic band gap, and lasing from nano-scale photonic structures. His scientific findings are published in high-impact journals and are highlighted in international scientific magazines like Nature India, Science, and Optics and Photonics News of Optical Society of America. Dr Nair was the recepitant of Dr. K S Krishnan Fellowship from Department of Atomic Energy, National Academy of Sciences in India (NASI) young scientist prize in Physical Sciences for the year 2012, and Indian Science Congress award in Physical Sciences for the year 2011-2012. Dr. Nair was awarded the Swarnajayanti Fellowship by the Ministry of Science and Technology, Govt. of India in 2020 and also selected as one among 75 Indian scientists below the age 50, who are shaping today's India by Govt. of India.

text:
AB
Dr. Ritu Gupta
ritu.gupta@iitrpr.ac.in +911881 A-M28, Har Gobind Khorana Block
Dr. Ritu Gupta is an experimental condensed matter physicist with specialized expertise in crystal growth design and characterizations. Her research focus revolves around the growth and characterization of fascinating quantum materials, including Quantum Spin Liquids, van der Waals materials, and complex low-dimensional magnetic systems, along with the exploration of Dirac and Weyl semimetals. She adeptly tunes their properties using external factors like pressure, strain, and disorder. During her doctoral studies at IIT Kanpur, Dr. Gupta specialized in the fields of superconductivity and magnetism. She worked in the growth of single and polycrystalline samples within the RPt2Si2 series, employing a range of techniques. She conducted extensive property analyses using various characterization methods, which further she tuned with chemical pressure. Additionally, she gained valuable experience during a six-month research stint at Neel Laboratory in Grenoble, France, supported by the Raman Charapk Fellowship. During this period, she conducted transport measurements under hydrostatic pressure. In her initial postdoctoral role at the Paul Scherrer Institute, Dr. Gupta delved into the phase diagram of strongly correlated electronic systems, employing pressure and doping as tools of investigation. Her utilization of muon spin relaxation techniques allowed for a deep exploration of these states under various conditions. Subsequently, at Geneva University during her second postdoctoral appointment, Dr. Gupta honed her skills in growing single crystals of 2D topological-magnetic materials, insulators, and superconductors using a variety of advanced techniques. Dr. Gupta's current research at IIT Ropar remains focused on the growth and characterization of intriguing quantum materials, including Quantum Spin Liquids (QSL), van der Waals materials, and complex low-dimensional magnetic systems while continuing to explore Dirac and Weyl semimetals. She remains actively engaged in the manipulation of their properties through external stimuli such as pressure, strain, and disorder. Beyond materials research, Dr. Gupta maintains a keen interest in the investigation of fascinating quantum phenomena, including unconventional superconductivity, non-Fermi Liquid behavior, and anomalous critical phenomena at low temperatures, particularly in proximity to quantum critical points influenced by quantum critical fluctuations.

srinivasarao.konda@iitrpr.ac.in +91 A-M33, Har Gobind Khorana Block
Dr. Srinivasa Rao Konda joined the Department of Physics at Indian Institute of Technology Ropar as an Assistant Professor in February 2025, where he is establishing the Strong-field Radiation and Kinetics Quantum Photonics Laboratory (SRKQPL). His research focuses on ultrafast photonics, nonlinear optics, terahertz (THz) science, strong-field light–matter interactions, and advanced spectroscopy of novel quantum and low-dimensional materials. Dr. KSRao received his Ph.D. degree from University of Hyderabad in 2016, and his doctoral thesis was awarded the “Best Thesis Award” at the National Laser Symposium (NLS-25). From 2017 to 2024, he worked at the GPL Photonics Laboratory, Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics, where his research involved the simultaneous generation of higher-order harmonics and THz radiation from emerging materials and nanostructures. During this period, he developed comprehensive THz generation and detection systems and carried out terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) studies to investigate ultrafast carrier dynamics, nonlinear optical responses, and photonic functionalities of newly synthesized materials, particularly novel 2D and quantum materials. He also gained experience in femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (fs-TAS) during his tenure as a short-term postdoctoral fellow at American University of Sharjah. In recognition of his scientific contributions and innovation activities, he represented UOH at the FION-2017 Meeting of National Innovation Clubs held at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Dr. KSRao has published more than 60 peer-reviewed research articles, authored one monograph, and serves as a reviewer and editorial board member for several international journals. At IIT Ropar, his current research aims to advance ultrafast dynamics, nonlinear and quantum photonics, THz spectroscopy, and strong-field phenomena for applications in next-generation photonic, optoelectronic, and quantum technologies.

● New Frequencies Generation
● THz- Time domain spectroscopy of 2D materials
● Photonics applications of perovskites and quantum materials
● Strong field interaction with matter for attosecond pulse generation
Our research focuses on the fundamental and applied aspects of ultrafast photonics, nonlinear optics, and advanced quantum materials. The work primarily explores light–matter interactions under intense electromagnetic fields and their applications in next-generation photonic and optoelectronic technologies. The major research themes include: Low- and Higher-Order Nonlinear Optical Effects Investigation of nonlinear optical phenomena arising from intense laser–matter interactions, including second- and third-order nonlinear responses, ultrafast carrier dynamics, harmonic generation, and nonlinear refractive effects in emerging materials. Generation of New Frequencies Study of nonlinear frequency conversion processes such as harmonic generation, sum- and difference-frequency generation, and terahertz wave generation for the development of tunable coherent light sources across broad spectral regions. THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy of 2D Materials Exploration of carrier transport, ultrafast conductivity, and low-energy excitations in two-dimensional materials using THz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS). This work aims to understand the dynamical properties of novel layered systems for high-speed electronic and optoelectronic applications. Photonics Applications of Perovskites and Quantum Materials Research on perovskite and quantum materials for advanced photonic applications including photodetectors, optical modulators, light emitters, and energy-efficient optoelectronic devices, with emphasis on their ultrafast optical and electronic properties. Strong-Field Interaction with Matter for Attosecond Pulse Generation Investigation of extreme nonlinear interactions between intense ultrafast laser pulses and matter, focusing on high-harmonic generation and attosecond pulse production for probing ultrafast electron dynamics at atomic time scales. Overall, the research integrates ultrafast spectroscopy, nonlinear optics, THz science, and quantum materials to advance both fundamental understanding and technological applications in modern photonics and condensed matter physics.

Subhendu Sarkar is an Associate Professor in the Department of Physics. He works in the area of surface and interface physics. His past research includes molecular ion formation aspects under low energy ion solid interactions and interfacial alloy formation in multilayered materials. Currently, his investigations include surface patterning using various physical and chemical techniques, evaporative self-assembly, light-matter interactions and their applications. His studies on surface patterning dealing with pattern transitions for mono and binary systems. Under evaporative self-assembly, his group tries to examine the role of surface fluctuations in drying of sessile droplets. within the area of light-matter interactions, he studies plasmonic responses from disordered matter. After obtaining his doctoral degree from the Surface Physics Division of Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, Kolkata, he went on to work as a post-doctoral fellow at Inter-University Microelectronic Centre (IMEC), Belgium. He was also a visiting scientist at Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, Kalpakkam before joining IIT Ropar. AB
Dr. Vijay K. Singh
vksingh@iitrpr.ac.in +91-1881-232483 A-320, Har Gobind Khorana Block
Dr. Vijay K. Singh is an experimental condensed matter physicist leading the Quantum Engineering for Science and Technologies (QuEST) research group at the Department of Physics, Indian Institute of Technology Ropar. His research is rooted in a strong passion for exploring how the quantum behavior of materials at the nanoscale can be harnessed to solve real-world challenges in energy, sensing, and healthcare. His academic background spans premier Indian institutions, beginning with B.Sc. in Physics with Honours from the Indian Institute of Science, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, M.Sc. in Physics from the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur. He earned his Ph.D. in Condensed Matter Physics from the Institute of Science, BHU, focusing on quantum confined van der Waals (vdW) nanomaterials and their heterostructures with a strong emphasis on their potential applications as per societal need. He undertook a postdoctoral fellowship at Jeonbuk National University (JBNU), South Korea, and later served as a DST INSPIRE Faculty Fellow at Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur, where he built a research trajectory in multifunctional nanoengineered quantum materials. As a scientist, he is deeply motivated by curiosity and the transformative potential of materials research. As a mentor, he is committed to fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and idea-driven research culture where team members are encouraged to pursue both fundamental questions and socially impactful applications. He believes in balancing scientific rigor with creativity, and mentorship as a shared journey where students are empowered to become independent thinkers and problem-solvers. He actively encourages interdisciplinary collaborations across all the branches of natural science, materials science, and engineering, believing that the future of innovation lies at the intersection of disciplines. He also prioritizes scientific communication and outreach, and welcomes opportunities to engage with the broader academic and public communities to promote awareness of the role of quantum materials in building a sustainable future.

AB
Dr. Vishwa Pal
vishwa.pal@iitrpr.ac.in +91-1881-232472 A-315, Har Gobind Khorana Block
Dr. Vishwa Pal is an Associate Professor in the Department of Physics at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar, Punjab, India. He earned his PhD degree in 2014 from the School of Physical Sciences, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi, India. As part of his doctoral research, he conducted a portion of his work at the CNRS Laboratoire Aimé Cotton, Orsay, France, under the Indo-French collaborative framework. His Ph.D. research focused on the investigation of semiconductor laser systems, specifically exploring noise correlations and dynamical control using delayed optical feedback. Following his Ph.D., Dr. Pal was awarded the prestigious PBC Fellowship for Outstanding Postdoctoral Researchers by the Council for Higher Education of Israel. He joined the research group of Prof. Nir Davidson and Prof. Asher A. Friesem at the Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel. His postdoctoral research focused on phase-locking large arrays of lasers and utilizing them to explore topological effects, simulate spin systems, and solve computationally hard problems. Additionally, he contributed to industrial laser beam shaping applications in collaboration with Israeli industry partners. In 2018, Dr. Pal joined CREOL, The College of Optics and Photonics, in Florida, USA, as a Research Scientist. There, he worked on the synthesis of non-diffracting optical beams in free space by leveraging space-time correlations. In the same year, he was awarded the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Individual Fellowship by the European Commission.

Our research focuses on understanding and designing next-generation quantum and energy materials using first-principles computational methods. We employ Density Functional Theory (DFT), many-body perturbation theory (MBPT), molecular dynamics, data-driven and machine learning approaches to investigate the structural, electronic, magnetic, transport, and optical properties of emerging functional materials and heterostructures. The group is particularly interested in materials for energy conversion and storage, low-dimensional magnetic systems, quantum materials, and novel electronic functionalities. By combining quantum-mechanical modelling with analytical theory and data science, we aim to uncover fundamental materials design principles and accelerate the discovery of high-performance materials for future energy and electronic technologies.

SNEHITA
WELLBEING
Message

Welcome to the Snehita Well Being Cell at IIT Ropar! We are dedicated to providing comprehensive mental health care and counseling services for our students, faculty, and staff. Our mission is to promote self-care, nurture resilience, and foster positive growth within our community. Through addressing psychological difficulties and facilitating healthy coping strategies, we empower individuals to understand themselves better and enact positive changes in their personal and emotional well-being. Join us as we embark on a journey of self growth and thriving in life. We conduct various promotional activities on mental health eduction to enhance awareness and knowledge among our fraternity.

ACHIEVEMENTS
Counselled 600+ students

Snehita at IIT Ropar has offered counseling to over 600 students, playing a vital role in supporting their mental health, fostering a healthier campus environment.

Solved 1000+ cases

Snehita at IIT Ropar has made a positive impact on more than 1000 cases, nurturing a supportive environment and advancing overall well-being within the campus community.

150+ Red Flagged cases

Addressed and resolved over 150 red-flagged cases, showcasing Snehita's commitment to promoting a secure and thriving campus environment at IIT Ropar.

COUNSELLOR'S MESSAGE
Deepak Kumar
Counsellor, Snehita Well Being
We know that Campus life can be exhilarating, but it can also be overwhelming at times. Balancing coursework, extracurricular activities, social life, and personal responsibilities can put a strain on your mental health. That's why it's crucial to prioritize self-care and seek support when needed. Although after COVID, the attitude of individuals in society towards mental health is gradually changing positively. I feel as we navigate the challenges and responsibilities of academic life, it's essential to pause and reflect on our mental health and wellbeing. Your overall wellness is not just important; it's imperative for your success and happiness during your college journey.Here are a few reminders and resources to help you maintain your mental health and wellbeing: Take Breaks, Establish Boundaries, Connect with your loved ones, Practice Self - Compassion, and seek help when needed.

Remember that seeking help is a sign of strength, not weakness. Your mental health matters, and there's no shame in asking for support when you need it. Acknowledge your accomplishments, no matter how small, and forgive yourself for mistakes or setbacks. As your Institute Counsellor, my door is always open to you. Please don't hesitate to reach out if you need assistance or simply someone to talk to. Your wellbeing is our top priority, and we're here to support you every step of the way.

Thank You,

Deepak Kumar

Don't hesitate to seek help when needed - we are here for you. When Mind controls the body, It should matter!!!

If you are experiencing stress, worry, loneliness, or emotional fatigue, please remember that you do not have to navigate it alone. Support is available, and reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness. Our counselling services are here to provide a safe, confidential, and understanding space where you can express yourself freely.

Your mind influences every aspect of your life — when it is nurtured, everything else functions better. Prioritize your mental wellbeing. It truly matters, and so do you.,

It helps you stay focused, build strong relationships, and make the most of your time. So, make time for self-care, talk to someone if you need to, and remember, you're not alone in this. We're all in this together.

## SNEHITA
Snehita - Well Being Cell has been set up with the objective of providing assistance to the IIT Ropar fraternity for overall psychological well being, with a major focus to cater the mental health care and counselling needs of our individuals. With the intent to address and to help with resolving emotional and psychological issues of the individuals is the core aim of this cell. This cell encourages our students to understand themselves better and to enable them in solving their personal, emotional as well as psychological problems and also to facilitate positive changes in their overall growth and behaviour.

Wellbeing and Counselling services at IIT Ropar are a part of Student Support Service which comes under Student Affairs Section. The cell has been providing services like individual counselling on various psychological issues like academic anxiety, adjustment problems, depressive reactions, sleep difficulties, relationship concerns, confidence building, problem solving, decision making, unhealthy internet use, etc. We have a group of Student Volunteers known as our Snehita Buddies who are actively engaged in helping us in reaching out to the unreached and in conducting various promotional/educational activities on mental health. With the mix of reactive and proactive approaches, Snehita Wellbeing Cell has proactively taken up the initiative of promoting the information & knowledge within the students, staff and faculty on various healthy issues in the form of online/offline talks, poster competitions, etc.

Every year Snehita-Well Being Cell conducts Induction/Orientation program for the fresher's both UG and PG students just to orient the new students about various challenges during the time of transitions from school to college and help them enable in how to deal with those challenges effectively. Also, this cell conducts various informative seminars and activities (online/offline) regularl y with the help of prominent experts/consultants/faculties from medical colleges and academic institutes on Wellbeing, Quality of Life, and related to General Mental Health issues with the purpose of creating awareness among the Institute population.

Dr. Puneet Pasricha is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics and currently serves as the Dean of Students Affairs at IIT Ropar. A strong advocate of student wellness and holistic development, he works closely with the Board of Wellness Affairs to foster a supportive, inclusive, and positive environment. text:
Dr. Abhinav Kumar

Computer Vision

I am an Assistant Professor at the School of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, specializing in medical imaging, deep learning, explainable AI, and trustworthy AI models for healthcare applications. I earned my Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from IIT BHU, where I developed an AI-assisted diagnostic framework for cancer classification, integrating machine learning, deep learning, and interpretability techniques to enhance model reliability and clinical usability. My research in medical imaging spans cancer diagnosis, class imbalance handling, federated learning for medical AI, and multimodal diagnostics, with a strong emphasis on explainability, robustness, and real-world deployment. Beyond medical AI, my three-year postdoctoral research extended to AI-driven antimicrobial peptide (AMP) discovery as an alternative to antibiotics. In AMP discovery, I utilized deep learning and generative models to predict novel antimicrobial candidates, contributing to advancements in precision medicine and computational drug discovery. Additionally, my work on livestock identification focused on computer vision-based biometric authentication and disease monitoring, supporting precision livestock farming and veterinary diagnostics. I have contributed to high-impact publications, algorithmic advancements, and interdisciplinary collaborations across healthcare AI, computational biology, and animal biometrics. As a reviewer for top-tier IEEE Transactions journals, I actively contribute to advancing the frontiers of AI, machine learning, and biomedical informatics. My ongoing research focuses on developing explainable AI frameworks for reliable medical AI, learning with limited data, deep learning solutions for complex computer vision challenges and federated learning for privacy-preserving medical diagnostics.

Welcome to Rajendra Catalysis Research Group, IIT Ropar

CSIR-UGC-JRF candidates at IIT Ropar for 2026 can write directly to rajendra@iitrpr.ac.in

One JRF position is available to join immediately in PAIR-Project. Contact at rajendra@iitrpr.ac.in

The objective of our research is to develop a new class of nanoporous materials or develop synthesis strategies that enable us to significantly improve the physicochemical properties of existing materials. In order to obtain the desired activity for appointed catalytic applications, multifunctional solid catalysts with isolated and/or well defined catalytic active sites are developed. Consequently, the synthesis, characterization and catalytic applications of microporous/mesoporous crystalline materials such as zeolites, metal oxides, polyaniline, hybrid organo-inorganic materials such as MOF, carbon materials, and nanoparticles are of significant interest to us. Catalysts with mono or multifunctional active sites allow us to use them in a wide range of applications that include, heterogeneous catalysis in chemicals synthesis, photo-assisted chemical synthesis, electrocatalytic applications (such as energy applications and sensing), production of alternative energy resources, etc. A selection of scientific articles published in the last 5-6 years showcases the research developed in my group.

Dr. Tanushree Meena is currently serving as an Assistant Professor at the School of Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (sAIDE), Indian Institute of Technology Ropar (IIT Ropar), where she is engaged in teaching, research, and interdisciplinary initiatives at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, healthcare, and intelligent computing. Her work focuses on developing robust, interpretable, and data-efficient AI systems for healthcare applications. Her current research emphasizes multimodal healthcare AI, interpretable deep learning frameworks, medical image analysis, computer-aided diagnosis, and advanced machine learning methodologies for clinical decision support. Dr. Tanushree is actively involved in interdisciplinary research aimed at translating AI innovations into reliable and practical healthcare solutions.

title: About Us | ANNAM.AI Mission & Vision
text:
IIT Ropar, Punjab, India – 140001

About ANNAM.AI

Alliance for Next-Gen Nourishment through Agriculture Modernization

Innovation Hub

Cutting-edge research in AI & agriculture

50+ Partners

Collaboration with top institutions

Excellence

Leading AI Centre in India

Global Impact

Transforming agriculture worldwide

Our Vision

A climate-resilient and data-driven agricultural ecosystem in India where farmers thrive through timely insights, precision guidance, and sustainable growth.

Our Mission

To deliver hyperlocal, AI-powered advisories by integrating crop intelligence, real-time microclimate data, and multilingual engagement tools, while building a national agricultural intelligence backbone as a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) that enables precision agriculture, climate resilience, and data-driven governance at scale.

IIT Ropar Campus

Punjab, India

About IIT Ropar

Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Ropar is a hub of innovation and technological advancement in India. The institution places a strong emphasis on fostering cutting-edge research and development, with a focus on addressing real-world challenges through technology.

It offers a conducive environment for innovative thinking, featuring state-of-the-art laboratories and research facilities. IIT Ropar actively collaborates with industry leaders and other reputed institutions globally, ensuring a rich exchange of knowledge and technology transfer.

Its initiatives in promoting technology include incubating start-ups, hosting hackathons and innovation challenges, and offering specialized programs in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, robotics, and sustainable technology.

About AI-CoE

AI Centres of Excellence (AI CoEs) are vital for fostering innovation, interdisciplinary research, and scalable AI solutions tailored to societal challenges. Focused on areas like agriculture, healthcare, and sustainable cities, AI CoEs enable cutting-edge applications that enhance productivity, improve quality of life, and address sustainability goals.

They facilitate collaboration between academia, industry, and government, leveraging advanced computing infrastructure and data-driven insights to solve critical problems.

By nurturing talent, driving entrepreneurship, and delivering impactful research, these centers play a crucial role in positioning nations as global leaders in AI, ensuring the technology's benefits reach diverse communities.

AI Innovation

Transforming the Future

Why Agriculture?

Revolutionizing agriculture through innovative and sustainable solutions

The Challenge

A Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Agriculture is essential for revolutionizing the sector through innovative and sustainable solutions. Agriculture faces challenges like unpredictable weather, declining soil health, water scarcity, pest infestations, and supply chain inefficiencies.

Our Solution

An Agriculture CoE leverages cutting-edge technologies like AI, IoT, and remote sensing to address these issues comprehensively.

By integrating traditional knowledge with real-time data, it can optimize resource use, predict crop yields, improve soil regeneration, and provide precise weather-related advisories.

Smart Farming

Technology Meets Agriculture

The Impact
Optimising Input & Output Efficiency for Smarter Farming
Driving Farm Income Stability Through Intelligent Data Insights
Fosters collaboration among academia, industry, and policymakers
Aligns with global efforts to combat climate change

Be part of the revolution in digital agriculture and sustainable farming

FIELD DATA COLLECTION
CropSense AI

CropSense AI: Smart farming app for crop, pest, and field data collection.

CropSense AI is an easy-to-use smart farming application developed by IIT Ropar. It helps farmers, researchers, and farming organizations collect and manage field details such as crop growth, pests, diseases, and environmental conditions in real time.

With CropSense AI, you can easily record farm observations, take photos of crops, and log precise GPS locations. The app works offline, meaning you can collect data in remote fields without internet connectivity, and it will automatically sync once you are back online.

Key features include intuitive digital forms for quick logging, automatic date and location tagging for every photo, offline mode for remote fields, secure log-ins for different team members, a simple dashboard to view reports, and compatibility across Android, iOS, and Web browsers.

Designed with simplicity in mind, CropSense AI bridges agricultural research with everyday farming, helping you keep track of your fields, document crop health, and make informed decisions easily.

Fasal Netra

AI-powered crop pest & disease detection for farmers by Annam.AI, IIT Ropar.

FasalNetra (फसल नेत्र) is an intelligent crop health assistant developed by the Annam.AI team at IIT Ropar. It helps farmers, farm advisers, and researchers instantly identify crop pests and diseases by simply taking a photo of the affected plant.

The application analyzes the crop photo using smart technology to recognize issues, estimate how severe the damage is, and provide visual guides to explain the detection.

Along with identification, FasalNetra provides practical, crop-specific treatment recommendations to help you protect your harvest. It works offline in fields with weak signals and saves your observations automatically.

The app supports major Indian crops including Rice, Wheat, Cotton, Maize, and Chilli, and is continuously updated to cover more crops to support healthy, pesticide-optimized farming.

SurvAI — India's First AI-Powered Tamper-Proof Digital Crop Survey App

Developed by ANNAM.AI, SurvAI empowers field surveyors to conduct transparent, corruption-free digital crop surveys.

Developed by the ANNAM.AI team at IIT Ropar (supported by the Ministry of Education, Government of India), SurvAI is a digital crop survey application designed to help field officers conduct transparent and secure crop surveys.

KEY FEATURES:
GPS-Locked Field Mapping

Draw field boundaries on the map by walking along the edge of the farm or tapping points on the screen. The coordinates are locked using GPS satellite details to prevent discrepancies.

Smart Crop Detection

Take pictures of the crops, and the app will recognize the crop type and health status, helping surveyors verify field productivity instantly.

Secured, Unalterable Reports

Every survey is digitally locked and sealed with timestamps, photo evidence, and GPS coordinates. This ensures the data is tamper-proof and authentic.

Farmer Verification

A quick verification code sent to the farmer's mobile phone confirms their presence during the survey, ensuring honest records.

Offline Survey Support

Allows surveyors to work in remote rural areas without internet. The collected data is stored securely on the device and syncs automatically once a mobile network is found.

WHO IS IT FOR:
Government field surveyors
Crop insurance verification teams
Agricultural department officers

SurvAI is built with the goal of providing transparent, verified, and real-time farming intelligence to protect both crop records and farmers' interests.

Sanket is built to provide timely, location-aware pest risk information that can help farmers become more aware of potential threats and make informed crop management decisions.

ANNAM.AI Hackathon 2025

Frequently Asked Questions

General Information
What is the ANNAM.AI Hackathon?
The ANNAM.AI Hackathon is an 8-week, full-time, hackathon-style internship organized by IIT Ropar's Centre of Excellence in AI for Agriculture. Participants work on real-world agricultural challenges using AI, receive expert mentorship, and stand a chance to win prizes and internship offers.
When does the hackathon take place?
● Launch & Orientation: 20th May 2025
● Final Submission: 20th July 2025
Who can participate?
The hackathon is open to:
● Undergraduate (UG), Postgraduate (PG), and PhD students
● Working professionals, researchers, and agri-tech innovators

Participation can be online or in-person at IIT Ropar.
How can I apply?
Applications are open through the official website: annam.ai/hackathon
Program Structure
I got a confirmation mail for the Hackathon, but I did not receive any mail for the competition. What do I do?
Please reply to the confirmation mail stating you have not received the competition link and instructions. Please note that the link and instructions will be shared only with the registered team leaders, who will respectively share it with their team members.
What is the format of the hackathon?
This is a full-time, project-based internship lasting 8 weeks. Participants work on real-world datasets, build AI models, and develop innovative solutions for agriculture.
What are the focus areas?
Participants will address challenges in:
● Soil Health (AI tools for soil diagnostics)
● Smart Irrigation (optimizing water usage)
● Pest Management (AI-driven pest identification)
● Crop Monitoring (growth analysis and yield prediction)
● Post-Harvest Systems (enhancing logistics and supply chains)
What deliverables are expected?
By the end of the hackathon, teams are expected to submit:
● A working AI model or prototype
● Complete documentation and codebase
● A short demo video showcasing the solution
Is there any difference in online and offline mode?
There would be no difference in the online and offline modes of the program. Participants can meet the mentors at a time of their convenience and availability. However, participation in both modes have to be full time.
Awards & Recognition
What are the prizes?
● 1st Prize: ₹5,00,000
● 2nd Prize: ₹4,00,000
● 3rd Prize: ₹3,00,000
● 4th Prize: ₹2,00,000
● 5th Prize: ₹1,00,000
● 200 Honorable Mentions: ₹15,000 each

Top teams may also be offered opportunities to continue working with ANNAM.AI.
Will participants receive any certification or academic credit?
Yes. Participants who successfully complete the hackathon will receive:
● An official certificate of completion from IIT Ropar
● 10 academic credits (through the Academic Bank of Credits system, subject to institutional approval)
Additional Information
What support will teams receive?
Participants will be mentored by experts from ANNAM.AI, receiving technical and strategic guidance throughout the hackathon.
How does this hackathon align with India's AI vision?
The hackathon contributes to India's national initiative: 'Make AI in India & Make AI Work for India.' Winning innovations may be further developed under Phase II at IIT Ropar's Centre of Excellence.
Who can I contact for more information?
Email: admin@annam.ai
Shortlisting and Certificate Eligibility
Will everyone who applies be selected?
A shortlisting process will be implemented.
What are the main criteria for shortlisting participants?
Preference will be given to applicants who meet the following:
● Final year UG or PG students (graduating in 2025 or 2026)
● Students from agriculture-related institutions
● Applicants with prior experience in AI, ML, agriculture, or related fields
● Candidates who already have an advisor or mentor
How will my prior experience be evaluated?
Your application should highlight relevant projects, internships, certifications, or research work. A strong portfolio will enhance your chances of being shortlisted.
Is having an advisor mandatory?
No, it is not mandatory. However, candidates who already have an advisor will be preferred during shortlisting.
Will every participant get a certificate?
Certificates will only be issued to participants who are officially shortlisted and complete all project deliverables successfully.
I am not from an agricultural institution. Can I still apply?
Yes. Applicants from all academic disciplines are welcome. However, in case of limited capacity, candidates from agricultural institutions will be given preference.
I am not a final year student. Can I still apply?
Yes, you are welcome to apply. Final year students (B.Tech/M.Tech) will be given preference if applications exceed the intake limit.
Is there a deadline to submit the application form?
All applications must be submitted by 9th May 2025 by 11:59 PM. Late submissions may not be considered, so we recommend completing your application well before the deadline.
Can I edit my application after submission?
If you need to make changes to your application after submission, please contact the ANNAM.AI team directly at admin@annam.ai for assistance.
Who should fill out the registration form if participating as a team?
Only one member per team should fill out the registration form on behalf of the entire team. The form will ask for the names and email addresses of all team members.
Can I register individually?
Yes! You can register individually, in which case you will be grouped by us based on relevant areas of interest. You may also apply as a team not exceeding five members. Please ensure only one application has been submitted per team.
Can I get assigned a mentor?
Yes! During registration, you will have the option to choose a mentor assigned by ANNAM.AI or specify your own advisor.
Will it be considered a hackathon project or an internship project?
While regular internships have students working on projects designed by mentors, this hackathon enables students to identify problems and design solutions of their own, thus giving the freedom to explore their potential. Students will also be mentored throughout the period. It will be considered an internship upon submission of deliverables and students will be provided with a certificate. Since students will also be provided with 10 credits, it also qualifies to be a course.
Will accommodation and food be provided for the teams participating on campus?
Accommodation at the hostel will be provided based on availability. Final allotment will depend on the number of applications received. You may refer to the institute website for charges. Details regarding food arrangements will be communicated closer to the event.
What are the selection criteria?
All participants are expected to complete an assignment that would be given in the first week of the program. Only participants who attend the orientation session and submit the completed assignment will be selected.
Can I join the program later or leave earlier due to other commitments?
Your certificate and credits will be given based on submission of weekly deliverables and full-time participation. Hence, no changes can be made in the timeline of the program for any participant.
Will I receive a stipend for participating?
Stipend is applicable only for participants who submit their work on time. Participants who do not submit will not receive any stipend or certificate.

INDIA'S AGRICULTURE HACKATHON
Bridging AI research with real-world farming
ABOUT THE COLLABORATION
A partnership built for impact

This hackathon is driven by a shared purpose: making agriculture smarter, more sustainable, and more resilient for Indian farmers.

Syngenta Biologicals
GLOBAL CROP PROTECTION

Syngenta Biologicals brings science-based innovation to give more choices and flexibility to farmers.

With the most comprehensive portfolio in the industry, Syngenta Biologicals offer additional solutions to manage pests and diseases, address abiotic stresses, and enhance soil health and nutrient use efficiency.

Backed by best-in-class internal R&D and strengthened by external partnerships, it provides growers with innovative and effective biological products focused on their needs.

ANNAM.AI, IIT Ropar
CENTRE OF EXCELLENCE IN AI FOR AGRICULTURE

India's first Centre of Excellence in AI for Agriculture, established at IIT Ropar under the Ministry of Education, Government of India.

ANNAM.AI bridges the gap between advanced AI research and real-world farming challenges, empowering farmers with data-driven insights, scalable digital tools, and AI-powered advisory systems in their own languages.

THE VISION
What we want to build

As the premier AI Agriculture Hackathon in India, HACK CORE 2026 challenges participants to design an AI-enabled, precision agriculture solution that empowers Indian farmers and the broader agricultural ecosystem to:

01
01
VISUALISE

Understand climate, soil, and disease risks specific to a region, crop, and season - and what these mean for yield outcomes.

02
02
RECOMMEND

Receive intelligent, data-driven recommendations on the most suitable biological products - what to apply and when.

03
03
TRACK & IMPROVE

Monitor outcomes during the season and feed that data back to generate continuously improving recommendations.

The solution must be practical, scalable, and designed with the Indian farming ecosystem at its centre -serving growers, distributors, and retailers alike.

HACKATHON STRUCTURE
Three tracks, one mission

HACK CORE 2026 is structured around three core tracks. Teams may choose one track or build a solution spanning multiple.

Explore all tracks
01
TRACK 01
RISK INTELLIGENCE

See threats before they strike

Build an AI-powered dashboard that helps farmers and advisors visualise climate, soil, and disease risks at a field or regional level. Data sources may include weather APIs, satellite imagery, soil maps, and disease surveillance data.

02
TRACK 02
BIOLOGICAL PRODUCT RECOMMENDATION ENGINE

Match product to need, precisely

Design a recommendation engine that matches biological products to specific crop, soil, and climate conditions. The model should incorporate agronomic data, product efficacy data, and local environmental variables.

03
TRACK 03
OUTCOME TRACKING & CONTINUOUS LEARNING

Build systems that improve with every season

Build a feedback and tracking system that allows farmers or field agents to log outcomes during the season. Use this data to improve product recommendations in subsequent seasons through machine learning.

Our Brand Story
The Story Behind the ANNAM.AI Logo: A Symbol of Earth, AI, and Curiosity

The ANNAM.AI logo is a powerful visual representation of our mission – bridging Artificial Intelligence (AI) with the natural world to drive innovation and discovery in agriculture. Designed with purpose, it captures the essence of Earth, intelligence, and the relentless human curiosity that fuels progress.

Earth: A Commitment to Sustainability

The circular form of the logo echoes the shape of our planet, reinforcing ANNAM.AI's commitment to sustainability, agriculture, and the balance between technology and nature. It symbolizes the interconnected ecosystems that sustain life and the importance of preserving them through responsible innovation.

The leaf element within the design represents growth, regeneration, and life – key pillars of sustainable agriculture. Our AI-driven solutions aim to enhance agricultural efficiency while maintaining harmony with the environment.

The integration of AI into our identity reflects our core approach: leveraging advanced technologies to revolutionize agriculture. AI processes vast amounts of data, uncovering insights that empower farmers, agribusinesses, and policymakers.

Every question leads to new discoveries, and ANNAM.AI is dedicated to turning curiosity into real-world solutions that benefit farmers, businesses, and communities worldwide.

title: HACK CORE 2026 | AI Agriculture Hackathon India at IIT Ropar
text:
ABOUT HACK CORE 2026
A collaboration built for impact

ANNAM.AI and Syngenta Biologicals have come together to address one of agriculture's most pressing challenges - making biological solutions genuinely accessible and actionable for Indian farmers.

THE PARTNERS
Who's behind HACK CORE 2026
Syngenta Biologicals
Global Crop Protection

Syngenta Biologicals brings science-based innovation to give more choices and flexibility to farmers.

With the most comprehensive portfolio in the industry, Syngenta Biologicals offer additional solutions to manage pests and diseases, address abiotic stresses, and enhance soil health and nutrient use efficiency.

Backed by best-in-class internal R&D and strengthened by external partnerships, it provides growers with innovative and effective biological products focused on their needs.

ANNAM.AI, IIT Ropar
Centre of Excellence in AI for Agriculture

India's first Centre of Excellence in AI for Agriculture, established at IIT Ropar under the Ministry of Education, Government of India.

ANNAM.AI bridges the gap between advanced AI research and real-world farming challenges, empowering farmers with data-driven insights, scalable digital tools, and AI-powered advisory systems in their own languages.

THE PROBLEM
The gap we need to close

Biological products offer a promising and sustainable path forward for Indian exists between their potential and what farmers can actually access:

Limited data on biological efficacy across diverse climates, soil types, and cropping systems in India

No integrated platform to help farmers visualise climate and soil risks and match them to appropriate biological solutions

Lack of real-time, season-long tools that track outcomes and build better recommendations over time

Fragmented access across the farming ecosystem - growers, distributors, and retailers remain disconnected from actionable, evidence-based guidance

The result: suboptimal product selection, reduced yields, and missed opportunity to protect crops in the face of growing environmental pressure.

THE VISION
What HACK CORE 2026 aims to build

An AI-enabled solution that empowers farmers and the broader agricultural ecosystem to:

VISUALISE

Understand climate, soil, and disease risks specific to your region, crop, and season - and what these mean for yield outcomes.

RECOMMEND

Receive intelligent, data-driven recommendations on the most suitable biological products for specific conditions - what to apply and when.

TRACK & IMPROVE

Monitor outcomes during the season and feed that data back to generate continuously improving recommendations for following years.

The solution must be practical, scalable, and designed with the Indian farming ecosystem at its centre -serving growers, distributors, and retailers alike.

title: HACK CORE 2026 | AI Agriculture Hackathon India at IIT Ropar
text:
HACKATHON STRUCTURE
Three tracks, one mission

HACK CORE 2026 is structured around three core problem tracks. Teams may choose one track or build a solution that spans multiple tracks.

PROBLEM TRACKS
Choose your challenge

Each track targets a distinct failure point in how biological products reach and benefit Indian farmers. Select the one that aligns with your team's strengths.

01

TRACK 01

RISK INTELLIGENCE

See threats before they strike

Build an AI-powered dashboard that helps farmers and advisors visualise climate, soil, and disease risks at a field or regional level. Data sources may include weather APIs, satellite imagery, soil maps, and disease surveillance data.

EXPECTED OUTPUT

An intuitive risk visualisation tool that generates actionable early warnings for farmers.

02

TRACK 02

BIOLOGICAL PRODUCT RECOMMENDATION ENGINE

Match product to need, precisely

Design a recommendation engine that matches biological products to specific crop, soil, and climate conditions. The model should incorporate agronomic data, product efficacy data, and local environmental variables.

EXPECTED OUTPUT

A smart advisory layer that tells farmers which biological product to use, when, and why.

03

TRACK 03

OUTCOME TRACKING & CONTINUOUS LEARNING

Build systems that improve with every season

Build a feedback and tracking system that allows farmers or field agents to log outcomes during the season. Use this data to improve product recommendations in subsequent seasons through machine learning.

EXPECTED OUTPUT

A closed-loop learning system that evolves with each growing season.

DELIVERABLES
Expected final product

An AI-enabled solution designed to support farmers in:

1

Visualizing the climate, soil and disease risks facing them and implications for their crop

2

Recommending the best fit biological products for their crop, soil types and field conditions and when to apply them

3

Track outcomes during the season and use the data to improve recommendations for the subsequent year

SUBMISSION FORMAT

A working prototype (e.g. an app, website, etc.) and a concise PowerPoint presentation.

EVALUATION
What we're looking for

Clear problem articulation

Clearly defined the identified problem.

Solution representation

Showcase the proposed solution prototype.

Functional highlights

Highlight the key functionalities: Awareness, recommendation and feedback loop. Any other functionalities or visualization is a bonus.

Decision-making process

Explain how the solution effectively tackles the identified problem.

Visual components

Include visual elements that enhance understanding (graphics, charts, etc.).

CORE REQUIREMENTS

–
Clarity in communicating the problem solution fit -how does this solution solve the problem
–
Usability of the solution based on the user base
–
Usage of latest technologies to simulate the algorithm and visualize the impact

FAQ
Frequently asked
questions.

Everything you need to know about HACK CORE 2026—format, eligibility, problem tracks, and what to expect.

PARTICIPATION AND CONFIRMATION
I applied for the hackathon. I did not get a response.
NEW

We received an overwhelming response from talented students and professionals across the country, making the selection process highly competitive.

After a careful review of all applications against the evaluation criteria, about 15 teams were shortlisted and communication was sent to them.

While we understand this may be disappointing, we would like to emphasize that this decision is in no way a reflection of your potential or capabilities. With a limited number of teams that could be accommodated, several promising applications could not be taken forward.

We encourage you to continue exploring AI-driven solutions for agriculture and sustainability and to stay connected with ANNAM.AI. We will be announcing future hackathons, innovation challenges, workshops, and collaborative opportunities, and we would be delighted to see your participation in these initiatives.

FORMAT & STRUCTURE
What is the format of HACK CORE 2026?
What are the focus areas of HACK CORE 2026?
When does HACK CORE 2026 take place?

HACK CORE 2026 will be split into two phases - the ideation phase; and BUILD SPRINT. Shortlisted teams will be given an orientation by mentors from Annam.AI and Syngenta Biologicals, followed by the ideation phase. Only the qualified teams from the ideation phase will be invited on campus to Indian Institute of Technology Ropar.

Ideation phase - 3rd - 16th August, 2026
BUILD SPRINT - 9th - 11th September, 2026

ELIGIBILITY & TEAMS
Who can participate in this AI Agriculture Hackathon?
What are the main criteria of shortlisting participants?
How do I form my team?
Should my team members be from the same batch and same institute?

No. Team members only need to have the required skills to develop AI solutions for agriculture. They can be from any background, institute or be employed as professionals. As long as the team has what it takes, we are happy to have you on board.

PROBLEM STATEMENTS & SUPPORT
Do we need to come up with our own problem statements?
What support will teams receive?

One of the defining features of HACK CORE 2026 is that participants will have access to world-class technology infrastructure during the hackathon. This levels the playing field and allows teams to focus entirely on solving the problem.

Syngenta Biologicals Product Data - Proprietary agronomic datasets on biological product efficacy across soil types, climate zones, and crop varieties, shared exclusively for use within HACK CORE 2026.

Mentorship Access - Dedicated technical mentors from Google, Syngenta GCC, and ANNAM.AI available throughout the BUILD SPRINT to support teams on architecture, modelling, and domain challenges.

Still have questions?

The best way to get answers is to apply and connect with our team. You'll receive an orientation session with mentors from ANNAM.AI and Syngenta once shortlisted.

For any queries, email us at hackathon@annam.ai

text:
DIRECTOR'S MESSAGE

Dear Friends,

It gives me immense pleasure to present Maanjhi: the Journalism Club of IIT Ropar—a unique endeavour to instill values, critical inquiry, and responsible storytelling within our community and beyond. We are living in an era when narratives may shape the future world, and the students of IIT Ropar should learn to diligently pursue the truth and give voice to diverse perspectives. This will be our first step to foster informed citizens and thoughtful leaders who carry forward IIT Ropar's tradition of excellence.

The club's name pays a homage to Dashrath Maanjhi, the legendary "Mountain Man" of India, who through extraordinary perseverance carved a path through a mountain. His labour and grit connected two diverse sides and ushered in an era of peace, prosperity and connectivity to his people. In the exact same vein, Maanjhi aspires to bridge divides and foster dialogue between the countless stakeholders of our institute, both within and beyond campus.

IIT Ropar is a microcosm of our great nation—singular, proud, and dedicated to excellence. We have been a trendsetter in academic programs, research, and outreach, having created a space where creativity, collaboration, and competition flourish at equal measures. We have also remained encouraging to cultural diversity, which forms the foundation of our students' careers and lives in and outside the IIT periphery.

A journalism club that documents the ideas, achievements and joys of campus life is therefore a timely and necessary step. Through the formation of Maanjhi, we seek to contribute to a national responsibility: preparing critical thinkers and responsible storytellers. This initiative strengthens our role as a crucible for scientific progress and democratic engagement with the world of academia, where knowledge meets conscience and local concerns connect with national purpose.

I warmly congratulate the editorial team of Maanjhi and welcome them to our collective march toward academic excellence and freedom of thought.

Jai Hind!
